To replace the screen of a Samsung A737 cell phone, first off, turn the phone off, remove the battery, battery cover and SIM card. Second, remove 6 Phillips screws from the back of the phone, 2 of which are under little rubber caps, which you can pry up with your flathead screwdriver. Remove the two silver side buttons. Third, disconnect the number pad connector from the main circuit board (it pops off by pulling gently up). Fourth, slide the number pad out from under the main circuit board (gently! Fifth, disconnect the main wiring harness (marked in red) from the main circuit board (marked in blue, but the connector is on the opposite side of the board as it sits in the picture). Sixth, pop the rubber keypad face (the thing with the actual numbers on it) out of the lower housing, and remove the white Samsung sticker and the skinny black sticker in the battery compartment. Seventh, see the two metal tabs marked in red above? Remove the six Phillips screws from the back of the upper half of the phone. Eighth, the phone should be in three pieces now, the upper housing still holding the screen, the middle part with the spring-loaded section, and the bottom housing. Ninth, flip the upper housing over, peel off the green piece of tape, and disconnect the main wiring harness from the back of the screen. Tenth, disconnect the upper keypad wiring harness from the back of the screen in the same manner. Eleventh, gently pry the screen up, starting at the bottom, with a flathead screwdriver. Finally, peel the protective plastic off of your new screen. You're screen should now work!

Fold the corners down the center from the pinpoint to form a folded triangle. Pin the bottom edge of the triangle with 4 pins. Repeat this pin and fold action many more times, for a total of three rows per hemisphere as follows: 4 points touching the pole. Find the "South Pole" of the ball. Line a 3-quart bowl with plastic wrap, letting excess hang over the sides. Pack your favorite ice creams into the bowl in layers. Cover the top of the bowl with plastic wrap and press down. Beat the egg whites on medium with a hand mixer until peaks form. Keeping the mixer running, slowly add a half cup of sugar and a pinch of vanilla to the mixture. Mix the sugar and eggs until stiff peaks form, about 2 more minutes. Preheat the oven to 500°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Cut your cake or brownie to fit the bottom of the bowl. Remove the ice cream from the freezer and take off the bottom layer of plastic wrap. Press your cake or brownie into the bottom of the bowl. Turn the bowl upside down on the parchment paper. Using a star-shaped pipette or another decorative icing method, cover the whole thing in meringue. Bake the entire thing for 3-4 minutes, until the outsides are golden brown.

Published on Apr 24, 2018 Page title: How to Make a Packing List Headline: Make sure it's clear where you are going, how long you will be gone, what the weather will be like, and how you are getting there. Article content: Write a packing list that is clear and easy to read. Start with an overview of the trip or adventure. bullet points are easy to read and get to the point. Next, write a detailed account of each item. For example, if you are going camping list out the tent, sleeping bag, and camp stove. Next, write down any entertainment items such as laptops, games, or books. Lastly, write down any financial or identification items. Start with a pen or wallet, and list any medications and identification such as a drivers license or passport. Lastly, write down any gadgets or toys you need for the trip. These last few items are fun to write and might be a surprise to you at the last minute. Go wild and list your surfboard, skis, or kayak. For a more compact packing list, you can create a checklist. This means having categories instead of an unlimited amount of individual items. For example, for clothing you can create a list for shirts, jeans, outerwear, undergarments, and socks. You should always double check your packing list before you leave. This way you don't forget anything and it is clear what you need to take. Finally, when you arrive at your trip destination, double check your packing list against your suitcase. This will help you avoid any loose items that slip through the cracks. Packing lists are useful for any trip or adventure. Always make sure you have a clear and detailed list before you leave. Good luck on your adventures! Lara It’s fun to plan and packing can seem overwhelming, but a simple packing list has many benefits. It’s clear, helps avoid forgeting things, and helps keep your belongings with you during your travels. Here are some tips for creating a packing list that works for you. Start with an Overview of the Trip Write an overview of your trip or adventure in a bullet point format. If you are going on a skiing trip you might have clothing, socks, and hiking boots on the list. If you are going to the beach you might have a few more items, like swimwear or floats. Duct tape makes an excellent inexpensive material for craft and DIY projects, and can even be used to turn a simple flip flop into a unique shoes. To make a duct tape flip flop, begin by tracing your foot onto a sheet of cardboard. Cut the foot shape out. Cut several strips of duct tape and horizontally lay them across the top of the sole of the flip flop. Turn the flip flop over so that the bottom is facing you, and cut little slits into the tape. Repeat this process for the other foot. Cut two 16-inch (40.64 centimeters) long pieces of duct tape. Fold each strip into thirds, lengthwise. Cut a 4-inch (10.16 centimeters) piece of duct tape and wrap this around the bottom of one of the flip flop soles. Place your foot down onto the duct tape flip flop and make a mark between the big toe and the one next to it using a pen. Poke a hole through the piece using the pen mark as a guide. Poke the toe strap through the hole and tape the excess to the underside of the sole. Fit the side straps and tape the side straps to the underside of the sole. Cover the bottom of the flip flop with long, vertical strips of duct tape to hide the raw edges. Finally, finish the duct tape flip flop by filling the footbed with sand or another material to give it a solid foundation. Then, complete the look by tying a piece of cloth around the top of the duct tape flip flop for a shoelace look. Finally, slip on a pair of sandals for a unique summer look.

Reformatting a Dish Network DVR's hard drive requires uninstalling the current DVR software and mounting the hard drive to a different computer, then using a tool like HDPARM to reformat the drive and assign usable volumes. First, uninstall the DVR software. Second, make sure the DVR is powered off. Then, open a command prompt as an administrator, and navigate to the directory where HDPARM.exe is installed. At the prompt, type "hdparm -s 0 /dev/hda", then "hdparm -s 0 /dev/hdb", then "hdparm -s 0 /dev/hdc". When finished, press enter for each command. Next, turn on the DVR. Place an external drive where the DVR used to place the hard drive. Attach the external hard drive to the DVR. Power on the DVR, and boot into the DVR's operating system. Navigate to the "Computer" folder, and open the "Disk Management" tool. Right-click the hard drive, and select "Format". Select the "quick format" option, and apply the changes. At this point, you can copy over any files that you want to keep from the old hard drive to the new hard drive. Once complete, unplug the external hard drive. Use HDPARM to assign a volume label and format to the new hard drive. Apply the new changes, and you're done!

Like WikiHow's Facebook page to get this and other how-to articles delivered to your Facebook feed.<|endoftext|>The Driftless Region of Wisconsin and Minnesota is a unique place, surrounded by water on three sides and yet possessing a diverse set of topography and soil types not found elsewhere. These conditions have fostered a distinct “seedier” culture than other areas of the midwest, and a more liberal leaning. As it has for many other regions across the United States, the changing face of rural America has impacted this trendsetting region. According to data from the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), the share of the population in the midwest living in rural areas peaked in 2000 and has been steadily declining since then. The effect has been dramatic in regions such as the Driftless Region, where the population was relatively stable over that time period. As of 2018, the decline in rural population had put the region among the 20 “most urbanized” in the United States. The challenge of rural population loss has been made more acute by the nature of many of the industries that drive rural economies. These often require significant upfront investments (such as the construction of production facilities or infrastructure) that are not easily duplicated in other regions or in other areas of the same region. Such was the case in the Driftless Region, which has been fertile ground for vineyards in particular. While wine production as an industry is not new to the United States, what is different about the Driftless Region is the ultra-high quality of the wine produced there. The area’s cool summers, diverse soil types and microclimates, and century-old vines have allowed for the production of critically acclaimed Pinot Noirs and other varieties that are difficult to grow in warmer climates. As a result, producers in the Driftless Region have developed a unique international following. Not only are their wines of the highest quality, but the people who make them are equally passionate about giving back to the community and improving the well-being of the region’s future generations. The Driftless Region Wine Trail is committed to supporting this culture of innovation and excellence, promoting the region’s natural beauty and agricultural heritage, and raising awareness about the region’s opportunities for rural economic development. As the region’s population has continued to decline, so has its wine production. Unlike so many other regions facing similar challenges, however, the Driftless Region is taking a different approach to rural revitalization. Dress up: Wear something light and comfortable for the evening. Implement the plans: Start dinner preparation as per your plans and try not to deviate much, in an impulse to impress. Get help: If you can get friends or family members to pitch in, request them to do smaller chores like fixing the table, arranging some fresh flowers, switching on some soothing music etc. Post preparation: If you finish the dinner preparation in time, grab a chair, get a glass of juice or water and mentally prepare yourself for the conversation you are going to have. Cleanup: This is the most difficult part of the entire evening, especially when all your tiredness comes flooding back. Relax again: Dip your feet in some warm water before you retire for the day. A Cessna 172 is a single-engine, low-wing, propeller-driven airplane with a conventional tailwheel undercarriage. It is one of the most popular single-engine piston aircraft in the world. The 172 model number refers to the maximum weight of the airplane, which is very similar to its performance. Begin your study of the Cessna 172 by examining its complex instrument panel. Learn the functions and basic operation of the altimeter, airspeed indicator, directional indicator, artificial horizon, turn and slip indicator, and heading indicator. A 172 pilot must be able to clearly read and interpret all these instruments during flight. Next, familiarize yourself with the six major switches and levers located throughout the cabin. These switches and levers are used for a variety of functions during flight. Learn how to operate the propeller switch, electrical switch, brakes, directional control switch, fuselage vent window close switch, and autopilot cutout switch. Last, but not least, practice setting and changing radio frequencies so that you can communicate with ATC (air traffic control) and ground-based personnel if necessary. After learning and practicing the functions of the 172’s instrument panel and control switches, it’s time to gain an understanding of how to operate its major engine and aerodynamic controls. Start by familiarizing yourself with the control surfaces on the yoke and understand how to move and trim them for maximum lift and to compensate for an aircraft’s angle of attack. Next, learn to handle the elevators by moving the pitch lever to demonstrate directional control and apply rudder to execute aileron control. Do not forget to monitor and observe the engine instruments during flight. Learn about the airplane’s fuel, oil, andboost pressures, how to adjust engine power, and how to shut down the engine. Practice all of the above procedures in a safe, static environment under the guidance of a qualified instructor. Only after you have gained sufficient experience can you move on to more difficult flying situations, including full flight maneuvers and instrument approaches. Finally, in order to safely operate the Cessna 172, you must also understand and be comfortable with the operation of its primary flight controls and mechanisms, such as the autopilot, flaps, aileron, and rudder pedals. In addition, you must be able to coordinate your actions with the movements of the yoke and throttle. Congratulations, you have completed your study of the Cessna 172, and can now fly this plane safely under almost any conditions!

How to Make Baby Blankets Start off with two one-yard strips of fleece material. Lay your first piece of fleece with the rougher side facing up and then lay the second yard of fleece on top, soft side facing up. Slide your self healing mat under the fleece and cut off the rough selvage edges of the fleece using scissors or a rotary cutter. Pin your four-inch by four-inch square template to any corner of your fleece and cut around it so that there is an outward facing right angle chunk cut out. Take your tape measure and lay it across the fleece from the top of one right angle to the other so that there is a four-inch strip of fleece below the tape measure. Keep the tape measure in place and use your scissors or rotary cutter to cut strips of fleece one-inch thick all along the four-inch section. Repeat for the remaining three sides of the fleece, making sure to pin the tape measure in place. Separate the top layer of fleece from the bottom layer of fleece for each fringe and tie the two together in a double knot. Double-check to make sure that each tie is tightly knotted and you're finished!

Pinochle is a casino-style card game typically used as a filler between other card games or as a standalone game. Bidding is a part of the game, where one player states how many points they are bidding and the other players can either match the bid or increase or decrease the bid. The game is played with two common decks of playing cards. Trick-taking is when the player that won the bid takes all of the cards played in that round. Combined with their partner, the winner will have the highest score or "telling". There are some scoring differences based on the cards played. If a player takes a wild card, that card will be taken by the winner of the trick. Each face card played along with a trump card (royal, kingly, or an inverted trump) ties the player who played it for that round. Combine your points with your partner's and you've finished your first round of Pinochle. Learn a little background information first. A bill is first introduced by someone in either the House of Representatives or the Senate. A representative may be hired to speak in support of the bill in either the House or Senate. After the hearing of the bill is scheduled, the committee will hear the bill. When the bill makes it to the two chambers of congress, it is sent to the House and Senates. Once the bill is sent to the two chambers of congress for voting, the bill can no longer be changed. When the bill is successful in each of the two Chambers of Congress, the House and Senate version of the bill may be different. Know that after the compromise version of the bill is created, the committee votes on the bill. Know that the compromise version of the bill is then sent to the two chambers of congress again for voting. Afterwards, the bill is sent to the Governor. Realise that even if the Governor sends the bill back to the two chambers of Congress, the two chambers can vote on the bill again.

Hernias are common conditions, and an inguinal hernia is a hernia in the groin that may strain or push on the nearby abdominal wall, causing pain. Learn the risk factors, look for the symptoms, get a physical examination, and have a hernia diagnosed by a doctor. If necessary, have an ultrasound done, and if necessary, have an inguinal hernia surgically repaired. Some of the factors that increase the risk of a hernia are being overweight or obese, having a family history of hernias, carrying extra weight around the abdomen, being older, having a high-intensity fitness training routine, and having a sedentary lifestyle. Some common misconceptions about risk factors are that hernias are only a problem for people who play sports, or that a hernia is serious or painful. The symptoms include a bulging area about the size of a golf ball in the groin, getting worse when you strain, or a hernia that gets bigger when you cough or sneeze. A hernia can be diagnosed by a doctor through a simple physical exam. If your hernia is complicated (e.g. if it has caused bowel obstruction or another emergency condition), you may need an ultrasound. If your hernia is very large or cannot be completely diagnosed with a physical exam, your doctor may recommend an ultrasound. Open and laparoscopic hernia surgeries have similar success rates, but the latter uses smaller incisions and is less invasive. After the hernia is diagnosed, you'll discuss your options with your doctor, and the vast majority of hernias are repaired as an open surgery. After the surgery, you'll need to rest at home for a day or two, and then be able to slowly resume normal activities, such as light walking. It usually takes four to six weeks to fully recover. You may need stool softeners during the surgery, and you'll need to contact the surgeon if you observe signs of infection, blood in the stool, or if the hernia becomes larger or concerns you. The are several types of hernia surgery, and your surgeon will explain which one is best for you. A incisions is made either on the lower abdomen or groin, and then the contents of the hernia (usually bowel) can be seen and touched through the abdominal wall. A piece of mesh may be put in the abdominal wall to reinforce it, and the hernia is sewn shut. After hernia surgery, you'll want to make an appointment with the surgeon to have the surgical incisions cleaned and checked.

To make a small round coin purse, start by obtaining the following items: two 3/4 inch (2cm) circles of fabric, four 1 inch circles of fabric, four small circles of cardboard or plastic, a 1 inch zipper, a zipper pull, a needle and thread. Trace and cut out four circles from the cardboard or plastic. Cut four circles of fabric that are at least 3/4 inch (2cm) larger all around than the cardboard or plastic circles. Gather the edges of the fabric. Place padding and stiff circles inside two of the gathered fabric circles, and then place the cardboard or plastic circles and padding inside the remaining two gathered fabric circles. Gather the remaining two fabric circles around the cardboard or plastic circles. Measure the length of the zipper. If the length is more than 10 inches, shorten the zipper, if needed, by stitching a new zipper stop. Create a loop handle at this point if you want one. Sew the loop to the "stop" or non-opening end of the zipper. Roll the raw edges under and stitch again to make a smooth (French) seam. Assemble the layers. Place the edge of one unpadded fabric circle along the edge of the inside, unpadded fabric/cardboard circle. Hand stitch the edge of the fabric circle to the edge of the inner, un-padded circle. Repeat for the second fabric circle, placing it along the other unpadded circle. Open the zipper (if it's not already open). Place the edge of one gathered fabric circle along the edge of the padded, inner circle. Stitch this circle to the padded circle. Tie off the thread, remove thread and... enjoy your small round coin purse!

Heterocyclic organic chemistry is a branch of organic chemistry that deals with the chemistry of cyclic organic compounds which contain a heteroatom as one of the atoms in its structure. The insertion of a foreign atom into a cyclic organic compound is a synthetically challenging task for the practitioner chemist. Besides electronic and spectroscopic properties of heterocyclic compounds can be very interesting to study and to evaluate based on its applications in many types of industries. Hete Rho cyclic organic compounds have an interesting group of compounds which are called the aromatic heterocyclic compounds. Aromatic compounds are organic cyclic compounds which have unusual thermodynamic stability that is conferred due to the presence of three conjugated double bonds in its molecular structure. The synthesis of heterocyclic organic compounds is mainly by the process of cyclization of a linear compound that includes a heteroatom in its structure. This area of organic chemistry is a relatively new to the chemical science and there is still an actively ongoing research that is done on these compounds and its derivatives. The nature of the heteroatom that is incorporated into the ring can dictate its level of application and degree of toxicity. Being knowledgeable on the field of heterocyclic organic chemistry is very important as it has a wide application in industries such as pharmaceuticals, dyes, agrochemicals, natural products and so much more. Research on this field can lead to new drugs, dyes, and agrochemicals with improved properties such as increased stability, solubility and bioavailability. Corned beef and cabbage is a traditional Irish and Scottish dish. It is made from corned beef, which is beef brisket that has been salted and dried. It is simmered with a variety of vegetables including carrots, potatoes and small turnips. The dish is finished with butter and cabbage. This can be served with mashed potatoes on the side. This is a robust dish and can be served alone or with mashed potatoes. Depending on the duration of the brining process, the beef will take on a different flavor. The shorter the duration, the more intensely the salt will be flavored, but the less retained water will be. Longer brining times will remove more water, but will result in a more subtle salt flavor. While the beef cooks, prepare the vegetables. Peel and chop large carrots and potatoes into 1.5 to 2 inch sections. Peel 18 small turnips. Add the vegetables to the pot. The beef should be cooked to an internal temperature of 160F. Drain the vegetables and discard the liquid. Finish the dish with butter and some of the cabbage. This makes 6 servings. Each serving will have plenty of vegetables and beef. This is a robust dish and tastes even better the day after making it.

How to Weave with Seed Beads Learn a bit of terminology. Learn the differences between normal bead weaving and seed bead weaving. Warp the loom for seed bead weaving. String the loom so that you can slip the thread off the dowel holder without clipping all the threads. Tie the other end down with a double knot as well (on the opposite side from your starter knot) around the pin on the dowel. Thread your needle and secure the weft thread (white) with a double knot to the warp thread (pink). Slip 8 beads onto your needle and pass it through UNDER the warp threads. Push the needle back through the beads over the top of the warp threads, making sure that you do not split the thread. Continue weaving your beads until you have reached the required length for your item. Thread and sew the beginning weft thread through a row of beads to tidy it off. Loosen one dowel slightly and turn the pin towards the woven strip so that the threads can fall off the pin. Lift all the threads off being careful not to pull on them and so warp your strip. Gently lift your work over the loom and it will automatically slip off the pin on the other side. Instead of loose threads hanging off the sides, you should now have little loops. Start with a thread at or near the centre, to leave enough thread either side of the bracelet to finish off your work and still have enough thread to add a clasp. Hold the work firmly in one hand and start by pulling the centre thread. Continue doing this until all the threads are pulled through. Use the two remaining threads to add a clasp or finish the piece however you want.

Ultimately, evaluating teamwork in a business is a continuous process. As a team works together to achieve their goals, the team itself must also be evaluated to ensure that it is functioning as intended. New team members may need to be brought into the team, or team members may need to be reassigned. Processes may need to be improved, or new technologies implemented. New challenges may emerge. Evaluating teamwork ensures that these changes are made in a transparent and collaborative way, so that the team can continue to work together in the most effective way possible. Begin with the basics: identify the team, then the organization, then the department. Ask the team members questions together, as a group, and then one-on-one. Keep a confidential checklist of notes. Record observations about the technologies in use, and consult with others about challenges. Install a system for staff members to make fair suggestions or comments. Consult with others. Repeat as necessary until you have identified and satisfied your stakeholders' needs. Making changes as required is the final step in the evaluation process. However, to maintain a transparent process, it's important to start with the basics and keep a record of your observations, questions, and concerns. The steps above may also be useful for evaluating other aspects of teamwork, such as a team's goals, culture, and individual performances. The steps focus on collecting information from various stakeholders, and then establishing a process for evaluating teamwork. Such a process helps maintain transparency and encourages improvements over time. Make sure to consult with others to find and satisfy their needs. This process is similar to how a healthy team works together to meet team goals. Finally, as with any change process, be willing to go back and revisit these steps as needed to satisfy your stakeholders' needs. Begin by scanning or importing the photos into your computer's photo editing software. Next, open two separate windows for the photos you wish to merge. It is recommended to do this so you can easily select the backgrounds without affecting the foreground image. Then, you'll want to grab the Move tool from the tools palette and click on the photo you wish to use as a background. After selecting the background photo, you want to grab the foreground photo and click on it in the second window. Now you want to move the foreground photo into the background photo's window by dragging it. Be sure to drag it at least partially over the top of the foreground photo so you can easily select it and begin merging the photos. It's also good to resize the layers to make sure the merge looks good. This can be done by double clicking on the layer with the foreground image. If necessary, press "Enter" or "Return" on your keyboard to accept the changes made. When you're finished merging the photos, you'll likely want to add a layer mask to the foreground photo to blend it with the background photo. Select the layer mask and fill it with the gradient tool. The gradient tool should look similar to the gradient tool in Photoshop. Just click and drag to set a gradient for the two images to blend. Be sure to set the gradient so it blends from black to white or white to black to ensure both images are completely merged.

Know what you want. Assess your goals and mission. Determine your budget. Put together a timeline. Read other RFPs. Establish the projected scope and boundaries of your project. List your “must haves” and your “like to haves.” One way to know what you really want in response to your RFP is to make a list of your needs and your wants. Each of your needs or “must haves” should be included in your RFP. Decide who will read the proposals and award the project. Specify a candidate’s minimum qualifications. Draft a scorecard that you will use to evaluate proposals. Include all relevant details. Be specific, but not too specific. Organize the RFP effectively. Request references. Proofread your RFP before sending it out. Send RFPs to reputable consulting firms. Limit the number of firms or individuals you send your RFP to. If your RFP goes out to anyone and everyone, you will either receive too many proposals to realistically consider or your RFP will not be taken seriously. Give an adequate amount of time for individuals to put together a quality proposal. Stick to your deadline. Remember to thank the individuals who submitted a proposal and thank those who reviewed your RFP. Summarize the key points from each proposal. Then make a decision and pick a winner. The potty training process can take time, but is well worth it when your child is ready. It's important to remember that every child is different and the potty training process will likely take a different amount of time for your child. Understand that the process will be fluid and allow for plenty of practice time before moving to full diapers. When your child is ready, know that the right equipment can make a big difference. Start with a potty floor rug and narrow down from there. For example, Samuel recently told us he wanted to use the toilet and we got him a potty chair. He sits on the potty about twice a day now and we will likely go from there. Know that the process will be slow but take it one step at a time. A consistent schedule allows your child to get used to the idea and feel prepared for when the time is right. Get your child ready for potty training by introducing the concept to the potty in small increments. Start with 15 minutes a day and increase. This will allow your child to get used to using the potty and be prepared for the next step. Set a time to do a "trial run" so you can see how your child reacts. Most children will have some "accidents" in the beginning, but this is to be expected. Expect the unexpected and plan for it! As your child learns to use the potty, show him or her how to do so correctly and remind them to follow these steps when necessary. Use the right toilet-related words to build familiarity. For example, we refer to the toilet as "the big potty" and "potty time." Time alone isn't enough; let your child practice with you in the bathroom for a minimum of 15 minutes a day. This may sound like a lot, but just think about how much time you spend in the bathroom and multiply by 15 minutes. Remember, consistency is key! Stay nearby while your child uses the potty. This will help you to ensure your child is using it correctly and learn their "need-to-go" signals. Read potty-themed books to get familiar with the idea. Teach your child to pee standing up. Make using the potty part of your daily routine. For example, at nighttime, before bed, after waking in the morning, or whenever else you hold your child for a bit. Make it a rewards-based activity. This could be a special treat or a trip to the car for a favorite book or toy. Remind your child to wash their hands after using the potty. Share the good news with close friends and family. Let babysitters and teachers know. They'll likely be shocked, but they will get used to it and will know what to expect! When your child is ready, progress to nighttime training. This typically takes longer and your child may have an accident after going through the day without one. Remember to keep practicing! When your child is ready, progress to full diapers. There are no shortcuts, so keep practicing and continue to reinforce the concepts. This will likely take longer than day clothes, but you've got this! When your child is fully trained, remind them to wash their hands after changing diapers or wet clothing. Praise your child when they have an accident. Finally, offer rewards for success. A nap after an accident or successful potty training after a week or two will make the process go quickly! It takes a village, so share the good news with close friends and family! Congratulations on the new family member! Enjoy the journey and keep working hard. Thank you for reading my article and I hope this helped answer your question!"

Brick columns are a beautiful addition to patios, front entrances, or outdoor spaces. They are a great way to add some color and detail to your space without taking up a lot of space. Before beginning this project make sure you have all of the materials and equipment necessary. Brick size, amount and type should all be decided before beginning. You'll also need a blueprint of your brick column to ensure that the width and height are the same and that there is adequate space for the mortar between each brick. Plan for 7 feet of height and 12 inches of base width. First begin by wetting the bricks a couple of hours in advance. This will help the brick stay in place as you build and help the mortar set up faster. Begin by laying down the base of your brick column. As you work up the column use your string line as a guide to where each course should start and end. Laying the brick column on the ground where you want it to sit before you complete each course. For the first layer fill the joint between each brick with mortar using a thin layer and a screed. Once the first course is complete start laying the second course the same way but using only one brick. Continue this alternating layer technique until you reach 4 courses. At this point use a square design to fill the remaining gaps. Next fill in all of the joints with mortar using a whisk brush to smooth. Once the mortar is complete concave all of the joints using a concave tool. When the mortar is completely dry you are ready to finish the column. You can choose to leave the top sleek or embellish it with a design. Some ideas are Cubist patterns, brick patterns, or embedded rocks. Overall this project is fairly simple, however the planning and execution can vary based on the complexity you want in your column.

Here is a wikihow on how to use Remember the Milk on Twitter. Remember the Milk is a to-do list app, similar to Apple's iNotes or Google Tasks. On Twitter, users can create an RTM account and enter tasks through the Remember the Milk bot. Once the Remember the Milk bot notices you on Twitter, you'll be able to add tasks to your RTM account without a due date. You can also create tasks with a due date and postpone the tasks. Once a task is marked as complete, you'll know via Twitter. If the task has a reminder attached to it, the reminder will go off automatically. You can also add other users to RTM tasks through Twitter. Finally, you can get a list of tasks due in a timeframe and set up task reminders for projects that are due in real time. This will launch the XAMPP Control Panel, where you can click on the Start buttons next to Apache and MySQL to begin the process of starting these services. After clicking the Start buttons, you may see a couple of Windows messages. Now, start your web browser and in the Web Address area at the top, type in the following: http://localhost/, click on the language of your choice to continue to the configuration page. On this page, provide a password for your MySQL root user and click on the “Password Changing” button. Enter in the user name provided by the system (‘root’) and enter in the password you provided. Congratulations! You have now successfully set up a personal web server!

Note the different kinds of smokeless tobacco. Be aware of the brands of chewing tobacco available. Learn about the chemicals in chewing tobacco. Have your state-issued identification ready when purchasing chewing tobacco. Get an empty water bottle. Pack the tobacco. Check that the tobacco is properly packed. Lift a small amount of tobacco out of the tin with your thumb and pointer finger. Place the chew in one side of your mouth, between your lip and your bottom teeth. Move the tobacco around so that you can chew it and release the nicotine. Be very careful not to swallow any of it. Spit after you have chewed the tobacco for a little while. Remove the chew once the flavor is gone or if you start to feel ill. Take the chew out of your mouth with your fingers and throw it away. Chewing tobacco has the same serious health risks as cigarettes. Recognize you are at a higher risk for mouth cancer, disease, and infection. Get help if you are trying to quit doing chew or want to avoid trying chew.

Halo 3 is a first person shooter video game developed by Bungie and published by Microsoft Game Studios. Halo 3 was released for the Xbox 360 video game console on November 9, 2007. The game is the sequel to Halo: Combat Evolved (2001). Set in the 22nd century, the game follows the Master Chief, an officer of the United Nations Space Command (UNSC), who is investigating a raid on a Cortana-enslaved planet. Gameplay Halo 3 is played from a first-person perspective. The player uses a variety of weaponry, including assault rifles, sniper rifles, pistols, shotguns, and gravity knives. The game includes six multiplayer game modes, as well as the campaign mode. The campaign mode follows Master Chief as he is awoken from cryo sleep to execute a daring escape aboard a hijacked dropship. The story progresses through a series of dialog trees and cinematics, which are interspersed with cutscenes. The gameplay remains largely consistent with the previous game, Combat Evolved, with additional features including the inclusion of melee weapons, jetpacks, and a new setting; the capacity for players to construct outdoor environments. Multiplayer mode includes several gametypes. Arena mode, launched in 2005 as NO LIMITS, has variations including Free For All, King of the Hill, Capture the Flag, and Duel. The game mode Hammerpoint: Happy Hours, is a time-based gametype which is activated after a thirty minute period. Up to 32 players can compete in a large map-sized play zone. Metal, the latest iteration of the game mode, replaced Hammerpoint: Happy Hours in April 2014. In this variation, players must use specialized Beam Rifles to retrieve "mods", which are small discs that are placed around containers on both teams' maps. Teams are scored for each mod on their side of the map. The first team to reach 5 points wins the round. Warzone, launched in February 2011, is a vehicular combat gametype that utilizes the arsenal of the UNSC ikas assault rifle and Mamba assault shotgun. Up to 32 players are split into two teams and combat each other in alternating hot and cold areas. Players may spawn with one of four classes with distinct abilities: assault, support, heavy, and tank. Maps The multiplayer maps available in Halo 3 range from small to large in size, and may be classified into three general categories: close quarters, wide open, and large scale. Close quarter maps include Lone Wolf, Highlands, and Slipspace. Wide open maps include Outer Colony, Delta Labs, and Warlords. Large scale maps include Bluff, District, and finally, Bonestorm, which spans the largest area and includes a sky-high bridge, the Eiffel Tower of gaming. Development In February 2004, at the first preview of Halo 3, Bungie announced that the game was in development for the Xbox 360, then codenamed "Project Blackhole." At E3 2005, Bungie officially announced Halo 3, but did not reveal a release date. In October 2007, at the Penny Arcade Expo 2007, Microsoft officially announced that the game would be released for the Xbox 360 on November 9, 2007. Certain aspects of Halo 3 received criticism, including the artificial intelligence of the Covenant soldiers. The number of moving parts in the AI was criticized, with one reviewer stating that "the Covenant AI remains about as threatening as a third-grader with a loaded.45." Also, the way the sand interfered with the play of some of the game's maps. Reception Halo 3 received "universal acclaim" from critics, according to review aggregator Metacritic. The game sold more than 980,000 units within its first week of release in November 2007. Sales Halo 3 was the best-selling game in 2007, with 980,000 copies sold. It also received a "Gold" certification from the Entertainment and Leisure Software Publishers Association, for selling over 500,000 units in the United Kingdom. The debut of Halo 3 on the Xbox 360 was called "spectacular" by IGN, and it was praised for the ability to "play as both the Covenant and UNSC in the single-player campaign, or jump into the action as one of six classes in the competitive multiplayer mode." The sense of speed from the motion sensing controller was highlighted. However, the sound effects received criticism for being "so loud it's almost obtrusive." Tents can be quite bulky and take up a lot of space, so it's important to choose a location that has enough space and is free from excessive sunlight or other disruptions. Try to locate your tent at least 10 yards from any clear source of heat, such as a fire ring or a picnic table. The ground beneath your tent site should be flatter and more level than this, and the vegetation must be sufficiently mature to avoid any concerns about snakes or spiders falling into the tent. If the terrain is hilly or contains hard-to-push earth, consider another site. While it's tempting to choose the shadiest spot available, make sure this site has enough direct sunlight to keep your tent cool at night. Once you have chosen your site, begin the process of pitching your tent by unrolling the ground cloth. The tent itself must first be attached to the four corners of the ground cloth, then the three sides of the tent can be erected. To do this, first stand with your back to the rear of the tent, and put the stakes into the ground at the corners of the tent site, holding them firm for now. Next, stand at one of the ends of the tent and raise the end above your head, positioning it so it abuts the rear wall of the tent. Then, standing exactly in the middle of the tent, raise the two sides up to meet, making sure that the sides are level and the top of the tent is at the same height as the bottom of the rear wall. When you are happy with the alignment of the tent, hammer the stakes into the ground firmly but carefully at the corners and at the tent's base, then step away from the tent to allow it to settle. Once the tent is up, you can begin to decorate it. If you are using a black or camouflage tent, you should paint it with a suitable colourful camouflage paint to prevent it from being seen from the outside. Cover the seams of the tent with waterproof daps or clear nail varnish, and add any logo or symbols on the tent's exterior. A camp table and several chairs can be stationed inside the tent, and one or more windows can be cut into the tent's side walls. Finally, it's important to ensure that the tent itself is comfortable to sleep in. Install the fly, then remove the doors and windows, placing them in a safe location. The under-the-fly insulation can be removed to allow air to circulate between the two, and the space where the doors would have been installed can be insulated. Any seams along the floor of the tent can be insulated or waterproofed. Finally, any lights or appliances that you will be using must be plugged into a power supply, which can be secured inside the tent itself. Your tent is now fully ready for use, and can comfortably sleep two people. As a final preparation, make sure you and any necessary sleeping equipment are fully hydrated. Enjoy your camping trip!

Purchase an ink refill kit at an office supply store. Gather your kit, a roll of paper towels, and some clear scotch tape together on a large flat working surface, a table or desk. Remove the empty cartridge from your printer. Cover your hands with a pair of disposable plastic gloves while you work with the messy ink. Take a paper towel and fold it in half twice. Place the empty cartridge on it. Read the instruction manual included with the refill kit to learn how to refill your particular type of cartridge. Locate the fill holes on the top of the cartridge. Use a sharp pencil to pierce the refill holes in the top of the ink cartridge Or you can take the top label off with a knife or screwdriver (Correct places can also be found in the kit instructions). In addition to black, there are three colors of ink: magenta, cyan, and yellow. Insert the long needle of the refill ink bottle deeply into the correct hole penetrating the foam down into the bottom of the cartridge. Slowly, add the ink. Stop quickly as soon as you see a bit of ink oozing out of the hole. Carefully daub the cartridge contacts on the paper towel, you should see a splotch of the ink leaking out onto the paper towel. Cover the hole with a small piece of clear scotch tape. Repeat steps 11-15 for each ink color. After you have refilled all three colors, carefully blot (don't wipe or rub) the cartridge print head on a folded piece of paper towel. If the blot shows the colors either faded or not at all, blot on wet paper towel and again on dry, to get the ink flowing. Replace the ink cartridge into the printer. Immediately print something, anything, just to get the ink flowing. Follow the cleaning or priming cycles for your specific printer. This article was generated using our sponsor Self Hub. To install a stove, follow these steps. 1.Locate two unused spaces in the electrical service panel on one side or the other column of circuit breakers. Switch the main disconnect to the OFF position. Verify that the power is off by checking light fixtures in the space. Remove the cover on the electrical service panel. 2.Locate or create a space wide enough for the new circuit breaker. Remove circuit breakers by moving the switch handle to the OFF position and pushing on the handle away from the middle of the panel. Install the appropriately sized new circuit circuit breaker into the panel. 3.Remove a pre-punched knock-out ("KO") from the side of the electrical panel that is the same size as the connector. Install the connector into the opening from the outside and spin the lock nut over the threads from inside. 4.Determine where to drill behind the range to allow the cable to enter the space for the range outlet by inspecting or measuring the rear of the range. Pass the range cable through this last hole behind the range. 5.Wire the outlet. Strip the outer jacket. Wire the outlet. Cut the conductors for the outlet. Apply oxide inhibitor. 6.Secure the range outlet to the wall or baseboard in a location where when the range cord is connected, will not interfere with placement of the range and closing of any range drawers. Remove excess slack from the cable. Route the cable to the connector mounted in the electric service panel. 7.Connect to the circuit breaker. Connect to neutral and ground terminals. Secure the range cable with staples where exposed as needed for support and so that there is no less than 36" between supports (every other joist or stud). 8.Install the cable into the electric service panel through the cable connector. 9.Pass the cable through the space for the range outlet, from the back of the range to the electric service panel. 10.Secure the range outlet to the wall or baseboard in a location where when the range cord is connected, will not interfere with placement of the range and closing of any range drawers. 11.Remove the blank plates from the cover that are now occupying the place of the new circuit breaker. Secure the cover to the electric service panel and set the new circuit breaker to OFF. 12.Stand to the side of the panel (do not stand directly in front) and move the main service disconnect handle to ON. While still to the side, move the new circuit breaker handle to ON. 13.Check for proper wiring. If any measurements are not exactly as described, turn the new circuit breaker OFF and check the wiring of the range outlet, and if necessary the wiring in the electric service panel as well. 14.Re-connect the range. Wrap up.

Therefore, before you engage a private jet charter company, ask to see their FAA certification and customer reviews so you can validate the company and learn how others have responded to working with that company. Generally, there should be a single person responsible for your trip. This person will be your point of contact during the process and will have their own set of credentials for your reference. That person will typically be able to give you excellent customer service. Selecting an aircraft should start with learning what the company's standards are for minimum pilot hours. In addition, you should be able to get a clear quote, not a vague estimate that leaves room for surprises on the final invoice. Finally, find out how much it will cost, including the total cost of the flight and all applicable taxes, fees, and charges. While these should be detailed on the quote, make sure to verify the final price with your finalist by looking up the total cost of the flight in a well-known pricing publication.

The Mayan calendar is a system of counting time. It is one of many ways that the Maya observed time across the millennia. The calendar is comprised of two interlocking cycles, the Haab cycle and the Tzolkin cycle. The cycles together make a calendar round, consisting of repeating cycles of 20 Haab days and 5 Tzolkin days. Most Maya dates are expressed as a combination of the Haab and Tzolkin cycles. The two cycles form a system interlocking known as a long count date, which expresses a date in terms of its distance from a fixed start date. You can read more about the Mayan calendar in the following articles: - How to Count in the Haab and Tzolkin Cycles - Tutorial: Making a Maya Date - The Maya Calendar - The Long Count The Maya also had a system of dating that used a cycle based on a count of days known as the Long Count. The Long Count is much longer than the Haab and Tzolkin cycles combined, with repeating cycles of 18,980 days. The Maya could use a Long Count date to show how long a span of time was. For example, a Long Count date can show how long a particular event or duration was. The date January 10, 2022 could be expressed as 20.21.18.20.21.18.20. The Long Count was also used to express a creation cycle date. This expression incorporates the Haab and Tzolkin cycles in addition to the Long Count cycle, expressing the complete count of days as a calendrical epoch. The Maya creation cycle is called the Common Era. You can read the Long Count date January 10, 2022 in the following ways: - As 20.21.18.20.21.18 - As 18,980 days = 350.25.20.21.18 - As CE 350.25.20.21.18 You can compare a Mayan date written in the Haab and Tzolkin cycles with the same date written in the Long Count by expressing the date in terms of a difference from a fixed start date. For example, January 10, 2022 in the Haab and Tzolkin cycles is the same as January 10, 2022 in the Long Count. The Long Count cycle is much longer than the Haab and Tzolkin cycles combined, so a later Long Count date corresponds to a later Haab and Tzolkin date. Heart attacks, also known as myocardial infarctions, usually cause a patient to experience discomfort in the chest or upper arm. However, some sufferers report no symptoms at all. Dizziness, lightheadedness, and faintness are other common signs, as are nausea, vomiting, shortness of breath, and abdominal pain. If you or someone you know is experiencing any of these symptoms, it’s crucial to call emergency services immediately and seek medical attention. To prevent heart attacks and their complications, it’s important to eat a heart-healthy diet and exercise regularly. In particular, this means avoiding trans fat and cholesterol, which can build up in the arteries and increase the risk of a blockage. Additionally, people with high blood pressure, Type 2 diabetes, or obesity are at greater risk. Other risk factors can include a family history of heart disease, smoking, and advanced age. When cardiac arrest occurs outside of a hospital, or during minor symptoms, the patient’s survival rate is lower. However, immediate CPR, the deployment of an automated external defibrillator, and quick access to advanced medical care have been shown to improve outcomes significantly. Always wear a MedicAlert bracelet or tag, and make sure your emergency contact information is up to date. If you believe you are experiencing a heart attack, do not ignore it. Seek medical attention immediately. For more information, see your doctor regularly, and be sure to ask about symptoms related to heart health. Have a heart!

Keep the humidity at 45 to 50 percent during incubation and 65 to 70 percent during the 23rd day of hatching. Arming an infinity scarf is a fun way to increase the potential uses for this handy project pattern. The pattern is easy to find online and only requires two skeins of yarn in different colors. To start, find the ends of each skein of yarn and leave approximately four feet of each. Join these pieces together to form a long length of yarn that is the foundation for your scarf. Next, hold this foundation yarn between your thumb and index finger of your right hand. Pick up the first stitch on your right wrist with your left hand. Place the loop you are holding in your right hand over your left wrist and tighten. Repeat this process so that you have two stitches on your left arm. With your right hand, pick up the second stitch on your left arm (the one closest to your elbow). Pull the stitch over your left hand. Let go of all the yarn and tighten by pulling on the working yarn. Repeat the process of this entire section so far to move a stitch from your right arm to your left arm. Continue the same method until you have one remaining stitch on your left arm. Cut the working yarn leaving approximately two feet. Pull the cut end through the final loop on your left arm, take the loop off of your arm, and pull tight. Thread the cut end of the yarn through a needle. Match up the edges of the scarf and sew the two ends together. Turn the scarf inside out and sew through any loose ends. Choose a model that has enough cleaning power for the cleaning task at hand. 2. Think about how the pressure washer will be powered. Gas powered pressure washers are convenient for the user, but are more expensive to run and may not be suitable for cleaning under power lines. Electric pressure washers have lower running costs but may be heavier and less sturdy. 3. Consider how large an area the pressure washer will be used for. A narrow stream ensures the pressure washer covers a larger area, but may not be suitable for cleaning highly visible areas such as gutters. A wider angle spray nozzle is more suitable for cleaning highly visible areas. 5. Consider if the pressure washer has additional cleaning features such as a rotating scrub brush, a broom attachment for pavement or an attachment for cleaning gutters. 6. The heavier the spray gun and extension wand, the more you will be able to maneuver and clean at angles that may be difficult with lighter pressure washers.

Making terms and conditions and privacy policies for a business is a critical task that should not be undertaken lightly. Depending on your type of business, your terms and conditions or privacy policy may apply to different areas. For example, a photography business would likely have different terms and conditions or privacy policies for service than terms and conditions or privacy policy for images they sell. Terms and conditions and privacy policies should be written with the beginning in mind. The beginning of the terms and conditions or privacy policy for a business should describe what relationship the customer has with the business. For example, "This Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy Applies to Everyone Using the Services Provided by [business]". Next, the business should identify what relationship it is creating with the customer. For example, "This Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy Applies to [customer_name] Using [service name]"." The business should then provide a definition for some of the key words used in the terms and conditions or privacy policy such as "Services", "Customer", "Personal Information", "Business" and "Member". The terms and conditions or privacy policy should next address what products and/or services the business will provide to the customer. For example, "We will provide the [service name] service to [customer name]." Next, the business should state the terms and conditions related to pricing and payment. For example, "Pricing is as follows: Monthly payment is $x plus applicable tax. There is no discount for upfront payments. Payment must be received before we begin service. Our service agreement covers the products and services that are purchased. Refunds are only available if we fail to provide the services within the service agreement. If we sell different products and or services to the Customer, a separate fee will be charged." The business should also state the terms and conditions related to guarantees and warranties. For example, "Customer is buying the use of a service, not a product. Thus, the limited warranty associated with the product is not applicable to our services. We cannot warranty the performance or results of our services. However, we will perform the services to the best of our ability. If the results produced by our services are not as expected, we will refund any fees associated with the services." The business should also state the terms and conditions related to copyrights and how the customer can have their content removed from the business's service. Next, the business should address what information it will collect from the customer. For example, "We will collect the following information: Name, Email, Phone number, and Bank information." The business should also identify what third parties the business will share information with. For example, "We will share your Personal Information with our service providers and third parties that perform tasks on our behalf. This includes vendors who help us maintain our service, fulfill customer orders, and process customer payments." The business should identify what personal information will not be collected. For example, "We will not collect Personal Information about our customers except as described above." The business should also state what personal information will be retained. For example, "We will retain your Personal Information only as long as necessary to provide you the services you have purchased." The business should also state that the customer consents to the collection, use, and retention as described in this terms and conditions or privacy policy. A privacy policy is similar to terms and conditions but often has more legal jargon. The first paragraph or two should describe the business and clarify that the rest of the document is a privacy policy. The rest of the privacy policy should address what personal information the business will gather, what third parties the business will share that personal information with, and that the customer has consented to the personal information as described in the terms and conditions. Finally, the business should obtain the services of an attorney to review the terms and conditions or privacy policy for mistakes. While drafting the terms and conditions or privacy policy, a business should also ask someone with experience in the industry to review it for content and a business should consider using a service that will check the terms and conditions or privacy policy for drafting errors. There are many services available for small businesses to draft legal documents. After the business finalizes the terms and conditions or privacy policy, the business should print and sign it. Finally, the business should post the terms and conditions or privacy policy on its website and any other places where the customer might see it. The business should also encourage the customer to sign a document that they have reviewed the terms and conditions or privacy policy and agree to them. Signed contracts should be kept with the customer.

Do Poojas Poojas are a form of worship in which a deity or a group of deities are invoked,install in an idol or photo and then consecrated or offered food and drinks. Poojas are generally performed to please a deity in order to seek its help or to please the deities for a particular purpose like curing a disease or crossing something difficult etc. Invoking the deity begins with abhisheka or water ablution of the idol of the deity with water. In the Hinduism religious philosophy, the Atman (soul), resides in every living being as per Hindu belief and doctrine. The purpose of life according to Hindu belief is to reach Moksha (liberation) and any ritual that helps a soul in attaining Moksha is called Praarodha (atonement). Thus,in order to help the soul in attaining moksha,Poojas are performed in Hinduism. There are thousands of Hindu temples around the world where Poojas are performed according to a particular religious philosophy and belief. In India,Poojas used to be done only in Hindu temples till 1947 when Indian Independence Act got passed and it was made a constitutional right for every Indian to perform Poojas to their chosen deity in any form they wish. In this article, we will cover how to do Poojas for some commonly used Hindu deities.

In a mixer, combine flour and salt and combine thoroughly on a slow setting. Combine water, oil, and vinegar together separately. Continue mixing with the paddle attachment until the dough gets soft, about 1 minute. Switch out the paddle attachment with a hook attachment and continue mixing for about 10 minutes. Remove the dough from the mixer and continue to knead for 2 more minutes by hand. Use about 1 teaspoon of olive or vegetable oil to coat the entire dough. Cut the phyllo dough into roughly equal portions. Start rolling circular pieces of dough on a rolling pin or dowel. Continue rolling the dough on the pin or dowel by wrapping the dough around the dowel and rolling back and forth. Unwrap the dough by rolling the dowel back towards you. Roll, rotating after each big back and forth, until the dough becomes translucent. Take the translucent dough into your hands and stretch apart very carefully to get an even thinner dough. Place each finished sheet of phyllo on top of each other on a well-floured baking sheet. Repeat until your 7 - 10 layers are fully stacked. Enjoy.

How to Make a Board Game Using the Game Crafter Before creating your own board game, it is important to understand how the game creation process works. This will ensure that you have the proper experience and skills to complete your game. Game creation is broken down into five main steps: creating your game concept, creating your game world, creating your game mechanics, creating your assets, and testing and publishing your game. Creating your game concept A game concept is the idea that you want to communicate to the gaming public. It is the main feature of your game that will be recognizable when players see your game for the first time. It should also be able to stand on its own without any additional information. There are three main components that go into creating your game concept: setting, premise, and theme. Setting defines the game world. It includes all of the physical and imaginary rules that players must follow. Examples of setting include World of Warcraft, the Star Wars universe, or the fictional universe of your game. Premise is the main idea of the game. It explains how the world works and why it needs a new set of rules. The premise should make sense to the gaming public and be easy to remember. Theme is what makes your game unique. It should make the game special or memorable. It should give the game a clear vision or meaning to players. Once you have finished defining your game concept, it is important to put it into writing to ensure you have clearly defined it. Creating your game world Setting and premise are two important elements to creating a game concept. However, the setting itself does not create the game world. The game world is created through the usage of setting and premise. Within the World of Warcraft example, the game world is created by taking the Warcraft universe and putting it into a realistic world where player actions have real world consequences. In the Star Wars universe, players take the premise of protecting the Resistance and fighting against the evil First Order. After you have finished creating your game world, you will want to test it to ensure it is working correctly. This is done by acting out the game world and playing against it. As player, you should be able to recognize and understand the premise and setting of your game world. Any errors will need to be fixed. Once your world is ready, it is time to create your assets. Creating your game assets Game assets include anything used to represent something in a game. This can include sounds, images, character portraits, or any other type of media. Once you have created your game world, you will want to start creating your assets. This is done by capturing screenshots of your in-game world and turning these screenshots into digital assets. assets. In the World of Warcraft example, this would mean capturing in-game screenshots of your desktop and turning these screenshots into digital assets. In the Star Wars universe, capturing in-game screenshots would be turning into digital assets. Once you have finished creating your assets, you are now ready to start creating your game mechanics. Creating your game mechanics Game mechanics are what the player interacts with to tell the game story. The primary mechanics in a Star Wars game would be lightsaber fighting and exploration. In World of Warcraft, the main game mechanics would be leveling characters, skills, and gathering items. After you have finished creating your mechanics, you need to test and validate them. This is done by playing through the game and watching for bugs, missing mechanics, or other errors. Once your mechanics are ready, it is time to build out your game. Building out your game Once you have finished creating your mechanics, it is time to start building out your game. Building out your game is about organizing your assets into different scenes in the game. The order that assets are used in the game determines the pacing of the game. In the Star Wars universe, the game could start with the Rebellion flying through space and attacking the First Order base on Sullust. Understand the purpose of the non-disclosure agreement. A non-disclosure agreement or NDA is a contract between two parties that agree to keep certain information confidential. This information is usually disclosed to one party under the agreement. The purpose of the agreement is to prevent the revealing of this information to third parties, and to protect the confidentiality of the information in the event that one of the parties decides to breach the agreement and disclose the information. There are several other names for a non-disclosure agreement. It can also be referred to as an agreement not to compete, confidentiality agreement, secrecy agreement, jointly developed information agreement, jointly conceived invention agreement, or mutually agreed penalty agreement. A non-disclosure agreement typically covers two types of subjects: (1) information that the recipient is prohibited from sharing with anyone else and (2) information that the sender is prohibited from sharing with anyone else. The first type of information typically concerns commercially valuable and secret information, personal information about employees or customers, or information that belongs to the recipient and that the sender has no right to disclose. The second type of information typically concerns information about the sender’s products, trade secrets, or information that the sender has the right to keep to itself, but that the recipient can disclose. Typically, a non-disclosure agreement covers the time period during which the parties have been in possession of the information that they are protecting. It also typically covers situations in which one of the parties might want to disclose the information in the future, but only under specific circumstances. In many non-disclosure agreements, one party is responsible for all of the expenses arising from a breach of the agreement. In other non-disclosure agreements, the expenses arising from a breach can be apportioned between the parties, and can include attorney’s fees and other costs. There are several different types of alternative dispute resolution (ADR) methods that can be used in a non-disclosure agreement, depending on the circumstances. They include binding arbitration, neutral adjudication, facilitation, mediation, and negotiation. In a non-disclosure agreement, it is important to include some general terms about handing confidential information. This typically includes a time period during which the information is to be held confidential, a time period during which the information is not to be held confidential (after which it can be disclosed for the purposes of defending against a claim that the information is being improperly disclosed), as well as a definition of confidential information and information about what information is not confidential. In most non-disclosure agreements, there is at least one provision that excludes certain types of information from the agreement. For example, information that is publicly known or that the sender had no role in developing is usually not covered by a non-disclosure agreement. Also, information that the parties independently developed is typically not covered by a non-disclosure agreement. It is important to note that information that is based on public laws, regulations, statutes, and case law is not confidential. This type of information is considered to be in the public domain and is not protected by a non-disclosure agreement. A non-disclosure agreement typically covers two different situations. The first situation is where one party discloses the information to another party. The second situation is where one party discloses the information to anyone other than a third party, without specifying that a specific third party. This is commonly referred to as a “blanket” or “blank authorization.” Before signing a non-disclosure agreement, it is important to understand its terms, including all of the limitations and exceptions. It is also important to understand the repercussions of breaching the agreement, which could include monetary expenses, damages, or criminal charges. A sample non-disclosure agreement is attached to this article. If you have any questions about a non-disclosure agreement, or would like advice about writing or negotiating one, please reach out to a lawyer. How to Braid Leather Leather is strong, durable and easy to clean. These traits make leather well suited for a variety of applications. One potential application for leather is braiding. Braiding can create aesthetically pleasing patterns and volume in a small amount of material. While simple patterns are easy to achieve with a simple braid, more complex patterns can be created with more advanced braiding techniques. The following is a tutorial on how to braid leather. 1. Cut 4 separate strands from a leather strip. Tie the top ends of the strands similarly to the previous methods. 2. Take strand D and move it left over both strands B and C. From left to right, your strand order should now be A, D, B, C. 3. Pass strand B over strand D, also moving left. 4. Move strand A right so that it passes over both strands B and D. The strands will now be ordered B, D, A, C. 5. Cross strand D to the right so that it passes over strand A. 6. Take strands B and A into your left hand and strands D and C into your right. 7. Pass strand C to the left over both strands D and A. 8. Strands should now be B, C, A, D. 9. Move strand A left so that it passes over strand C. 10. Strands should be as follows: B, A, C, D. 11. Cross strand B to the right over both strands A and C. 12. Take strand C and pass it to the right over strand B. 13. Repeat steps 9-12 until you have used the desired amount of leather. 14. Tie the end of the braid once you have finished.

The treble recorder (or flauto traverso) is a instrument with a tone ranging from the low E to the high B flat. It is a simple recorder with three holes, played with the right hand while a stopped note is played with the left. The recorder was originally conceived as an instrument for the percussion section in early Baroque music ensembles, as it was (and still is) easy to play while marching. The treble recorder was also played by treble voices in early music ensembles, allowing other vocal parts to be played simultaneously. Choose a recorder that is about one-third of your finger length long. The recorder's body should feel firm but not too tight. You can hold the recorder by the neck or by the mouth. The mouthpiece is a little wider, which allows for a thicker sound. It's also easier to change notes when the mouthpiece is held this way. First, assemble the recorder by fixing the head to the body. Using some device to fix the head, apply glue to the holes and close the head. You can also use string to close the head. Don't forget to apply mucilage to the joints. Finally, tune the instrument. Place the end of the stick into one of the holes, and blow. The tone will be different depending on the hole you choose, because it's made of different materials. E is the second hole; this is where you'll put your left forefinger and thumb. The easiest way to start is by playing the E above middle C. Place your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the E. You should hear a ringing sound. This ringing sound is the fundamental note of the treble recorder. Now, you can start the scale by playing the E, followed by D, C, and finally G. Don't forget to remove your forefinger after playing the E, as it is on the first hole. Now, you can play the D and C above middle C. Using the same technique as before, put your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the D and C. You can now play the C major scale. Keep the D, C, and G from the previous notes. Now, you can play the A above middle C. Using the same technique, put your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the A. Now, you can play the G and B flat above middle C. Using the same technique, put your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the G and B flat. You can now play the A minor scale. Play the G, B flat, and A, in that order. Now, you can play the D sharp and High G above middle C. Put your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the D sharp and High G. You can now play the High F and High G# above middle C. Put your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the High F and High G#. Now, you can play the Bb and C# above middle C. Put your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the Bb and C#. Finally, you can play the High A and F#. Put your left forefinger and thumb on the second and third holes, and blow the High A and F#. Congratulations, you now know how to play the scale of a major scale on the treble recorder! Note: You can play pinched notes by putting a finger on one of the holes while blowing through another one. The left thumb is sometimes used to change the pitch. The B flat and F sharp are sometimes removed before playing the scale. The F sharp can also be changed to G sharp or B flat 7. Using these techniques, you can play almost every scale. Note: You can also play the scales in different modes. For example, you can play the Dorian mode by playing the G sharp scale, starting on the G sharp and then changing the F sharp to D. The Phrygian mode can be played by changing the B flat to C sharp, and the Lydian mode by changing the G flat to A flat. Finally, you can play the chromatic scale. This scale can be used to create new tunes. You can use the scale of a particular key to create another tune in another key. For example, if you know the C major scale, you can create a C sharp scale by starting on the C sharp and then changing the C to D. This can be repeated for all the sharps in the chromatic scale. After you determine that your idea is eligible for a patent, you can submit an idea for protection. The US patent and trademark office (USPTO) is responsible for examining the application and determining whether to grant a patent. Landing a taildragger is fun, but can be tricky. First, warm up the rudders by flying into a holding pattern in front of the airport, dropping down to a very low altitude, then increasing altitude very gradually. Second, keep the nose of the plane down (or close to the horizon), and follow the runway with your peripheral. This will give you enough room to adjust if you drift off course. Third, once you’ve reached the runway, slowly increase power and apply slight back pressure on the yoke. This will help keep the plane’s nose down as you approach the runway. Finally, once you’ve passed the numbers, relax back on the yoke - you’ve just landed! Straighten the plane out by applying gentle back pressure on the yoke, and then follow the pilot’s advice for the three-point landing. You’ve just landed your taildragger! The three-point landing is the most fun part, but easy to mess up. Don’t lose control or go too fast, and you’ll be fine. When flying a taildragger, you have to be a little careful. The plane’s unconventional design places the engine and rudder in the tail, making it harder to control. However, taildraggers are incredibly fun to fly, and make great sports planes.
