How to make Polish Kiffles Walnuts, sugar, egg whites, vanilla, chopped, wax paper, dough ball, powdered counter, fork, same bowl, walnut filling, folded corners Begin by separating the 4 egg yolks and the egg whites using an egg separator. Put the egg whites in the fridge in a covered container to avoid contamination. Beat the egg yolks using a fork or a whisk. Add 1 cup of sour cream to the slightly beaten egg yolks. Blend together the two cups of regular margarine, 4 cups of flour in a separate, larger bowl than the bowl that contains the egg yolk-and-sour cream mixture. Pour the contents of the small bowl into the larger bowl with the flour and butter. Knead with your hands until the dough is soft and smooth. Wrap the dough in wax paper and refrigerate overnight. Next, cut a generous sheet of wax paper and set it down on the kitchen counter. Remove the dough from the refrigerator. Prepare the kitchen counter for rolling out the dough by sprinkling it with some loose flour. Divide the dough ball into wedges that are easy to roll. Roll the dough wedge you are working with into a ball and lightly sprinkle it with some more flour. Set the powdered dough ball onto the powdered counter and begin the rolling process by just pushing your hand down on the dough in the center. Use the powdered rolling pin to roll out the dough ball. Stop rolling out the dough when it is as thin as it can be without holes poking through. Cut off the frayed, imperfect edges of the dough to make a clean rectangular shape and discard the dough edges for now. Cut the rolled dough into even squares. Place the dough-squares, evenly spaced, onto a previously prepared tin-foil-lined baking sheet as you work. Continue rolling more and more dough, incorporating the discarded edges into new dough balls until all the dough has been used and is on baking sheets. Use the fork you left in the walnut filling mixing bowl to scoop a little bit of filling into the center of each dough-square on the baking sheets. Fold two corners opposite each other on each dough-square as if the dough-square were hugging the walnut filling. Bake in the oven starting at 10 to 12 minutes for each baking sheet. Allow the kiffles to cool on the baking sheet (or eat them warm!). Sprinkle some powdered sugar on the top of the kiffles. Enjoy! Polish Kiffles are a traditional Polish dessert. They are deliciously buttery, with a sweet, earthy, smokey flavor that comes from the walnuts. This recipe makes a lot, so it is great to bring to a potluck or a party. This is a very basic recipe for Polish Kiffles. You can vary the recipe in a number of ways. For example, you can add different extracts or leave out an ingredient. You can also vary the walnut version. Some people like to toast the walnuts first, and others like to use brazil nuts in place of the walnuts. This recipe makes a lot, so it is great to bring to a potluck or a party. Ingredients 4 large eggs 1 cup sour cream 1 cup plus 2 cups flour 2 cups plus 8 tablespoons margarine 2 tablespoons sugar 1 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon vanilla extract Directions Separate the eggs. Place the 4 egg yolks in a bowl and add 1 cup of sour cream. Mix with a fork or a whisk. Add 4 cups of flour, 2 cups of margarine and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract to the bowl and mix thoroughly with a spoon. Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge for at least one hour. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Remove the dough from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature for about 10 minutes. Divide the dough into smaller pieces with your hands. This is easier if you flour your hands and the dough. Coat the pieces of dough with flour. Gently scoop about a Tablespoon of walnut filling (about 20 to 30 walnut halves) into the center of each piece of dough. Fold two corners opposite each other, as if the dough were hugging the filling. Place the kiffles onto a sheet of tin foil. Continue rolling and gathering the dough, and filling it, until you have used all the ingredients. You should have 12 to 16 kiffles. Place the kiffles onto a baking sheet and bake for 10 to 12 minutes. The kiffles are done when they are lightly brown around the edges. Let the kiffles cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes

This also creates a safe space for employees to express their hot-buttons and potential conflicts without fear of reprisal. Communicating and understanding potential conflicts ahead of time can help managers manage personality conflicts effectively and prevent them from occurring.

The first Shabbat Candle lighting ceremony for a three year old girl is full of meaning and special, not only because it's her first Shabbat, but because it's a Mitzvah, or good deed, that she will be responsible for honoring every Shabbat of her life. First, decide whether you would like to make this a private family event or a community event. If you would like to make this a private family event, you can invite close family to celebrate with you. If you would like to make this a community event, you should consider baking a cake for your little girl, as well as having her great-grandmother, grandmother, aunt, and mother light a Shabbat candle while reading a poem about the importance and meaning of the Mitzvah and why it's celebrated on Shabbat. Next, explain to your little girl that she now has a responsibility to send her own light into the world via her very own Shabbat Candle that blesses the entire family. At this age, she likely does not fully understand the full implication of what she is being asked to do, but she will likely understand that she has a special candle that she will be sending her light into the family candleholder. Make sure you take time to discuss with her how lighting this Shabbat Candle will help keep the lights on in the house lit up and shining brightly for Shabbat. When everyone is ready, follow step 5 in Part 1 of this guide, which has her female family members join in her lighting of the Shabbat Candle. Finally, have a fun and Shabbat-themed dinner, inviting people to come and celebrate with you and your family! Some ideas for Shabbat-themed food and drinks include: hamentashen, latkes, babaganoush, cupcakes, macaroons, applesauce, andPurim jelly.

The introduction of a new animal into a home can often lead to conflict between the previous pet and the new one. Fortunately, with a little preparation and patience, it is possible for the new and old pets to co-exist peacefully. Begin by spending time with both pets in their respective rooms so that the animals can get used to each other's scents. If one animal has a fear of dogs, for example, entering the room with the dog under the door can help desensitize it toward the cat. Once the two animals have a positive association with each other, it's time to put the plan into action! Introduce the two into the same room, but one at a time. Try to do this in a neutral location, such as a park or a friends house. As the two animals interact, keep a close eye on the interactions to note any signs of aggression. Do not hesitate to separate the two animals immediately if one displays aggression toward the other. When both animals appear non-threatening around each other, it's time to let them spend time together in real, daily situations. This can be as simple as leaving a window or door open so the animals can visit each other out in the real world. Enjoy watching your pets get along, and be patient. Like all relationships, it will take time for these two to grow old together, but the results will be well worth it!

Parking in a small space can be a challenging task, but with the right approach, it is possible to park safely in even the tightest of parking spots. First, locate an available parking space, and make sure it is big enough to fit your vehicle. Do not park in a space that is too narrow, as this may cause a collision with another object. Secondly, stop your vehicle in the space, and check your mirrors and side mirrors. It is recommended that you also fold your rearview mirror if possible. Finally, enter the parking space, and slowly begin pulling in. Continue turning the wheel as you drive forward into the parking space, and straighten up the steering wheel once you are fully in the space. The car wash process can be frustrating but also enjoyable once you understand the basics. The most important thing is to make sure the car is clean when you get into the car wash, as dirt and moisture can quickly get onto and damage cars flooring, walls, and other components. To start, locate a clean, empty spot in the car wash, and park your car in that spot. Look around to make sure no one is around, and lock your car. Next, scope out the car wash to see where the wash arms, racks, and drains are. Most car washes have three wash bays, with each bay having a wash arm, rack, and drain. Make sure your car is centered between the wash arms. Once you've located your car in the car wash, select a wash cycle, and let the car wash work its magic. The soap or wash and rinse cycles remove dirt from your car, while the pre-soak cycle removes most standing water from the surface of the car. Make sure to check the car wash display to make sure you select the correct cycle, and ensure the car is clean when the cycle is complete. After the car wash cycle is complete, rinse off any suds with the high pressure was cycle. Again, be sure to check the display to make sure you select the correct cycle. After the high-pressure rinse cycle is complete, walk around your car blasting any dirt or debris off with the low pressure nozzle. Make sure you move fast to avoid missing areas, as the nozzle can't blast as fast as you. Wash your car with the wax cycle, and make sure to go around your car in a full loop. Once you're finished washing your car, it's time to get the trash out. First, move the trash can to the appropriate area, and then use the car wash detergent dispenser to empty any remaining detergent into the trash can. Finally, vacuum the inside of your car, and toss any trash left over from the car wash into the appropriate can. Enjoy your cleaned car!

Clear a fence line around the rubbish. Measure the perimeter of the pile and calculate the length so you can estimate how much material you will need for the fence. Buy the fencing material and suitable posts, as well as a gate (if you don't build your own), and fasteners. Start at one side of the location where you plan to put your gate. Set the next post in line with the first, keeping an equal distance from the edge of the rubbish pile, and about 8 feet from the starting point. Continue setting posts equally spaced around the pile until you are near your starting point. Roll out the fence wire (if using) around the perimeter you have created with the posts, then attach one end to the first gate post. Nail rail boards (typically treated 2X4s) if you are using wood privacy fencing, one at the top of the post, one in the middle, and one about a foot from the ground between your posts. Add material to block the view of the rubbish pile if you need to. Hang your gate and install a latch on it, and your job is complete.

Get over an inter religious relationship break up asap, as it is simply for good. Your faith in them meant everything to you and them. Maintaining an online relationship can be a challenge, but here are some ways to make it fun and help you both stay engaged. Talk every day for at least an hour or longer. Avoid distraction. Use programs that enable you to talk to each other, such as the voice conversation feature on MSN or Skype or Facebook. Play the Anywhere Anytime Anyhow game where one person emails the other person a task and no matter what the person's doing, they have to complete the task (make the tasks fun!). Be romantic and send the other person random gifts such as flowers/teddies in their country that can work even if the couple lives in different countries by checking out websites that delivers flowers/teddies in their country and placing an order online. Trying each time you guys talk to make it interesting, don't make it look like a boring chat, or he/she will lose interest in you!

Step up onto the starting block. Select your entry point visually and mentally. Leap off the starting block once the starting “beep” goes off. Use a powerful dolphin kick off the starting blocks. Swim freestyle once you break the surface after about 5 yards (4.6 m) of underwater dolphin kick. Roll on to the side (so that this arm is facing down towards the bottom) that is going to pull first. Take the arm facing the bottom out of streamline position and pull it straight back in a forceful motion. Recover the arm that has just pulled over the water quickly in a bent but relaxed position. Engage the arm that has not pulled in a slightly bent position about 6 – 8 inches (20.3 cm) below the surface. Thrust arm into the water so that it is completely straight and is about 4 – 6 inches (15.2 cm) below the surface. Pull the arm straight back forcefully. Repeat (including both parts) until you are about two yards away from the wall. Remember to keep your head steady and have stamina and momentum in your arms and kick. With the final arm-pull into the wall, reach and start rolling into a flip leading with the arm and following through with the head. Bring both feet over the water quickly and place them about 10 – 12 inches (30.5 cm) under the surface of the water and on the wall. Push off from the wall. Treat the last part of the race just like the first part, and the same rules apply. Repeat until you touch the wall on a final stroke at the finish of your swim. End in a sportsmanlike way.

How to build a motor Wind wire around a cylindrical object like a pen or pencil cell. Separate the cylindrical object from the wire so all you are left with is the wire coil. Wrap the ends of the wire around the rest of the wire. Create another loop that is perpendicular to your previous to secure the wrapped wire. Hold the coil up against a flat surface like a tabletop. Scrape the surface of the wire to strip off the insulation only at one side of the loose end. Repeat the process of removing insulation for the other loose end of the motor coil so that the shiny part on both ends is facing upwards. Make the axle supports so the armature can be placed on them and spin easily. Place the armature so that the loose ends (with insulation stripped at one side) are going through the loops of the axle supports. Attach the other ends of the axle supports to the opposite ends of the battery holder. Attach the magnet on top of the battery holder so it is near the armature. Put the charged battery inside the battery holder. Give the armature a gentle spin to get it in motion.

Use crepe paper to make a beautiful peony. Start by rolling some crepe paper into a small ball. Cover the ball with yellow crepe paper and secure it to a wire stem. Wrap yellow embroidery thread 9 to 10 times around two fingers. Pull off the looped thread and cut it. Spread the floss across a strip of double-sided tape. Wrap the double-sided tape around the base of the ball. Cut crepe paper into rectangles for the base of the petals. Cut the rectangles into tabbed petal shapes. Shape the small petals into ruffed cups. Shape the large petals into plain cups. Glue the first small petal to the stem. Continue gluing the small petals to the stem. Finish off with the largest petals. Cut 5 small leaf shapes out of green paper. Glue the leaves to the bottom of the flower. Cut three 3-point leaves. Glue the leaves to wire stems. Wrap the top part of each leaf stem with florist's tape. Wrap the top of the main stem with green florist's tape. Secure the a leaf stem to the main stem. Secure the next two leaf stems, spacing them 4 inches (10.16 centimeters) apart. Finish wrapping the tape around the main stem. Finish shaping the flower.

Head‐to‐Toe Exam write down the acronym “DR ABC”., Evaluate the situation to see if you put yourself in immediate physical danger by assisting the victim., Check the victim’s response to see if the victim is conscious., Examine the victim’s airway to determine if he is breathing normally., Analyze the victim’s breathing., Check the victim’s pulse (circulation) and examine their body for signs of bleeding., Ask the victim about the history of the incident., Ask the victim to tell you their personal medical history., Have the individual describe their symptoms to you., Examine the victim’s body., Palpate the 4 quadrants of the person’s abdomen: upper left and upper right (including the shoulders and ribs, down to their waist) and lower left and lower right (including the lower ribs and stomach)., Exam the pelvis., Assess the person’s capillary refill by pressing on their fingernail., Exam the bones of the arms and legs to check for breakage.

How to Make a Rod Puppet -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Drill two small holes through all the dowels except the body one, the smallest one, and two rods. Drill a (small) hole through the center of what will be your body dowel. Drill one (small) hole in each of the rods. Place a small plastic tube through the body dowel so that its base touches the smallest dowel. Cover your plastic tube with glue at the top. Cut some newspaper into large pieces. Cover the crumpled newspaper with papier-mâché. After the papier-mâché has dried, mix some corn syrup in a bucket with water for a paste and tear up more newspaper. Use a pocket knife to scrape away at newspaper to form a neck. Cover the entire plastic tube with regular glue. Repeat step three of "Making the Head" Take two pieces of wire and bend them halfway so the two ends (of each wire) are parallel to each other. Repeat step four of "Making the Head" Cut a piece of wax string. Repeat the previous two steps on the other wire to create the second arm. Take a small piece of wood. Use regular glue to attach the bottom of the hand into the chair shape. When the glue has dried, drill a small hole near the end of the hand that is curved and not covered by the "chair". Choose a base color. Paint facial features. Take a piece of cardboard and some yarn. Carefully remove the yarn from the cardboard by slipping it off. Cut a piece of fabric twice your desired length. Remove the smallest dowel. Slip the costume through the dowel until it reaches the neck. For a short-sleeved dress or robe, roll up the excess side fabric. Using a needle and thread, stitch the left front/back and right front/back together. Congratulations! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Rod puppet is now ready! You can dress it up to act as any character.

Do not confuse aspirin side effects as allergic reactions.Find out if you have any of the following medical conditions that can increase your chances of having an aspirin allergy: Asthma: inflammation in your breathing airways causing coughing, shortness of breath or tightness in your chest Urticaria: raised spots on your skin Sinusitis: inflammation in your nasal passage due to infection from virus, bacteria or fungus Look for the following symptoms that indicate aspirin allergy: Red bumps (hives) on your skin Itchiness and rashes, especially near your mouth Nasal congestion or a watery nose Eyes watering or becoming itchy Symptoms similar to an asthma attack such as wheezing or breathing difficulties Swollen lips or tongue Consult a doctor if you experience dangerous symptoms such as rhinitis (inflammation in your nose) or anaphylaxis. Don't take the following medications if you are allergic to aspirin: Alka-Seltzer Aspirin in any form or under any brand name Dristan Ecotrin Ibuprofen such as Motrin and Advil Kaopectate Naproxen such as Aleve, Anaprox and Naprosyn Pepto-Bismol Inspect the ingredients of all food and drinks. Eat protein like chicken, fish, eggs as well as fresh vegetables. Avoid items that contain mint or mint flavoring because they can contain a high amount of salicylates. Be careful when eating fruits. Refrain from eating dried fruits and canned fruits. Increase the intake of vitamin C with bioflavonoids in your diet. Use the following home remedies to avoid or control allergic reactions: Apply a mixture of cinnamon powder and honey on infected areas of your skin.

This is particularly helpful if you ever need to fix your sewing machine, or if you are planning on upgrading the machine's accessories, such as the bobbin or presser foot. First, find the machine's spool pins by locating the bottom left-hand side panel, near the needle. The spool pins will have two small holes in them, one on either side of the pin. Each Necchi sewing machine is different, so make sure you check the specific instructions for your model. Second, make sure the sewing machine is turned off, and unthread the needle. Thread one end of the desired thread through one of the holes on either side of the spool pin. Gently tug on the thread to remove any slack. Thread the rest of the desired thread onto the spool pin, until you reach the front of the pin, near the presser foot. Once you have threaded the entire length of the pin, your thread should hang behind the presser foot. Finally, test the thread by placing the presser foot down on a fabric. The bobbin thread should now come up through the middle hole in the spool pin, and the newly threaded thread should pass over the front of the pin. Pull both threads slowly, and the newly threaded thread will pass over the front of the spool pin, and under the presser foot. Congratulations, you are now a Necchi threading master! Create a budget in Excel Write a budget in Excel. Keep track of your income and spending for 1 or 2 months before creating your Excel budget. Evaluate your income at the end of the first or second month to determine your average monthly earnings. Look at what you have spent money on during the 1 or 2 month period, and make categories for your budget based on that. Open Excel, and create a new spreadsheet. Save the spreadsheet. Type the name of each month in the top row of the budget spreadsheet, and start in column B. Type the word "Income" in column A of the second row. Type =sum(B#:B#2) in the box next to the box containing "Total Income." Type =sum(letter#:letter#2) for the remaining columns of months. Add a final column to total your income for the year. Type the word "Expenses" in the next row underneath the Income section in column A. Choose a category to insert underneath expenses. List any expenses for housing in the rows below. Type "Total" in the final row of the "Housing" category, then type the =sum formula in each column for each month. Type "Anticipated" or "Estimated" in column A of the row below "Total," and then type in what you expect to spend on housing during each month based on your previous tracking. Continue to set up sections on the Excel spreadsheet for each category of your personal budget. Type "Total Expenses" in column A in the row beneath all your budget sections. Type "Over/Short" in the row beneath "Total Expenses" in column A. After completing your budget, you may wish to share it with a spouse or partner, a family member, or a close friend. Be sure to keep track of your expenses separately from your income. If you find that you are spending more than you make, you can make changes to reduce expenses. For example, you can look for a cheaper place to live, cut back on spending for entertainment, or trim unimportant expenses such as subscriptions. Budgeting is an important financial habit that will benefit you and your family over the long run. Use this budgeting advice to create a strong financial future. Nitrate toxicity or poisoning affects both humans and livestock. In cattle, it can cause such symptoms as restlessness, running around, hyperactivity, rapid heart beat, high fever, decreased appetite, and even death. Animals most susceptible to nitrate poisoning include young cattle, cattle raised on pastures, and cattle that have recently undergone surgery or medical treatment. The most dangerous plants to accumulate nitrates from include wheat, corn, beans, and potato plants. Animals that consume these plants may accumulate high levels of nitrates in their bodies, causing toxicity. It is possible to limit nitrate ingestion by avoiding these plants, feeding animals only concentrated ruminant feeds that are low in nitrates, and monitoring animals carefully for signs of toxicity. If you do discover cattle exhibiting signs of nitrate toxicity, treat the symptoms as well as possible and contact your veterinarian. The veterinarian can prescribe home treatments to help the animal and remove it from the dangerous feed. Because this is an emergency situation, the home treatments include IV injection of a 1% or 4% solution of methylene blue. Once the animal has been removed from the dangerous feed and is no longer exhibiting symptoms, it is necessary to continue to monitor the animal carefully for a few days to make sure no signs of toxicity arise. It is important to remember that certain environmental and climatic factors may increase or decrease the risk of nitrate accumulation. These factors include environmental temperature, humidity, and the amount of fertilizer applied to soil. It is possible to time harvests of crops and timing of veterinary medical treatments and pastures to reduce nitrate levels in feed and the environment.

Find a low fence and place the unicycle parallel to the fence so that you can use it for support as you mount the unicycle. Position the pedals of the unicycle in a slightly offset, vertical position so that one pedal is in the 4 o'clock position and the other is in the 10 o'clock position, mirroring the hands of a clock. Tilt the unicycle toward you until the seat of the unicycle rests between your legs. Continue to squeeze the seat between your thighs and place both of your hands on the fence. Step on the pedal closest to you in the 4 o'clock position with your dominant foot. Give yourself a little push with your other foot and sit on the unicycle seat, placing your non-dominant foot on the pedal furthest away in the 10 o'clock position. Hold on to the handrail and begin to pedal very slowly at first. Practice mounting and pedaling while holding on to a fence until you feel comfortable balancing on your own. Put the weight of your body directly over the seat. Move the unicycle forward by leaning your entire body and the unicycle forward as a single unit. Sit up straight when riding at a normal speed. Pedal backwards by sitting up straight with your torso over your seat and pedal the feet in short, 1/4-turn revolutions backwards. Continue to practice pedaling forward and backward while holding on to a fence or handrail for as long as necessary. Position your upper body directly over the seat and steady yourself for a turn. Use your hips to turn the unicycle quickly to the right or to the left. Pivot sharply on the wheel of the unicycle as you swing your hips by guiding the pedals with your feet. Hold on to a handrail when attempting to turn for the first few times. Remember to tilt your body slightly as you turn to encourage motion in the desired direction. Continue to pedal immediately after you turn. Position the pedals in the same vertical position you used to mount the unicycle. Transfer your weight to the foot on the lower pedal. Hold on to the handrail with one or both hands depending on your comfort level. When you feel stable, step down with the highest, dominant foot first. Immediately step your lower foot off as the first foot hits the ground to dismount. Unicycling is a form of bicycling that uses a unicycle rather than a bicycle. It is a low impact form of exercise that many people enjoy. Like bicycling, unicycling can be performed for transportation or exercise. Most unicycles have pedals that the rider sits on while straddling the unicycle wheel. Some unicycles do not have pedals, and the rider steers with their feet, similar to a motorcycle. The bicycle has two wheels, while the unicycle has one wheel. The unicycle wheel is attached to the front of the rider's leg like a bicycle's wheel, and the rider typically pedals with their feet. The unicycle's wheel makes a single turn once every revolution the pedals make. While unicycling like bicycling, the rider must position their upper body over the unicycle wheel to balance. When unicycling, the rider typically moves their whole body and the unicycle as a single unit while leaning their body towards the direction they want to turn. This type of turning requires more skill and practice than bicycling. When learning to unicycle, it is recommended to first learn how to balance on the unicycle without holding on to anything. This will allow you to focus on balancing while you gradually learn to hold on to something to keep from falling. Once you have learned how to balance without holding on, you can start to practice with something to hold on to. As you become more comfortable unicycling, you can increase the item you hold on to and the size of motions you practice.

Drill three holes about 1 1/2 inches (3.8cm) from the center of your plywood disk, equally spaced around it. Thread one string through each hole in the plywood, snug them slightly, and while holding the disk level, drop some hot-melt glue on each to secure it in place. Cut a smaller disk of your plywood, about 1 1/2 times the diameter of your bamboo pieces smaller than your first (top) disk. Secure these strings to the plywood, using hot-melt glue again, keeping this smaller disk level also. Cut a shape of plywood or other material to hang below the hammer, or lower disk, and tie it on the end of your three strings. Finally, Finished. Mount St. Helens, located in the snoqualmie national forest in the snoqualmie and landing counties in the state of Washington, is a frequent target for casual hikers and trail runners due to its proximity to the Seattle metropolitan area and the rich cultural history that the mountain holds. However, despite its beauty and significance, mountain climbing on St. Helens is very rarely performed, with only a handful of people annually reaching the summit. The most common method of reaching the top is to use the Ptarmigan Trail, which is an exposed, Class 2 route that gains roughly 3,000 feet of elevation. However, this route is often snowbound from late November to early May, and is frequently littered with large boulders and difficult to travel due to its high elevation. If you would like to climb Mount St. Helens but are not able to during the winter months, there are other options available to you. The most popular time to climb the mountain is between the months of March and November, as this is when most of the snow has melted off of the mountain and the weather tends to be most suitable for climbing. During these months, a permit is required in order to climb the mountain, and you must check in with the Lone Fir Resort, which is located roughly 10 miles from the nearest trail head on Forest Road 5465, between 10am and 3pm. If you would like to climb the mountain outside of these months, you will still need to purchase a permit in advance and check in with the Lone Fir Resort, but the most important bit of preparation is checking the weather ahead of time and making sure you are able to hike enough elevation in order to properly prepare your body for the rigors of the climb. Because mountain weather can be unpredictable, it is important to plan ahead and make sure you are able to complete at least 8-10 miles of hiking with at least 3,000 feet of elevation gain in order to properly prepare for your climb. While this may sound daunting, many people find that short, steep hikes near their home to be more than adequate for this purpose, and if you live near the Portland metro area, Silver Star via Sturgeon Rock Loop is often considered the best hike to build strength for St. Helens climb. Once you are properly prepared, pick up your permit at the Lone Fir Resort, which is located on FR 5465, near the intersection of COHORUS Lane. From there, it is only a short hike to the summit. Be sure to pack enough food and water to keep yourself comfortable on the hike, and once you reach the summit, enjoy the spectacular views of the destruction the mountain endured over forty years ago and the beautiful forest that has since grown back! If you are able to reach the top outside of the climbing months, be sure to register your visit with the Lone Fir Resort so that they may begin tracking the statistics and preserve the mountain for future climbers!

Choose a Business Structure: It is very important to follow a proper business structure for your business. A business structure is how a business is organized and it can affect how the business is run. There are three basic types of business structures: sole proprietorship, partnership and corporation. Sole proprietorship: A sole proprietorship is the simplest form of business structure. It is often the first business structure that entrepreneurs start because it is easy to set up and there is only one member of the business. The business owns the business and its assets and responsibilities. The business can employ one person and that is the owner. All business activities will take place under the name of the business. This structure is convenient and easy to set up, but it has some limitations. Since only one person is involved in the business, the sole proprietor will have to make all important business decisions and take all important actions. The sole proprietor must also make sure the business follows all applicable laws and regulations. One major challenge of this structure is lack of separation of business and personal life. Partnership: A partnership is an alternative business structure that has some advantages over the sole proprietorship structure. A partnership is similar to a corporation in that it is a separate legal entity from its partners. There is no single owner of the partnership. There is also no single managing member. Instead, there is a partnership agreement that defines the rights and responsibilities of each partner. Each partner has certain responsibilities that include conducting business activities, making business decisions and taking action. The partnership also has advantages over the sole proprietorship structure. Since each partner has a defined role, the partnership structure helps reduce risks of abuse of dominant position, as each partner can check the other partners' power. Partnership is also appropriate for businesses where there is a need to pool resources, skills and knowledge. Corporation: A corporation is a separate legal entity that limits the personal liability of its owners. The corporation can also be set up to have limited or no partnership interest. There are many types of corporations, such as C corporations, S corporations, passthru corporation and foreign corporations. A C corporation is a legal entity that deals primarily in business activities, such as manufacturing, selling and services. A S corporation is another type of corporation that is more similar to a partnership in that it has owners and shareholders who share in the profits but not the business operations. A passthru corporation is similar to a C corporation except that it performs no active operations other than the business activities performed by its parent company. A foreign corporation is a legal entity established in a jurisdiction outside of the United States. It can be used for international business operations. A corporation is a complex business structure, and it is the most common business structure for a company that has complex operations and multiple shareholders. Format your document. Your distributor agreement should begin with a short statement of the fundamental information about the parties, including the effective date of the agreement. Next, identify the parties. This is best done by listing all of the parties’ names on the first page. Add your recitals. A recital is a statement that introduces a new idea or adds explanation. In a distributor agreement, the recitals might explain why the parties are coming together and the purpose of the agreement. State the effective date of the agreement. Most agreements state that they become effective on the date they are signed, but distributor agreements often take effect at the date of shipment. That is, the agreement will be in effect even if there is no signatory until after the effective date. Therefore, most distributor agreements state the effective date as the later of the signing date or the date on which the goods are shipped. Identify the distributor and the parties. The distributor will be the main party to the agreement, and the other parties will be additional parties to the agreement. As a rule, distributors and end customers will be different parties. The reason is that the parties are usually different legal entities, and the agreement usually covers different transactions. Distributors will normally only agree to represent one end customer. The agreement should then set out the distributor’s territory. A typical distributor agreement will say that the distributor has the exclusive right to sell the end customer’s products in a specified territory. This is an important detail to establish to make sure that customers in different territories do not interfere with each other. Defining the distributor as an “independent contractor” will help ensure that the distributor is not your employee or agent. The distributor is an independent contractor in the sense that they have a business and can enter into distributor agreements with other companies. State the parties to the agreement. Usually, there are four parties to the agreement: the distributor, the end customer, the original supplier (also called importer) and the distributor’s parent company. The distributor agrees to buy goods from the original supplier and sell them to the end customer. The original supplier agrees to sell the goods to the distributor and the distributor agrees to buy the goods from the original supplier and sell them to the end customer. The distributor’s parent company agrees to provide capital to the distributor to help the distributor buy the goods. State the effective date of the agreement. The effective date is normally the signing date of the agreement, unless the parties agree to a different date. If the parties agree to a different effective date, the effective date should also be specified. In most cases, the distributor agreement will take effect at the signing date. That is, all obligations of the parties will occur on the signing date. The distributor can begin performance on this date. However, many distributors require that they be paid within a certain number of days after the effective date, so often the parties choose the later of the signing date or the date of shipment as the effective date. Identify how prices are set. Prices will usually be set in the goods or services agreement. This is a separate agreement between the distributor and the end customer. The prices will often be agreed upon up front at the beginning of the agreement or as part of negotiations in setting up the agreement. In some cases, the distributor will have a different pricing structure for different customers. In such cases, the distributor agreement will specify how different customers are to be treated differently. For example, the agreement could state that the distributor will apply different prices to different customers on a case-by-case basis. State how prices are determined. If there is a pricing agreement, this should be stated in the agreement. Most distributor agreements are bilateral, which means that only one distributor and one end customer will be involved. But some distributor agreements are multilateral, meaning that there are many distributors and end customers. In that case, the agreement will state how the prices are to be divided up between the distributors and end customers. Payment terms are usually determined in the goods or services agreement. In a distributor agreement, most of the important payment details will be in the arrangements for payment. It is usually preferable to have a single payment that will apply to all of the customers. It is sometimes impractical to set up a complex network of payments with different dates and conditions. The distributor could agree to provide notes or a line of credit to cover all of the payments. State how payments are made. Most distributor agreements provide that all amounts will be paid up front, except for a percentage that is paid on delivery or shortly thereafter. This percentage is most likely to be 50%. However, payment terms can be as long as two years. When paying the distributor, the distributor will usually deduct their own expenses, such as transportation or advertising costs, before paying the original supplier. The original supplier will usually take a commission from the distributor for the expenses that they have paid. State how prices and payments are set for different customers. Build a model pirate ship with polyurethane foam. Model pirate ships can be used as landmarks at parks and events, or can be a fun project for a small group to build together. This article provides directions for obtaining sufficient polyurethane foam to build a 1:6 scale ship, with the basic shape provided on a paper plate. The basic steps for constructing the ship are as follows: 1. Draw the basic shape of your ship on a sheet of paper; 2. Mark the shapes of each layer; 3. Cut the layers; 4. Fit the layers together; 5. Add ballast, if desired; 6. Trim and smooth the ship; 7. Coat with paint. You can add details to your ship, such as masts, rigging, yards, and flags. A 1:6 scale ship typically takes between 150 and 200 foam polyurethane block, depending on the complexity of the ship. Obtain sufficient polyurethane foam for your project. Draw the basic shape of your pirate ship on a sheet of paper, noting the length, height, and width so you can transfer these dimensions to the foam sheet. Mark the shapes of each layer on the foam sheet. Cut the top layer, beveling the cut slightly as the next layer should be narrower, since the sides of the ship should taper toward the bottom, becoming narrower near the keel. Cut enough of these layers so that when they are laminated together, they will give you the desired height of the ships hull. Remove any material you need to so you have a space for ballast, if desired, by hollowing out the middle layers of foam with a hand saw such as a drywall saw or a narrow trim saw, as shown in the illustration. Check the fit of the layers, then glue them together with a waterproof, latex adhesive sealant, or with a low-temp hot melt glue gun. Trim the exterior of the ship with a sander, rasp, or other tool so the joints are flush and clean, and trim enough so the sides of the ship are shaped the way you want them. Add blocks of foam at the fore and aft of the ship to create the raised stern and prow common on sailing sips. Shape your finished ship's hull by hand sanding the foam so that it is smooth and correctly shaped, taking care to keep the opposite sides as symmetrical as possible. Build your ship with the basic hull shape provided, or shaped as desired. Coat all exposed surfaces of your ship with an adhesive latex caulking or a multipurpose latex primer. Spray the entire hull with a good quality enamel spray paint, using the color you choose. Build your masts and rigging out of the lightest material you can find. Tie the yardarms and rigging to the masts with brown thread to simulate ropes, gluing the knots to keep them secured with a plastic cement or hot melt glue gun. Add whatever details you want to your finished ship, possibly including a crow's nest, a rudder, a skeg to the keel for balance, flags, portholes, and others. The resulting pirate ship is small enough to fit in the palm of your hand, and the method is very easy to follow, even for beginners. The large variety of polyurethane foam shapes and sizes available means that you can customize your ship to your exact specifications. This project provides a good way to learn basic carpentry skills and also get creative with a simple design. In addition to the basic 1:6 scale pirate ship detailed here, you can vary the design by including different features such as a cabin, cannons, masts, sails, and anchors. You can also adapt this technique to make other ship designs, such as a fishing boat, submarine, or cruise ship. Many thanks to readers Artweaver, MonkeyGunk, PapaDuch, and rogerimo for submitting similar ideas for this article. This project is suitable for beginners, and the materials are inexpensive. Be sure to follow the instructions carefully and you will have a fun model pirate ship within a few hours. You can paint your model as desired, or leave the hull natural for a more realistic look. Finally, you can adapt this technique to build other ship designs, such as a fishing boat, submarine, or cruise ship.

Do not attempt to start your vehicle with the cutoff switch engaged, or you will blow the fuse. Remove the screws under the dishwasher door. Find the inlet valve. Shut off the water and power to the dishwasher before starting. Remove the screws under the dishwasher door. Find the inlet valve. Detach the water hose from the valve and remove the fitting that attaches the valve to the dishwasher. Remove the valve. Locate and remove the two quarter-inch screws. Angle the inlet valve downward to remove the electrical harness that is attached to the valve's solenoid assembly. Using a pair of needle-nose pliers, squeeze the spring clamp fastening the outlet hose to loosen it and move it up. Pull the old valve out and discard it. Remove any old plumbing tape and clean the fitting with a stiff wire brush. Using a vise-grip plier, tighten the fitting before it is placed back inside of the dishwasher. Place the spring clamp back onto the outlet hose and reattach the hose to the inlet valve. Using the needle-nose pliers, squeeze the spring clamp once again and wiggle it back down the outlet hose. Reattach the new valve to the side of the machine with the two quarter-inch screws that were used to mount the old inlet valve. Reattach the valve's water supply hose and carefully connect the electrical harness to the inlet valve solenoid. Turn on the electricity and the water supply to the dishwasher and start it up.

To create a spirallic spin particle path or necklace, open a new Excel workbook, and set preferences as follows: In Excel's preferences, under the "Editors" category, make sure the Use R1C1 cell reference style is unchecked. In the same Excel preferences, under the "Preference" category, set "Display options for Cells and Named ranges" to "Use native references for... : Roman and Hanxhs." Create some named variables. Select cells A1:E2 and insert name create in the top row. In cell C2, input.125 or "=1/8". Create some more named variables. Put the entire sheet in font Lucida Fax size 9. Do edit go to cell range F6:F2886 and input the formula =( (sin((A6)/(B6*2))*GM*sin((A6)*GM*(cos((A6)/(B6*2)))*GM)+D6))/(ShrinkExpand) ). Find out if you are too clingy by asking yourself if you try to satisfy your needs completely, instead of waiting for your partner to do it for you. Listen to your inner guidance. If you hear fear, desperation or resentment, you are probably being too clingy. If you fear that your partner will abandon you, you are probably being too clingy. If you feel unable to make decisions for yourself, you are probably being too clingy. If you search your relationships for people who will never leave or break up with you, you are probably being too clingy. If you search your relationships for boom and bust cycles, you are probably being too clingy. If you are afraid to be alone, you are probably being too clingy. If you lack confidence in yourself and fear that your partner doesn't like you for who you are, you are probably being too clingy. If you feel that your friend is incomplete without you, but you won't allow yourself to accept that they have moved on, you are probably being too clingy. If you feel that your friend is illogical or "strange" but you can't admit that you are bothered by it, you are probably being too clingy. If you spend a lot of time reading stories about people who have strong, healthy interpersonal relationships, but you don't have one yourself, you are probably being too clingy. If you feel that your partner has too many friends but you don't have any, you are probably being too clingy. If you have a sense that your partner is not honest with you, and they tell you that you are being too clingy, you should examine the situation more closely. If your answer is "yes" to most of these questions, you may be being too clingy.

To ensure your name is correctly recorded on your apartment lease, ensure your lease includes your full name, as well as the full name of any sharing a unit with you (for example, if you have a roommate). If your lease does not include your full name, you can provide that information to your landlord when you move in so that it can be recorded. Next, ensure you understand who your landlord is, and identify any property managers or other responsible parties on your lease. Your landlord has the right to enter your unit to maintain and ensure the safety of your living space. As your landlord, they will be responsible for paying the property taxes, maintaining the HVAC and water systems, and ensuring that the proper utilities are paid for and provided. You may share liability for other charges associated with your unit with your landlord, such as the cost of monthly maintenance of common areas like the kitchen or roof. A common mistake made by new residents is failing to recognize the due date for rent payments. If you share responsibility for paying rent with your landlord, ensure you are aware of when your payment is due to avoid late fees or other penalties, and be aware that your landlord may hold rent as security until you meet your obligation to the unit. If you will be paying your rent via a service, ensure the lease details the fees for that service, including any fees for late payments or returned payments. Understanding any penalties for late or returned payments and knowing when any increases will take effect allows you to plan your budget and your usage of services to make sure your financial obligations are met. Knowing what resources or services your landlord has access to allows you to understand the responsibilities of both you and your landlord for the unit, and communicate clearly with your landlord as needed. For example, some leases allow the landlord to enter your unit to conduct certain routine maintenance, such as fixing the hot water tank, the furnace, or the plumbing. The lease should include details on when maintenance must be done and when it must be reported to the landlord. If you need service on the unit, you should let your landlord know as soon as possible so that they can arrange for service on your behalf. Review the details about who is responsible for paying the property taxes, maintaining the HVAC and water systems, and ensuring that the proper utilities are paid for and provided. Knowing the period of the lease allows you to determine the length of your lease term. Keep in mind that your landlord may have the right to renew the lease for an extended term; you may wish to review your lease to understand your obligations and rights during the term of the lease. If your lease covers services included with the lease, ensure the lease includes the entire agreement, including details on any fees or additional charges, any warranties or representations made by the lessor or the lessee, any limitations on your use of the property, and any penalties for breaching the lease. Be sure that the lease includes your name, your landlord’s name, and any other responsible parties on the lease. Place mulch around your squash for the first few weeks if you have a weed problem. Water your squash mounds when the soil begins to dry out. Look out for squash vine borers that leave “sawdust.” You can remove them by hand. Test the acorn squash individually after two to three months. A good travel itinerary is crucial for a successful trip. With the right itinerary, you’ll be able to spend more time enjoying your trip and less time worrying about logistics. To create the perfect travel itinerary, it’s important to know your boss well, and ask several colleagues for their opinion. You can also ask your boss to share their travel preferences. Additionally, it’s essential to determine the purpose of the trip, as well as any details that might impact the trip, such as when your boss needs to arrive or which airport they’ll be able to depart from. Once you have all of this information, it’s time to create a detailed checklist of items that your boss will need for the trip, such as passports,Medicine, suitcase or purse, cellphone, laptop or tablet, Powerbank, headphones,and an umbrella. When you’re ready to book your trip, make sure you account for the most cost effective or convenient route, as well as alternate airports, and ask about any discounts or loyalty programs your boss may be eligible for. After you’ve booked your trip, make sure you have an arrival packet prepared, including information about any car services or public transportation available at the destination so your boss won’t have to worry about organizing that information while on their trip. Finally, make sure you create a travel packet that includes important receipts or agendas so your boss will know how to organize all of their documentation. By following these steps, you can create the perfect travel itinerary to ensure a stress-free trip for you and your boss!

This page should help enable RAID or AHCI without reinstalling Windows, especially for AMD SB85 and SB8XX chipset-based RAID controllers. Firstly, make sure you have a current backup of your important data. It's always good to have multiple backups, in case one fails. Secondly, backup your Windows registry. This is where settings for Windows, applications and hardware are stored. It's possible that some of these settings may be invalid/broken after a clean install of a new operating system. It's recommended to use a tool like Revo uninstaller to make sure no files and fragments are left behind. Boot your system into Linux. This can be done by either pressing the Shift key immediately after powering on the machine, or by using an installation disc or live USB. If you have any installation discs, try them in order starting with the earliest release date (eg: 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010) until you find one that works. The exact name of the disc does not matter as long as it starts with "Linux". If you don't have a installation disc, there are many free Linux live USB creators available online. Once inside Linux, view chipset information with the command: lspci -vvnn | less The result might look like this: [email protected]:~$ lspci -vvnn | less 00:14.2 PCI bridge: Intel Corporation 88x PCI-root devison (rev e8) Subsystem: Hewlett-Packard HP 88w837y -- 01:00.0 Ethernet controller: Intel Corporation 82571EB 10/100 Network Connection Subsystem: Hewlett-Packard HP 82571EB -- 01:02.0 Ethernet controller: Intel Corporation 82571EB 10/100 Network Connection Subsystem: Hewlett-Packard HP 82571EB -- 01:04.0 Ethernet controller: Realtek Semiconductor Co., Ltd. RTL-10Gbit/s Combo Network Connection Subsystem: Hewlett-Packard HP RTL8111G -- 01:08.0 IDE interface: Intel Corporation 82371AB IDE (ICH4/ICH4-M) -- 01:08.2 SATA controller: Intel Corporation 82801HM/HEM (SATA)'. Understand that the card with the highest face-value wins the trick, provided it's in the same suit as the lead card. In a four-player game, continue all gameplay until 13 tricks have been played. After all tricks have been played, teams or players tally up their tricks. If your tricks won exceed the number of tricks bid, give yourself one "sandbag" or "overtrick" point for each extra trick won. Select a clear, zip-close plastic bag for storing your map. Lay the map face down on a table or other flat surface. Fold the top edge of the map down to meet the bottom edge. Lay the plastic bag flat on the folded map, one edge flush with the folded edge of the map. Move the plastic bag so that its edge extends a half-inch past the folded edge of the map. Hold the plastic bag in place with one hand as you fold the top layer of the map up, creasing it along the near edge of the bag. Extract the bag from inside the fold and lay it on top of the new fold, with the edge of the bag overlapping the uppermost fold by a half-inch. Fold the top layer of the map down toward you again, creasing at the far edge of the plastic bag. Extract the plastic bag and set it aside. Fold the uppermost layer of the map up, creasing in line with the crease of the layer directly below. Continue folding the uppermost layer of the map back and forth until it's completely accordion folded. Turn the map over and repeat the accordion-fold process on the other side, using the plastic bag as a guide.

Get over your pre-speech jitters. It may be easier said than done, but a key aspect of all successful presenters is their ability to get past negative feelings prior to the presentation. Plan a script beforehand. Although any creative presenter will leave themselves enough room to improvise, a successful presentation will almost always come with a tightly scripted plan to fall back on. Speak slowly. Offer a conversational style of presentation. Although you'll want to have a clear idea of where you've been and where you're going during your presentation, it's a good idea to ultimately keep your tone of voice casual. Practice. Practice and preparation will be your best aids when it comes to a strong presentation. Use assertive body language. In an in-person presentation, your body is a method of expression like your voice. Dress to suit your presentation. Your audience well gather a lot based on the way you present yourself physically. Include funny images to keep your audience engaged. Even if your audience is interested in the subject itself, chances are they are looking for entertainment as well as information. Create handouts. Handouts offer a visual boost for your audience to hold onto. Move around your stage. In addition to assertive body language, you should make yourself into a moving target for your audience. Begin your presentation with an attention-grabber. An attention-grabber is something that will interest your audience in the project at hand, regardless of their prior experience of the subject. Encourage audience participation. Your audience is a living, breathing entity. Quiz your audience. Survey your audience's opinion. By catching up on what your audience thinks or feels towards a subject partway into the presentation, you offer the possibility of turning your project into an open forum for discussion. Bring food. Be passionate about your project.

First, determine if the wall you want to remove is a load bearing wall, meaning it supports the floor above. If the wall you want to remove is at a right angle to the floor joists - STOP. Look at the wall for electrical outlets, switches, etc. Since demolition will bring up a lot of dust and debris, empty as much from the rooms as possible and cover any doors with plastic sheets to contain dust. If you are relatively sure the wall is void of any obstructions, don't smash into the wall with your foot or a sledgehammer. Once all the drywall has been removed, you can start to remove the wall studs. After all the wall studs are removed, you can remove the floor plate. Once all the debris is removed, you'll have to patch the ceiling where the wall was removed with a strip of drywall and patch the floor with a new piece of flooring. On the ceiling, measure the width of the hole created by removal of the wall. The drywall should be cut almost as wide as the new opening (tape and mud will cover any gaps). Mud the edge of the new drywall and the existing ceiling with drywall compound ('mud'). Allow the mud to dry (check the box/container for drying time required) and sand the drywall mud. Add another layer of mud, using a wider trowel to taper the edges. You may need to do the above steps several times to obtain an almost seamless match between the patch and the existing ceiling. Once you are satisfied with the patch, you can add a coat of drywall primer/sealer and repaint the patch to match the existing ceiling. Depending on the type of flooring, you will need to add a patch to the carpeting, tile or hardwood from the adjoining rooms.

The 12 Steps of Alcoholics Anonymous Admit that you are powerless over your addiction – that your live has become unmanageable. Believe that a power greater than yourself could restore you to sanity. Make a decision to turn your will and your life over to the care of God or your higher power. Make a searching and fearless moral inventory of yourself. Admit to yourself, others, and to God or your higher power the exact nature of your wrongs. Be entirely ready to have God remove all these defects of character. Humble ask God or your higher power to remove your shortcomings. Make a list of all people you have harmed, and become willing to make amends to them all. Make direct amends to those you have harmed wherever possible, except when doing so would injure them or others. Continue to take personal inventory and promptly admit when you are wrong. Seek through prayer and meditation to improve your conscious contact with God or the higher power. Carry this message to addicts and/or alcoholics to practice these principles in all their affairs.

Cut the rabbets Cut the sides of the chest using the marks from step 5 as a guide. Step 7. Join the side and end boards Apply wood glue to the joint and lay the side and end boards together. Step 8. Form the lid and add the lid handles Use the strips you prepared in step 8 to cover the four edges of the chest lid. Glue the strips and form a tight cover. The response of five anesthetized, premature puppies with hypoxic pulmonary hypertension (0.25 ml/kg/min for 90 min; n = 5) was compared with that of five littermate controls (n = 5). The increase in ventilation above control levels was 92.0 +/- 7.4% in the controls and 65.4 +/- 10.4% in the puppies (p = 0.07). The decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance and the increased cardiac output during hypoxia were not significantly different between the groups. Classic car owners tend to take very great care of their vehicles, so the same level of care should be taken to ensure the longevity of the vehicle. This involves taking the time to thoroughly clean the vehicle and preserving the original color and upkeep of the vehicle by not washing it with cleaning products that may damage the original paint and keep it clean with products tailored to the original materials. Car storage can be achieved in a number of ways, but the most important steps are to ensure the car is fully drained of all fluids (with the exception of the fuel tank), leaving any batteries and accessories intact and not blocking any openings or seams with stuffing materials. In addition to draining the fluids, it is important to lubricate the components including the steering, brakes and universal joints. To help the engine and other components "bleed" ensure there is oil in the joints and throughout the system, it is a good idea to let the car sit with the brakes and engine running for at least an hour after draining fluids. This will help generate enough heat to loosen the gummed up metal surfaces. When storing your classic car, it is important to remember it is essentially an old vehicle, and due to the age have the propensity to accumulate moisture. Moisture is particularly dangerous for classic cars as it can cause rust. One effective way to prevent this is to remove as many air leaks from the vehicle as possible, including windows, vents and broken seals. In order to do this safely, ensure there is a way to seal each of these openings, such as with an air bag or plastic bag over openings such as vents. If necessary, fill the empty space with some baking soda which acts as a moisture absorbent. Overall, classic car owners take great care of their vehicles and properly storing the car is an essential part of ensuring its longevity and keeping it in mint condition.

To pull a computer logoff prank, make sure you're an admin (or have admin rights), or else if the victim has a password that you don't know, you can't do this. If the victim has a password and you are an administrator, go to the start menu and click Control Panel. Log off your account and log on to the victim's account. Open their start menu, click All Programs, and scroll down to Start up. Right-click on start up and click open. Right-click anywhere in the window that opens except on a file or folder. Under New, click Text Document. Name it log off.bat, being sure to have the.bat extension rather than.txt. Right-click on your new file and click Edit. On the first line, if you are running Vista, type without quotes, "cd c:\users\<ACCNAME>", replacing <ACCNAME>with your victim's user account name. For the second line on either operating system, type, without quotes, "log off". Save the file. To change it back on Windows Vista, on your user account, go to the start menu and click computer. Alternatively, to change it back, restart Windows and start up in safe mode. Prank successfully pulled! Your victim may have thought their computer had a bug or a virus. Note that in some cases, this prank can cause permissions errors and other problems on the victim's computer. Be sure to test it on a duplicate computer before using it on someone you actually know!

An irrevocable trust can provide for a disabled loved one, protect your assets, and protect your children's inheritance. It can also gain tax advantages and ensure your desired distribution of your assets after you pass on. An irrevocable trust avoids the probate process. A trustee can be appointed to oversee the administration of the trust. A beneficiary can designate who will receive the benefits of the trust at the benefactor's death. Once created, the trust is irrevocable, which means the trust cannot be altered or revoked. This ensures that the trust's intended purposes will be carried out as described in the original creation of the trust. To avoid probate after the benefactor passes away, the trust must be registered with the appropriate state office. The trust must be funded, and the named trustee must apply for a tax identification number for the trust with the Internal Revenue Service. The assets in the trust must be controlled, either directly or through a custodial account, until distribution. Once the distribution is authorized by the creator of the trust, the assets in the trust can be distributed directly to the beneficiaries or to a trust for the benefit of the beneficiaries.

Horses gain fitness through conditioning just as humans do. To assess how fit your horse actually is, you will first need to determine where he falls on a scale of 1 to 10, with 1 being the most unfit and 10 being fit-to-ride. For example, a 1, might have poor color, sunken eyes, slow heart rate, and other substandard physical characteristics. Meanwhile, a 10 might be terribly muscled but have all the physical characteristics of a 1. Then, slot your horse into the appropriate level and work your way up to riding him. For example, if you think your horse is a 5, start by riding him for 5 - 10 minutes each side every other day for a week. Next, increase to 10 - 15 minutes each side for another week. Finally, try riding for 30 minutes straight, and eventually incorporate slopes, walk uphill, and canter. Once you have conditioned your horse to where you are comfortable riding him, you are ready to start timing yourself over distances. To increase the distance you can ride your horse, first take him on trail rides, and then, as he gets fitter, take him on "trail" rides consisting of only slight uphills. Once your horse is consistently trotting for 20 - 30 minutes, incorporate slight downward slopes. To increase the distance of your rides, first work on longer trotting durations, and then introduce cantering. Once your horse is consistently trotting for 30 - 45 minutes, canter for 5 - 10 minutes. Keep conditioning your horse and timing yourself over increasing distances until he is consistently trotting for 60 - 90 minutes, walking for 30 - 45 minutes, and eventually, playing in the mud.

Prepare your area and get everything ready before you start. Ensure you have a very clean hard surface on which to knead the bread, a large bowl, a wooden spoon, warm water, your ingredients and a bowl of warm soapy water to wash your hands. You will need some plain white bread flour, maybe some High Fibre flour, some warm clean water, some salt, possibly sugar (lo cal for diabetics) and some yeast - the small packet type that doesn't require mixing. Place an amount of flour in a large bowl. Add a small packet of yeast per kilo. Add approximately one teaspoon and a bit of salt for each loaf you are making. Sprinkle some sugar over the top. Add the butter or margarine. For a kilo you will need about one cup of boiled water to two cups of cold water to make a tepid mix. Pour two thirds of the liquid in and mix with a wooden spoon. You can add more flour or water until it forms a lump of soft dough. Take the dough out of the bowl and start to knead. Flour the surface you are kneading on and whenever the dough gets sticky, put in more flour until it becomes elastic. After 5 - 10 minutes (according to your strength, press the dough and, if it bounces back, it's ready. Put the dough in the original bowl and cover with a wet tea towel. Turn out the dough and give it a thump - that's very satisfying. Shape into rolls or loaves (approx 3 small loaves for a kilo of flour) and place in a tin covered with the wet cloth again. Allow to rise for half an hour or so. Put some milk over the top with a brush or your fingers and sprinkle with poppy seeds, sesame seeds according to taste. Put in a hot oven - not quite the highest level but almost. After 15 minutes, cover with a bit of aluminium foil and /or move around the oven depending on how brown the bread is getting. Cook for about 30 minutes for loaves and 20 minutes for rolls. Turn out. Leave to cool. Experiment with different combinations of flour. How to Draw What You See Get comfortable. Use a pencil to draw. Don't use an eraser at first. Look carefully at the scene or object you want to draw. Remember the general rule: objects higher up on the plane (closer to the sky) are generally smaller and farther away than objects lower, which are closer to you. You'll notice some artists stick their pencil out in the air between their eye and their subject - this is to measure objects. Sketch the entire scene lightly, keeping the above rules in mind. Don't worry if everything doesn't look right the first time. Don't start drawing a tiny portion of your scene and work on that part for a long time. Once you are happy with the general scene you sketched even though it is not perfect, fill in slightly darker lines. Sketch general shapes; a person's head is an oval, a rock that is resting on the ground should have a flattened bottom, an animal can be drawn with a series of ovals, circles, and hot-dog shapes. If you are drawing geometric shapes like buildings or mechanical objects, you will want a ruler and some templates. Shade what is not completely drenched in light: use soft line, or crisscrosses, or whatever way you feel comfortable making darker areas. Color should be used sparingly with pencil drawings, because the lead is sensitive and will smear easily across the page.

Build a home cinema subwoofer cabinet By following the steps in this article, you will be able to build a subwoofer cabinet for your home cinema entertainment. 1. Determine the size of box you want First you will need to decide how big a box you want. Sound engineering software can help with this, as it can calculate the size of box needed to fit the shape of the speaker you choose. You can also measure your space, and create a box to fit that. A small box will result in more bass, but may be limited by space, and a large box may exceed the noise floor, yielding no bass. You can also figure out the box size by using the free space around your chosen speaker and tuning the size of the box to fit the bandwidth of the speaker. A wide bandwidth speaker will require a larger box. 2. Detail the materials of the cabinet The materials you choose for your cabinet will impact its sound and appearance. You can make your cabinet from particle board or Medium Density Fiber (MDF), both of which are fairly inexpensive and widely available. You can also choose wood for richer sound or aesthetic appeal, although this will be more expensive and harder to find. The thickness of your cabinet will also impact its sound. 18mm or thicker is recommended. Vented design is also recommended, as it will allow air to move within the cabinet, improving the bass response. 3. Determine the size and shape of your subwoofer You can either choose to build your cabinet around an existing subwoofer or buy a subwoofer designed for a specific cabinet. The process of determining the size and shape of your subwoofer is mostly trial and error. You start by listening to your favorite soundtracks with your speaker placement and tuning the frequency to maximum bass response. 4. Design the shape of your cabinet Design your cabinet to fit your room and your choice of material. The box can be triangular, square, rectangular, or any other reasonable shape. The side of the cabinet can also be curved or flat. 5. Assemble your cabinet Using the materials and design you chose in the previous steps, assemble your cabinet. You can use basic tools and basic skills to build this. You can also find plans and pre-built cabinets on the internet to save time. 6. Cut holes for your speaker, the vent, and the amplifier You can choose to cut these holes before assembling your cabinet, or as a final step. Holes should be sized to fit your chosen speaker and bass handling abilities. The hole size and location can also impact the bass response. 7. Add panels to your cabinet You can use wood glue or nails to close your cabinet. Add panels along the sides and bottom of your cabinet. If you opted for a vented design, you can add a vent panel to the top of your cabinet. 8. Add carpet or acoustic wool to dampen room reflections You can also add carpet or acoustic wool to the inside of your cabinet to dampen room reflections. This is especially important if you plan to place your cabinet near a wall. 9. Connect your speaker to your amplifier Connect your speaker to your amplifier using a long "RCA" cable. The cable must have a.1 connection on one end and your speaker's input on the other. 10. Listening and fine-tuning Listen to your music with your speaker in the designed position. Tune the frequency to the maximum bass response. Fine-tune the frequency until the response is consistent and smooth. You can also move the placement of your speaker to find the "sweet spot". 11. Placement and room setup Find your favorite soundtracks and listen to the bass with different speaker placements. This will allow you to setup your listening position and evaluate the effectiveness of your cabinet design. 12. Enjoy your new subwoofer cabinet! You can now enjoy your new subwoofer cabinet! You can place it in your living room, bedroom, or other room in your house for music playback. I hope this has helped you build your own subwoofer cabinet! Like most things in life, building a subwoofer cabinet is an art that takes some practice to get right. Some people find they need to tune their cabinets for several days to a week before they find the "sweet spot". This article aims to provide you with some of the tips and steps you can take to build a good subwoofer cabinet that sounds great. Materials and design are key to a good subwoofer cabinet. Choose your materials carefully, and make sure your cabinet is the correct shape and size for your room, your chosen subwoofer model, and your listening position. The Swedish number system is a base 10 system, similar to that of English. However, in Swedish you must specify how you want the number written, including commas and separators between groups of digits. For example, 95 is written som 95, while 33, written tre tre, is pronunced as trrə trrə. Swedish uses the pronounciation to make formations like 23-53 easier to say, instead of the confusing som 23,53. Learn how to say twenty, thirty, forty et cetera in Swedish., The final -o in trettio - nittio is almost never pronounced., Practice. Many numbers up to 99 can be said by using combinations of number words and ordinals. For example, 95 can be said som 95, or trittio, or some people pronunce it as trrə 95. Most numbers from 100 to 499 can be said using combinations of fyrtio, fem, sex, sju, åtta, and ordinals. Some numbers from 500 to 999 can be said using combinations of 500, femton, tretton, arton, nitton, and ordinals. Bigger numbers can be constructed by combining numbers and ordinals with the summations symbol (+). 95+45 can be said som 95+45, or trittio + nittio, or some people pronunce it as trrə 95+45. 3000 can be said som 3000, or träd 3000, or some people pronunce it as trrə trrə 3000, or som 3000, or träd 3000. 40000 can be said som 40000, or som + sexton, or som + tretton, or som + fjorton, or som 40000. Add distilled water to the test chamber and set the test chamber down and wait for a minute or two until the soil settles back to the bottom and the watercolor changes. Collect samples for nutrient levels at the same depth as those for pH. Pour 5 cups of distilled water into the container with the soil. Use a dropper to fill the test chambers and reference chambers in the container provided with the kit with the test sample water. Put the test chemical into the water. Seal the test chamber tightly and shake it vigorously. Do a separate test for nitrogen, phosphorus and potash. Pick out your fertilizer. Remove the top 2 inches of soil at the test site with a dirt shovel. Wear rubber gloves to avoid altering the soil pH with your skin. Turn the analyzer on. Twist the probe back and forth in the mud a few times to insure good contact with the soil. Consider purchasing a digital soil analyzer.
