Learning how to crochet a pair of fitted hand warmers can be a great way to utilize your skills in a practical way. Hand warmers are a useful project to make any winter season much more tolerable. Although crocheting straight tubes in a single color can be somewhat basic, learning how to create a product that will fit properly and have some style of your own personal touch can be a bit of a challenge. However, with a bit of patience and knowledge of a few techniques, you can achieve a great pair of fitted hand warmers that will last you a long time. 

The first thing you'll need to do before you begin is make sure you have the right equipment. You will need a crochet hook – the size will be determined by the size of the yarn you choose – and any yarn of your choice. We recommend a worsted-weight or chunky-weight yarn for this project. You will also need a tapestry needle to weave in your ends and a pair of scissors to cut the yarn when necessary. 

To get started, you will need to make a sample piece of fabric so that you can measure your work and make sure it fits correctly. With your chosen yarn and your crochet hook, make a row of single crochet stitches. Locating the number of stitches needed for this sample fabric can be tricky, so be sure to count each one and write them down. If done correctly, this piece of fabric should end up roughly twice as wide as it is long. When you are done, measure it against the person for whom the hand warmers are being made (this step can be skipped if you plan on making a pair for yourself). 

Once your sample piece is complete, you can determine how much fabric you will need for the cuff of the hand warmers. Measure the wrist or arm of the person for whom the hand warmers are being made and determine the number of single crochet stitches that will provide the width of the fabric to wrap your cuff around it. Make sure to add a few extra stitches in order to provide some degree of comfort when wearing the hand warmers. Chain three stitches at the end of the row as a turning chain and single crochet back across, beginning in the third chain from the hook. 

Continue working back and forth for the desired length of the cuff. Once you have completed enough rows to fit comfortably around the wrist, join the two ends together. Be sure to account for the thickness of the arm or wrist and add more rows if necessary. 

Once the cuff piece is complete, you will need to measure it against your arm or wrist again and adjust the edges as necessary. With this done, you can begin to work around the piece in single crochet rounds. Keep in mind that the more you increase and decrease, the better fit your hand warmers will have. 

A few rows in, mark the place where your thumb begins by adding a stitch marker. This will help you later on in the process when you need to distinguish between the fingers and the thumb base. Just below this same marked stitch is where you will make a second division; this will create the opening for your pinkie finger. Now, continue to single crochet around in rounds until you reach the marked stitch again. 

To create the ‘fingers’, single crochet only into the opening that goes around your fingers. This will provide a nice snug fit that will also trap warmth next to your skin. It is important to try the glove on a few times and add or remove stitches from the chain if it feels much too tight or too loose. 

For some open-fingered styles, you may chose to stop crocheting around in a tube just under the knuckles. Doing so will decrease the length of the hand warmers and allow more freedom for the fingers. On the opposite end of the spectrum, you could also choose to go just above the knuckles for the fullest possible length. 

Crocheting these fitted hand warmers is a great starting point for learning the basics of garment-making in crochet. With patience and practice, you can create a great pair of hand warmers that will fit comfortably and keep you warm in any cold weather.

How to Make a Fidget Quilt
Making a fidget quilt is an easy and fun project that is sure to provide a sense of calm and accomplishment when you’re finished. Fidget quilts are used to help those with autism, down syndrome, and attention-deficit disorder focus and relax. Here is an easy step-by-step guide to make your own fidget quilt.

First, make a template of any size. Next, cut 3 squares of the same color of fabric and repeat two more times with each fabric color. Then, sew the squares together into strips. Sew the strips together using a 1/4 inch seam and remember to iron your top, making sure all the seams are ironed the same direction and laying flat. 

Once that is finished, you’ll need to purchase several different yarns and ribbons. Cut all your ribbons and yarn to the same length and pull them through a ring and fold it in half. Use a sturdy piece of string or yarn to tie everything together at the top. Now it’s time to start the yo-yo process. Cut circles of any size out of fabric and hand-sew around the outer edge of the fabric. Once that’s complete, remove your needle and pull on both ends of the thread. Use glue to add a big bright button to the center of each yo-yo. 

Now that the yo-yos are complete, it’s time to add velcro. Add velcro using some glue, then sew the other side of the velcro down. This will help you easily attach your fidget elements to your quilt. Next, add a fleece teddy bear to your quilt. Decide on which fidgets you want to use and pin all your fidgets on the top of the quilt. Sew the fidgets onto the quilt and make sure the ribbons are reinforced so they cannot be pulled off. 

To finish, pick up the back fabric and cut the batting. Lay the finished top quilt on top of the batting and cut it a 1/4" bigger on each of the sides. Lay the batting on top of the back fabric and cut the back 1/2" bigger on each side of the batting so you can fold it over and pin it to the quilt top. Pin the top, batting, and back fabric together. Fold the backing fabric up 1/4" so there are no raw edges and fold it once more. Pin the corners by bringing them to a point and folding them in. Begin quilting it all together by sewing the border first. Quilt the 3 pieces together by using a straight stitch and you have a finished fidget quilt.

How to Synchronize Multiple Cameras to a Video Switcher

Having multiple cameras ready to switch to whatever scene is being shot is essential for any video production. But before that can happen, they must be properly synchronized to the switcher. This tutorial will outline the steps needed to synchronize multiple cameras to a video switcher, be it an analog or digital unit.  

There are two main types of switchers: those that need to be "genlocked" with other video sources to ensure synchronization, and those that don't. Before attempting to synchronize multiple cameras to a switcher, check with the owner's manual to identify the type of switcher you're working with.

The cameras that will be used to feed the switcher must also be of a type that can be genlocked. Consult the owner's manual for the cameras to ensure they can synchronize properly with the switcher.

To synchronize cameras to a switcher, you'll need a set of BNC cables, which are used for transmitting analog or digital video signals. Depending on the number of cameras you're using, you'll need to acquire enough cables for the job. Once you have the correct amount of available cables, it's recommended to use tape to label one cable as "REF" on both ends, and the other cable "VID" on both ends. This will help you easily recognize the cables and keep them organized when plugging them in. 

Start by connecting the BNC cables labeled "REF" to any BNC connector at the back of the switcher (or Video Distribution Amplifier, or VDA). At the cameras, connect the BNC cable to the "REF IN" or the "GEN IN" connector. This serves as the reference signal for the cameras to synchronize with the master heartbeat or genlock video signal.

Find the "PROGRAM OUT" on the back of the switcher and use a BNC cable to hook it up to a color monitor. This will enable you to view any video sent via the switcher, as well as any reference signal sent from the cameras. Find the switch on each camera (or the Camera Control Units, or CCUs) and turn on the camera's internal color bars.

An engineer may use a waveform monitor and vectorscope to accurately time the system. However, if you do not have access to an engineer, but are still trying to synchronize the system, then the following procedure is recommended.

Start by setting up a "horizontal wipe" on the system, which is used to determine the timing of the cameras. On the PREVIEW bus, punch up switcher COLOR BARS, if the switcher has built in color bars. Monitor this on the color monitor. Then on Camera 1, find the adjustment for "H-PHASE," which will enable you to adjust the horizontal timing of the camera. Tweak this until the camera bars line up vertically with the switcher bars. Repeat this procedure with Camera 2. Once the cameras are horizontally timed, both cameras must be adjusted to get the colors in sync. Find the S/C PHASE (sub-carrier phase) adjustment on the first camera and set it up according to the instructions. Monitor for any camera jumps or tears while pushing the switcher buttons and sliding the T-bar. If all looks good, try adjusting the S/C on the second camera. The colors should match with the switcher bars and more importantly, with each other.

When the colors match, and there are no camera jumps, you've successfully synchronized multiple cameras to a video switcher! From there, you can switch back from bars to the actual cameras. All that's left to do then is to start shooting!

How to Heal After ACL Surgery
Healing after an ACL ( anterior cruciate ligament ) surgery can be a long process full of ups and downs. You may start to feel better soon after surgery and your recovery could progress at a steady pace, or you may experience setbacks or complications that may cause the healing process to take longer. It is important to talk closely with your doctor and therapist as you progress through your recovery in order to ensure a successful outcome.  

Talk to your doctor about necessary medications. After surgery, your doctor may prescribe medications like nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or opioids to reduce pain and inflammation. Work closely with your doctor to determine the best type and dosage so that you can avoid side effects and be able to manage your pain effectively. 

Ask about other medications and supplements. There are some supplements or medications that may help with inflammation or pain relief. Your doctor can guide you to the right options for your situation, as well as provide more information about how the medication works and potential side effects. 

Monitor your side effects. Make sure to pay attention to the side effects of any medications you are prescribed. Some common side effects can include nausea, dizziness, and drowsiness. If you experience any of these, discuss them with your doctor as soon as possible. 

Be responsible. Do not take more medication than is prescribed or recommended. This can be dangerous and could lead to serious medical complications.

Watch for a fever. Any temperature over 101.5°F can be a sign of infection, so make sure to take your temperature if you are feeling unwell. Keep in touch with your doctor if you experience any other signs of fever. 

Take excessive pain or swelling seriously. If the pain you are experiencing is persistent or if you notice any swelling, let your doctor know. They will be able to advise you on the best course of action and give you the treatment you need. 

Look for increased bleeding or redness around your incision. Signs of infection include redness, swelling, warmth, oozing, and increased pain. If you have any of these symptoms, contact your doctor or seek medical care.

Call your doctor if you notice purulent or foul-smelling discharge coming from your incision. This could be a sign of infection and should be evaluated. 

Talk to your doctor about the pros and cons of cold therapy. Immediately after your surgery, your doctor may advise that you use cold therapy to reduce pain and swelling. Discuss the benefits and potential risks before deciding if this is the right option for you.

Follow your doctor’s instructions. It is important to follow the instructions given to you by your doctor in order to ensure your successful recovery. Make sure to keep all appointments, take medications as prescribed, and follow all aftercare instructions. 

Apply cold therapy outside your surgical dressing. It is important to make sure that you are taking the right steps when using cold therapy. Apply the cold pack or gel pack outside your bandage or surgical dressing rather than directly on your skin. If you notice any signs of skin irritation or discomfort, stop the cold therapy and contact your doctor. 

Start with clear liquids. After an ACL surgery, your doctor may advise you to start off with very light, clear liquids like broth or transparent juice in order to help promote healing. Speak to your doctor about other dietary recommendations and what types of foods you should start to incorporate back into your diet. 

Get plenty of omega-3 fatty acids. foods rich in omega-3 fatty acids can help reduce inflammation and swelling. Examples of such foods are fatty fish, flaxseeds, walnuts, and olive oil. 

Increase your intake of vitamins C and E. Vitamins C and E are antioxidants, which can protect against tissue damage. Some of the best sources of these vitamins are citrus fruits, green leafy vegetables, nuts, and berry fruits.

Elevate your leg. Lie down or prop your leg up after surgery in order to reduce swelling and to help with the healing process. Make sure to follow your doctor’s instructions on the best way to do this. 

Use crutches. Crutches can help you to remain mobile and will help prevent you from putting too much pressure on your leg. Speak to your doctor or physical therapist about the right crutches for you, and how you should use them. 

Stick to showering. In order to reduce the risk of infection, it is important to keep your wound dry until it has fully healed. Your doctor may advise you to take a shower instead of a bath, and to avoid swimming until your leg has healed. 

Discuss your return to work or school with your doctor. Depending on the intensity of the surgery, you may not be able to return to work or school for several weeks. Get advice from your doctor about when you can return and which activities you should avoid in the meantime. 

Avoid strenuous activity outside of physical therapy. While physical therapy is essential to your recovery, it is important to avoid any strenuous or high-impact activities until your doctor has given the green light. 

Use caution when beginning to drive again. After your surgery, it may take weeks or sometimes months before you can get back behind the wheel. Listen to your doctor or therapist before taking any risks. 

Perform post-operative exercises with care. Your doctor and physical therapist will advise you on the best exercises to help your recovery. Follow any instructions or advice they provide carefully and gradually increase the intensity of the exercises over time. 

Return to sports only when your doctor approves. Your doctor will provide you with specific guidelines about when it is the right time for you to return to your favorite sport. Do not rush back into high-intensity activities before you are fully healed or your risk of re-injury is much higher. 

Healing after an ACL surgery is a process that can take many months, and each step must be taken with extreme care in order to get the best possible recovery. Talk closely with your doctor, physical therapist, and other healthcare professionals about any questions or concerns you may have. Listen to their advice and be diligent with your post-operative plan in order to ensure a successful outcome.

Wearing ankle boots with dresses can be a surprisingly versatile look. Whether you're going for a casual boho feel or aiming for a dressier look, ankle boots are a great way to give your dress an edgier feel. Here are some tips to help you choose the perfect pair to go with your dress.

Pick boots in neutral colors so that you can wear them with more outfits. Neutral colors like black, tan, beige, and dark brown can easily be matched to any dress. The beauty of this is that you can mix and match your outfits without having to find a new pair of boots for each one. However, you can also choose boots in bolder colors to add a pop to your look. 

Go for boots with a heel if you'd like to make your legs appear longer. Low or mid-heel boots are a great choice, but if you're feeling daring, you can always opt for a stiletto heel. However, if comfort is your priority, you might want to look for boots with a block heel.

Wear boots made from a matte material if you have large feet. Materials like suede, nubuck and leather can make your feet appear larger than they are, so opt for a matte material like canvas or cotton. This will help downplay the size of your feet and make them look more proportional.

Go for boots with a wider cuff if you want your legs to appear slimmer. You may also want to pick boots in a light shade, as darker shades tend to make the ankles look bigger. Wider cuffs can help make your ankles appear slimmer and longer, thus helping you achieve a flattering look.

Consider boots with rounded toes and a shorter heel if you will be on your feet a lot. Pointed toes can look great, but they're not the most comfortable when you're on your feet for extended periods of time. A shorter heel will also help to alleviate any pressure on your feet that a higher heel would create.

Consider boots with pointed toes and a higher heel for special occasions. These types of boots can be a great way to dress up any outfit. Pointed toes elongate the legs, while the higher heel can help you to feel more confident. 

Choose boots that flatter your body shape. Everyone's body shape is different, so choosing boots that will enhance your figure is essential. For example, if you are petite and curvy, choose boots with a pointed toe and a low heel. 

Choose boots that flatter your body type and make your legs appear longer. If you're going for a dressy look, consider opting for boots with a higher heel. Depending on the type of dress you're wearing, you may also want to look for boots that come up to just above your ankles.

If you are petite and curvy, choose boots with a pointed toe. Pointed toes can help give the illusion of a longer line, which can be beneficial for petite women. Heels also come in handy for creating the same effect.

Consider dresses that end above the knee for the most flattering look. These types of dresses will help to emphasize the length of your legs. You may also want to opt for a dress with an A-Line skirt to create the illusion of a more slender figure.

Wear longer and maxi-length dresses with care. For a balanced look, choose boots that come up just past your ankles. Otherwise, you risk cutting off your legs at the shaft. You may also want to look for a dress that flares out a bit to give the appearance of length.

Consider a simple dress if you plan on wearing lots of accessories. Accessories like jewelry, belts, scarves, and hats can detract from the overall look if the dress is too busy. So if you plan on wearing lots of accessories, it's best to pick a dress that is relatively simple. 

Avoid wearing sleek, sheath dresses with boots that are too chunky. If the boots are too chunky, they can overpower the sleek look of the sheath dress. You'll want to find a happy medium between the two to avoid looking top-heavy.

Mix and match boots and dresses with care. When it comes to pairing boots and dresses, you'll want to consider the theme of the outfit. For a more boho look, try pairing a flowing dress made from cotton or linen with a wide, leather belt over it. Or if you're trying to achieve a dressier look, try wearing a sleek dress with pointed toe boots and a pair of elegant earrings.

Incorporate your boots' style into your accessories, but be sure to match your dress. Shoes are often the anchor of an outfit, so you'll want to make sure your accessories and dress work with the style of your boots. If your boots are heavily embellished, tone down the accessories, but if they're relatively simple, you can pepper in some brighter pieces.

Play around with layering by adding a jacket. Layering can add depth to your outfit and help to highlight the features of both the boots and the dress. Depending on the weather, you may want to try a lightweight trench coat or a tailored blazer. 

Tone down the accessories if your boots are heavily embellished. You don't want your accessories to compete with your boots, so keep them to a minimum. A simple pair of earrings, bracelet, and necklace can add just enough sparkle to your outfit without being overwhelming. 

Spice up the accessories if your boots and dress are simple. Here is where you can show off your personal style. Try accessorizing with a patterned scarf or bold statement necklace. It will help to emphasize the look without taking away from it.

Try some patterned tights if your dress and boots are simple. Patterned tights can help to spice up even the most basic of outfits. A pair of leopard print tights can add a playful touch to your look, or a thin pair of polka dot tights can brighten up an otherwise dull outfit.

Add a belt to make your waist look slimmer. A belt can help to draw attention to the smallest part of your body, making it appear slimmer and more trench. Choose a belt that begins above your natural waist and cinches below it for the most flattering look.

The state of your hair is important to how you feel about yourself, but it can be difficult to feel confident if your hair is dry. Dry hair is caused by a variety of factors like environmental stressors, using the wrong products, or the wrong amount of shampoo. If you’re looking to restore softness and hydration, here’s how to deal with dry hair.

First, make sure that you’re conditioning your hair every time that you shower. Conditioner helps to lock in the moisture that’s been lost due to heat, exposure to weather or other elements. Additionally, apply a leave-in conditioner to your hair after you’ve showered. These can help you retain the strength and shine of your hair, while preventing split ends or other damages.

Alongside your daily routine, once or twice a week, you should apply an intensive moisturizing mask to your hair. Many masks can be purchased from the store, but you can also make an easy mask using natural ingredients from your kitchen. For a deep conditioning treatment, you can combine warm honey—an excellent humectant—with a few drops of your favorite oil to restore shine. Alternatively, apply a mashed up avocado, banana, or even egg whites straight to your hair and let it sit for 30 minutes before rinsing.

Sometimes shampoo can leave your hair dry and brittle. Over-shampooing (more than two or three times a week) can strip away protective oils and weaken your hair, leaving it vulnerable to breakage. If you’re using a shampoo with high sulphates levels, that could be contributing to the problem as well. Try switching to a low-sulphate or sulfate-free shampoo, and once in a while, do a no-poo—using common household items like baking soda and apple cider vinegar to cleanse your scalp while restoring natural resilience and strength.

Finally, be careful with any heat-intensive hair styling. Heat styling like blow drying or flat-ironing can strip your hair of its natural oils, so use a heat protectant and limit these techniques to essential times. 

With the right care and routine, you can restore the softness and shine of your hair and reduce the amount of dryness. Use these tips to maintain your hair’s moisture levels and keep yourself feeling confident and comfortable.

The thought of writing a letter to prove your income may make you feel a bit overwhelmed. After all, it's important to make sure the letter is accurate and up-to-date. One small mistake could lead to major problems down the road. Taking the time to trim down the contents to legitimate forms of income is something you need to do in order to succeed. Here's what you need to know about writing a letter of proof of income.

Begin by listing your contact information at the top of the page. This should include your name, address, telephone number, and email address.

Explain the purpose of the letter in a few words. In this case, you want to clearly state that the letter is written as proof of your income.

Begin the actual letter with a polite greeting followed by the proper name of the recipient. Give a brief introduction of yourself and your current position.

Introduce yourself and explain why you are submitting the income verification letter. You need to make sure you explain the reasons for your request and provide any pertinent documents for the request.

Provide details about your basic income. This should include your salary, wages, commission, and any bonus you may have received. Note the length of your employment and if there have been any changes in employment since then.

Mention any additional income you have, in addition to your basic employment. This could include freelance income, side hustle income, investments, or any other income that is not related to your employment.

Finish this section by summarizing your total income and suggesting how it will be sustained or increase in the future. Give an accurate assessment of your current financial situation and how secure you feel it is.

Include a note at the end signaling that there is additional paperwork included with your letter. This paperwork will be used to back up the information that was included in the letter.

Thank the reader for their time and consideration. This is a courteous gesture that goes a long way in ensuring that the letter is not taken lightly.

Type "Enclosure" under your name. This enclosure will include all of the items that are to be included in your proof of income letter.

Include a disclaimer such as, "all of the information above is true to the best of my knowledge." This makes it clear that you have taken responsibility for all of the information you have provided.

Sign the letter by hand, if you are sending a printed copy. This shows that the letter is a valid document and that it is being signed by the person it is intended for.

Have your income letter notarized by an official notary public. This will ensure that the letter has been properly concluded and is more likely to be given serious consideration.

Enclose copies of check stubs as income documentation. This will prove your regular income and will help to give the recipient an accurate picture of your earning history.

Enclose copies of tax returns as income documentation. This will help to prove employment income as well as other types of income that are not logged in other documents.

Provide documentation for other types of income. This could include investment income or income from a side job, such as tutoring or other freelance work.

Overall, it is important to take your time when writing a letter of proof of income. Accurate documentation is essential to the success of the letter and the recipient's consideration of it. Carefully follow the steps outlined above to ensure that your letter is as accurate as possible. This will help you to provide proof of income and help you get the financial assistance you need.

Making Green Bay Packer Jello Shots is a fun and easy way to wow your friends when hosting Packers parties or tailgates. To make these delicious concoctions, you’ll need access to gelatin mixes in different colors, condensed milk, vodka, edible icing, cupcake paper cases and a muffin pan. Here’s what you need to do to make these fun and tasty Packers themed treats.

First, you need to assemble the items needed for these jello shots. You can use any flavor of gelatin mix you would like, however, for this Packers themed jello shot, you should use green and yellow for the two jello layers. You’ll need 3 packets of each mix, 1/2 cup of water, 1/2 cup of vodka, one can of condensed milk.

Next, take the muffin pan and spray each hole lightly with cooking oil. Place the pan in the refrigerator to get cold while you work on the jello mixes. Follow the “fast set” instructions for each jello mix. Pour 1/2 cup of water into a bowl, then add the gelatin mix to it. Pour the bowl of water and gelatin into a saucepan and place it on low heat. Stir until the gelatin is all dissolved, then remove from heat. Then, pour in 1/2 cup of vodka to the green jello mix and stir.

Once this is done, remove the refrigerated muffin pan and pour the green jello mixture into each hole. Fill every hole about 1/3 full. Next, pour the condensed milk into a bowl. In a separate container, pour 3 cups of water. Sprinkle the 4 packets of green gelatin over the top of the water in a pie plate, then pour the water and gelatin mixture into a saucepan. Stir to help dissolve the gelatin completely, and then remove from heat.

After the green jello layer has set, pour the condensed milk into the clear jello mixture. To this, pour in 1 cup of vodka and stir thoroughly. Then, remove the pan from the fridge and pour the condensed milk mixture over the top of the green layer. Fill each hole to about 2/3 high. Repeat the steps 3-5 for the yellow jello layer. No need to put vodka in this layer.

Once the holes are all filled, print out the Packers’ logo using edible icing or paper and allow the designs to dry. Then, trim each design to shape. Now that the yellow layer has completely set, it’s time to remove the jello shots from the muffin pan trays. Place the cupcake paper cases onto a large serving plate and arrange each jello shot to sit on a flat cupcake paper case, with the widest end down on the plate and the narrowest end at the top.

Finally, add each edible design to the shots just prior to serving, once they’re neatly arranged on the plate. Your Green Bay Packer Jello Shots are now ready to be served! These easy to make jello shots will be a hit, no matter the occasion. All Packers fans will love the combination of the green and yellow colors, along with the iconic Packers logo. With just a few simple steps, you can make these tasty and unique jello shots that will be the talk of any gathering.

If you're looking for a way to add a unique touch to your home or garden, an aquaponics system is the perfect addition. Aquaponics combines fish farming with hydroponics – a method of growing plants without any soil. Not only is it visually stunning, but an indoor aquaponics system is also functional, providing you with fresh fish and vegetables all year around! Here's how to build an indoor aquaponics system.

First, you'll need to visit IKEA to pick up the necessary materials for the setup. Look for a storage chest that is the same width as your fish tank, as this will become the frame for your aquaponics system. You'll also need a wire basket, a 25 liter (6.6 US gal) plastic container, some threaded adapters, and a bell siphon and media guard kit. If you'd like, you can customize the aquaponics system to compliment your home décor. 

Once you've bought all of the materials, you'll need to assemble the frame. The wire basket should fit snugly at the top of the frame for support. Then, the 25 liter plastic container can be placed over the wire basket. It will come in handy as the growbed of your aquaponics system. 

Next, make sure that the pump is set up correctly. An electric submersible pump with a 600 lph (litres per hour) rate is ideal for an indoor system. Place the pump in one corner of the fish tank and make sure you get the right piping and tubing to connect the pump to the growbed container. 

The threaded adapters must be set up properly too, so they can form a watertight seal. The male adapter should go the top of the growbed and the female adapter should be on the pump. You can find the correct size adapters in your bell siphon kit. 

Finally, you can attach the bell siphon and media guard to the growbed. Place the 60mm bell siphon in the middle of the tank, then add the 100mm media guard as shown in the picture. This will help to keep the growbed media from going into the bell siphon.

Once all the components have been set up, the next step is to install the ball-valve-by-pass. This will help to maintain a better balance of water in the growbed and ensure a smooth flow of water throughout the aquaponics system.

After this, all that's left to do is fill the containers with water and start the pump up. Place water in the fish tank first, then fill the top container (which should already have the growing media in it) with water too. Finally, you'll be able to add the fish and plants to your system and get it up and running. You may need to do some read up on the basics of aquaponics before setting up your system to ensure you make the most of your indoor aquaponics system. 

The whole setup should take less than an hour, and you should be able to enjoy all the beauty of an aquaponics system in the comfort of your own home. Not only that but you'll be able to appreciate the added benefits of fresh fish and vegetables all year round! With just a bit of knowledge and some simple materials, you'll be enjoying your indoor aquaponics system in no time!

Protecting your baby from the flu does not have to be an overwhelming task. With proper knowledge and a few simple measures, you can be sure that your little one is safe and healthy all year round. 

Getting a flu shot is the first and most important step when it comes to protecting a baby from the flu. Babies can start receiving a flu shot as early as six months of age; it is recommended that they get one every year to ensure protection. As for the parents, it is just as important to get vaccinated. Getting a flu shot is the best way to reduce the chances of transmitting the virus to your baby. 

When it comes to keeping germs out of the house, a policy of “no sick guests” is ideal. This is especially important when the baby is under six months of age, as they are most vulnerable to infections early on. 

Breastfeeding exclusively for the first six months of life is also recommended to give babies all the nutrients and antibodies they need to build a strong immune system. This also helps to protect them from the flu, even more so than formula feeding. 

In addition to breast milk, keeping your baby isolated in the first two months of life also helps to protect them. In that time, they will not have received their full complement of vaccinations yet, and their bodies are not as well-equipped to fight off infection. 

Finally, if you do notice any signs of illness in your baby, it is important to consult your doctor. It is better to be safe than sorry when it comes to the health of your little one. 

Overall, protecting your baby from the flu does not have to be difficult if the right measures are taken. Be sure to get your baby vaccinated at six months of age and be sure you and all family members receive a flu shot as well. Avoiding contact with anyone who is sick is also critical, in addition to breastfeeding exclusively and minimizing exposure for the first two months of life. Of course, if you notice any signs of illness, make sure to consult your doctor as soon as possible.

How to Prepare for a Trip to Japan
Travelling to Japan can be a daunting task – from the language to the customs to the culture – but with the right preparation, your trip can go as smoothly as possible. Here are some things to consider when planning a trip to Japan. 

Study basic Japanese phrases. Before going to Japan, it can be beneficial to learn some basic Japanese phrases to help you get around. While English is more widely spoken in the larger cities, it might be helpful to understand simple Japanese phrases like please (kudasai), thank you (arigatô), and hello (kon'nichiwa).

Order a bilingual map. A bilingual map will help you get around Japan and find specific locations. Many cities have bilingual maps available and some specialty stores carry bilingual maps from the mountain ranges to the islands.

Obtain a kanji dictionary. Kanji is the written language of Japanese and it is essential to learn a few basic symbols in order to navigate. You can buy kanji dictionaries or print out a few online.

Print important addresses in Japanese. For destinations you plan on visiting, print out the addresses in Japanese to help you and potential guides recognize where you are trying to go. Every single prefecture in Japan has websites devoted to providing information in both English as well as Japanese. 

Print out a card with your medical information. If you have allergies or a medical condition, print out a card in English and Japanese to inform those around you of your needs. This can be a necessary precaution in case of an emergency.

Verify all prescriptions with the Japanese embassy. Many countries have laws or restrictions on medications, so contact the Japanese embassy about any medications you may need to bring.

Inform restaurants of your dietary restrictions. Japan is known for its seafood, so inform restaurants catering to vegetarians, vegans, or those who do not eat fish that you are in Japan.

Practice bowing. Bowing is a sign of respect and politeness in Japan, so it is important to practice before you leave. Bow when introduced to people, when exiting a conversation, or when thanking someone.

Get your documentation in order. Make sure you have your passport, confirmed tickets, and any other necessary documents before travelling to Japan. 

Purchase travel insurance. In case of an emergency, have some form of travel insurance to help you pay for an unexpected medical bill or emergency flight.

Invest in a Japan Rail pass if you plan on traveling the country. The Japan Rail pass is an economical way to travel throughout the country on trains.

Consider domestic flights. Domestic flights can take you to places the train can’t, and often at a much lower cost and travel time. Investigate which airlines offer domestic flights in Japan before you leave.

Accustom yourself to subway maps. Since Tokyo has the most extensive subway system in Japan, look into getting a map of the train lines.

Familiarize yourself with bus services. For destinations that are not easily accessible by train, buses may be available. Check the cities that you’re travelling to and look for a list of services that buses offer.

Learn about taxis. Some cities in Japan offer flat-rate taxi services. The cost may vary depending on the city, so make sure to check the fare charts. 

Investigate car rentals. If you plan on exploring the country, you can rent an automobile with an international driver’s license.

Find locations to exchange money. Look into places that exchange currency and compare different rates. Find a few places you can easily access when in Japan.

Consult your bank over ATM card policies. Before going to Japan, look into what bank’s ATM machines accept your card and what fees you may incur when using it. 

Locate ATMs that you can use. Look up banks that have ATMs that accept your card and look into whether they are close to any of your destinations.

Bring money to exchange for a prepaid card. If you plan to take the train, it can be helpful to research prepaid cards that you can use instead of cash. Many prepaid cards accept deposits in foreign currency.

Book your room months in advance. While some more luxurious accommodations require more advanced bookings, there are standard places that can be booked fairly quickly.

Check into ryokans. If you want a unique experience in Japan, you can book a room in a traditional Japanese inn, known as a ryokan.

Look into western-style hotels. If a ryokan isn’t for you, there are plenty of standard hotels throughout Japan that may be suitable for your needs.

Consider Japanese guest houses. Japanese guest houses are a blend between a western-style hotel and a ryokan. Depending on personal preference, these guest houses allow for some of the conveniences of a hotel along with the traditional aspects of a ryokan.

Search for houses or apartments. If you plan on spending an extended period of time in Japan, you can look for traditional homes or apartments to rent.

Also check out hostels. For travelers on a budget, many cities in Japan have hostels that are great for meeting other travelers and interacting with the locals.

Speak with a travel agency. To help organize your trip, contact a travel agency that specializes in Japan or use a generic travel agency to help arrange for guides, hotels, etc.

Bring formal clothing. Depending on the time of year, some cities may require formal clothing for special events or occasions. Make sure you bring appropriate attire for the areas you’re visiting.

Choose clothing with standard colors. While some western clothing is acceptable in Japan, you may want to avoid loud colors and prints that could be disruptive.

Pack warm clothes for cold months. Depending on the time of year, temperatures can dip to harsh lows in some parts of Japan. Make sure you are prepared for the colder months when planning a trip to Japan.

Pack a raincoat. Japan is known for its frequent rain showers, so make sure to bring a raincoat and possibly waterproof shoes.

Pack light clothing for the summer months. For those sunny summer days, make sure to bring light clothing that can help keep you cool.

Pack a bathing suit, if necessary. If you plan on visiting hot springs or public beaches, bring a bathing suit.

Bring shoes that are easy to slip off. Traditional Japanese homes require the removal of footwear before entering – make sure you bring shoes that can be slipped off easily. 

Stockpile extra medication. Make sure you have adequate medication – especially if you require medication with a specific schedule.

Buy an electric cord converter. Japan’s electrical outlets are geared for angled flat-pin plugs, so make sure you buy a converter for your devices.

Bring a towel and hand sanitizer. Since many public toilets do not provide toilet paper, it is handy to bring a few tissues as well as a hand towel. Since you will be using a lot of public transportation, it is also useful to have hand sanitizer within reach.

Rent a portable Wi-Fi hotspot or SIM card. Connections can be patchy at times, so it can be beneficial to rent a portable Wi-Fi hotspot or SIM card for a constant connection.

Get a SIM card. Many stores in Japan sell SIM cards for use on mobiles. Make sure to shop around for cards that don’t have an excess of data, as some come with large data packages.

Consult your mobile phone carrier about data charges. Before travelling to Japan, discuss with your carrier what kind of fees you may incur while using data abroad. 

Make a list of locations that have free Wi-Fi hotspots. If you are using a phone, make a list of cafes or libraries that may have free Wi-Fi hotspots so you can stay connected to the web.

Determine where you’d like to go. You can research destinations online, buy travel guides, or speak with a travel agency to determine the best places to visit. 

Work out your budget. Before planning a trip to Japan, calculate a reasonable budget and use it as a guideline when planning accommodations and activities.

Search for tours and tour guides. Tours can help you explore Japan in a limited amount of time, so make sure to look into local tours and guides. 

Search for appropriate restaurants. Depending on where you are in Japan, the cuisine will change drastically, so research into local restaurants or have a guide take you to more traditional eateries.

Research shipping. Before buying souvenirs or gifts in Japan, make sure you are aware of the shipping policies for larger items as some airports may have restrictions for bulky items.

How to Get Rid of a Sore Throat Fast and Naturally
Sore throats can be quite painful, and interfere with your ability to eat, talk, or sleep. It’s important to recognize the signs of a sore throat and take actions to quickly reduce the pain and get rid of the problem. Here are some of the best ways to get rid of a sore throat fast and naturally.

Recognize the symptoms of a sore throat. The most persistent symptom of a sore throat is throat pain that may get worse when swallowing or talking. Other signs might include mild fever, runny nose, swollen lymph nodes in the neck, and bumps or white spots on the tonsils.

Look for other signs of infection. Most sore throats are the result of viral and bacterial infections. If you also have a stuffy or runny nose, watery eyes, or cough, it’s likely you have a cold. It’s also possible to have an infection caused by a bacteria, which may require medical treatment. 

Consider getting a medical diagnosis. Most sore throats will go away within a few days to a week with simple home treatment. However, if you develop difficulty swallowing or breathing, swelling in the neck, fever higher than 101F (38.3C), or a rash, you should get immediate medical attention.

Drink plenty of water. Though it’s hard to swallow when your throat is sore and raw, it’s still incredibly important to stay hydrated. Drink it at room temperature to avoid further irritating your throat. 

Humidify the air. Dry air will only make your sore throat worse with every breath you take. To keep the air in your home or office more balanced, use a humidifier or keep a few bowls of water around.

Drink lots of soups and broths. The old tales of treating colds with chicken soup are true! Soups and broths will offer up not just calories, but also much-needed moisture and relief to soothe the throat.

Chew your food well. Cut it into smaller pieces with a fork and knife before putting it in your mouth. The smaller they are, the less you have to swallow and the less you irritate your throat. 

Make your own throat spray. Mix salt and water to make a saltwater spray to help temporarily numb the throat. Use noniodized salt and mix it in warm water.

Gargle with salt water. Salt water will help relieve the soreness and reduce swelling. Add 1 teaspoon of salt to a cup of warm water, and repeat about 3-4 times a day for the best results.

Use apple cider vinegar. Though there’s not yet a scientific explanation for it, apple cider vinegar seems to work much better than any other sort of vinegar at killing bacteria. It will also help clear your throat. Mix a half-teaspoon of ACV in 8 ounces of warm water and drink.

Consider baking soda as an alternative. Baking soda is alkaline, which can help soothe sore throats. Try mixing one teaspoon of baking soda with 8 ounces of warm water to gargle.

Make a cayenne pepper tea. Just like baking soda and apple cider vinegar, cayenne pepper helps kill bacteria and soothe the throat. Try mixing half a teaspoon of cayenne pepper into 8 ounces of warm water and drink slowly.

Drink licorice root tea. This is not the black or red licorice that comes as candy. The taste isn’t the same, but it has just as many benefits as a sore throat remedy. Boil a teaspoon of licorice root in 8 ounces of water and drink it.

Enjoy drinking clove or ginger tea. Cloves and ginger are also known to have both antiviral and antibacterial properties. Even if you didn’t have a sore throat, you could just enjoy the pleasant taste and aroma of these teas, though. To make ginger tea, boil a teaspoon of sliced ginger in 8 ounces of water.

Add a stick of cinnamon to any tea you are drinking. Just like the other ingredients, cinnamon has antiviral and antibacterial effects that will help reduce a sore throat. It’s also incredibly tasty. 

Make yogurt popsicles. To make them, take two individual cups of plain yogurt, mix them together in a medium-sized bowl, and pour the yogurt into popsicle molds. Freeze.

Prepare the popsicle for eating. Before using the popsicle, warm it up a bit so it can easily slide out of the mold and not scrape your throat. Wait for a few minutes before you take it out. 

Try making tea popsicles, too. Boil 1 cup of water and steep your preferred tea for a few minutes before adding it to the popsicle molds and freezing.

Make homemade lozenges for children over five. Dissolve 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid in 1 cup of boiling water. When cool, add 2 teaspoons honey and mix. Swirl the mixture in a saucepan over low heat until the syrup forms slightly thick strands when drizzled from a spoon. Cool the syrup and drop into a prepared clean container to form drops to store for later use.

Learn when to get immediate medical attention. Most sore throats will heal with with home treatment within a few days to one week. If your sore throat is severe or lasts more than two weeks, seek medical attention.

Determine whether the infection is viral or bacterial. Viral throat infections generally don't call for any medical treatment. On the other hand, if it’s bacterial, your doctor may recommend antibiotics. 

Take antibiotics for a bacterial infection as directed. You have to complete the full course of your antibiotic treatment, even if you start feeling better. If you don’t finish the course, the infection could come back even worse.

Eat yogurt with active cultures. Eating yogurt with live, active cultures can help reduce the duration of a sore throat and get rid of the infection quicker since the active cultures help fight off the bacteria. Choose any plain yogurt, without added sugar. 

With these helpful steps, you’ll soon be on your way to a healthy and happy lifestyle. If your sore throat is persistent for more than a few days, however, it’s important to seek medical attention. Remember to always stay hydrated and take the time to get the proper rest and nutrition to keep your body functioning at an optimal level.

How to Silver Leaf Furniture
Silver leafing has been a popular way to add a unique decorative touch to furniture for centuries. Silver leafing can look sophisticated and luxurious, making a piece of furniture seem more impressive. Silver leafing can be an expensive process to buy already done, but if you have the right tools, it's not too difficult to do yourself. Here's a step-by-step guide to help you achieve a perfect silver leafed piece of furniture.

The first step is to go to your local craft or home improvement store and buy all the supplies you will need for silver leafing. You will need some silver leaf, gilding size, a grey primer, and a sealer. Depending on the project, you may want to buy a book of silver leaf, which is usually cheaper than purchasing individual sheets. Additionally, if you're looking to save money, some craft stores sell aluminum leaf as an alternative to silver leaf.

Once you have all of the tools needed to get started, decide how you want to silver leaf the piece of furniture. Do you want to apply silver leaf to the entire piece or do you want to spray paint some of the surfaces? If you are opting to use spray paint, make sure to buy a suitable primer or paint color. If the piece will be silver leafed, you will also need to purchase some gilding size and soft bristled paintbrushes. Gilding size usually only takes 3 hours to set before silver leafing can begin.

Strip off any paint chips on the piece of furniture and sand the surface down. Once the surface is smooth and free of any dirt, the next step is to apply a grey primer. Let the paint completely cure before beginning to silver leaf, as any moisture will interfere with the leafing process. Once the primer is dry, paint the furniture with the gilding size, leaving it to set as per the package instructions.

Start to apply the silver leaf while the gilding size is still wet. Position your hand at one corner of the surface and pick up the book of silver leaf, with the spine of the book facing your palm. Apply the silver leaf by gently laying it onto the gilding size. Continue to lay the sheets of silver leaf onto the furniture, making sure to remove any air bubbles that form. Once you have finished silver leafing all the pieces of the project, use a soft bristled brush to burnish the silver leaf.

Finally, you will need to seal the piece of furniture with a coat of some sealer. There are many varieties of sealers, so choose one that works best with the project you are doing. Be sure to apply the sealer with a gentle stroke and wait for the surface to cure completely before using the piece. 

Silver leafing furniture can be a fun and rewarding project to take on. With the right tools and knowledge, it's easy to achieve an elegant look. Now you are ready to begin your silver leafed piece of furniture and enjoy the result for many years to come!

How to Be a Roller Hockey Goalie'
Roller Hockey is a fast-paced and exciting sport, that relies on its goalies to protect the goal and stop all of the shots from the opposing team. Becoming a successful roller hockey goalie is a difficult task, but with the right mindset and enough practice, you can make it. Here's what you need to do to become a Roller Hockey goalie: 

Obtain all the right equipment- all the pads, the helmet, and everything else. When it comes to goalie equipment, it's important to make sure you have the right size and fit. Make sure that the goalie pads fully cover all vulnerable parts of your body, such as your knees, chest, and boobs. Make sure your helmet is well padded, and make sure it fits snugly around your head. 

Stretch out thoroughly. This is especially important for a goalie, as they have to be agile enough to move from side to side quickly. Make sure to stretch all the muscles that will be involved in goaltending – legs, arms, and torso. Spend some time doing dynamic stretches such as squats and arm circles to ensure that you're warm and limber when playing. 

Try skating around the goal. While most of a goalie's job will take place within the crease, it's also a good idea to get some practice in outside the crease. One way to do this is by skating around the goal and doing criss-crosses. This will allow you to get used to different angles and shooting trajectories, and it will improve your footwork and agility. 

Get in the net and start to get into your ready position. Most coaches will suggest “the classic” goalie stance – legs slightly more than shoulder-width apart, bent slightly at the waist, and hands at around chest-level. Think about how you can spread out, so you can cover the maximum amount of the goal. 

Stand in your ready stance, and ask the coach or another player to warm you up with shots getting progressively better and faster, while the rest of the team is doing something else. This is the best way to get used to goaltending, as it allows you to get used to different types of shots and how to respond to them. Remember to stay relaxed, and concentrate on noticing the puck and reacting accordingly. 

Get ready for drills/games once you're warmed up. The drills and games require a different level of focus, as the shots are now real, and a goal can be scored against you at any time, so focus is key. Pay attention to the shots that are coming in, and jump into action as soon as they are released. This is also a good time to practice any new techniques you might have learnt. 

Positioning and timing are crucial; you should position yourself so that most of the goal is covered, and that which isn't covered should be easy to cover quickly. Remember to stay patient and not over commit, as this could leave you open to giving away unnecessary goals. 

Don't get discouraged when you let a shot in and everyone starts to celebrate, goalies are one of the toughest positions to play and don't usually get comments like, "nice save" unless you do something spectacular or have very nice teammates. Don't dwell on mistakes: instead, focus on the positive aspects of playing a goalie - the important saves you make, and the joy of stopping a goal at the last moment. 

Arm positioning: Keep your arms up covering as close to the top corners as you feel comfortable with, have your catcher-mitt with the palm facing the puck/ball so that all you have to do is move it in front of the puck/ball to catch it. Holding your arms too low can leave big gaps in the goal for shots, especially low ones. Keep your arms up as much as you can, and make sure your palms are facing away from your body. 

Finally, think about how you can improve after training, what you might change next training, or even do some research on alternate stances or useful goalie stretches or off-ice conditioning. Goalie training should be tailored to your own capabilities and weaknesses - work on these areas and be persistent in raising your game. With enough dedication, you can become an excellent roller hockey goalie. Good luck!

Make sure both your clothes and shoes are free of dirt or odors, and that their colors still look vibrant. Your goal is to look the part of a new junior high student.

Second, arrive to school early. This will give you the opportunity to find your locker and look up where your classes are. Check your school's website if you don't remember the location of your locker or classroom. This will help save you a few minutes of nervous wandering. 

Third, get to know the people around you by introducing yourself to your classmates. If you know any people from last year, be sure to greet them. Fitting a backpack is essential for finding one that will be comfortable and supportive when you are on a long walk or a hike. Knowing how to fit a backpack properly is important to ensure it doesn't cause you pain or discomfort.

The first step in fitting a backpack is to measure your waist size and torso measurements. The waist size should be measured from the top of your hipbone to your belly button, while the torso measurement is the length from the top of your spine down to the top of your hipbone. If you have a large frame, or broad shoulders, you may want to look for a unisex or men’s fit backpack, while a slender individual will likely need to look for a women’s fit backpack. If you find that in either case your torso measurement is less than 18 inches (46 cm), you should look for a small frame pack. Medium frame packs are best for someone with a torso measurement between 18 and 20 inches (46 cm to 51 cm). If your torso measurement is over 20 inches (51 cm), then look for a large framed pack.

Once you have your waist measurement, you should use this to determine which belt size is best for you. You can use this when looking for packs at outdoor stores, so that you can test out how they fit. It is best to look for stores that offer a wide variety of packs, so that you can look through the sizes and test how these subtle differences in construction feel.

Once you have found a backpack that looks suitable, load it with 20 lbs. of gear. Start by loosening all of the straps along the shoulders, waist, and hips. Then place your shoulders in the loosen straps. Finally, bring the hip belt stands 1 inch (2.5 cm) above your iliac crest (hip). Now, you can start tightening the shoulder straps until they are flush with your upper back. Snap the load lifter strap into place, and walk around the store for a while to test how it feels. Take note of any discomfort or pressure points you feel, and adjust the straps accordingly to better accommodate your body and provide more support.

Be sure to try on different types of packs and adjust the straps throughout your search. Doing this will help ensure you find a backpack that fits you and is comfortable to wear. Finally, it is a good idea to practice wearing the same size packs for a couple of weeks at home before committing to purchasing it. This will allow you to get comfortable with how the pack moves and fits on you. Remember, properly fitting your backpack is essential for ensuring you don’t experience pain or discomfort while on your journey.

How to Have a Spa Party for Girls'
A spa-inspired girls’ party is a perfect way to enjoy some down time with your friends. Here’s how to plan a successful spa party that’s fit for a group of girls. 

Think of your friends. Before you do anything else, you need to decide who’ll attend the spa party. Consider the age group of your attendees and the types of activities you can do in the Spa. Depending on the size of your group, you may decide to invite other family members like parents and siblings as well.

Clean. After you decide on the guest list, it’s time to get the room ready. Make sure you have all the supplies you need like towels and body scrubs. Vacuum or mop the floor if necessary and don’t forget to put out some relaxing decorations like lit candles, flowers, and music.

As guests arrive, offer them mints or a small hard candy while you wait for the other girls. This will give everyone time to settle down and start feeling relaxed.

Go into a television room, and put on facemasks. Pick a mask that works for everyone’s skin type and don’t forget to apply your own! This is a great time to catch up with friends while the masks are on.

Have girls find a partner (if there is only three people, then take turns) and have one do the girls' hair, then switch. Choose different hairstyles according to the length or type of hair and consider using fun decorations like beads or feathers.

Do the girls' nails, or have partners, but be sure to wait to do someone else's until yours are dry. Have a selection of polishes ready, and don’t forget to offer a base and top coat as well. You can also use other fun decorations like glitter, coloring pens, or nail stickers for extra pizzazz.

If you are allowed, do makeup on each other. Show everyone different techniques to apply makeup and don’t forget to practice healthy makeup application like washing your hands or using disposable applicators for eyeliner and lipsticks.

Have another snack, or pizza or some dinner, then watch a movie. Pick out a few fun films that everyone will enjoy and some cozy blankets, pillows, and pajamas as well.

Try on different outfits of your own, or ask girls to bring some clothes over before hand, and mix and match. Have a fashion show and let everyone vote on the winner of the most creative look!

Try a fun sleepover chant game, where one girl lies on the ground, and everyone else puts their fingertips under her body, and then chant, "Light as a feather, stiff as a board," 20 times, and then lift her. This is a great way to open up the imagination and encourage laughter.

If allowed, do prank calls, but only to people you know. Have some funny scripts prepared ahead of time and come up with creative ways to change your voice.

Dance to some songs from your iPod or radio, or MP3 player, and even sing along if you like. Put on some of your favorite tunes and have a mini-dance party.

Tell ghost stories. This is an old classic but a great icebreaker. Have every guest contribute to the story and encourage creativity as you go along!

Go to sleep, and don't be too loud if you talk for a little while, because chances are, your family is trying to sleep too. Spend a few seconds contemplating the night’s events and give yourself a big compliment for a successful Spa Party!

How to Organise an Event
An event can be as small as a birthday party or as large as a music festival, but most have the same basic steps to ensure they go off without a hitch.Organizing an event can be overwhelming. To make sure the event goes smoothly, you should plan properly and have the right people in charge. Here are some tips to help you with the process.

Define the event's purpose. It is important to have a clear purpose for the event. Make sure to have a good understanding of why you are organizing the event and what you would like to achieve. This will help you make the right decisions and put the necessary resources to the best use.

Set goals. Come up with a list of measurable outcomes that should be achieved. Write down a timeline of specific tasks that must be completed and any milestones you need to reach.

Gather volunteers. Figure out who will be helping you out. Volunteers are essential for the event to run successfully. Once you have found the people who are willing to donate their time and effort, make sure to explain their roles and responsibilities clearly to avoid confusion.

Prepare a budget. Find out what you will need to fund the event. Set aside money for marketing, advertising, catering, decorations and any other costs related to the event. Try to plan ahead and stay within your budget to avoid any surprises.

Decide on a time and place. You should choose dates and a venue based on the type of event and the expected attendance. Make sure to pick a convenient location for your guests and to inform them about it in advance.

Think about logistics. Logistics involve details like parking, refreshments, transportation and related services. Plan in advance and hire professionals to manage the logistics on the day of the event if needed.

Think about marketing and advertising. You need to let people know about your event. Create and distribute flyers, post information on websites, social networks and local newspapers.

Organize yourself. Have a plan for the day of the event, keep schedules and backup plans at hand, and make a "to do" list with every detail of the event. This will help you to stay organized and make sure all the details are taken care of.

Make sure everything is a go. A few days before the event, double check all the details like the venue, catering, number of attendees, and make sure the contracts are signed.

Meet with your team. Hold a meeting with all the people who are involved in the event. Discuss their expectations and suggestions.

Delegate work to different people and let an experienced person coordinate all activities. The experienced person should also coordinate with any companies that are involved in the event, like catering, security, or entertainment companies.

Make sure to update any websites connected to the event. To make sure that everyone knows the latest information about the event, keep all related websites and social networks up to date.

Collect sponsors and other sources of money from delegates. You can get funded by sponsors, from the sale of tickets and other sources.

Market the event. Use the internet and different mediums to reach out and inform a large number of people about the event.

Gather items needed for the event. Things like decorations, audio-visual equipment, writing materials and refreshments and drinks should be collected well ahead to the event.

Make arrangements for everything. Make sure that everything will be set up and ready in time. Choose appropriate people for this task and assign them with the responsibility.

Prepare a contact list. You should have a list of people to contact in case of an emergency. These could be your team members, venue managers, sponsors, and any other people related to the event.

Visit the venue with your team members. Make sure that the place is ready for the event, and check for any potential issues that may arise.

Stay calm. This is very important. Don't panic if something doesn't go as planned. Just stay calm and make sure everyone is doing their job.

Do one last check-in with your team. Before you leave the venue, make sure all the necessary items are taken care of.

Check all invitations and responses. Not everyone will answer your invitations, but you should make sure to contact them to see if they will be attending the event.

Go to the venue and check if everything is ready. Make sure that the setup is complete, all the audio-visual equipment is in place, and everything else is taken care of.

Make participants' kits. Prepare welcome packs for the participants and hand them out at the event. This includes any information about the event, contact details, maps and anything else relevant.

Make a running sheet. Write down the exact activities that are going to take place in the event, like the speeches, presentations, musical performances, etc.

Make a checklist of the things to be taken to the venue. Make sure all the necessary items for the event are taken to the venue and all activities are properly done.

Arrive early to the venue with your team members and volunteers. Be there early enough to take care of the setup and other tasks.

Set everything up. Use the plan you prepared in advance and make sure everything is in place before the event begins.

Make sure the people who matter know what's going on. Have a meeting with all the important people involved in the event to discuss any last details.

Take photos! Have a photographer on the day of the event to capture memories of the event.

Give a takeaway. Hand out something memorable at the end of the event like a badge, a notebook or a hat.

Clean up the place! Leave the venue in the same condition it was before the event.

Take care of all the post-event duties. Make sure to contact people who helped in the event, thank sponsors and fill out any paperwork.

Have a post-review meeting to perform better next time. Talk about the successes and failures of the event, and make sure to set aside what you have learnt and use it for the next event.

Organizing an event can be daunting, yet rewarding. Follow these steps and you will be sure that your event goes as planned.

How to Grow Vanilla
Growing vanilla can be a fulfilling experience for any gardener wanting to produce their own vanilla beans. While this process does take some time, patience, and practice, it is possible to successfully grow vanilla plants from cuttings. With the right environment and some basic know-how, this venture may be just the thing for a passionate green thumb. 

Construct a tall greenhouse or hothouse. The best way to grow a vanilla orchid is to create an environment where the humidity is high and the temperature is around 70 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit with some variety. While many types of orchids will survive in cooler temperatures, vanilla orchids need the extra warmth. This requires the use of a greenhouse or hothouse to ensure that the environment is properly maintained in order for your plant to grow correctly. 

Try growing several types of orchids before you attempt to grow a vanilla orchid. Different orchids have varying levels of needs when it comes to water and soil mixtures and sunlight. It is wise to practice growing a few other types of orchids before attempting to grow a vanilla orchid.

Purchase a vanilla cutting. A vanilla cutting should be available from gardening or orchid nurseries or stores. If at all possible, ask to see the cutting before you purchase it so you can verify that it is healthy. Make sure that the cutting has one or two nodes, which are small bumps that appear on the stem.

Immerse your cutting completely in a tray of water for 10 minutes. This will help to give the cutting a better chance of survival. 

Remove the cutting from the water, but reinsert the ends in the tray. This will help the cutting to establish roots. Change the water every couple of days.

Ready a space in your hothouse or outdoor tropical garden next to a tree or a trellis. The space that you choose should get a lot of indirect sunlight in order for the vanilla orchid to grow.

Pour orchid potting soil into a pot. Choose a pot or a potting mix that has good drainage and that contains organic matter such as peat moss, perlite, and other orchid soils.

Cover these nodes with 0.8 inches (2 cm) of orchid potting soil. Ensure that the cutting is planted firmly with just enough soil so the nodes are barely covered.

Tie the remaining plant to the trellis or a stake. This will provide the new plant with more vertical support as it grows.

Keep the soil slightly drier for the first month, but never allow it to completely dry out. The soil should be kept slightly dry for the first month in order for the new roots to be able to establish themselves.

Water the plant regularly as time goes on. Provide the orchid enough water to keep it from becoming dry, but not so much as to make the soil soggy. This is something that will require monitoring and adjustment as time goes on.

Add mulch to the soil every few months. Mulch will help with soil moisture and humidity levels.

Move the plant as needed for the next nine to 12 months to ensure it gets sunlight for approximately 50 percent of the day. As the vanilla orchid grows, you may have to readjust the location so that it gets the right amount of sunlight.

Allow the vanilla orchid to grow and mature for several years. You should begin to see some results, in the form of growth and flowers, within two years or so.

Mist the orchid daily with soft water. This will help the environment stay humid and assist with the process of pollinating.

Watch out for clusters of vanilla orchid flowers. When they appear, make sure to perform the necessary pollination in order to get pods.

Wear rubber gloves to avoid problems with orchid sap. Orchid sap can be caustic and can cause skin irritation. 

Push the anther up. This will expose the sticky gray pollinia, which will need to be transferred to the stigma in order to promote pollination. 

Watch to see if the stem turns downward. This is an indication that pollination has occurred successfully.

Continue caring for the plant and pollinating the flowers. Rinse off the pollinia after every pollination in order to prevent the process from being hindered.

Pick the pods when they are green and begin to turn yellow at the bottom. Pick the pods before they become too ripe in order to get the best flavor.

Cure your vanilla beans before using them. Place the freshly picked vanilla pods in an airtight container with a damp cloth and allow them to cure. The curing process helps to lock in the flavor and aroma of the vanilla beans.

With some dedication and practice, this process can be used to produce wonderful vanilla beans. Taking the time to create a suitable environment and providing the care that is necessary will result in having your own homegrown vanilla beans.

Creating an edible Hello Kitty figurine is a great project to make a unique and special cake decoration. With the right supplies and techniques, you'll be able to make a deliciously cute edible Hello Kitty figurine with ease. 

To make the figurine, you’ll need to gather: food coloring, powdered sugar, white and red fondant, edible glue or gelatine, a toothpick, a ball tool and fondant cutters. 

First, prepare colored fondant. To make colored fondant, knead the white fondant with food coloring. Prepare the mat for use by sprinkling powdered sugar over it. 

Use white fondant to make a ball for the Hello Kitty head. Punch two slight indentation at the left and right side of the fondant ball by using the ball tool. Mark three holes on the face side for eyes and nose, by using the pointed side of a brush. 

Make a flat butterfly shape for the bow by using red fondant. To form the whiskers of Hello Kitty either you can paint them with black food color or use black fondant to make the whiskers. To make the body of the Hello Kitty, make a 3–4 centimeter (1.2–1.6 in) long oval shaped white fondant ball and flatten its base to make it stand. 

Make a thin flat blue strip of fondant of about 3/4th of the size of the body and wrap it around the bottom part of the body by using edible glue. For hands, make a shooting star shape using white fondant. Now as hands are ready, attach them to the body using edible glue or toothpicks if needed. Attach the head of Hello Kitty and the body using a toothpick and a little amount of edible glue at the attachment site to assemble them together. 

For shoes make two oval shaped fondant balls and flatten them to decrease the width. Place your Hello Kitty on the shoes resting part while still supporting the back side of your Hello Kitty to check the stability of shoes. Now cut a circular flat fondant of pink color using fondant cutters of size approx. Attach the shoes to the body of the Kitty using edible glue. 

For the final touches, make Hello Kitty's mouth and ears. For the mouth, roll out a thin pink fondant and cut it into a heart shape. For the ears, roll two small white fondant balls and flatten them slightly on the top side. Place them on the head using a dab of edible glue. 

Your edible Hello Kitty figurine is now ready for you to enjoy. Be creative with your decoration and make your Hello Kitty stand out with different embellishments. Place it on top of a cake or in between some cookies and your Hello Kitty will be the star of the show. Have fun with your edible Hello Kitty figurine and enjoy her deliciousness.

Steam Bammy is a delicious dish of grated cassava root that is steamed over a warm broth and coconut milk. It is native to many Caribbean cultures, and is an easy and nutritious meal. Here's how to steam bammy:

1. Start with a root of cassava. First, peel the cassava root and cut it into manageable pieces. Then set each piece on its flat, cut end.

2. Grate the root into fine shreds. Once you have completed this task, wring out any excess moisture.

3. Sprinkle a pinch of salt over the grated root. Divide the mixture into smaller portions and flatten each ball into a disc shape.

4. Mix together flour and salt, then slowly pour in just enough water to create a stiff, dry dough. Set the dough aside for 30 minutes.

5. After the allotted time, divide the dough into smaller pieces and roll each portion out into a thin disc.

6. Heat a skillet over low heat and add the broth and coconut milk. Place the bammy discs into the simmering liquid.

7. To add an extra layer of flavor, preheat a broiler and place the bammy discs on a pan. Broil for a few minutes on each side.

8. Heat oil in a skillet and reduce heat to low-medium. Fry the bammy on both sides until golden brown.

9. To give the bammy even more flavor, soak each disc in coconut milk before returning it to the skillet.

10. Steam the bammy over medium heat for five minutes or so, until it is hot and fluffy.

11. Serve the steamed bammy warm. Enjoy!

How to Choose a Summer Beach Wedding Dress'

In such cases, finding a wedding dress for yourself that is light with the right fabrics, colors and style will be of utmost importance. Here are a few tips that can help you find the perfect summer beach wedding dress.

First and foremost, if the budget permits, consider buying a designer wedding dress for your summer wedding. This way, you will be able to get exactly the kind of dress you want for a reasonable price. When it comes to light fabrics, there are a few considerations that must be made.
