Being a middle school student is a thrilling yet scary experience. You have to juggle academics, social life, and looking great too! Here are some tips on how to get it all done so you can conquer middle school like no other:
 
Stay organized: Make sure you have all the necessary papers, notebooks, etc. in order and in the right place. Binder, locker, and backpack should be clean and organized each week. Get a homework planner or agenda notebook and write down every assignment so you won’t get behind or overwhelmed.
 
Study: Start studying for any test or quiz at least a week before the day of it. Take good notes and review often; this will help you retain the knowledge more easily.
 
Teamwork: Learn how to work well in teams. When it comes to projects, remember to take charge, but not to be too bossy.
 
Social life: Be nice, kind, sweet, and caring. It isn’t wise to argue and fight your way through the hallways. Be yourself and don’t be afraid to show it. Always try giving different people compliments throughout your day. If it’s possible, see if you can give every person in your school or grade a true, kind compliment throughout the year. This way, you can establish constructive relationships with everyone.
 
Be helpful: Sit with different people at lunch and in class. Every once in a while when a newbie looks lost, subtly guide them in the right direction. If you see someone drop something, help them pick it up. Don’t be afraid to talk to other people. But, keep in mind that it’s middle school, and sex is not cool and is something you should not get caught in.

Hygiene: Clean your ears with q-tips weekly and if you have earrings, also clean those. Shower or bath at least every other day and shave your underarms and your legs if need be. Each night before bed, make sure you are wearing an antiperspirant or deodorant. You should have found a product that works well with your hair, and shampoo and condition it each day. Wash your body with a nice smelling soap and body wash. Use a washcloth to scrub any areas of dead skin. After the shower, if possible, use a leave-in conditioner. Air drying your hair can help minimize damage. Don’t go anywhere with soaking wet hair. Make sure to brush and floss your teeth with a toothpaste and mouthwash at least two times each day. Moisturize your hands, feet, or any other dry areas at least twice a week.

Make-up: Don’t be afraid to put make-up on. Find colors that look good on you and apply it. Your lashes will be black, and in that case, use black mascara. For the color of the eyeliner, that is just a personal preference. When it comes to eyeshadows, stay natural. Try using a facial cleaner each morning and night.

Clothing: Wear clothes that look nice and make sure they are ironed with creases. Polish your shoes regularly as well.

In the end, all you need is to do your work well and follow these steps to stay organized and look great. Of course, if you fall behind, don’t be afraid to get help. With these tips, you’ll be surviving middle school academics and social life like a total pro. Good luck!

How to Lose the Nerd Status
It might not usually be said out loud, but let’s face it – having the "nerd" moniker can make you feel like an outcast. Whether you're dealing with acne, atypical hobbies, or a dorky wardrobe, you can learn to shed the nerd status. With the right approach and lifestyle changes, you'll be able to show the world your confidence and individuality without having to become someone you're not.

Take a look at yourself in the mirror. Think of someone else – a hot girl at a bar, or a group of people you'd like to be friends with – and imagine what they would think of your image. Do you have zits? Are your clothes making you stand out for the wrong reasons? Figuring out what others might see as unattractive can lead to steps in the right direction.

If you have moderate to severe acne, there are plenty of advice columns and resources devoted to minimizing such skin conditions. Remember, though, that acne doesn't automatically make you a nerd - addressing the issue can help your self-confidence and may give you a new outlook.

Good hygiene is an important aspect, too. Being clean, well-groomed, and having fresh breath can go a long way in making you more comfortable in social settings. However, this isn’t enough in itself, so don't neglect the other must-haves.

Hairstyle is key. This is a great place to show off your individualism – find a style and color that works for you. This doesn't mean you have to go wild and dye your hair neon green. Subtle changes in color and shape can give you a boost and can open the avenue for further experimentation.

Clothing is another way to express who you are and creative ways to show the world you are not a nerd. To start, focus on cleanliness and comfort. Opting for a fitted look will give your frame more structure and confidence. Dressing up initially means making smart investments via classic pieces, which don’t have to be expensive. They just have to make sense in terms of size, fabric, and color.

Widen your hobbies and skills. Are you all about computers, video games, and comic books? That's great, but it is likely to be a conversation piece, not a conversation. Have a few topics ready in advance that show your interests and the different layers to your personality. Another way of widening your skillset is to take classes that are outside of your comfort zone. This gives you the opportunity to learn something different and can put you in contact with people who share your interests.

Speech is a crucial piece of the puzzle, but it doesn't have to be changed - just what you say. Try not to blurt out random questions or weird facts when you're trying to talk to someone. Practice conversation starters and speaking in a clear and eloquent manner. If you’re particularly nervous, avoid caffeine. As soon as you feel yourself panicking, just take a deep breath and think about the conversation you want to have.

Lastly, don't stick out. Pick up on trends and the popular music. People are very passionate about the music they enjoy. If you’re only interested in one or two genres, you're confining yourself to only certain locations. Music taste not only speaks volumes about you, but it's also a great avenue to make new friends. Opening yourself up with different genres can help you explore new bars and clubs as a way to both lose the nerd status and make lasting relationships.

Remember, if the changes you’re making are pushing you away from your true self and deeper into the nerd category, you’re off track. There are plenty of ways to look and sound cool without having to completely change your personality. With a little bit of self-reflection and strategic changes, you'll be looking and feeling like the new you in no time.

Grilling up the perfect Filet Mignon can be intimidating, but it's nothing to worry about if you follow these eight simple steps. 

Step 1: Choose a thick cut of meat. Filet Mignon is best cooked at high, direct heat, so choose a cut of meat that is at least 1.5-2 inches thick. 

Step 2: Resist the temptation to outfit your filet with additional rubs or smother it in marinades. The flavor of the Filet Mignon stands on its own, so opt for olive oil, butter, and salt and pepper to season.

Step 3: Decide whether to salt the filet before or after grilling. Salting before grilling is essential for adding flavor and richness, so if you're forgoing a rub or marinade, salting your steak is a must.

Step 4: Wait for the filet to come to room temperature. Letting your steak come to room temperature before cooking helps it cook more evenly and quickly.

Step 5: If possible, use lump charcoal over briquettes and try to stay away from gas grills. Lump charcoal imparts a certain smokiness to the steak as it cooks, and gas grills don't maintain a consistent temperature as well as charcoal grills do.

Step 6: Position your coals to form a hot side and a cool side in your grill. This will create a direct and an indirect heat source that will give you better control of your cooking.

Step 7: Brush your filet with a little bit of oil. This will keep the steak from sticking to the grill and allow it to cook evenly.

Step 8: Decide whether to cook your filet primarily over high heat or low heat. For Filet Mignon, high heat (500°F) is recommended, as it will quickly sear the outside of the steak while cooking the inside to the desired temperature.

Step 9: Cook your filet over indirect, "cool" heat until the filet is about 15° - 20° F from your ideal temperature. This will help you get an even cook on your steak without burning it.

Step 10: For a medium-rare filet, transfer it over to the direct, "hot" side of the grill when its temperature reaches 110° to 115° F. Sear the meat on both sides, using tongs to flip the filet when necessary.

Step 11: Remove the filet when its internal temperature is 5° F away from its ideal temperature. For a medium-rare steak, this is usually between 135° and 140°F.

Step 12: Make sure to let the steak rest for 5 to 10 minutes before cutting into it. This will allow the steak to redistribute its juices and create an optimal flavor and texture.

Step 13: Pepper your steak generously. This will add flavor and the perfect finishing touch.

Step 14: Serve and enjoy your perfectly cooked king of steaks. Filet Mignon, when cooked properly, is incredibly flavorful and tender, making it one of the most sought after items of any steakhouse menu.

How to Take Minutes
Taking minutes is an important part of holding a meeting. Minutes are the written record of what happened during the meeting and are a source of accountability to ensure actions are taken and information is documented. Without meeting minutes, it can be difficult to remember details from one meeting to the next. It is important to have an efficient process for taking meeting minutes so you can effectively capture the important elements of the meeting.

Know your organization's meeting policies. Before the meeting starts, it is important to have a sense of the policies in place for meetings. Make sure to familiarize yourself with the protocols for different types of meetings. Depending on the type of meeting, you may need to make sure to highlight certain points or sorts of motions.

Prepare a template in advance. To take effective meeting minutes, you'll need a template to work with. A standard template includes the date, time, those in attendance, motions and decisions made. This will help you to note down the salient points during the meeting.

Bring a notebook or laptop with you. Whatever you choose to use for taking meeting minutes, make sure to bring it with you to the meeting. You'll need something to write down the information in. It's also a good idea to bring an extra pen or two in case one runs out of ink.

Distribute an attendance sheet. At the start of the meeting, hand out an attendance sheet to each person present. This will ensure that everyone is accounted for in the meeting, as some people may have questions or comments to make afterward.

Fill out as much of your template as possible. As soon as the meeting begins, start to fill in the details for the date, time, and attendance list. Then, take down the details of motions and decisions that are made throughout the meeting.

Note the result of the first motion. Before the first motion is made, make sure to note who brought it up and what it is. Then, make sure to note the result of the motion (passed or failed).

Record other motions throughout the meeting. As other motions are made, take careful note of each one. Who brought it up, what it is, and the outcome (passed or failed).

Listen to reports and obtain copies. Throughout the meeting, if reports or presentations are made, make sure to take note of those. If possible, try to get a copy of any reports that are presented.

Record actions taken or assigned. If the meeting comes to the point where people are asked to take on tasks or actions, make sure you record these. This is a good time to find out who is responsible for what.

Record all points of order and rulings. During the meeting, any rulings or disagreements need to be documented as well. It's important to record the outcome so that everyone can be held accountable later.

Only if asked, record summaries of discussions. Upon occasion, the discussion or debate that takes places during a meeting can be useful to record for reference. However, as this can be lengthy, ask if it is necessary to make a summary.

Wrap up at the end of meeting. When the meeting is over, make sure to wrap up the process of taking minutes. Record any remaining action items, any unresolved motions, and the date, time, and place of the next meeting.

How to Grow Plants Using Hydroponics
Gardening has been around since ancient times, but now, with the rise of hydroponics, it has become even easier to grow plants anywhere. Hydroponics uses nutrient-rich water medium instead of soil to grow plants. This method is perfect for small-scale home gardens and people who don't have access to soil. 

Before you get started with hydroponics, there are a few things to consider. Firstly, do not go overboard buying hydroponic supplies that they may need in the future but will not need in the beginning stages of hydroponic gardening. Have a dedicated space for your hydroponic gardening. This can be indoors or outdoors, depending on your preferences. Make sure the spot has access to water, but not direct sunlight, as this can overheat your plants. Secondly, get the right hydroponics supplies. An aeroponic system requires different supplies and needs than a water based hydroponic system, for example.

When choosing on the plants that you want to grow, pick those that are suitable for hydroponics, such as lilies, basil, tomatoes, and more of the plants common to this method. Once you have the plants of choice, you will need to start the process of germination. Take wet paper towels and place the seed(s) inside them. Put the bag in a warm, dark place and give the seeds some time to germinate. A few days later, the seeds will begin to sprout. Keep in mind that, when the seeds have germinated and is showing at least one inch of stem, it is a seedling.

When the seedlings are strong enough, move them into their permanent hydroponic container. Fill the container with water, making sure the water remains oxygenated and is properly balanced with nutrients. Place your grown seedling into the water, so that only the roots are submerged. Change the water every few days, especially if it seems to get murky or translucent. For a better understanding of how to properly maintain your hydroponic garden, read the instructions that came with the supplies.

Watch the seedlings carefully and make sure that they grow straight. If you notice a stem that is too low, it often means that the stem is too heavy, and this may damage the plant. If you are growing a fruit-bearing plant, watch for flower buds growing near the leaves. Make sure that the flowers don't weigh the stem down, if you chose a flowering plant. 

When it's finally time to harvest the fruits and vegetables of your labor, making sure to take great care in pulling the plants out of their containers carefully. While harvesting the fruits and vegetables, check the plants for pests or diseases that may have caught on. Finally, enjoy your fruits and vegetables with your family! 

Growing a hydroponic garden is a fun and engaging activity that anyone can do. With the right supplies and knowledge, anyone can start their own hydroponic garden. Just remember to get the right supplies, maintain the garden, and watch your plants grow straight and strong. In no time, you will reap the rewards of your garden in the form of delicious fruits and vegetables. Good luck!

How to Survive a Personal Financial Crisis is no easy task. The path to economic stability can be difficult and may require difficult decisions. However, if you anticipate and plan for a crisis, you may be able to minimize the impact of financial stressors, make responsible decisions, and recover faster. 

Be aware that negative emotions are normal. When confronting financial difficulties, many individuals become overwhelmed with stress, anger, and fear of the unknown. It is normal to experience these negative feelings as you grapple with a personal financial crisis. 

Focus on accepting your financial situation. Taking ownership of your financial woes is key to initiating a plan to get back on track. You are the only one responsible for your situation, and ultimately you are the only one who can get yourself out. So, accept your situation and move on to the next step of recovery.

Talk about your situation. Financial crises can be an isolating experience, but it is important to communicate. Speak openly and honestly with close friends or family about the difficulties you are facing. This can bring a sense of relief and may even provide objective advice.

Be honest with your family. The truth will ultimately prevail, so it is important to be forthcoming with your family early on. Although it may be difficult to tell them the severity of the situation, it is important to include your family in the recovery process so everyone is on the same page.

Commit to staying positive. A financial crisis is no easy feat to tackle, but staying positive and optimistic can help your recovery in the long run. Remind yourself that recovering from a difficult financial situation is not impossible and do everything in your power to stay positive throughout.

Determine your assets. Determine what properties you own, how much they are worth, and what income you receive from them. Assets can include but are not limited to stocks, bonds, vehicles, real estate, and cash savings.

Determine your liabilities. Next, list out all of your debts and obligations. This includes any mortgage payments, car loans, credit cards, student loans, or other debts that you are obligated to pay.

Calculate your net worth. This is a valuable exercise as it gives you a true picture of how far you may have fallen or how close you may be to emerging successfully from the financial crisis. Subtract your liabilities from your assets to determine your total net worth – this is a guiding metric for financial recovery.

Determine your income. It is important to calculate the income you have coming in each month. This includes earnings from any job or business, as well as income from investments or other sources.

Determine your expenses. Itemize the expenses you have each month. This includes fixed expenses such as mortgage, rent, and car payments, as well as variable expenses such as groceries, utilities, and entertainment.

Determine your monthly net income. This is the key metric for your current financial situation. Subtract your monthly expenses from your monthly income to get your net income for the month. This will be an important number for assessing the consequences of your situation, creating a plan, and tackling your recovery plan.

Assess the consequences of your situation. Consider the effects of financial difficulty on other areas of your life. This could include credit scores, relationships, personal wellbeing, and future plans.

Create a plan suited to your needs. A financial crisis can be a daunting challenge but a plan of action will allow you to tackle it head-on. Develop a roadmap that will guide you back to economic stability based on the specifics of your situation.

Determine your fixed and discretionary monthly expenses. Split your expenses into those that are essential to survival and those that are discretionary that can be reduced or eliminated.

Reduce your variable expenses. Review your variable expenses to determine where you can cut back or eliminate spending. Try to make responsible decisions that will cut monthly expenses but still provide you with a reasonable quality of life.

Reduce your fixed expenses. Outline your fixed expenses, such as rent, mortgage, or car payments. Negotiate with creditors for a lower payment or consider refinancing in order to reduce your fixed expenses. 

Pursue additional sources of income. If you have lost your job or are in a difficult financial situation, consider taking on a part-time job or freelance gigs to supplement your income.

Apply for government assistance programs. Depending on your country of residence, you may be eligible for government assistance programs that provide financial relief or other benefits during difficult times.

Consider selling assets and using the proceeds to pay off debt. Evaluate the possibility of selling additional assets to reduce or eliminate your liabilities. 

Consider filing for bankruptcy. Depending on the severity of your situation, you may need to file for bankruptcy. Be sure to research the process and the long-term consequences before making this decision.

Implement your recovery plan. Once you have determined your financial situation, developed a plan, and put it into motion, focus on sticking with it. Remind yourself how far you’ve come and set small goals that will help you stay motivated and on track.

Prioritize your debt repayment. Subdivide your expenditure into priority and non-priority debt repayment. It is important to make minimum payments on all your liabilities, but prioritize paying off those with the highest interest rates. 

Understand the importance of staying in touch with your creditors. Communicate regularly and honestly with your lenders so that they can understand your situation and work with you to make arrangements. 

Contact your creditors and explain your situation in open and honest terms. Remain in contact and be upfront about any changes in your circumstances. Doing so may help in negotiating better repayment terms or limiting late fees.

Consider debt consolidation loans and/or balance transfer cards to reduce payment amounts. Consolidation loans and balance transfers can help reduce interest significantly and bring payments down to a manageable amount.

Consider debt counseling. If your situation has become difficult to handle you may consider seeking professional help from a credit counseling agency. Experienced debt counselors can provide sound advice and help you develop a plan to get back on track.

Maintain your recovery habits. Once you’ve implemented your recovery plan, it is important to maintain the same habits and not fall back into your old habits.

Rebuild your credit. As you are paying off debt, establish and maintain healthy credit practices. This includes regularly utilizing credit accounts responsibly and maintaining a low credit utilization rate.

Apply lessons you’ve learned. Learn from your mistakes. Reflect upon the lessons from your financial crisis and strive to prevent a similar crisis in the future.

Save or prepare to prevent another crisis. Financial crises are difficult to predict, but taking preventive measures can help minimize the chance of a repeat. If possible, establish an emergency fund or plan for the future to mitigate the effects of a potential future crisis.

How to Play Dodgeball'

Playing Dodgeball is an exciting game that requires quick reflexes, great hand-eye coordination and teamwork. It is a great game to play during recess or at parties. Here is a guide on how to play Dodgeball.

First of all, it's important to understand the basics of the game. Dodgeball typically has two teams of six players each. The object of the game is to eliminate all players from the opposing team by throwing balls and-or catching them. A player is eliminated when hit with a ball, catches a ball thrown by an opposing player or carries the ball outside of the playing area.

In a game, each team's players must stay behind a line that divides the two sides of the field. The balls must stay on your side of the line, if you throw a ball across the line your team will lose the point. The game starts with each team behind the center line. The referee then throws the balls (usually six) out to the center of the field and each team rushes to grab as many balls as possible.

Once you get a ball, hold on to it until the other team's best players have thrown theirs, then go up and throw it at some of the people who are not as good. While getting ready to throw, stay crouched low to the ground and start to sort of gallop towards the line that divides the two sides. When throwing, do not be afraid to turn sideways and almost fall then catch yourself with your hand to help increase power. This will provide more power and accuracy in your throws.

When catching a ball, let it come to you, don't go to it. If someone throws the ball at you, do not move. Remain stationary and act like a wall or a net. When dodging, always be ready to jump, as they will most likely go for your feet. Practice jumping, throwing, and running...the essential ingredients to becoming a good dodge ball player.

Think of the game as war. Strategize the game by keeping an eye on all directions. Always be alert and watch the balls closely, anticipate where they might go and where they are headed. Get two balls and throw one at an enemy's foot. When you're throwing the ball towards an opponent do not aim for the upper body as it makes it easier for them to dodge it or catch it, aim for the shins as they can't catch it and makes it harder for them to dodge it.

Overall, Dodgeball is a great game that is fun for all ages. It is a great way to have fun with friends and exercise simultaneously. With practice, skill and a bit of luck, you too can become a master at playing Dodgeball. Good luck and have fun!

How to Do the Electric Slide
Doing the Electric Slide is an iconic dance move that's been an essential part of many people's party dance repertoire for years. This fun dance move involves shuffling your feet and turning 180 degrees, and it is sure to get you energized and in the mood to party. If you want to learn how to do the Electric Slide, just follow these simple steps!

1. Step to the right with your right foot.
2. Step to the right with your left foot, crossing it behind your right.
3. Step right with the right foot.
4. Close your feet together while tapping your left foot by your right.
5. Step to the left with your left foot.
6. Step to the left with the right foot, crossing your right foot behind your left foot.
7. Step left with your left foot.
8. Close your feet together, tapping your right foot next to the left foot.
9. Step back with your right foot.
10. Step back with your left foot.
11. Step back with your right foot.
12. Tap your left foot next to your right foot.
13. Step forward with your left foot.
14. Bring your right foot behind your left foot, and tap your right big toe to your left heel.
15. Step back with your right foot.
16. Tap your left foot in front of your right foot.
17. Step forward with your left foot.
18. Hop on your left foot as you turn yourself to the left 90 degrees.
19. Repeat all these steps until the music fades.
20. Do a grapevine to the right and tap.
21. Do a grapevine to the left and tap.
22. Take 3 steps backwards and tap.
23. Step forward and tap your foot, step backward and tap your foot.
24. Step forward and turn left.

By following these steps, you will be able to master the classic Electric Slide. Make sure to have a friend around to help you practice the move so you can feel the music as you dance. It's even better if you have a group of friends who can help you practice and show you the timing and groove. Once you've got the moves down, don't forget to have fun with it! Making your own hard cider is a fun and rewarding experience. With the proper ingredients and equipment, you can make a delicious brew that can be enjoyed by the entire family! In this article, we'll explain how to make hard cider, so you can enjoy a refreshing beverage with just a little bit of effort.

Firstly, you must choose the right ingredients for making your hard cider. You'll need a good, high-quality apple juice. This can be store-bought, or prepared from freshly-pressed apples. You'll also need yeast, sugar, water, Campden tablets, a hydrometer, yeast nutrient, and pectic enzyme.

Once your ingredients are ready, you'll need to sanitize your supplies to make sure that your cider stays free of bacteria and other contaminants that could spoil the brew. Make sure to thoroughly clean and sanitize all fermentation vessels, airlocks, tubing, and any other ingredients or equipment you'll be using. 

Before you begin the actual cider brewing, you may want to consider making a starter the day before. A starter is basically a small amount of liquid, like apple juice, that you premix with yeast, and can be used to test the viability of your yeast. This is not a necessary step, but it can help give you assurance that your yeast is alive and ready to ferment, and will get the fermentation process started a bit faster.

If you decide to make a starter, you can do it one of two ways. The first method is to simply heat the apple juice to 165 degrees Fahrenheit (75 degrees Celsius) for about 15 minutes, and then cool it in an ice bath. This can kill off any wild yeasts or bacteria that could be present in the juice, and prevent them from competing with your yeast in the fermentation process. Alternatively, if you have access to a source of boiling water (like a hot water heater or a camping stove), you can simply heat the juice to 165 degrees Fahrenheit for 2-3 minutes, and then cool it as before. The heat brewing method has some pros and cons, so make sure to understand them before deciding on one or the other.

After your starter is complete (or skipped), and your supplies are sanitized, it's time to start brewing your own hard cider. Here's how to do it:

1. Pour your apple juice into a large saucepan, and simmer it for 15 minutes to sanitize it.

2. Cool the juice in an ice bath.

3. Pour the cooled juice into your fermenter.

4. Crush two Campden tablets and stir them into the juice to add sulfites (for sanitation).

5. Allow the cider to sit for two days to let the sulfites do their job.

6. Heat your water to a boil and add the yeast nutrient and the pectic enzyme.

7. Combine the heated mixture with the juice in the fermenter.

8. If desired, add sugar to the mixture to increase the alcohol content.

9. Add your yeast.

10. Cover the fermenter and attach an airlock to it. This will allow gases to escape, while preventing outside air from entering, that could spoil your cider.

11. Allow the cider to sit for several weeks, while the yeast ferments and the cider matures.

12. When you feel it's ready, use a hydrometer to check the alcohol content in the cider.

13. Once the cider has reached the desired alcohol content, bottle it and enjoy.

Alternatively, if you'd like a crystal-clear cider, let the cider sit for an additional couple of weeks. This will allow the suspended solids in the cider to settle, leaving you with a clear, tasty beverage.

With a bit of patience, persistence, and knowledge, you can craft your very own hard cider at home. Once you've gathered your ingredients and equipment, it's fairly simple and straightforward. The best part? You get to enjoy a truly delicious treat of your own making!

Growing nutmeg is an exciting project that can produce crops of flavorful spices for years to come. Taking the time to ensure that the soil, location, and other conditions are favorable is essential to having success with nutmeg. Here are the steps you follow to ensure a crop of nutmeg.

1. Verify that the location is warm enough. Nutmeg requires a minimum temperature of no lower than 65 degrees Fahrenheit. If you live in an area that has cooler temperatures, take the necessary precautions to ensure that your nutmeg isn’t exposed to temperatures that are too cool, such as providing a greenhouse or a protective barrier.

2. Check the soil’s pH level. Nutmeg thrives in soil with a pH range of 4.5 to 7.5. A soil test can determine whether you need to add lime to adjust the pH level.

3. Find a sunny spot with light afternoon shade. Nutmeg is a tropical plant that needs full sunlight to thrive, but can be harmed by too much afternoon sun. Place the tree in a location where it will get full sun during the morning and morning-to-early afternoon shade.

4. Sterilize a knife. Nutmeg grows from a seed that is encased within a pink-to-orange aril, or covering. Cut the aril from the base of the seed and peel it off carefully.

5. Soak the nuts in water for a day. Soaking the nuts helps initiate germination and reduces the risk of disease. Change the water every 12 hours to make sure the nuts are evenly hydrated.

6. Fill a pot with soil. A well-draining soil should be used with a pot size of between six and eight inches. Plant two to three nutmegs per pot.

7. Place the seed beneath the soil surface. Gently place the nutmeg seeds approximately two inches deep and then cover with soil.

8. Water the pot thoroughly. The nutmegs need to remain moist but not overly saturated. Water the soil until the water begins to come out of the bottom of the pot.

9. Set the pot in a warm area to sprout. The tree needs to be kept in warm temperatures of at least 70 degrees Fahrenheit. Monitor the pot daily and mist with water when necessary.

10. Store the tree where it receives several hours of sun daily. Once the nutmeg tree has reached six to eight inches in height, it should be transplanted outdoors and given at least four to five hours of direct sunlight each day.

11. Mist the tree twice a day and water the soil when necessary. Mist the entire tree, including the fruits, until they are covered. Nutmegs need to remain moist but not overly wet. If the top of the soil begins to dry out, water the soil.

12. Rotate the tree each day. This will ensure even sunlight exposure.

13. Move it to larger containers as necessary. As the root system expands, move the tree to a larger pot.

14. Clear the area of debris and add natural amendments. Remove any debris from the area and spread a light layer of compost or manure around the tree to help retain moisture.

15. Dig a deep hole that is larger than the tree’s root ball. Find a spot in your yard that is not prone to flooding and dig a hole as deep as the tree’s root ball.

16. Remove the tree from its growing container and place it in the hole. Make sure the tree is standing upright.

17. Fill the hole halfway with soil and add water. Add enough water to make the soil moist.

18. Add more soil when the water drains. Fill the remainder of the hole with soil to the top and add a little more water if necessary.

19. Spread mulch around the tree. Add a three to four inch layer of organic mulch to help keep the soil moist and discourage weeds.

20. Water the tree when the soil is dry. The soil should remain damp, but avoid overwatering.

21. Prune the tree regularly. Prune off any old or diseased branches, and lightly trim the tree every few months to give it a more balanced shape.

22. Harvest the tree several months after it flowers. The nutmeg should be harvested before the outer shell becomes too hard.

23. Keep an eye out for diseases and pests. Diseases such as root rot, leaf curl, and fungus can affect nutmeg, as well as pests like mealy bugs and aphids. Pay attention to any changes in the leaves or stems of the tree and take appropriate measures to treat the issue.

Carving a Model 1911 Colt pistol is a challenging and rewarding task that combines craftsmanship, imagination, and an attention to detail. The resulting gun will be a work of art, and one that many gun enthusiasts and collectors value highly. This DIY guide will teach you the basics of carving a Model 1911 Colt pistol from start to finish.

Start by selecting a blank. This is a piece of suitable lumber that's large enough to trace or draw out the outline of your pistol. You'll also need a bench top bandsaw with a scrolling woodcutting blade; this is the tool you'll use to cut out the basic gun shape from the blank. Additionally, you'll need a spiral cut saw or a die grinder with a spiral cutting bit, as well as a chisel or carving tool.

Next, you'll want to trace the outline of the gun you're replicating; either procure an actual Colt pistol and trace it, or draw it from a template. When drawing, move slowly and precisely to ensure that the shape will be as accurate to the real gun as possible. Once you've finished drawing, position the gun (or template) on the blank so that any large knots fall near the location where the grip meets the action of the weapon.

Using the bandsaw, cut the outline of your pistol out of the blank. Be sure to keep your cutoff wheel perpendicular to the edges so you don't distort the shape of the gun; once you're done, rip the stock to the correct width.

Now you can move onto the details of the pistol. Begin by using a power sander to round the edges of the grips, font of the barrel, and trigger guard, but be careful not to remove too much material. Then, use a sharp knife or carving chisel to cut out any recessed areas, such as the trigger/trigger guard assembly, cartridge ejection port, and the taper underneath the barrel near the muzzle.

To bring the gun to life and give it that realistic look, you'll need to do more detailed work. Use a rasping bit or drum sander on a die grinder to smooth the recesses in the trigger guard, as well as the flats between the grips and the frame. With a cut-off wheel, make the lines in the frame, barrel, and action, as well as any checkering or knurling to make the gun more authentic looking. Finally, use the same tooling to shape and carve the contours and curves of the frame, action, and barrel of your gun. 

Once the carving is complete, sand the gun with a medium and then fine grit sandpaper to give a smooth, finished surface. Finally, you can apply a stain or finish of your choice to protect the wood and give it a professional-looking color.

Creating a Model 1911 Colt pistol is a time-consuming, but highly rewarding, exercise in artistry and craftsmanship. Follow these steps carefully, and you'll have a result that looks beautiful and is sure to impress your peers.

How to Make Sidewalk Chalk with Cornstarch

Making your own sidewalk chalk is an easy and enjoyable craft for the whole family. It can also keep your kids entertained outdoors when the weather is nice. With a few simple ingredients and a bit of creativity, you can make unique pieces of sidewalk chalk art that will brighten up any garden, driveway, or sidewalk. Here's how to make sidewalk chalk with cornstarch:

Start by gathering your supplies. You'll need cornstarch, water, tempera paint, powdered drink mix, baking soda, food coloring, a squeeze bottle, and a spray bottle with white, distilled vinegar.

Begin by preparing your colored chalks. In a large cup, combine 1/3 cup (40 grams) of cornstarch and 1/3 cup (80 milliliters) of water. Stir in 1 to 2 tablespoons of tempera paint. Carefully pour the mixture into a muffin tin well. Repeat the process for the rest of the colors. Then, tear open 6 small packets of powdered drink mix, and empty them into the muffin tin.

Next, make the chalk base. In a large mixing bowl, combine 3 cups (700 milliliters) water and 3 cups (375 grams) of corn starch. Pour the cornstarch water into each muffin tin well. Stir the contents of each muffin tin well until the drink mix dissolves. 

Then, prepare the squeeze bottles. In a large bowl or cup, combine 1/3 cup (80 milliliters) of water, 1/3 cup (40 grams) of cornstarch, and 1/3 cup (40 grams) of baking soda. Stir in a few drops of food coloring. Carefully pour the mixture into a plastic squeeze bottle. Repeat the process for the rest of the colors, if desired.

Now it's time to use the sidewalk chalk! Fill a spray bottle with white, distilled vinegar. Draw designs on the sidewalk with the liquid chalk. Then, spray the designs with vinegar while they are still wet. For an extra special touch, you can also freeze colored sidewalk chalk. Simply mix equal parts water and cornstarch in a large cup or bowl. Stir some tempera paint into the mixture. Carefully pour the mixture into your ice cube tray or popsicle mold. Transfer the ice cube tray or popsicle mold to the freezer. After several hours, the chalk should be ready to use. 

Now that you know how to make sidewalk chalk with cornstarch, grab your supplies and get creative! Your sidewalk will be sparkling in no time.

Setting up a home PC with multiple modems and phone lines can be a daunting task; however, with a few steps and some extra hardware, it can be done relatively easily. 

The first step is to check with your local Internet Service Provider (ISP) to see if they offer a Multi-Link (ML) account. These types of accounts allow you to connect multiple modems and phone lines together, allowing for more consistent internet access and faster download speeds. If your ISP does not offer ML, then you may have to look at alternatives.

Once you have confirmed your ISP provides ML services, the next steps would be to acquire the hardware for the setup. You will need a functioning computer, along with a second modem (which you can either buy or use the one that usually comes pre-installed in your computer). To connect the modems and phones together, you will also need a phone line junction box.

If you are using Windows XP, you will need to open the dial-up creation dialog. This is the same window you would use to connect to the internet without your ML connection. In this window, you will set up the telephone number you need to access the internet. You will then also need to enter the user name and password for the connection, as well as any other required information. Make sure to check the relevant check boxes in order to ensure the connection runs smoothly.

Once the dial-up connection is set up, the next step is to connect the modems and phones. First, make sure both phones are clear in tone with no static or wavering noises. Then connect one side of the phone line to each phone line junction box. If you are running two computers, then use a CAT5 cable to connect them together via a 5 port Switch.

The next step is to open the connection dialog for your ML account. Here you will need to enable software compression, as well as negotiating a multi-link connection. On one computer, you can also set up a gateway dial out on the advanced tab. 

Finally, double click the icon for your connection and you should be ready to go. You may have to reference your ISP's website for instructions on making sure settings and other information is up to date, as this can be highly variable. With the right hardware, however, you should soon be well on your way to setting up a home PC with multiple modems and phone lines. Good luck!

How to Survive A Levels
It’s no secret that A Levels are a stressful experience, and getting through them can often be a challenge. However, with the right approach, surviving A Levels can be much easier. Here are some tips for succeeding at A Levels.

Firstly, don't choose a college based on friends or your boyfriend/girlfriend who will be attending with you or currently attends there. Whilst it may seem like a great idea to be in close proximity to people you know, most often this will not be a beneficial decision for your future prospects. Focus on the courses available to you and what each college has to offer before you decide.

Secondly, give serious consideration to the subjects you will be studying. Make sure you pick something that you actually have an interest in and something where you see yourself having a future career. It is important to think about what you may want to do next and if a college has the courses and resources to enable you to do that. 

Thirdly, you have to like the place. Consider the lifestyle of the college; do you think you could cope with living here for the next two to three years? Are there enough sports, facilities, societies and good things to do that you feel you get a balance between work and leisure? 

Fourthly, consider what career you might want after completing college. Do you already have an idea of where you would like to go after college? You won't be able to decide for sure what your ambitions are until you've finished your studies, so the best thing you can do is think carefully about what options may be available to you and research them further. 

Finally, make sure you have enough time in your schedule to see your family and friends. It is a stressful and intensive time, and having friends there to support you and share your experiences is an invaluable help. You should make time for yourself as well, although this could mean saying no to parties and other activities at times.

As well as making enough time for yourself and your loved ones, balance your schedule out. Don’t forget to make time for important things such as driving lessons, doctor and dentist appointments, the gym, part time jobs, and hairdressers—all of which can be important to your wellbeing. Think about your day; is there anything you can do to make it more efficient? It may be tempting to try and fit more into your day, but spreading yourself too thinly can be damaging to your mental and physical health. 

Another important thing to do is to ask questions. If you don't understand something, ask immediately. Don't wait. Whenever a teacher covers a subject you don’t understand, be sure to ask them to explain it further or clarify any questions you may have. Also, try to get a copy of the specification for your exam, and go through it to familiarise yourself with it. If there are any topics you are unfamiliar with, you can plan your study time accordingly and work to cover these gaps. 

Finally, before you go to bed each night, reflect on what you learnt in each lesson that day. This could be as simple as making a few notes to yourself, such as concepts you need to research further or topics you don’t understand. Reviewing your learning every night is a great way to review what you’ve learnt and measure your progress. 

In conclusion, surviving A Levels requires effort and dedication. Being well prepared and organised is essential. Make sure you pick the right college for you and choose courses in which you have a passion. Make sure to be balanced; don’t overload yourself with work but also don’t forget to make time for the people & activities you enjoy. If you understand something, ask questions. Don't be afraid to seek help when necessary. Lastly, take time to reflect on your learning every night. With these tips in mind, you will be well on your way to coming out of A Levels a success.

Changing the front disc brakes on a 1998 Toyota Corolla is a common maintenance task that many drivers are capable of completing, with the right tools and knowledge. While there are a few steps involved in the process, it is relatively simple and most jobs can be completed in an afternoon. With the car safely raised up, the old brake pads and the rotor can be replaced in short order.

Things You'll Need:

Socket set
3 ton or higher floor jack
Jack stands
Tire iron
Torque wrench

Step 1: Gather all the tools listed in the "Things You'll Need" section, as well as any other tools you think you may need for the job.

Step 2: Place the car on the ground and jack it up high enough so the jack stand can fit beneath. Make sure the car is jacked up securely and is on level ground. Use the tire iron to remove the lug nuts from the wheel and take off the wheel.

Step 3: Detach the brake caliper from the mounting bracket. CAREFUL! Do not let the caliper fall off its mount! Once it’s off it can be disconnected from the brake line.

Step 4: Remove the brake pad clips from the caliper mounting bracket, and then remove the rotor by unscrewing the screws holding it onto the wheel studs. Discard the old rotor and put the new one in its place.

Step 5: Use the socket set to put the caliper mounting bracket back on the car and re-attach the brake pad clips to the bracket.

Step 6: Insert the new brake pads into the caliper mounting bracket and then place the caliper back on the bracket using the socket set and the caliper bolts.

Step 7: Put the wheel back onto the car and hand-tighten the lug nuts with the tire iron. Torque the lug nuts to the specifications found in the dealer's manual using the torque wrench.

Step 8: Double check to make sure all the bolts and nuts are in place and firmly tightened. Once you are certain everything is secure, lower the car down so the jack stands can be removed and the job is done.

This guide provides you with the steps you need to complete a brake disc replacement job on a 1998 Toyota Corolla. While the job may sound intimidating at first, with the right tools and proper know-how, it can be completed safely and effectively. Remember to always follow the instructions closely and be extra cautious when working with the car's brakes, as mistakes can have costly and dangerous consequences. Happy wrenching!

How to Use a Sauna Safely
Using a sauna can be an incredibly relaxing experience, especially after a long and stressful day. Whether you are at the gym, resort, or spa, a sauna can be the perfect solution for a little bit of peace and privacy. However, relaxing in a sauna does require a few extra precautions and good habits. Here's how to use a sauna safely, no matter your setting.

Be in good health and avoid saunas if you have any high-risk medical conditions. People with certain breathing problems, heart conditions, or skin conditions should avoid using a sauna. If you're pregnant, it is best to avoid saunas during your first trimester. Talk to your doctor if you have any questions regarding your specific condition.

Drink two to four glasses of water before going into a sauna. Your body needs to be well-hydrated before spending time in a sauna. Avoid sugary and alcoholic beverages at all costs, as they will make you more prone to dehydration.

Bring a clean, cotton towel to sit on. Not only will you need it to dry off after you get out of the sauna but it also provides a layer of protection against bacteria and germs that may be present.

Do not wear anything dirty or tight-fitting to a sauna, including things that you wore throughout the day. Make sure that you wear something loose fitted and bring a change of clothes with you for after the sauna.

Skip on the creams, lotions, and jewelry. Not only are these items almost impossible to clean and maintain in a sauna, they can also cause further skin irritations.

Be well-rested and don't go in after a big meal. Spending time in a sauna will cause your body temperature to rise, so if you have just eaten a big meal or haven't gotten enough rest, your body might not be able to handle the increase in temperature.

Bring a friend with you. While the sauna is a very peaceful and personal experience, it is still a good idea to bring a friend with you. Not only can having a sauna buddy help to keep you extra safe, but it can also make the experience more enjoyable.

Read the instructions to the sauna that you're using. Every sauna is different and has its own instructions for use. Taking a few extra minutes to read these instructions can help to ensure your safety as well as maximize the health benefits.

Use a lower temperature, especially if you are new to using saunas. The maximum allowed temperature in Canada and the United States is 194°F (90°C). Some European countries allow much higher temperatures, which can be unsafe, especially after longer periods of time.

Limit your experience to 15 to 20 minutes at the most. It's okay to get out sooner if you start to feel uncomfortable. Despite its calming effect, spending too much time in a sauna can cause serious side effects.

Get out immediately if you start to feel dizzy, nauseous, or lightheaded. Spending too much time in a sauna can put you at risk of heat stroke, which can be a very serious condition.

Cool down slowly after the sauna. You can do this by drinking some cold water or simply sitting in a cooler room.

Rest for at least ten minutes after getting out of a sauna. Your body needs time to adjust before any physical activity and this is especially true after a sauna session.

Follow up with a shower, but skip on the soap. Soap and shampoo can dry out your skin after a sauna.

Drink two to four glasses of water after getting out of the sauna. Your body loses a lot of water through sweating, so you will need to replenish that water quickly.

Consider eating a salty snack after leaving the sauna. Eating salty snacks will help to replace the minerals your body loses through sweating.

Keep your sauna clean to prevent the buildup and spread of bacteria. Make sure to bring a few clean rags with you and wipe down the benches after you use the sauna. If you are at a spa, it's usually a good idea to bring your own towel and leave it there for future use.

By following these simple steps, you can ensure a calm and relaxing sauna experience no matter where you are. So take advantage of the therapeutic effects of the sauna, just make sure you do it safely!

How to Stay a Christian in a Public Setting
Staying true to your Christian values can be difficult in a world that is often quick to criticize or mock faith. But it is possible to remain a Christian in a public setting without becoming isolated or compromising your values. Here are some tips for doing just that.

First and foremost, remember that since you are already a Christian, you are not going to get high on the social ladder. That doesn't mean, however, that you won't be popular at all. With prayer, you will find the best friends and that’s as popular as it gets.

Second, try to read the Bible and pray every day, even if it means waking up at 4am! Knowing the Word will help guide you in the public setting and, of course, prayer will place you in God's presence no matter where you are.

When you enter a public setting, attempt to be as innocent as a dove, yet wise as a serpent. People will still tease you about being Christian. Despite that, try to stay humble and remember why Jesus Spirit is within you.

If you can find a strong Christian adult from church to pray for and with you, then you can find comfort in stressful situations. This person can also help you confront your public obstacles with an even greater force than what you usually would.

In school, it's especially important to find other Christians with whom you can associate fully. Rallies, support groups and bible studies are all good ways to meet people who share the same values and perspectives. If there are no activities like this available, you can always attend church services or even start your own group!

Another way to stay a Christian in a public setting is by keeping yourself steeped in the Scriptures, particularly in the New Testament Gospels. You can do this by having devotions every day to keep yourself grounded and focused on God. Also, it’s recommended to find and use the most accurate translation of the Holy Bible that is at your own reading level.

Finally, it is important to assess your own heart and actions. What makes you “unlovely” and how can you change that? By calming yourself (through prayer, yoga, exercise or other techniques) and visualizing Jesus standing beside you, the answer will come naturally. Open your heart to why he loves them and pretend they are your own beloved children, animals or projects. Keep in mind WWJD—What Would Jesus Do?—and keep up the conversation between yourself and God. How to Become a Videographer
Becoming a professional videographer can be a fulfilling and rewarding vocation. It takes hard work, dedication, and a great deal of practice to become a successful videographer. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to become a videographer:

1. Get a high school education. To become a videographer, you will need to have a solid foundation in the basics of video production. Make sure to take classes in media, art, film, and computer-based production classes that allow you to explore and develop your skills. These foundational skills allow you to better understand and navigate the world of video production.

2. Get a college degree. If you want to be taken seriously as a professional videographer, it is important to get a college degree with a focus in Video Production. Not only will this provide the knowledge you need to be a successful video professional, but it will better equip you to apply for jobs or internships. The education you receive should include classes in camera work, lighting, sound production, scriptwriting, and post-production. 

3. Learn everything you can about video equipment and software. As a videographer, you will constantly be working with camera equipment and editing software, so it’s a good idea to start practicing with these right away. Take the time to learn about the latest technologies in gear, camera operation, and video editing.

4. Look for internships or apprenticeships. If you’re planning on making a career out of becoming a professional videographer, a great way to gain experience and knowledge is by taking on internships or apprenticeships. Not only will this help you learn more about the field, but it will provide invaluable industry connections. 

5. Become certified, if desired. If you’d like to become certified in videography, you can earn certifications from The Society of Professional Videographers, the National Institute of Video Arts, and the Royal Photographic Society. Although certification is not required, it can demonstrate your expertise within the field and help you garner more respect within the industry.

6. Plan before shooting. Spend some time sketching out your ideas before you film any subject. Planning ahead ensures that you’re able to capture the desired shots and content right off the bat. When planning, make sure to create a shot list of the angles and shots that you will need.

7. Practice taking different kinds of shots. Becoming a great videographer requires you to constantly practice taking different kinds of shots. This includes everything from close-up shots, wide shots, point-of-view shots, dusk shots, and more. Continue to practice and hone your technique to make sure to get the most effective shots. 

8. Utilize different camera moves. A stationary camera pointed at a single subject can be simple and effective, but it can also get a little boring. Incorporate different camera moves, like pans, tracking, and zooms into your videography to make your videos interesting and engaging.

9. Incorporate a variety of camera techniques. Getting creative with your camera techniques used to be necessary for a good video. Nowadays, more and more styles of shooting are becoming available, such as steady-cam, time-lapse, or drone shots. These types of shots require careful planning and skill, so practice as much as you can.

10. Practice using the “wide, medium, tight” method. This technique is a proven one to help you get good footage of many different kinds of subjects. Wide shots are generally used to establish the setting, while medium shots are used to add visual interest, and tight shots are used to focus in on a subject or object.

11. Experiment with editing. Utilizing the software and equipment that you have, try arranging your raw footage in various ways for practice. Learning about the basics of video editing will help you become a more well-rounded videographer and add an extra set of skills to your arsenal. 

12. Build a portfolio. Once you have started producing some strong, edited video footage, you should assemble a portfolio of your best work. This is a great way to show potential clients what level of quality you can provide and the type of projects you can create.

13. Join a professional organization. There are several professional organizations for videographers, such as the Guild of Television and Film Producers or the National Association of Broadcast Employees and Technicians. Joining and networking with other organizations can help you stay up to date on the latest developments in the industry.

14. Look for jobs. Start applying to local video production companies or looking for independent freelance videography jobs. You can also post your services on websites like Craigslist or advertise on social media.

15. Utilize social media to create a brand for yourself. Using social media to advertise your company or services as a videographer is key to getting clients. Create your own portfolio website, use platforms such as LinkedIn or Instagram to promote yourself, and create a niche for yourself.

16. Explore alternative careers. Not every person that is trained as a videographer becomes one, or remains one forever. There are several career paths you can take with a background in video production, including becoming a cinematographer, a filmmaker, an actor, or a media coordinator.

17. Attend conferences and professional meetings. Joining professional organizations can help you stay up to date on the latest developments in video production technology. Keep an eye out for conferences and workshops related to the field to make connections with other professionals and stay informed.

18. Take workshops. Workshops are a great way to immerse yourself in the world of video production and hone your technical skills. From getting the basics of shooting down to mastering advanced editing techniques, there are plenty of workshops to choose from that will help you become a better videographer.

19. Try to win contests and awards. The best way to catch the public’s attention is to win awards or get recognized in various festivals. Entering your best work in contests can help boost your reputation as a videographer and increase the recognition you get for your work.

20. Be creative. Above all, the most important thing to remember when becoming a professional videographer is to be creative. As a videographer, the sky is the limit. There are so many ways to approach a project and so many unique ways to showcase your talent. Keep an open mind, experiment, and have fun!

How to Install Neon Lights'

Installing neon lights under the car is a popular way to spice up the look of your ride, and you don't have to be a professional to do it. You can do this yourself with a few simple steps and the right neon light kit. 

First, obtain your under car neon light kit, all the tools, and other supplies you will need for the installation. This will save you time and make the process smoother. Make sure to read the instructions of your light kit so you are familiar with the installation procedure.

Second, disconnect the vehicle's battery. Doing this will prevent any shock or electric discharge from occurring. If your car was just running, wait for several minutes so that the alternator can cool down before disconnecting the battery. 

Third, find the best location for your neon light tubes. It's best to keep them out of sight of the outside of the vehicle as this will give your car a cleaner, more stylish look. Make sure the location you pick can accommodate the needed tubing and wiring.

Fourth, raise up your vehicle with a lift or jack, and make sure the vehicle is secure. You don't want the car to move around on you while you're installing the neon lights. If you don't plan on lifting the car, you can use an adjustable jack stand to support the car while you do the installation.

Once the car is raised and secure, place the neon tubes on the chassis of your vehicle so the lights are not visible on the outside. You might need help from a friend to hold the tubes in place while you secure them to the chassis.

Fifth, install the neon light tubes on the chassis for 1 side of the vehicle. Make sure to mark the center points for each tube for accuracy. Once marked, use a center punch to create a small dent in the metal. Next, drill holes at each center-punched location for the mounting brackets. Make sure to choose a drill bit sized correctly to fit each screw included in your kit.

Sixth, screw the kit-provided screws into the holes. If necessary, use a level to make sure the mounting brackets are aligned properly. Then, connect the wires inside the vehicle to each tube, and secure the mounting clips. Be sure to follow the kit's instructions to make sure you don't accidentally short circuit the lighting system.

Seventh, repeat all the steps for the remaining 3 light assemblies. It is important to follow the same instructions for each assembly in order to correctly and safely install your neon lights.

Eight, mount the transformer in the engine compartment. Make sure to follow the directions of your kit so you don't damage any wiring in the process. Cruise Control systems present in older vehicles often interfere with the installation process, so you might need to disconnect this system or move the transformer somewhere else.

Ninth, connect the transformer to the lighting circuit by following the kit's instructions. Make sure all of the connections are tight to avoid an electrical failure. Then, connect the power wire on the transformer to the positive side of the car battery.

Tenth, mount the on/off switch to the dash or other convenient location. This switch can be used to turn on and off the lights without having to open the hood. Finding a suitable place for the switch is up to your preference and the type of vehicle you have.

Eleventh, complete additional wiring if instructed by the kit. This will depend on how you are mounting the neon lights, and the complexity of your system. Again, make sure to reference the instruction booklet; improper wiring can cause damage to the car or even a fire hazard.

Twelfth, reconnect the negative battery cable. Check for a spark when doing this to make sure the cable is installed correctly.

Once you have done the above steps, your neon lights should be installed correctly. Test all connections and components by turning on the car's headlights. If everything is working, the neon lights should turn on. Congratulations, you have just installed your own neon lights!

How to Delete Protected System Fonts in Windows 7
We all know that there are certain system fonts that are required for Windows 7 to run correctly. The problem is, those fonts can't be easily removed since they are protected by the system and require certain permissions to properly remove them. In this guide, we'll show you how to delete any protected system fonts in Windows 7 and ensure they don't bother you ever again.

First, you need to determine if the font actually is a protected system font or not. To do this, open the Registry Editor (type "regedit" in the start menu search box and hit enter). Then, on the left side of the Editor, open the folders HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE → Software → Microsoft → Windows NT → CurrentVersion → Fonts. On the right side of the window, you should see a list of all the installed fonts. All system fonts are noted with either a "(TrueType)" or "(TTF)" tag on the end of their names. Make a note of all the protected system fonts you want to delete.

Once you've determined the fonts you want to remove, open any program in which you can change the font. Then, navigate to the folder C:\Windows\winsxs. You should see a long list of folders, scroll about a fifth of the way down and you should see a series of folders beginning with "amd64_microsoft-windows-font-truetype-", where  is the name of a font. Right click on the folder containing the font you want to delete and select "Properties".

Click the "Security" tab and click the "Advanced" button at the bottom of the window. Click the "Owner" tab in the resulting window, then click "Edit". Open the folder's properties again (right click on it and select "Properties"), click the "Security" tab, and click "Edit". Select the account you chose in step 11, check the box under "Full control", and click "OK". Exit the Properties window.

Now that the permissions have been changed, you can delete the font file and folder. To delete the font file first, right click on it and select "Delete". Then delete the parent folder containing the font. Once you've done that, open the Registry Editor again and delete the font's entry. 

Finally, restart your computer to ensure that the font is no longer present, and you're finished! With the above steps, you should have no problem deleting protected system fonts in Windows 7. How to Prevent Pneumonia
Having a healthy lifestyle and taking steps to keep your immune system up are key to preventing Pneumonia. This article will outline 10 key steps to take to reduce your risk of getting Pneumonia. 

Firstly, stay away from other sick people. Being around people who are sick increases your risk of coming down with something yourself. If you are in contact with someone who is ill, try to avoid tight spaces or person-to-person contact with them. 

Second, wash your hands frequently. This is one of the easiest but most effective ways to prevent Pneumonia. Your hands come into contact with many objects and people each day, and keeping them clean is essential if you want to avoid getting sick. Make sure to scrub your hands for at least 20 seconds using warm water and soap. 

Thirdly, stop smoking. Smoking has been linked to an increased risk of Pneumonia, as well as many other serious illnesses, so it's important to quit any time you can. If you're having trouble quitting, there are many programs and resources available to help. 

Fourth, live a healthy lifestyle. Eating healthy, exercising regularly, getting enough sleep, and drinking plenty of fluids are all important when trying to avoid Pneumonia. Eating a balanced diet with lots of fruits and vegetables will help your body stay as healthy as possible and fight off any infection. 

Fifth, get enough sleep. Adults need to get between 7 and 8 hours of sleep each night to stay properly rested. When our bodies don’t get enough rest, it can weaken the immune system which increases the risk of contracting a respiratory illness such as Pneumonia. 

Sixth, know the symptoms of pneumonia. Symptoms can include a cough that produces greenish or yellow mucus, chest pain, fever, and shortness of breath. If you are experiencing any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. 

Seventh, know if you have any major illnesses. Having a weakened immune system due to an existing illness, such as HIV or diabetes, increases your risk of getting Pneumonia. It’s important to be aware of any underlying issues you have and be extra vigilant when it comes to looking after your health. 

Eighth, consult a doctor if any of the symptoms of Pneumonia appear. If you’re experiencing any of the symptoms mentioned above, or think you may be getting Pneumonia, it’s important to contact a doctor right away. Early diagnosis and treatment can make all the difference in avoiding any serious health complications. 

Ninth, get vaccinated. Children will typically get the pneumococcal vaccination, which will help their white blood cells learn how to recognize and fight infections like Pneumonia. It’s important to make sure your vaccinations are up to date to help your body fight off Pneumonia. 

Lastly, schedule routine checkups. Regular checkups are one of the best ways to maintain a healthy lifestyle and prevent Pneumonia. In addition, getting preventive care means that if any symptoms of Pneumonia do appear, they can be diagnosed and treated quickly. 

Following these 10 steps can help you reduce your risk of getting Pneumonia. You should also take other steps such as drinking plenty of fluids, taking acetaminophen to reduce pain and fever, and getting plenty of rest when you are sick to keep your body as healthy as possible. If you have any concerns, it’s always best to consult your doctor and get a prescription if necessary.

How to Come in Contact With the Father You Have Never Met

Have you always wondered who your father is, but never met him? Reuniting with a parent you never knew is an emotional and complex process. Here are the steps to take to find, and if desired, reconnect with a father you have never met.

Search for your father. Depending on his circumstances, he may have moved away after you were born, left the town before your birth, or passed away. If you do not have his name, there are several online companies offering services to help people search for their biological parents. You may also be able to access many public records such as census data, government or court records, marriage or death certificates, obituaries, and military records that can provide you with a starting point for your search.

Research relevant state or national laws. Laws and regulations vary from state to state and country to country, so researching the laws of the place where your father may have lived or where your parents married, if they did, can help you access information about your father that would otherwise be unavailable.

Search adoption or reunion registries. Many organizations provide reunion services, and often keep lists of birth parents who wish to be contacted or who are searching for their children. Searching the lists can give you information about your father and your possible siblings. If you don’t already have it, you will need your birth certificate or adoption papers in order to be allowed to search the lists.

Talk to relatives in order to assemble information about your father. If your mother is still living, she may be a good source of information. Your siblings, uncles, aunts, and grandparents may also remember stories about your father and the circumstances of your pregnancy. If your father lived with your mother for a time, neighbors or other people who knew them may also be able to provide information.

Hire a professional or volunteer searcher. Hiring a professional can give you quick results, and can also provide you with a detailed report of your father’s whereabouts. Alternatively, look into volunteer searchers who specialize in reuniting birth families. They are often non-profit, and charge less than professional services.

Decide whether you want to meet your father. Meeting someone you don’t know can be extremely nerve-wracking. Before making contact, imagine all the possible outcomes and consider if meeting your father is something you really want.

Prepare yourself emotionally. No matter what the outcome, you will be likely to experience a range of emotions, so make sure you are in a good emotional space before initiating any contact. Consider talking to a counselor or spiritual advisor who can help you to move through any difficult emotions and prepare you to handle whatever conversations you may have with your father.

Think about what your hope to get out of meeting your father. Are you hoping that he will be an integral part of your life? Are you just looking for answers? Knowing what you hope to get out of meeting your father will allow you to be emotionally prepared for whatever outcome may occur.

Avoid fantasizing about your “ideal” father. The reality of meeting someone you never knew could be very different from what you imagined. Be prepared to accept what you find and be flexible in your expectations.

Don’t share too much too soon. When meeting someone for the first time, avoid telling too much too soon. Take things slowly in order to get to know the person you are reuniting with and to allow the relationship to develop naturally.

Arrange a meeting with your father. When meeting an estranged parent, it can be helpful to choose a neutral location. Consider meeting in a public place with friends or family members, or in a lawyer’s office.

Ask questions. Ask your father questions about his life. Give him the opportunity to explain the situation from his perspective and be open and honest about your expectations.

Don’t make grand plans for the future. Reuniting with a parent often brings high expectations, however, it is better to take a gradual approach and build up to any formal relationship. Don’t expect things to be perfect from the beginning; your relationship may take a lot of time, patience, and understanding to develop.

Set up a support system for yourself. After reuniting with a parent, it is important to have a support system in order to process your varied emotions. Consider talking to a therapist, a spiritual advisor, or a close family member or friend who can provide you with emotional support.

Don’t let a disappointing first meeting define the relationship. Reuniting with a parent can be a complicated and emotional process, and the first meeting may not be all that you are hoping for. Allow for time and understanding in order for the relationship to develop and deepen.

Recognize that there may be a “honeymoon” phase. After initially meeting, it is not uncommon for a father and a daughter who have never met to be overly excited to be reunited. This can cause unrealistic expectations and can be difficult for both parties when the relationship doesn’t turn out as they hope.

Establish limits about each other’s lives. Set boundaries that you both respect, even if the contact between you is limited. Talk about your expectations and interests, and decide whether you want to have a formal relationship or meet on occasion.

Beginning with minimal expectations can help you both to build a stronger, more enduring relationship. Allow yourself and your father to grow in the relationship and build trust before trying hard to deepen the bond.

Allow time for the relationship to develop. Reuniting with a parent is a complicated process, and building a relationship may take time. Allow yourself and your father to get to know each other better and, if possible, avoid pushes and expectations.

Accept the relationship may not deepen or may not last. Although reconnection often carries great benefits, some people find that they do not want a lasting relationship with their father after all. Don't neglect your childhood family while focusing on a newly developed relationship with your father.
