How to Treat Obstructive Shock
Obstructive shock is a medical emergency that needs to be addressed immediately. It can be caused by a variety of conditions, including a massive pulmonary embolism (blood clot in the lungs), tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, and aortic stenosis. In order to treat the shock, it must be determined what is causing it, and then treatment must be tailored to the underlying cause.

Examine for signs of a massive pulmonary embolism. A massive pulmonary embolism may be a cause of obstructive shock, so it needs to be identified and removed as soon as possible. Evaluating for signs of a pulmonary embolism includes screening for slow or blocked blood flow to the lungs, which can be assessed using an echocardiogram or other imaging study.

Evaluate for a possible tension pneumothorax. A tension pneumothorax is another possible cause of obstructive shock. Check for a buildup of air in the lung, which builds up pressure around the heart and can reduce the amount of blood that can enter and leave the heart. If this is the cause of the shock, it needs to be treated as soon as possible by inserting a needle in the affected area to release some of the air.

Watch for symptoms of a cardiac tamponade. A cardiac tamponade is when blood pools around the heart, causing a buildup of pressure and a subsequent inability for the heart to effectively pump blood around the body. Check for low blood pressure, rapid heart rate, muffled heart sounds, or a bluish discoloration of the skin. If this is the cause of the shock, it needs to be treated with a procedure called pericardiocentesis, which involves draining the fluid from around the heart with a needle.

Look for "constrictive pericarditis" as a possible cause of obstructive shock. Constrictive pericarditis occurs when the sac around the heart (called the pericardium) becomes inflamed and tightens with scar tissue over time. Symptoms include shortness of breath when lying down or extreme fatigue. Treatment of the underlying cause of constrictive pericarditis needs to be addressed in order to bring relief to the shock.

Evaluate for aortic stenosis as a possible cause of obstructive shock. Aortic stenosis is when the valve that allows blood to exit the heart becomes tightened, blocked, or otherwise compressed, leading to a reduced amount of blood that can effectively leave the heart with each heartbeat. When aortic stenosis becomes very severe, it can lead to obstructive shock by significantly reducing the amount of blood that can exit the heart, and thus reducing blood flow to the body's vital organs. Common intervention to relieve aortic stenosis issued by cardiologists includes using an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) and/or an artificial heart valve replacement.

When dealing with obstructive shock, it is key to identify and treat the underlying cause. Treat the clot from a massive PE (pulmonary embolism) if this is the underlying cause. For a tension pneumothorax, use needle decompression and a chest tube to help reduce the pressure. If a cardiac tamponade is confirmed, perform pericardiocentesis to drain the fluid around the heart. And if the cause is confirmed to be constrictive pericarditis or a related condition, then it is key to determine and treat the underlying cause. In the case of aortic stenosis, relieve the condition with a IABP and/or a heart valve replacement. It is important to take immediate action when dealing with obstructive shock, as leaving the condition untreated for too long can lead to serious or life-threatening consequences.

How to Make and Shoot Mini Paper Bullets with Rubber Bands
Making your own mini paper bullets and shooting them with rubber bands can be lots of fun and a great way to pass some time. It can be done safely with a little forethought. Here’s an easy-to-follow guide on how you can make and shoot mini paper bullets with rubber bands.

Requirements
Before you start, you’ll need a few items:
-A few squares of thin paper 
-2-4 rubber bands of the same size 
-The index and thumb of one of your hands 

Gather what you need 
First and foremost, you need to round up the assets needed to make the mini paper bullets and the rubber bands to shoot them with. 

Make your ammo
Once you’ve gathered the items you need, it’s time to start making your ammo for shooting. It is highly recommended that you use thick paper. Thin paper will just rip and will not be sturdy enough for a successful shot. Take your thin paper and cut it into chunks that are the size of your fingertips. Heavy duty scissors may be required. Shaping the paper is solely up to you. The more creative the better. 

Take the Rubber band
Now that you’ve made your ammo, you need to get the rubber bands out and ready for the fun ways to shoot. You can decide yourself how tight or how loose the rubber bands should be. Make sure they are of the same size.

Grab a bullet and move it in between the rubber band
Take the mini paper bullet and slowly move it in between the two rubber bands. Take care not to put any pressure on the rubber bands as that can cause them to shoot unpredictably. Make sure to move the paper between the rubber bands all the way up to the tips.

Pull the bullet towards you
Once the mini paper bullet is in between the rubber bands and has reached the tips of the band, lightly pull the bullet towards you. Make sure to do so slowly and cautiously.

Draw, aim and let it go
Once you’ve set up your rubber band and mini paper bullet for shooting, you can take aim at your chosen target. Draw in a breath, aim, and let go. This will cause the rubber bands to slide off the back of the bullet, shooting it forward. 

Repeat the setup for the first method without fitting the bullet
The same method can be used for a second time but in a slightly different way. 

Pinch and place the bullet outside of the rubber band away from you 
For the second method, instead of putting the bullet in between the two rubber bands, pinch the bullet and place it outside the two bands away from you. Make sure to place the bullet between the tips of the two rubber bands.

Draw, aim and fire
Once the bullet is secured in place, draw a breath, take aim at your chosen target and let the bullet fly. As before, the rubber bands should slide off the back of the bullet, propelling it forward.

Repeat the setup as before without fitting the bullet
The same second method can be used for the third time, just without fitting the bullet between the two rubber bands.

Pinch and place the bullet in the same way as the second method
You can pinch the bullet and place it, just like before, outside the two rubber bands. As before, make sure the bullet is placed between the tips of the two rubber bands.

Pull the bullet towards you
In order to get a successful shoot, you will need to pull the bullet towards you. Make sure to do this lightly as a too tight pull can cause the rubber bands to shoot unpredictably.

Draw, aim, release
Once the bullet is in place, take a breath, aim, and release the rubber and bullet at your target.

Setup the rubber band wrapped around your thumb and index finger
For the fourth method of shooting your mini paper bullets, you can setup the rubber band wrapped around your thumb and index finger. Try to make the rubber band as tight as possible on your fingers.

Hold the band closest to you
Once the rubber band is tightly wrapped around your two fingers, hold the band closest to the mini paper bullet.

Move it to the base of your middle finger without any twisting
Move the rubber band away from the bullet and to the base of your middle finger. Make sure you don’t twist the rubber band, as twisting the band can cause the rubber bands to shoot unpredictably.

Place the bullet in front of the higher rubber band
Place the mini paper bullet in front of the higher rubber band. Make sure the bullet is tightly held together in a bullet-like shape.

Pull back the rubber band and twist the band
Once the bullet is in place in front of the higher rubber band,pull back the rubber band and twist the band. This will give the bullet more power and better accuracy when fired.

Pull back, sight, fire
Once the rubber band is twisted and the bullet is in place, pull back, take aim, and let it go.

Setup the rubber usually
The fifth method requires you to again setup the rubber band as you usually do.

Hold the furthest band and take it under the other band towards your middle finger
Once the rubber band is secured tightly around your two fingers, take the furthest band and move it up and under the other band toward your middle finger.

Take your mini-paper bullet
Once the rubber band is securely in place, take the mini paper bullet and fit it into the middle of the two rubber bands. 

Let it go and watch it fly
Once the bullet is securely in place, let it go and enjoy watching it fly.

Hide the bullets
After running out of ammo, make sure to hide the bullets and the rubber band so that no one can find it. This is an important aspect of safety.

Act casual
When shooting the mini paper bullets, make sure to act casual. You don’t want anyone to know what you’re up to. 

Hide the rubber band
Finally, make sure to hide the rubber band after you use it, so no one knows you’re the one behind the shooting. Make sure to keeping your mini paper bullet shooting safe and minimal. Now it’s time to have some fun with your mini rubber band bullets. Enjoy!

Dealing with panic attacks while in school can be incredibly difficult, but there are ways to get through them and maintain a healthy and successful academic career. Preparing for panic attacks can be the best way to manage these episodes, but it takes time, patience, and practice. 

In order to best handle panic attacks while in school, the first thing to do is to alert your teachers beforehand that you may have an episode. While it may sound counterintuitive to tell other people that you might experience a panic attack, it is an important step in being able to handle the episodes. Your teachers can be a great resource in helping you prepare and plan for panic attacks, so having an open communication with them before anything happens is key.

Once you have alerted your teachers, the next step is to come up with a plan. Decide where you will go if a panic attack occurs, and make sure your teachers are aware of your plan. This way, if a panic attack does arise, you will be able to excuse yourself without being disruptive to the class and have a safe place to mindfully take care of yourself.

If you have access to medications that help you manage your anxiety, make sure that you always have them on hand. Many universities have student health centers that might be able to provide medication, so be sure to explore this resource if it is available to you. If you have already started taking medication to help with anxiety, it is important you take it regularly and as prescribed by your doctor.

Once a panic attack has started, it can be difficult to get back to the normal flow of everyday activities. So, start by getting to the agreed upon location that you determined with your teacher. There, you can practice deep breathing or other anxiety-reducing techniques, try to distract yourself from the panic, or talk yourself through it. If the anxiety doesn’t improve, find a responsible adult that you can talk to or reach out for help.

When the panic attack is over, it is important to continue going about your day. Even if it feels easier to just go home or avoid the situation altogether, try to stay in school and finish out the day. It can be beneficial to communicate with your parents and teachers about the incident, and they can help to provide support and even strategies for next time.

Furthermore, if you think that the anxiety is stemming from something else, such as bullying, relationship problems, academic stress, or home life issues, it is essential to speak out against bullying, practice better time management, and make lifestyle changes, like finding time to relax and get organized.

When you are in school, it is also beneficial to take advantage of additional resources. Talk to the school counselor, who can offer support and helpful tips on managing anxiety. Universities also often have counseling centers that can offer further services or talk therapy with an experienced professional. Additionally, speaking with your professors, finding supportive peers, and focusing on taking detailed notes during lectures may help to alleviate some of the anxiety.

Taking the time to build anxiety management skills is important for any student. With patience, practice, and openness, handling panic attacks while in school can be made much more manageable.

How to Get Better at Tennis
Are you looking to take your tennis game to the next level? With the right techniques, practice, and awareness of both your opponent and the court, you will be able to master the game of tennis. This wikiHow article will outline some of the ways you can become a better tennis player. 

Step 1: Learn the right way to grip a tennis racket. It is important to learn and use the proper grip for a tennis racket. There is a difference in the way a forehand and a backhand should be gripped. A proper grip will help you have better control and generate more spin when you swing. 

Step 2: Choose a racket that is suitable for your age and strength. It is important to pick a racket that won't tire you out quickly and one that works with your playing style. 

Step 3: Practice hitting and get to know other players on court by introducing yourself. Being familiar with the playing atmosphere will help boost your confidence and allow you to play better. It's also a great way to make friends and have more people to practice with. 

Step 4: Warm-up and practice playing matches about twice a week. This will help you get into the habit of playing in a game like scenario, plus it will improve your reflexes, reactions, and decision making. 

Step 5: Try out different plans of attack in a match. When playing a match, try different tactics such as: Serve & Volley (serve hard and charge the net position), Chip & Charge (hit a deep ball and charge), Inside-Out Forehand (sidestep around a ball hit to your backhand side and hit it using a forehand stroke), Junk Balling (hit only slices with backspin), and Rally & Wait (exchange ground strokes and look for a hard winner). 

Step 6: Always keep your eye on the ball. It is important to keep visual contact with the ball throughout the entire motion of the shot. This will help ensure that your ball travels to where you intend it to go. 

Step 7: Stretch before and after you play so you don't pull a muscle. Muscles after all have memory, so by stretching you can make it easier to perform movements that can get enhance your game. 

Step 8: Do not rush your shots. It is important to imagine your movements in slow motion during a match. Really focus on getting in the correct position and in control before every ball that comes to you. 

Step 9: Plant your feet just before hitting. Getting in the proper stance will help you generate more power with your shot and it will give you better control.

Step 10: Be aware of your position on the court. Make sure your feet are not overlapping and that you have good balance in each step you take. 

Step 11: Determine your playing style. Are you an attacking player? Do you prefer to play defensive? You have to know your playing style in order to adjust it and become as well rounded as possible. 

Step 12: Be aware of your opponent's game plan. Figure out their weaknesses and strengths so you can tailor your game to it. 

Step 13: Use the whole of the court. This applies to both your positioning and your shot direction. When leading the attack, avoid hitting balls down the middle, which makes it easier for your opponent to react. 

Step 14: When rallying from the baseline, try to achieve as much height over the net as you can without compromising speed. The more height you get over the net, the more difficult it will be for your opponent as they will have to move and readjust their positioning. 

Step 15: Make a conscious effort to use different spins. Try to hit both topspin and backspin shots and vary it from time to time as it will be difficult for your opponents to adjust to. 

Step 16: Don't be afraid to get up to the net. If you get the chance, run up and get closer to the net where you can attack with volleys or half volleys and optimize your winning chances. 

Step 17: Lots of players aren't that concerned about their serve. It's wise to put importance into developing a powerful serve, as a good serve can give you an advantage from the start of the point. 

By following these steps, you can enhance and refine your tennis game. With the right practice and effort, your game will improve and you will eventually become a better tennis player.

Go for it! Start adding your decorations to the front cover of your notebook. Don't be scared to get creative here. Make sure that your decorations coordinate with the rest of the notebook.

Open to the second page. This is the page where you will create your weekly calendar.

Divide the right page into three sections. You want to divide the page into three sections so that there is enough room for all of your classes and activities. Label each section with the day of the week and the date.

Title the left page "After School" or “Upcoming Events.” This side is where you keep track of extracurricular activities, like band practice, sporting events, and dance class.

Draw a table with two rows and six columns. You want a table that is wide enough to accommodate your classes in the right column and notes in the left column. Label each column with a day of the week.

Write the date range above the calendar. You will want to make sure you have dates for the whole school year so that you can plan ahead.

Lay your notebook flat so that you can see both pages. This will make it easier for you to write in both the weekly calendar and the upcoming events section.

Add useful sections in the back of the notebook. You could add a section for homework assignments, a section for notes, or a section for contact information. Use sticky tabs or flags to label the sections.

Write in your assignments. Once you have everything organized and set up, you can start writing in your assignments and extracurricular activities. Make sure that you double-check the dates and times of each assignment.

Making your own school planner is an easy and effective way to stay organized all school year long. Not only will it help you keep track of your assignments and upcoming events, but it will also show off your creativity. With a few supplies and a bit of imagination, you can make a custom school planner that is tailored just for you.

Knowing how to play second base in fast-pitch softball is a key component of any successful team. And while it can take some time to learn and develop the skills needed to take on the position, there are some tips and tricks that can help you get a head start. 

One of the most important things when playing second base is to acquire a glove that is the right size and fit for the position. This is because the range of positions you’ll need to cover are varied and having a glove that is customised for each of them is essential. A well-fitting glove will allow you to have more control and better accuracy when making throws and catches. 

Once you have the right glove, the next step is to practice finding the correct position. As a second baseman, your role is to stand between first and second base and act as a ‘bridge’ between them. This position will provide you with the best combination of support for both of those players whilst also providing you with enough space to make two sets of moves if necessary. 

It’s also important to know the count and where the play is. This is so you can accurately judge how far away the runner on the base is, as well as what type of throw you may need to make. Keeping a close tab on the count will also help you to make better decisions and move quicker to make the play. 

The next step is to understand where it is best to throw the ball, as well as any cut offs or back up moves you may need to make. Generally second basemen will throw the ball to first or third base, so by knowing your field it will make it easier to make accurate throws. Cut offs involve throwing either to first or third depending on where the play is on the field. Similarly, it is important to back up your team elates in case of any bad throws. 

The next part of playing second base is to watch the lead runner closely, being prepared to take action if needed. It’s important to remember to never get distracted when doing this, as the lead runner could potentially gain an advantage. Additionally, it’s important to never forget about cut offs, even if the ball is hit to the outfield. After each pitch thrown by the pitcher, it is important to back up the catcher’s throw – and if there is a runner on second base, don’t go to second for a throw down.

When a batter is walked, it is important to step up to the plate and be ready to cover first base in case of a bunt. Additionally, if you’re in the position to cover second should the catcher make a throw down, then be prepared to do that as well. If the ball is hit to you with runners on base, it will depend on where you are as to whether you throw to first or stepping on second. 

Finally, remember to have fun playing second base. It’s okay to make mistakes when starting out but as long as you remember the basics and keep practicing, you’ll soon be a pro.

How to Prepare for a Members Meeting in a Community Association'

Holding a Members meeting in a Community Association is a crucial part of the organizational process. This type of meeting allows the members of the association to vote on important changes and to discuss the direction of the organization. It is important for organizations to be aware of the applicable regulations and laws governing a member's meeting, as well as how to properly prepare for this type of gathering.

Notice, Agenda, & Proof of Notice

Before the members meeting can be held, the association must give notice and an agenda to all those involved. In the case of a mandatory members meeting, the applicable laws will dictate how far in advance the notice must be given. In some cases, the stated By-Laws may provide for a set time frame for notification. In any case, the notice must be included in the printed or mailed document which includes the agenda. Further, the association may have to provide proof that the notice was given to all individuals associated with the meeting.

Proxies, Ballots, Envelopes

The association may wish to allow members to appoint a proxy to represent them in the meeting. These proxies must meet certain criteria such as having their identification documents signed by the member to authenticate their representativeness of the member. The same procedure must be followed if members wish to cast a proxy ballot. The association must also have a system in place to ensure that all members sign out their ballots in sealed envelopes upon leaving the meeting, and then return them to the meeting in the same envelope.

Alpha Sign-In Sheet

The Board of Directors of the Association should prepare an Alpha Sign-In sheet before the meeting. This sign-in sheet should list all of the members attending the meeting, as well as those members attending via proxy. It should also include the number of shares held by each member, as this will affect the votes each member holds.

Minutes of Last Meeting

In order to best serve the needs of the meeting, it is important for the Secretary of the Board of Directors to keep and be able to present a copy of the minutes and votes taken at the previous meeting. This will enable the members to properly review the decisions made by the Board.

Copy of Documents

The association must also have copies of the documents which will be discussed at the meeting available for all the members. This includes the By-Laws of the Association, the Reports of the Officers and Committees, and any other document which will be discussed at the meeting.

Copy of Last Financial Statement

It is important for the membership to be kept abreast of the financial condition of the association. Therefore, before any vote is taken in a members meeting, they should have the most up-to-date financial statement available.

Law Procedures on Elections

The state statutes and By-Laws of the Association must provide for the election procedures specific to a members meeting. In most cases, the Board of Directors will be elected by a majority vote of the members present. The procedure for holding such an election should be clearly provided in the By-Laws and the state law.

Ballot Box

The ballot box should be present for the members to submit their ballots or proxies. In some cases, the Board of Directors may wish to place the ballot box in an area which is not within view of the members during the voting process.

Signature & Corp. Report of Officers & Committees

At least two officers of the Corporation must sign the report which will be presented to the members. The report must include all of the reports of the officers and the committees, including a review of any actions taken by the officers or the committees during the preceding year.

Materials for Minutes and Sign-Ins

The Secretary of the Board of Directors must prepare the necessary documents and have them available at the meeting for recording the proceedings and the votes taken at the meeting. The materials which will need to be prepared include a Minutes form, an Alpha Sign-In sheet, and any other forms which may be necessary.

Extra Pencils, Batteries and Tapes

Before the meeting it is a good practice to check the organization's level of supplies. Make sure the association has enough pencils, batteries, and tapes to be used in the members meeting. It is a good practice to provide extra supplies since they can come in handy during a technical problem.

In anticipation of a membership meeting, check your association's By-Laws, review the state statutes concerning membership meetings. Any committee which will be participating and or helping to run the meeting should be formed and or informed of their specific duties. Begin your preparation now in order to insure for a well run annual members meeting. Formulate an agenda in advance containing the topics which will be discussed and have documents ready and available that will facilitate the discussion. Pamphlets or handouts related to the topic should also be prepared to be distributed to members. Make sure the facility where the members meeting will be held is available and appropriate for the number of members attending. Make sure all of the necessary audio-visual equipment, boards, markers, and materials are available for the member's meeting. Create a reasonable timeline and plan each step of the meeting thoroughly in order for it to run smoothly. Finally, designate leaders for the meeting, assign duties, and make sure their schedules are coordinated. Taking the time to properly plan for the members meeting will help create an atmosphere of unity and progress within the association.

How to Be a Rainmaker
Making money in the business world is often referred to as "being a rainmaker". A rainmaker is someone who creates new business opportunities and attracts new clients and customers. Rainmakers often have an entrepreneurial spirit and are creative in their approach to finding and dealing with new business. If you want to become a rainmaker or simply create new business for your existing enterprise, here are some steps you can take to get started.

1. Print business cards with your contact information, including your name, company, telephone number and email address. This not only helps you make a great impression when you meet people, but also increases the chances that people will be able to connect with you afterward.

2. Record an appropriate message on your voice mail that invites potential customers and business contacts to leave a message. Introduce yourself with your name and position and invite recipients to leave their name, company, and contact information.

3. Wear appropriate business attire at all times. It's always important to look professional and polished in order to make a great impression. This will show potential customers and contacts that you take your business seriously.

4. Train yourself to treat everybody you meet as a potential business associate or customer, no matter where or when you meet them. Even if you're just waiting at a bus stop or walking down the street, you never know who you'll end up meeting and having a conversation with.

5. Maintain a positive, informative but approachable tone in all your communications at all times. Connect in a friendly way so that people remember you as professional and knowledgeable as well as helpful and friendly.

6. Educate yourself by attending seminars, conferences and classes about your field of industry, and stay abreast of developments in the news that could affect your business and open up new markets. Make an effort to stay on top of changes in technology and in the news that may impact your business.

7. Be social and active. Attend events related to your industry and network actively. Take advantage of online social networking software such as LinkedIn and other sites to reach out to potential clients and contacts.

8. Inform potential customers of the value of what you're selling. Share information about the benefits of your products or services, either by talking about them or by sending out promotional materials or press releases.

9. Negotiate deals and contracts with interested parties. Make sure that all contracts and agreements are in writing to protect both yourself and the customer.

10. Deliver on all your business dealings. It's important to keep all your promises to make sure that you deliver exactly what you promised.

11. Enquire whether your clients could use your services again. Check in with all your clients regularly to see if there's more business you can do with them.

12. Keep in touch with all your clients, and continue to expand your network both physically and online. Networking is essential if you want to be a successful rainmaker, so make sure to keep your network strong by establishing relationships with new people.

13. Review your own performance regularly. Take a step back and have a thorough assessment of your progress and performance so that you can learn from your successes and failures. With this insight, you can understand the steps needed to take to succeed.

Being a rainmaker is not an easy task. It requires hard work and dedication. As long as you stay informed, organized, and persistent, you will make progress in becoming a successful rainmaker. With the right skills and knowledge, you can make life better for your business and for yourself as you make more money.

How to Identify a Victim of Child Abuse
Identifying a child victim of abuse can be an extremely sensitive process that requires careful consideration and respect for the child’s emotional and physical safety. In order to understand how to recognize a child who may be the victim of abuse, it is important to be aware of the various types of abuse, know the signs of abuse, and have a basic understanding of how abuse can affect a child’s mental and physical health. 

Recognize symptoms of physical abuse. Physical abuse can take many forms, such as bruising, broken bones, burns, and other physical marks or injuries. While these are signs of physical abuse, it is important to remember that not all victims of physical abuse will have visible injuries. Watch for certain behaviors and ask questions about possible accidents that could be a sign of physical abuse.

Watch for symptoms of emotional abuse. Unlike physical abuse, which often leaves behind visible signs, emotional abuse is often much harder to detect. Emotional abuse may manifest itself as a child exhibiting withdrawn, sad, or overly obedient behavior; limiting their range of emotional expression; or self-harming.

Look for symptoms of sexual abuse. Sexual abuse can be particularly difficult to identify, as victims may hesitate to speak out for fear of embarrassment, guilt, or putting themselves in further danger. Signs of sexual abuse may include an increase in masturbation, inappropriate sexual knowledge or activities, and bedwetting after an age where that is no longer normal.

Identify signs of neglect. Neglect is one of the most common forms of child abuse and is often characterized by a lack of proper physical care for the child, inadequate nutrition or clothing, and inappropriate levels of supervision. This form of abuse can be intentional or unintentional, and is often difficult to spot unless looked at from an outside perspective. 

Watch for any behavioral changes. Many victims of child abuse experience shifts in their behavior that can range from slight to drastic. Common signs of this include disobedience, lying, bedwetting, bed-sharing, and violent behavior. Pay close attention to any sudden changes in behavior that could indicate emotional struggles and struggle to trust those in authority.

Consider changes in the child’s social interactions. While it is normal for a child’s social behavior to vary slightly as they age and interact with different people, drastically different behavior when interacting with those the child is familiar with can be an indication of abuse. Be on the lookout for changes in the child’s relationship with both friends and family members, as well as changes in the kind of activities they participate in.

Watch for any changes in the child's general mood. Signs of a sudden or drastic change in mood or activity levels, such as excessive tiredness, stress or anxiety, or becoming easily irritated or angered, can be indicative of a child who is struggling with abuse. A child may also display an extreme need to seek approval from others, or have a total lack of interest in activities they once enjoyed.

Notice changes in school attendance or performance. A child who is being abused or neglected may frequently be late to class or miss school entirely, and may have trouble focusing on classes. Assignments may go unfinished or the child may be slow to complete them. Pay attention to signs of avoidance of interaction with other students, particularly if the child used to be an enthusiastic participant in school activities. 

Look for self-destructive behaviors. Self-injurious behavior, notably cutting and skin-picking, can be a sign of abuse, particularly in older children or adolescents. Even behaviors such as eating disorders or reckless activities may indicate a child who is struggling with emotional abuse.

Realize that it may not be obvious. Some forms of abuse can be subtle and difficult to detect, and abusers often use threats and manipulation to keep their victims silent. It is important to remember that even if a child does not show visible signs of abuse, it is still possible that they may be suffering.

Check for physical health problems. Abuse can have serious physical consequences, including physical ailments such as infections, illnesses, and chronic physical pain. It is important to pay attention to any physical conditions that the child may be suffering that cannot be explained by other contributing factors.

Pay attention to mental health problems. Symptoms of mental health problems, such as sudden changes in mood and sleeping patterns, panic attacks, and severe anxiety, can also be signs of child abuse. Reach out to the child’s school or a health professional if you become worried about their mental health.

Consider criminal history and violent behavior. A violent history or involvement in criminal activity can indicate a history of abuse. This is especially true if the child does not seem to have any significant connections to the criminal activity, and it is not part of their usual behavior.

Look for social disconnection or isolation. While some people are natural loners and may not prefer to socialize much, someone who was abused as a child may be more likely to reject social advances from others, have a history of broken relationships (such as divorce or breakup of significant relationships), or be unmarried and live alone. This lack of connection to others or attempts to distance themselves from social interaction can be an indication of being a victim of child abuse.

Watch for abnormal stress responses. Abuse can cause a child to be in a constant state of stress, even after the abuse is no longer occurring. This may be manifested as an extreme fear in certain situations or environments, or an overall fear of authority figures or other adults.

Know when to call for help. If you think that a child may be suffering from abuse, it is important to seek help. Contact the authorities immediately if you suspect that the child is in immediate danger, or call your local child abuse hotline to report any suspicions you may have.

Learn about the different types of child abuse. Knowing the various types of abuse can be helpful in recognizing signs and symptoms of abuse and can help you prepare mentally for a difficult and emotional topic. Understanding the different forms of abuse can help identify potential warning signs before they become an issue and allow you to spot potential signs of abuse early on.

Understand misconceptions about child abuse. Common misconceptions about child abuse can lead to a dangerous situation if left unchecked. Be aware of common myths, such as a child who hints at abuse being just “acting out” or “seeking attention”, or an abuser being someone the child knows well or living in a single parent home. 

Research the effects of abuse on children. Take the time to understand what impact child abuse can have on a child’s mental and physical health, and the long-term effects this can have on the child. Knowledge of these effects can give you a better understanding of how to identify potential signs of abuse before it becomes dangerous. Additionally, it is important to be aware of the legal repercussions of abuse so that the appropriate measures can be taken against abusers.

How to Do Well in Your Exams'
Exams can be the source of a lot of stress for students. Even though they may cause anxiety, you can do well in them if you follow certain steps and strategies. The key is being prepared and organized before you ever step foot in the exam room.

Before the actual exam, make sure that you pay attention in class. Paying attention in class can give you an advantage in the exam because it helps you remember terms and concepts that you may not know or remember if you just study without paying any attention. In addition, taking good notes is essential. This way, when you are studying for the exam, you can refer back to the different notes that you have taken about the material and it can help you remember better.

Another important step to prepare for an exam is to study smart, not hard. Spend a few minutes each day to read over the material that you need to remember for the exam. Try to make sense of it, and imagine that you are connecting the different ideas together. If you have the time, take half an hour each day to focus on one particular topic. Try to use simple language and explain each fact in terms of all the different relationships that it has with other facts. This can help your understanding of the material deeper and more coherent. 

It's also important to take breaks after studying. Studying can cause your brain to fatigue, and taking breaks can help you make the most effective use of your temporal memory. You can also try reading out loud the concepts that you have just learned. This can help you remember better and test the level of your comprehension. Additionally, taking practice tests can also help. It's different than just reading the material because it puts the knowledge to the test and helps you understand which areas you are stronger or weaker in.

If you really want to do well in your exam, it's important to take good care of yourself. Try to get a good night's sleep before the exam and eat foods that can help fuel your brain. It's also very important to avoid last-minute cramming right before the exam. The information that you studied before will be more useful for you. Also, it's key to not let yourself get stressed out because this can impair your ability to remember the information.

Try to stay positive throughout the entire process. Don't listen to people who tell you that you will not do well in the exam. Believing in yourself and remaining confident can help make a difference in the end. Also, make sure to answer all the questions even if you don't know some of them. When doing multiple-choice questions, make sure that you cross out some of the answers that don't make sense or are unlikely to be the correct one.

After you finish the exam, try not to talk about it with anyone. Take a break and focus on something else. It's also important to stay calm and believe that you did your best and that your results will be great. After you receive your papers, make sure you read the questions that you got wrong and try to learn from your mistakes. This will help you do better on any future exams that may come your way.

When it comes to outfitting your child for snow fun, it’s important to make sure your little one is well protected from the elements. A snowsuit is essential for young children’s enjoyment of snow and outdoor winter sports; it will ensure that they stay warm and dry while playing outside. 

Snowsuits come in a variety of styles and materials, such as one-piece suits, two-piece suits, nylon, polyester, down, flannel, and taffeta. When looking for the perfect snowsuit for your child, it’s important to consider their activities and the temperature range they will be exposed to. 

For young children who will be exposed to snow and very cold weather, a one-piece snowsuit is the best choice. One-piece snowsuits are especially beneficial when dressing a baby or a toddler who is not very active yet. Dress your child in a long sleeve cotton shirt and pants, and then put them in the one piece suit. It will be more difficult to get your child out of a one piece than a two piece suit, but it will ensure their comfort and warmth.

When looking for a two-piece snowsuit, it’s best to get one for an older child who can use the bathroom on their own. When layering children in two piece suits, the layers should include a cotton base layer in order to wick away moisture. Also, be careful how long your child plays outside in a two piece snowsuit, as they can become wet and cold more quickly.

The fabric of the snowsuit is also important to consider. Nylon is a waterproof, lightweight, and affordable material that’s popular for snowsuits. However, polyester is only water resistant and not very breathable. For better protection, Polartec is a great choice and is warm, lightweight, and wind and water resistant; flannel is also comfortable and keeps heat in. Down is a great lightweight option, but only for children in a more humid climate who won’t be too active and sweat. Finally, taffeta is more expensive than down but is durable, lightweight, and warm. 

When you’ve found the perfect snowsuit fabric, make sure to look for one that is water resistant or better yet, waterproof. Furthermore, it’s suggested to buy a snowsuit one size larger to allow for more room in order not to constrict your child’s growing body. And of course, it is essential to have your child try on the snowsuit before purchasing it. Look for cuffs that fit tightly around your child’s ankles and wrists, and have them wear close fitting hat that covers their ears. A neck warmer or scarf should also be wrapped around your child’s neck, and they need socks, gloves, or mittens (depending on age) and snow boots if the snowsuit does not have them attached. 

Finally, there are a variety of places to get a snowsuit for your child: local shopping malls, sporting goods stores, online shopping, etc. With the proper research, consideration, and care, you can ensure your little one has a safe and enjoyable time in the snow.

Having a leaking heart valve can be a serious health issue that requires medical intervention. There are a variety of treatments available, depending on the type and severity of the heart valve leak. Understanding the options available to you can help you decide on the best course of treatment for your particular situation.

Medications

In some cases, medications may be prescribed to treat the leaky heart valve. Digoxin (Lanoxin) is a prescription drug that helps increase the heart’s pumping power and decrease how much blood it needs to push through the heart. Anticoagulants, such as warfarin or aspirin, may be taken to reduce your risk of blood clots forming on the valve. Statin drugs may be taken to lower your cholesterol levels. Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) are a class of drugs that may be useful in reducing the pressure in the heart and improving the flow of blood. ACE inhibitors may also be used, assisting with the easing the heart’s workload, decreasing the amount of fluid in the body, and helping blood flow more easily. Beta-blockers can help your heart beat slower and with less force, preventing it from having to work as hard. Finally, diuretics can be taken to help remove any excess fluid from your body.

Surgery

In some cases, surgery may be necessary to repair or replace the heart valve. The type of surgery you have will depend on the type of heart valve leak you have. Surgeries to repair the heart valve may include open heart surgery, where a surgeon cuts through the chest cavity and physically stitches shut any leaky valves. Complete valve replacements may be necessary, replacing either the entire valve or just part of it with a new valve that is usually made from animal tissue. Balloon valvuloplasty surgery is much less invasive and doesn’t require open heart surgery. During this procedure, a tiny balloon is inflated within the defective valve to push the flaps of the valve closer together, reducing the amount of leak.

Lifestyle Changes

In addition to medications and possible surgery, there are lifestyle changes you can make to help manage your heart valve leak. Quitting smoking can significantly reduce the risk of heart valve damage and other heart issues. Eating a low-fat diet can also improve the condition of your heart. Regular exercise can help you reach your weight and health goals. Taking good care of your teeth and gums can be beneficial as well, as it lowers your risk for endocarditis, a serious infection of the heart valve.

Monitoring Your Condition

It is important to stay on top of your heart condition. Provide your doctor with your full medical history so they can better assess you. An echocardiogram can be used to analyze the condition of your valves and the pattern of your blood flow, and an electrocardiogram can be used to detect any abnormal electrical signals from your heart. Your doctor may also order blood work to check for any signs of infection or nutritional deficiencies. If further testing is necessary, you may need to undergo cardiac catheterization, a CT or MRI scan, or a stress test.

By understanding the treatment options available for your condition and following the advice of your doctor, you can take control of your health and find a path forward. Taking steps to manage your leaky heart valve can help you reduce symptoms and get back to living your best life.

Making a tsetse fly trap doesn't have to be a tedious process. With a few simple materials and the right steps, you can easily make your own trap to catch tsetse flies. Here's how it's done:

Start by gathering your materials:
• Blue material (piece C) 
• White netting (piece D)
• Black material (pieces B1 and B2)
• Clear selected trap site of any vegetation 
• Deet-based insect repellent 
• 2 containers 
• Attractant liquid substance (e.g., acetone) 
• Cow urine 
• Transparent polythene bag 
• Two side poles 
• Back pole 
• String 
• Thin sticks 
• Polythene cage 

Now, let's begin assembling your trap:

1. Label the material A,B,C,D, and draw diagonal lines joining the points as shown on the blue material (piece C). Then, fold the material diagonally to form a triangle.

2. For the white netting (piece D), label the material A,B,C, and D, and draw diagonal lines joining the points as shown.

3. For the black material (piece B1), label the material E1,F1,G1,H1 as shown.

4. For the black material (piece B2), mark the material I1, J1, and L1.

5. Clear the selected trap site of any vegetation. Determine the wind direction so as to site the trap facing the windward side.

6. Erect a back pole to guide in setting up of two-side poles. 

7. Fit the polythene cage at the apex of the erected trap and support the cage with strings stretched from thin sticks that are fastened on one of the side poles.

8. Firmly fix two containers, one for carrying attractant liquid substance (acetone) on the ground next to the back pole and the other for carrying cow urine.

9. Apply deet-based insect repellent on the sides of the trap.

10. Fix transparent polythene bag to the top of the trap frame.

You've just made your very own tsetse fly trap! All that's left to do now is to monitor the trap regularly to determine if it's been successful in trapping tsetse flies. Good luck!

So you have decided to learn how to ride a personal watercraft (PWC)! Knowing the basics of PWCs, and their operation, is paramount to your safety and the safety of others. It is important to understand that safety begins before you even make it to the water. Here are some simple steps for you to follow in order to ensure a saferide. 

Before operating, you must secure the PWC lanyard to your life jacket. If your life jacket does not meet US Coast Guard approval, you may be subject to a citation. All operators and passengers must also wear Coast Guard approved life jackets at all times when underway. It is important to also familiarize yourself with the navigation rules of the state. Most states have an age-limit for PWC operators. Generally, the minimum age for operating a PWC is 16 years old.

Once you have gone through the safety steps, you should be ready to launch into the water. Before starting your engine, it is important to look around and make sure the area you will be operating in is free of items that could clog the water intake grate and/or the exhaust outlet. You also want to ensure that the water is at least 3 feet deep when starting/running the PWC. When you launch, it is important to be aware of the fuel level. 

When underway, many new operators forget the basics of responsible PWC operation. Always observe the no-wake zones and idle speeds in residential coves, and never exceed 5 mph. Additionally, pay attention to changing weather conditions. Strong winds and thunderstorms can create hazardous conditions on the water, including choppy waves, sudden wind shifts, and lightning. It is essential to be aware of your surroundings and to navigate around submerged rocks, obstacles, and hazards.

An important part of responsible operation is to also be aware of other vessels on the water. When travelling in a group, it is important to consolidate together and travel as a pack when navigating congested channels and areas. Additionally, be polite and courteous to other vessels. For example, never jump the wake of another boat or linger behind a boat as if they are pulling a water skier. Jumping is prohibited in many areas and most are turned off by water getting sprayed in their boat. Additionally, never weave through congested boat traffic or harass wildlife.

By following these steps and knowing the proper etiquette for operating a PWC, you will be sure to have a safe and enjoyable time out on the water. It is important to remember to be respectful of other boaters and users who are sharing the water with you. Lastly, if you are unsure of something, ask an expert in your area or contact your local Coast Guard station for assistance. How to Catch a Student Cheating on a Written Test
Cheating is a major problem in schools today and catching students doing it on a written test can be difficult. Fortunately, there are measures that teachers can take to prevent cheating and detect it when it is attempted.

Prevention is Better Than Cure
The best way to catch a student cheating on a written test is to ensure that it does not occur in the first place. Remain vigilant to any signs of potential cheating prior to or during the test. Remind the students of the rules and the penalties for cheating before they take the test, and ensure that they will be strictly enforced.

Separating the students or seating them in such a way that they cannot look at one another's papers can reduce the rate of cheating greatly. Also be sure to maintain complete silence in the exam so that whispering can easily be detected.

Keep an Eye Out
The most obvious sign of cheating in a written test is a student glancing at their lap, pencil case or other potential hiding place. Make sure that you are constantly watching the students so you can easily spot unusual behavior.

Another sign of cheating that is not as obvious is when a student wasn't paying attention during class and you had to call their name. This may mean that the student was spending too much time copying someone else's paper. If you suspect cheating, make sure to keep an eye on that student as they take the test.

Maintaining Standards
It is important to ensure that all students are on a level playing field. Make sure that students are allowed to practice the material before the test so they get an idea of what they are doing. If you are given a paper or project from a student which seems to be above their usual abilities, a quick oral test will usually determine if they are actually knowledgeable or if they are cheating.

If the student does surprisingly well on the test and there is no evidence of cheating, congratulate them and tell them that you expect them to maintain the standard. This will hold them to the integrity of honest work and discourage potential cheating in the future.

In conclusion, It is important for teachers to be vigilant of potential cheating in written tests. Remind your students of the rules and consequences before they take the test, and enforce them rigorously. Be on the lookout for suspicious behavior and make sure to recognize honest accomplishment when the students do well. Taking these steps will help ensure that all students get an equal chance to succeed.

The process of choosing a mortgage lender can be complicated and overwhelming, but taking the time to research your options can save you money and give you peace of mind when making such a long-term financial commitment. To help you make the best decision when selecting a mortgage lender, consider the following steps.

Put together your financial portfolio. Before you start shopping around, determine exactly what type of loan you need, and determine what kind of loan terms you are looking for. Gather as much financial documentation as possible (like two years of tax returns, recent bank statements, proof of income etc.), so you can provide accurate information to your prospective lenders.

Refresh your memory of loan terminology. Read up on common loan terminology, such as Fixed-Rate or Adjustable-Rate, so you can intelligently discuss the options with your lender.

Decide what you’re looking for in a mortgage. Consider the size of the loan you are seeking, adjustability of the interest rate, and the length of the loan you are looking for.

Make a list of questions to ask. Print out a list of questions to help you compare lenders. This might include; how long have you been in business, are you a lender or a broker, do you offer in-house financing, are there any hidden fees I should know about?

Ask around for recommendations to reputable mortgage brokers who can give more options by being independent from the lenders and banks. Ask other homeowners, real-estate agents, financial consultants, or trusted advisors for recommendations to reputable brokers.

Ask each prospective mortgage lender what their interest rates are for the type of mortgage you are considering. Be sure to compare the rates across several lenders, as interest rates can vary quite a bit.

Gather the interest rates applicable to various loan terms at each mortgage lender. Interest rates will fluctuate depending on the applicable loan terms, so make sure to compare the rates for the specific loan terms you are interested in.

Request a written explanation of the estimated charges, costs and/or fees that the lender would require of you at closing time. Don't just take the lender's word for it, ask for this information in writing so you can compare the estimates across the lenders.

Confirm that the lenders in question are licensed. Check the licensing for each lender with your state or the National Mortgage Licensing System & Registry.

Think about how helpful each lender seemed. After you submit your request to each prospective lender, consider how quickly they responded and how easy they made it for you to get the information you needed.

Look for lender reviews. Look up online reviews of each lender to get basic customer feedback, and assess how the lender’s website looks and functions.

Try negotiating the fees on the Good Faith Estimate. Shop around and compare fees to find the best all-in cost.

Compare all written documentation from each mortgage lender. Carefully assess the considerations included in each of the estimates and make sure you understand the terms of each loan.

Narrow your possible choices of mortgage lenders. Once you have gathered enough information to make an informed decision, narrow down your choices to the top two or three lenders.

Contact the mortgage lender you’ve selected. Ask questions if you have any remaining doubts, and make sure you understand all of the final terms and conditions of the loan you are going to commit to.

Read the fine print of the mortgage contract before signing. Even after you have made your choice, read every sentence thoroughly. This is an important and long-term decision, so make sure you are completely comfortable with every detail of the agreement. Now that you have taken the necessary steps to choosing a mortgage lender, you can move forward with the confidence that you have made the best decision.

Learning how to recognize a good listener can be beneficial in many areas of your life. Whether you are talking to a friend, seeking advice, or discussing a work-related issue, a good listener will demonstrate certain traits that show they are genuinely interested in what you have to say. Here are the key signs to look out for.

See if the listener is 'in the moment': When you are talking to someone, it can be hard to tell whether they are truly listening or if they are just going through the motions. Pay attention to the listener's facial expressions, body language, and eye contact, as these are all important indicators of whether a person is engaged in what you are saying.

See if the listener is maintaining, or making, eye contact: Eye contact is one of the most crucial components of meaningful communication. A good listener will often make prolonged eye contact as a sign that they are paying close attention to what you are saying.

Look to see if he is responding in any fashion: It can be difficult to tell if someone is listening or not, especially if the conversation is one-sided. Look for signs that the listener is responding with facial expressions or body language.

Note if the listener is actually listening, or interrupting: This is a big one and can be quite telling. A good listener will not interrupt you or jump in mid-sentence; they will let you talk without interjecting or speaking over you.

The Listener Will Parrot Back What You Are Saying When Appropriate: Every once in a while, a good listener will parrot back what you say to indicate they are paying attention and that they are right in your story with you.

The Listener Will Only Finish Your Sentence When Appropriate: A good listener will only finish your sentence when the timing is right, not to try to rush you through your story or to help you out when you are at a loss of words, but to show that they are on the same wavelength as you.

The Listener Goes By the 80% Listening, 20% Talking Rule: A good listener knows that the art of being a good listener (whether that is because they just intuitively know or because they are actually aware of the rule) will listen approximately 80% of the time during the course of the conversation and spend only 20% of the conversation talking.

The Listener Will Keep The Conversation Focused on Your Topic of Discussion: There is nothing more annoying than to open a conversation with someone and they change the topic on you in the middle of what you are trying to express. A good listener will recognize when the conversation is veering off course and will politely redirect the conversation back to the main topic at hand.

The Listener Will Ask You Thoughtful and Open-ended Questions About What You Are Talking About: A good listener will ask you thoughtful questions that will lead you into opening up into further detail about your topic of discussion. These questions will be open-ended and will allow you to explore the topic further.

The Listener Knows How to Empathize With You: When a good listener feeds back how you are feeling, their description of the feeling or emotion will actually match how you are feeling. This empathy can help you feel heard and understood and can also deepen the connection between yourself and the listener.

By noting these signs of a good listener, you'll be more capable of recognizing and appreciating the people that truly have a genuine interest in what you have to say. When you identify someone with good listening skills, you can be sure that you have found a person you can trust with important matters. With this knowledge, you can be sure to seek out those individuals who will be the most supportive, insightful conversation partners.

How to Paint a Metal Bed Frame' is a project that many people find intimidating, but it doesn't have to be. Painting a metal bed frame is a relatively straightforward process that requires several steps, and a few tools, but with a bit of patience, you can have your frame looking like new in no time. 

The first step is to find a good spot to work. Most people will want to work in an area with good ventilation and plenty of room to spread out. A garage, porch, or other large area is best. The next step is to strip the bed frame as much as possible – such as removing any loose or detachable parts.

After your frame is stripped down and your workspace is ready, it's time to start cleaning the frame. Begin by washing the frame with hot water and dish detergent, and be sure to wipe it dry afterwards. Then use medium-fine sandpaper to sand the entire area. Do this even if there is no prior paint or rust on the frame as it will help the paint adhere better. Once the sanding is done, use a tack cloth (found at most hardware stores) to remove any remaining particles from the sanding process. Finally, use a damp, soft cloth to go over the frame one last time.

To ensure the best paint job, you'll want to prop the metal frame pieces against something—like a sawhorse or wall—as you paint them. Begin by spraying on a metal paint primer over the entire surface. Once the primer is dry (follow the instructions on the can for dry time), spray on your base coat of color. Once that is dry, apply a second coat of paint using the same method. This will create a more even, finished look. Depending on the type of paint you're using, you may want to add a third coat of paint or a clear sealer for a smoother finish.

As you are painting the frame, don't forget to spray the bolts and screws, so that the heads will match the frame color. Place the bolts or screws in a cardboard box, heads up, and spray on the matching paint. After each coat, allow it to dry. 

When the paint is finished drying, put the frame back together and you should have a brand new looking metal bed frame. As long as you follow the steps carefully, and take the time to properly clean and sand the frame, you should have a beautiful metal bed frame that looks brand new.

Building a brick wall to your home or garden is not a difficult task as long as you have the right supplies and take a few precautionary steps. Many people are intimidated by the prospect of a such a big project, but it's actually quite straightforward. With the right guidance and materials, you can complete this task in no time.

Before you begin, be sure to select the right type of adhesive for your brick wall. You'll need to consider whether the wall will be built next to your house, in the garden, or somewhere else outside. If your wall will be exposed to the elements, you may need to use a durable adhesive such as masonry cement or mortar.

Once you've chosen your adhesive, you'll need to purchase the appropriate amount of bricks and other supplies. Depending on the height, width, and layout of your wall, you'll need to determine how many concrete blocks, 4 foot by 8 foot cement boards, and other necessary items. 

Next, you'll need to start digging a trench for the foundation of your wall. It's important to make sure the trench is level; you can check using a leveler. Once the trench is complete, drive level wooden stakes into the nearby ground to serve as guideposts for the wall.

When you have the guideposts in place, mix and pour concrete up to the tops of the guideposts. Let the concrete dry before continuing to the next step–typically overnight. 

Gather your other supplies while the concrete foundation dries. You'll need boards, tarps, plywood, wet bricks, a leveler, a hammer, brick jointer, drill, and brick trowel. Lay down tarps or pieces of plywood to catch the mortar, and then sort your bricks into piles.

Now, start laying down your first row of bricks. Test the fit by starting a dry run. This dry run will give you an idea of the height of the wall. To ensure that all the bricks are level with each other, use a clamped line–a string with clamps on either end–on your first guideline.

Once you’ve done the dry run, set the bricks aside to soak in a bucket of water. Wait for the bricks to dry before you lay them in the foundation.

Mortaring the bricks is the next step. Start by adding 1/2 inch of mortar along the base of the foundation. Then, press each brick into the mortar and level it with the first brick. 

Add mortar between the next 2-3 bricks and press them into place. Scrape away any excess mortar with your trowel, and make sure each brick is level with the previous one. 

Continue adding bricks until you have a completed row. 

After completing the first row, move your guideline up to the corresponding marker. This will help ensure that the second row is at the same height as the first row. You may need to use a hammer to tap on the bricks in order to get them to fit evenly.

Since the second row will have the same number of bricks as the first row, you'll need to cut a brick in half to make it fit. To do this, point the sharp end of your hammer above the center of the brick, then tap it firmly until the brick splits. Place the two halves on the opposite ends of the second row. 

Once you've got your pieces and clamps in place, start to lay down the second row. Start by butting your first brick, a full piece, against the two halves you just cut. Then, fill in the rest of the row.

Continue building your wall from the ends inward. Lay each brick in the mortar bed and make sure to add enough mortar to make them level. Consider using unique brick patterns for the top of the wall, such as herringbone, basket weave, or running bond.

Fill in any missing patches of mortar between the bricks along the wall. If you're feeling fancy, use a brick jointer to indent the mortar professionally. Consider other jointing patterns for your wall if you want to make it look neat and even.

Finally, you can also add pillars to your design if you would like. Doing this will offer extra support to your brick wall. 

Congratulations! You've just built a brick wall. With the right supplies and a bit of patience, you can create a wall that lasts for years to come. Enjoy the pride that comes with a job well done.

Making an Eiffel Tower Cake is an impressive way to wow your family and friends, and with the right materials it can be a relatively straightforward process. As with any cake, your first step is to bake two sheet cakes or one large one – whichever your creative heart desires. Then, cut four 12" x 12" (30.5cm x 30.5cm) squares from the sheet cakes to act as the base and middle sections of the tower – the size of the squares will depend on the dimensions of the cake. Use the remaining cake left from the sheet cakes to cut three squares, which will form the sides of the tower.

Once you have the base and middle section shapes, you can dismantle the base and middle section to make it easier to crumb coat each section with its appropriate icing. Since the real Eiffel Tower is gray, use gray fondant for the majority of the cake combined with gray butter cream icing. To separate the two sections and give the cake a more genuine look, use a darker gray for the bottom border of the middle section and roll a brick pattern over it before cutting it into strips and applying them to the edges of the arch.

Once all the sections are correctly iced and prepared, it's time to start adding the different elements. Cover the squares from the base and middle section with the gray and red fondant, alternating between the two colors. Begin the piping details, using food coloring if desired – this is where any bumps or blunders will be hidden! In a uniform fashion, continue to pipe the middle section of the cake and then stack it on top of the base section as displayed below.

For the top portion of the Eiffel tower, use Styrofoam covered with gray fondant. Create a cylinder shape covered in fondant with a small tower at the top, and attach it to the top section of the cake. The size and shape of the cylinder may have to be adjusted to fit the dimensions of the cake – but with a little bit of patience, the perfect-size Eiffel Tower should soon be ready to impress!
