How to Handle Long Layovers at an Airport
Long layovers can seem like an inconvenience when you’re in a hurry to get to your destination, but with a bit of planning, they can actually make for a fun experience. There are many great ways to make the most of a layover at an airport, so you can turn what would otherwise be a boring wait into something exciting. Here are some tips for handling long layovers at airports.

First, think of your long layover as a bonus. The hours spent waiting at the airport can give you a chance to explore your surroundings and get a sense of the local culture, even if it’s limited to the airport. So start by selecting a flight with the shortest layover that fits within your budget. 

Secondly, do some research on the layover airport. Check out its website, and look for local attractions that are close to the airport. If it’s possible, arrange for a few hours to do some sightseeing during your layover.

Another great tip when you’re waiting for your next flight is to sign up for the VIP club. Airports often offer discounts and other special benefits to members of their VIP club. Joining this club will give you access to lounge services and more suited to your needs.

Make sure to carry on luggage that you’ll need during your layover. Have provisions such as snacks, food, and books that will make the wait more comfortable. Plus, having everything you need within reach at all times could save you time. 

Once you’ve landed, find out the exact time your next flight leaves and which gate it’s departing from, by checking with an airline agent or the departure board. You may even be able to change your flight by requesting a switch with the agent.

If you’re travelling with kids, plan ahead to keep them entertained during the wait. Have a few items that can keep them occupied and amused such as toys, books, coloring books, or get them onto the airport’s WiFi to watch a movie or play games on the tablet.

To keep yourself entertained during the layover, bring something to read. If you don’t have a physical book, there are many online communities you can join to download digital versions. Freshening up can also be a great way to break the monotony, so bring along a few skincare items or a change of clothes. As the airport can be an unfamiliar environment, try to stick to the simple and small ones that can fit inside your carry-on.

If you have time, take a walk around the airport. People watching can be a fun pastime and you may even learn some interesting facts. Surf the web during the wait for your next plane, or use the time to get some work done.

Finally, make sure to check on the status of your flight from time to time. When the time comes to board the plane, arrive 45 minutes before the scheduled departure to make sure you don’t miss it. 

To recap, handling long layovers at the airport can be an efficient and enjoyable experience. Select your flight with the shortest layover that fits your budget. Do some research on the layover airport and look for local attractions. Join the VIP club to get special discounts and benefits. Carry on what you need during the layover. Find out the exact time and gate your next flight leaves. Keep the kids entertained during the wait. Bring something to read, freshen up and take a walk. And, check on the status of your flight from time to time. With a bit of planning and these helpful tips, long layovers can be just as exciting as the trips themselves.

How to Burn Fat and Stay Healthy
Burning fat can help you look and feel better, and it can also provide health benefits. If you want to burn fat and stay healthy, the good news is that it isn’t hard; often small lifestyle changes can make a big difference. Here’s a rundown of the basics:

1. Reduce your total calories. This is the key to successful fat loss; to burn fat, you will need to take in fewer calories than you expend. Thankfully, you don’t need to count every calorie; you can just make smarter food choices that are lower in calories than their counterparts.

2. Control your portion sizes. Many portion sizes served at restaurants or even eaten at home are much larger than they should be. If you’re interested in losing fat, you should try to get into the habit of eating smaller portions. To do this, avoid eating directly out of packages and try to serve yourself using measurements, like one-fourth or one-third of a cup. Even splitting meals with friends and family can help control your portions.

3. Eat more healthy fats and fewer unhealthy fats. The types of fat you consume can impact whether your body chooses to burn fat or store it. Incorporate healthy fats, such as olive oil, avocados, and unsalted nuts, into your diet. Also try to avoid unhealthy fats, like saturated and trans fats, that come from processed foods and animal products. Olive oil has shown to be beneficial in reducing fat and cholesterol levels.

4. Reduce or Cut Out Processed Foods. Many processed foods are high in calories, unhealthy fats, and sodium, making them unhealthy choices for weight loss. To reduce the amount of processed food in your diet, start reading nutrition labels. This will help you identify which foods are high in calories and unhealthy fats and which have more nutritious values.

5. Get more fiber. Fiber is a carbohydrate that our bodies cannot digest. It helps fill us up, can help regulate our blood sugar, and can help us lose weight. Fiber can be found in grains, fruits, and vegetables. Studies have shown that fiber can also help reduce the risk of type-2 diabetes as well as heart disease.

6. Drink more water. Water is essential to good health and can also help you burn fat. Researchers have found that drinking plenty of water can boost your metabolism and help you burn more calories.

7. Eat many small meals throughout the day. Eating many small meals throughout the day, like three small meals and two snacks, is better for weight loss than eating one or two large meals a day. This will help keep your metabolism going and it also keeps your energy levels up.

8. Exercise three to four times a week. Exercise is an important part of losing weight and maximizing the amount of fat you burn. While it’s impossible to spot-reduce fat, exercising will help you lose fat overall. Aim for three to four days a week of vigorous exercise, such as walking, running, biking, or swimming.

9. Incorporate strength training into your workout. Strength training is a great way to increase your muscle mass while burning fat. When you gain muscle, your body burns more calories throughout the day. You don’t need to lift heavy weights; dumbbells and resistance bands will work just as well.

10. Do more cardio. Cardio is another term for aerobic or endurance activity. Cardio activities, such as running, swimming, biking, or walking, can help you burn fat and boost your metabolism. Aim for around 30–60 minutes of cardio exercise five times per week.

11. Get more sleep. Adults over 17 should get seven to nine hours of sleep each night, and children from six to 17 should get 10–11 hours. Recent studies have shown that sleep deprivation or those with sleep disturbances are more likely to be obese than people who get the recommended seven to nine hours.

12. Make small but meaningful lifestyle changes. Making small changes in your lifestyle can often result in big changes in your body. Often, even small changes, such as cutting out sodas or eating slowly, can make a big difference. Practicing mindful eating practices and getting enough sleep can also help you lose fat and stay healthy.

Following these tips can help you burn fat and stay healthy. Try to incorporate these activities into your daily life and you should start seeing results. Remember that fat loss takes time, so be patient and consistent. Good luck!

How to Ski
Are you interested in skiing but don't know where to start? Learning how to ski can be both intimidating and rewarding; it requires determination, a keen understanding of the terrain, and the proper safety precautions. While pro skiers make it look like a breeze, learning how to ski is a process that takes time and dedication. This article provides a step-by-step guide to get you skiing in no time!

1. Distinguish Trail Difficulty. Before skiing down a mountain, it is important to understand the difficulty of the trails. Most ski resorts label their trails in a simple system of difficulty. Green-circle trails are for beginners, blue-square trails are for intermediate skiers, and black-diamond trails are for advanced skiers. Knowing the difficulty level of a trail will help you determine your ski route and be more prepared for any terrain and difficulties you may encounter.

2. Know the Right of Way on the Slope. When skiing, it is important to be aware of the skiers around you and their position relative to you. The skiers above have the right of way and must be granted the right to pass ahead of you. It is important to ski with caution and continuously check in case there is any skier coming from behind who has the right of way.

3. Always Stay in Control. Once you start skiing down the slope, it is important to stay in control even when going faster and having a lot of fun. Remember the most important rule of skiing is that it is important to stay in control and avoid sudden movements and turns.

4. Know Your Limits. It is important to only ski trails that are within your abilities. It is important to ski only slopes you can handle and not attempt any runs that are too difficult for your level. Doing so could cause you to injure yourself or put yourself in danger.

5. Don’t Stop if You Cannot be Seen from Above. If you need to stop on the slopes, make sure you can be seen from above, as they are generally safer spots to stop on the run. Stopping in the middle of the run can put yourself in danger if another skier is coming behind you and cannot see you in time to stop.

6. Put on Your Ski Boots. Before you can start skiing, it is important to put on your ski boots. Make sure to make proper adjustments to the boots for a comfortable fit and to help with performance. It also helps to wear a pair of good, warm socks to prevent your feet from getting too cold.

7. Separate Your Skis. Once you have put on your boots, it is time to separate the skis and set them up correctly. Make sure the bindings are tight and that the skis are in the correct position before attempting to ski down the mountain.

8. Step into Your Skis. Once the skis are prepared, step into the bindings and adjust them accordingly to your feet. Make sure they are secured to your feet to prevent any unnecessary injuries.

9. Learn to Take your Skis Off. For beginner's, learning how to take skis off can be a bit tricky. It is important to learn how to take them off when necessary and keep them off when not in use.

10. Enroll in Ski Lessons. Ski lessons are a great way to hone your skills and be able to ski with confidence. It is important to learn the basics of skiing from a qualified instructor and get comfortable with the ski techniques before attempting any complicated trails.

11. Learn to Walk in Skis. ski exercises  such as walking in skis is a great way to familiarize yourself with the equipment and movements used while skiing. Learning how to balance and control your skis without necessarily going down the hill can help improve your confidence and control on the mountain.

12. Know Which Technique is Best For You. Once you start skiing, you will find that different techniques can be used and that they work differently for different people. It is important to know which technique works best for you and to use that technique on the slopes.

13. Assume the Basic Skiing Posture. The basic skiing posture consists of leaning slightly forward and maintaining a good balance while going down the mountain. This posture allows for easier movement and better balance, both of which are very important when skiing.

14. Keep Yourself From Sliding in Any Direction. While skiing, it is important to maintain control and avoid any sudden movements that could cause you to slide in any direction. Keeping your feet close together and leaning slightly forward will help you maintain control and accuracy.

15. Learn How to Stop. Knowing how to stop safely can help prevent any injuries from occurring while skiing. Generally, you can slow down by shifting your weight back and edging one ski out, applying your brakes to help slow you down.

16. Learn How to Turn. Knowing how to make turns is important as it allows you to control your direction and your speed. To do this, you will need to shift your weight to the edge of the ski.

17. Learn How to Fall. Knowing how to fall is a very important skill to have. Knowing how to fall can help prevent any potential injuries from occurring. Generally, you will want to fall to the side and roll toward the ground, ensuring that your body is always moving away from the direction of your fall.

18. Learn How to Use a Chairlift. Going up a chairlift is something that you will likely be doing a lot. Knowing how to use a chairlift safely is key to ensuring that you have an enjoyable skiing experience.

19. Start on the Bunny Hill. The bunny hill is where all beginners should start. The bunny hill is a beginner-friendly area that has an even, gentle slope, making it the perfect place to practice your skiing skills and techniques without risking any serious injury.

20. Ready Yourself At The Top. Once you are ready to ski down the hill, make sure you are ready to start. Check that your skis are placed correctly, that you have your body in the correct posture, and that you are in control.

21. Go Down the Slope. Once you are ready, start skiing down the hill. Remember that speed comes with confidence, and that it is important to ski at a speed that is comfortable for you.

22. Keep Your Weight in the Correct Place. Maintaining the correct posture and pushing your weight in the right direction is key to keeping in control when skiing down the hill.

23. Move On to More Advanced Trails. Once you are confident skiing on the bunny hill, it is time to move on to more advanced trails. Start by attempting the beginner and then the intermediate blue-square trails.

24. Try Skiing Without Using the "Pizza Technique”. The pizza technique is a technique used to gain speed while skiing. Once you are confident skiing without using the technique, it is time to move up to the more advanced intermediate trails.

25. Try Your First Intermediate Trail. If you are ready for a more challenging ride, try your first intermediate trail. Remember to keep your weight in the correct place, as moving too fast on this type of terrain can put you in danger.

26. Stick With the Intermediate Trails For a While. To master the intermediate trails, it is important to ski them regularly to hone your skills and practice techniques. This will help you become a better skier and eventually tackle more advanced terrain. 

27. Attempt a Black Diamond Trail. Once you are an experienced intermediate skier, you can attempt a black diamond run. Before attempting this run, make sure to ski a few blue-square runs first to warm up.

28. Try Skiing the Moguls. Moguls can be challenging, but they are also a great way to practice the technique needed for advanced runs. Skiing moguls can be tricky, but don’t be discouraged if you don’t get it right away. With practice, you can master them and be ready for an even more advanced run. 

Skiing can be fun and exciting, but it is also important to take the time to learn how to ski safely and confidently. Following the steps in this article, you should be able to move from the bunny hill to black diamond runs in no time. Stay safe and enjoy the slopes!

Installing a temporary irrigation system can be a great way to provide water to your lawn or garden without having to establish a permanent irrigation system. However, before dabbling in this project, it’s important to consider whether the cost and labor involved in a temporary system is worth it in your particular situation. Once you’ve decided to go forward, the next step is to decide where and how you will connect to the water source. Then lay out the area you’ll be watering in order to figure out how many sprinkler heads you’ll need and the number of pipes and other materials needed. 

Once you've determined this, choose the type of sprinkler head you’ll be using and look at the manufacturer’s literature to determine the spacing and the water requirements for each head. Next, connect to your water source. To do this, you’ll need to use utility approved devices to control backflow as well as to meter water usage if needed. 

With this secured, run the main lines –– these are the bigger pipes that give water to the branch lines and individual zones (if you need to separate or break the system down for effective watering). The pipes should be laid along the edges of sidewalks or buildings. After that, install adapter tees to the spots where you intend to install the sprinkler heads. Make sure the spacing of each of the tees adhere to the design or manufacturer’s literature.

Flush all the new piping systems and sprinkler head adapter tees with water to wash away any trash that could block the sprinkler heads when they are installed. While purging the piping system, also carefully examine for any obvious leaks. Following this, connect the heads to the adapter tees using suitable connectors; preset the rotation of any rotating heads so that they cover the desired radius of the area and don’t spray onto adjacent buildings or pavements, causing excess water. 

Once all this is ready, turn on the water gradually in order to avoid water hammer or other shock to the equipment. Readjust any sprinklers that aren’t covering their targeted radius and watch for dry spots that often occur when two heads’ radius meet. It’s important to keep in mind that since this is a temporary system, the pipes, valves, and heads will be situated on top of the soil or grass. As such, take extra caution when preparing the piping system to make sure it won’t be easily disturbed.

Traveling the world on a limited budget of $50 a day seems impossible to most people, but it is actually attainable with a little bit of planning. 

Your first step should be researching what airlines have the most flights out of your home airport. Many of these airlines will also include frequent flyer miles programs which, when enrolled, can help you toward reaching your goal of free airfare. Consider signing up for a mileage credit card with your chosen airline, as well. As part of most airline mileage programs, there are opportunities to collect enough miles (or points) to purchase a free ticket once per year. Once this ticket is acquired, you’ll have more funds to explore the surrounding area.

Fly to a major airport and then hop around the region. Many airlines will discount the price of tickets if you’re willing to fly to a major airport, and then connect to more affordable airlines to explore the areas around it. Keep an eye out for last-minute package deals or Groupons to get even better deals on your flights from one destination to another.

You’ll want to make the most of the $50 a day, so stay in a place for more than two days if you can. If you’re brave, consider creating an account on www.couchsurfing.org to stay with locals and share cultural experiences for free. Arrange a home exchange if you can. Look for monastery housing which offer cheap bed for a night in certain areas. Book your travels through Hotwire or another travel site and choose hostels over hotels. 

If you are willing to rent a car, some countries have a lot of affordable gas stations. Double check if trains can be booked for same-day travel, as these can be a bit expensive. Think about buying "saver" rail passes if you want to travel across countries. 

When you’re in your destination, ask locals for advice on the best places to shop. Cook your own meals when you can and shop at local markets for fresh ingredients to get the most out of your budget. Be adventurous and try the local delicacies but still pay attention to your budget. Some cities offer museum passes which allow access to multiple museums at a discounted cost – search for these and purchase the passes if they are available. Many cities also allow people to take a ferry to get from one destination to another.

Research free tours and walking tours to get a taste of the destination you are visiting. Bring a tablet or smartphone with you and download the Trail Wallet app to help you budget and track your expenses. Use the Wi-Fi on your device to search for free entrances to different attractions, and purchase Groupons to see the sights. 

When you combine all of these tips, you can reach the goal of traveling the world on a budget of just $50 a day. You won’t be able to do everything, but with a little bit of research and planning, you will be able to experience a lot during your time abroad.

How to Perform Ghusl
Ghusl is an important Islamic practice that involves complete cleansing of the body. It is a full body wash that combines washing and purification. There are several scenarios when Muslims must perform ghusl, such as, after ejaculation, after menses and postpartum bleeding, after a wet dream or after death. One must ensure that they are in a place where they can perform the ghusl in total privacy. 

Finding a source of clean water is an essential part of the process. Do not use impure water, water from fruit or trees, or leftover ghusl or wudu water. If you are traveling and cannot find a source of clean water, use clean earth to rub over your face and hands instead. Remember when performing the ritual, to begin with the intention of performing ghusl for purification.

Position yourself in front of the water and begin the ablutions by reciting the Basmala (“Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Raheem”) - it is recommended to recite the entire phrase out loud. Start by washing your private parts with your right hand three times then switch to your left hand and repeat the process three times. Afterwards, you should cup your right hand and sniff some water from it into your nostrils. 

Then, move onto washing your face, starting with your forehead then finally your chin. Wipe your face downwards three times with your right hand. Similarly, wash the right arm up to the elbow three times, and afterwards, pour water over your head three times. Wipe or massage the neck area as well. 

Next, move on the left arm, pour water liberally over your shoulder and self, then finally wash your head again but this time entirely by pouring water over it. After you are done with the washing ritual, move away from the area you just performed the washing. 

Finally, when you're finished, dry your body with a clean and dry towel and dress yourself. 

Performing Ghusl can be an important ritual particularly at times when purifying oneself is essential. Whether performing Ghusl because of ejaculation, menstruation or death of someone close, ensure you use clean water and are in a private setting, and begin the process by reciting the Basmala. Following the steps described here, you can confidently and correctly perform Ghusl to fully cleanse your body.

Enjoying less food can be a great way to get healthy and stay trim. But getting there is often much harder than it sounds. Depending on your situation, it can take months before you see a visible difference in your weight. But these nine tips will definitely help you on your journey.  

First and foremeost, get rid of all junk food from the house, not by eating it, but by giving it away or dumping it out. If the unhealthy food isn't around, it will be less tempting to reach for when you're hungry. 

Second, familiarize yourself with the serious consequences of eating unhealthily, and scare yourself into hating any food that isn't healthy. Find out more about how unhealthy food affects your body, and try to keep that in mind when you're tempted to indulge. 

Third, post sticky notes all over the place, reminding yourself to eat healthily. Keep a positive attitude, and focus on the way you will look and feel once you've dropped the pounds. 

Fourth, set up a weight loss goal so that you know how much weight you plan to lose. Setting up a timeline will help you keep your focus and stay on track with your diet. 

Fifth, plan out your daily diet, using the healthy food pyramid. Make sure that you are getting the right combination of proteins, fruits, vegetables and grains. When it comes to calories, aim to reduce them gradually or you can slow down your metabolism. 

Sixth, drink at least eight glasses of water per day, and two glasses of milk to ensure a healthy life. This will help flush out toxins, and make sure your body is functioning properly. 

Seventh, exercise daily, focusing on calorie burning and weight-lessening exercises. Exercise not only burns away fat, but can help tone muscle as well. Make sure to fit in some cardio and light weights on a daily basis. 

Eighth, if you find that you still have problems with not including unhealthy food in your diet, think about how good you will look when you finally lose all that unwanted weight. Visualizing the future outcome can sometimes be the best incentive. 

Ninth, to ensure that you will definitely hate eating unhealthy food, watch a few movies that will disgust you about processed, unhealthy foods, such as Food Inc. If you still find yourself tempted, look up disgusting pictures of very overweight people that weigh more than you do. These visuals should help you remember why you started, and remind you to stay strong. 

These nine tips will help you to enjoy eating less and live a healthier life. With effort and dedication, you will soon be surprised at how easily you survive and thrive on the healthiest of diets.

Are you ready to get ready for an Airsoft game? You bet you are – and we are here to help! Let's start getting you kitted out for the game day, and make sure you have all the things that you will need. 

The first thing you should do is get yourself a nice sturdy duffel bag. This will be used to carry all of your equipment to and from the game. Make sure to get one with comfortable straps and good padding on the bottom, so you can carry it a good distance with all of your stuff inside. 

Once you've picked out your bag, it's time to pick out your Airsoft gun. You'll want to determine what type of game you are playing before investing in a gun, due to the different tactics and strategies that are used depending on the size of the field, the number of players and the type of game. That said, you can't go wrong with the general purpose varieties of AEG's, the M4A1 and the AK-47, which provides a great balance between power and maneuverability. 

Safety is paramount, so make sure to buy some proper protective goggles, either wrap-around or over-the-head. It's also recommended to buy binoculars if you're playing on a larger field, which will help you keep an eye on the enemy forces by spotting their positions. 

When you're shopping for Airsoft gear, you should be aware of what's appropriate and what isn't. Don't bother getting any illegal items such as rubber knives, explosive smoke capsules, slingshots, practice hand grenades or metal or plastic BB's. 

It's also fun to consider buying some Airsoft missiles or grenades, which can be fun to use during the game. Just make sure you are extra careful while handling them, as they could hurt yourself or someone else if you're not careful. 

If you're playing in a dark environment, you may want to purchase a flashlight for yourself, and if your primary or secondary weapon has a rail system, you can equip it with a flashlight attachment.

Now it's time to dress the part. The best way to do this is to purchase a camouflage suit, which you will have to change into right before you enter the field. You don't want your hair to stand out in sunlight, so make sure you have a secondary head gear like a headwrap or winter cap, coupled with a balaclava. You'll also want to buy your BB's or replacement gas or CO2 as needed, so you don't run out during the match. Another thing to consider is investing in a good pair of boots. Make sure they fit properly and are comfortable enough so that you can run around and play without any distracting pains. You should also have a compact emergency first aid kit, as well as an extra battery for your electric or AEG. In addition, make sure your antiperspirant does not have a strong scent as it can give you away too easily, but you could also purchase a specialized kind with insect repellent that will in effect reduce your sweat. 

Before you go out there playing, make sure to check the range of your toy guns, and make sure you have standard equipment such as zip-ties, a screwdriver, a pocket knife and duct tape with you. A good idea is to wear gloves, and if you are playing on a team then you may want to look into purchasing arm bands or patches in the team color, to easily identify teammates from the enemy. Finally, if you have the budget for it, you can buy Airsoft mines and place them strategically around the map. 

Now you're all set for the game. Follow these steps and you'll be sure to have an amazing Airsoft game. Good luck and have a blast!

Working with obnoxious people can be one of the most frustrating aspects of a job. It can be difficult to tolerate coworkers who are constantly loud, make unfunny jokes, or talk endlessly without a care for whom it may offend. Here are some tips to help you navigate this distressing situation. 

First and foremost, try deep breathing. Deep breaths relax your body and help you mentally focus your energy on something other than the person causing you annoyance. Another technique, and perhaps more practical course of action, would be to take regular breaks from your work. This can provide a breather from the situation and encourage productivity. Using headphones can also be a great way to create a physical boundary between yourself and your co-worker. 

Aside from physical tactics, it is important to work through the emotions that their behavior instills. Venting to someone outside of the office is helpful for getting these feelings out in a non-confrontational way. Speaking to a trusted friend or family member can make you feel less isolated and also provide a listening ear. Additionally, consider leaving yourself notes of encouragement or setting reminders to remain calm. As another form of self-encouragement, you may choose an inspiring word or phrase, such as “relax” or “be strong” as a reminder to reset your focus and not let your workplace irritations overcome you. 

If all else fails, address your supervisor about the situation and explain that a change needs to be made. Ask to be moved to another work area if it comes to that. When you confront the co-worker directly, choose what battles to fight. Not every situation needs to escalate into a heated debate, and sometimes it is best to take the high road and be discreet. This can be difficult so make sure it is worth the emotional investment. 

Finally, recognize that your co-worker may not even realize the extent of their annoyance; try to listen to what they have to say without interjecting your opinion. Consider the possibility that they are struggling just as much as you are. Speak up at the next scheduled meeting to offer solutions on how to reduce stress and form better connections. If you set the example, you can inspire others to follow your example and create a positive work atmosphere for everyone.

How to Do a Feasibility Study 

Feasibility studies are important tools for understanding the economic potential of a project. They provide an essential understanding of the project's objectives, how the project may perform in the market, its potential cost, cash flow and profit, and its financial assets and liabilities. By conducting a thorough feasibility study, project operators can gain an informed insight into the financial potential of their project and decide on the most beneficial development option.

Conduct a preliminary analysis.It sounds strange to say that you need to a pre-feasibility study in order to know if you need to do a feasibility study, but it's true! A preliminary analysis is the initial step in determining the potential success of a project. This can involve evaluating the market and identifying current and topical trends, conducting a risk assessment, and gleaning preliminary financial figures. It is important to take the time to flesh out the relationship between project objectives and the potential market before deciding whether or not to move forward with the project.

Consider your options. Once you have evaluated your project's potential, you can decide if a feasibility study is required or not. If you decide to move forward with the project, you have a number of options for further study: a preliminary feasibility analysis, a detailed feasibility analysis, or an expert consultation. Depending on the scope and complexity of the project, it is important to decide which option is best suited for your project.

Begin to assess the demand for your idea. A fundamental component of any feasibility study is the assessment of market demand. To do this, you must consider the size of the market, the segment of the market that is interested in your product, and any competitors currently operating in that market. Have conversations with potential customers or partners, conduct surveys, and scour existing online and offline data to gauge the level of interest in your project.

Begin to assess the competition. Once you have an understanding of the existing market, you must examine the competition. Look at their pricing, customer coverage, profile, and products to get an idea of their current market position. By collecting and analyzing this data you can create a competitive landscape map, which gives you an idea of how your product may fit into the existing market.

Assess the challenges. Before committing to a project, you need to assess the potential challenges you may face. Identify any major problems that you may meet in the implementation of the project such as regulatory restrictions, labor issues, or legal issues. A thorough understanding of the challenges you may meet is important to reducing the potential risk of embarking on a project.

Decide if you should hire expert consultants. Depending on the scope of your project, it is a smart move to hire experienced professionals who can bring additional knowledge and insight into the project. Do your research, look for people with the right mix of skills and experience that match your project's requirements and objectives.

Set a time-table. To keep everything on track during a feasibility study, it is important to set a realistic timeline. Estimate the amount of time that will be needed for research, development and testing, and for any activities related to the project. The timeline should also take into account any unforeseen delays or obstacles that may arise.

Learn about the market. Research the market, competitors and customer opinions. Review existing studies to gauge the current state of the market. Review demographics, technologies, industry trends, and other relevant economic data.

Use data from the Economic Census. For many industries, data can be collected from a Census or other publicly available surveys and economic data. These include such information as industry gross exports, personal income, state and local taxes, and state employment levels. With this data you can identify areas where current customers are located and how your project may redress any issues identified.

Survey people directly. This is a great way to gain detailed feedback and opinions about your project. Set up interviews with potential customers, market experts and opinion leaders in the field. Use any insights gained to refine your project and gain an idea of how it stands out from the competition.

Conduct market surveys by other means. There are many other methods you can employ to survey potential customers. These include cold-calling, email surveys, online surveys, focus groups, and customer relationship management software.

Design your surveys carefully. Any survey should provide the necessary information about potential customers in order to gain an accurate assessment of the market. Ensure that your survey language is straightforward and that participants understand the questions posed.

Analyze the competition's claim on the market. Analyze their pricing and services, and assess how well they have penetrated the market. What are their selling points, what is their value in the market. By evaluating their existing relationship with their customers, you can gain an understanding of the competitors' current market position and how to move forward.

Identify your potential share of the market. Using market data, review the current levels of market penetration and projected growth. Based on the findings, construct your expected market share. Forecast the potential demand for your product in the market and determine when it is best to launch the project.

Determine where you'll need to work. Analyze the staff and resources needed to execute and implement the project. This includes personnel, materials, transport, subcontractors, and technology. Ensure that you have the staff and resources to match the scope and complexity of your project. 

Decide how your company or team needs to be structured. Review the organizational structure and decide who will head the project. Develop a clear chain of command, roles, responsibilities, and ownership of tasks. Set up any necessary team strategies and performance indicators. 

Determine what materials you will need. This is the point at which you'll have to carefully research and list all of the materials you'll need for each specific stage of your project: what raw materials will you need, how much will they cost, and what type of technology will be needed. 

Identify the cost of your materials. Make sure you have the most updated pricing information on all of the materials you need, including the cost of delivery to the project site. Add up the cost and formulate a budget.

Identify any required technology. Some projects may require specialized IT or machinery. Know the exact specs and requirements of the technology needed to implement your project and include this in the feasibility study.

Outline your start-up costs. Start-up costs can vary greatly from project to project. Take the time to go through all of the steps required to move from the idea stage to the commercial stage. Make sure you factor in any start-up fees, licenses, permits, and taxes you may incur.

Estimate your operating costs. Operating costs are the ongoing expenses associated with the operations of a project. Include production costs, staff costs, and payment terms for ongoing work.

Estimate your revenue predictions.  Calculate your estimated revenues based on the market demand, the number of customers, and the average price point. Make sure you validate the assumptions used to reach these predictions.

Estimate the outcome for other types of projects. Make sure you account for the potential outcome of various scenarios. For example, look at the potential return of investments when the project is complete and consider alternative sources of funding in the event of unexpected issues.

Identify your funding sources. Review the potential sources of funding for your project. This includes government grants, bank loans, trade shows, venture capital, and crowdfunding sources.

Crunch the numbers. Once you've gathered your data, procedures, revenues, and costs, crunch all the numbers to estimate the profitability and financial statement of your project. The use of budgeting, forecasting and financial statements can provide a clear picture of the financial health of the project.

Compile all of the information. After you have gathered the necessary data, compile it into one cohesive document. Make sure the information is accurate and current. 

Look at your financial predictions first. Evaluate the potential return on your investment and any other financial benefits that may result from completing the project. The financial projections will be the guide to determine the success of the project.

Balance your estimated business profits against your personal financial needs. Consider the financial loss you may incur in the event of failure. Make sure you factor in enough money for personal expenses, rent, and other living costs. If the project fails or is delayed for any period of time, do not be at risk of having to incur significant financial losses.

Consider the human costs of your project. When assessing the cost of a project, don't forget to factor in the impact of the project on people. This includes the time and money spent on staff, the need for training, security issues, and potential disruption to other businesses and customers. 

Analyze your findings. After the data has been collected and compiled, take some time to step back and analyze the findings. Compare and contrast the findings and make sure the conclusions and recommendations for action are valid and up to date.

Write it up and distribute it. Write up a report with the findings and recommendations and distribute it amongst the project stakeholders. Make sure it is easily accessible and the language is clear and concise. 
Finally, review the report for accuracy and consistency before presenting it to decision-makers.

How to Add Insulation to an Old House
Adding insulation to an old house can give you cost savings in the form of lower energy costs, improved indoor air quality, and a quieter environment. It can also increase the value of your home. Here's how you do it.

Begin by renting a blow in insulation machine, which is specifically designed for adding insulation to old houses, not new ones. The machine is relatively easy and affordable to operate. Purchase the necessary amount of insulation in bags that will fit in the machine. 

The next step is to locate the studs in the walls of the house and then mark the center between them. When blowing the insulation you want make sure the center of the hole is approximately 6" down from the ceiling. This will help the insulation remain in place and stay where you want it.

Start the machine and begin blowing the insulation into the area between the walls. The process will take roughly 30-45 minutes for most rooms, depending on the size of the room and amount of insulation being used.

Once you have finished blowing in the insulation it is important to secure the insulation. Cut a piece of 1/2 inch plywood that is two inches wide by six inches long and insert it into the hole. Make sure the plywood fits snug in the hole and center it between the studs. Secure the plywood piece with 1 1/4 inch sheet rock screws.

Also, take the round piece of sheet rock that you had cut out at the beginning of the project and attach it to the plywood with sheet rock screws as well. Make sure all screws are tight and the heads are below the surface of the sheet rock.

Now you will need to fill the screw holes and smooth the entire patch with joint compound or mud. You will need to press the mud fairly hard against the wall so the patch is even. Once you have applied the mud allow it to dry. To help the drying process you can use a fan or a hairdryer.

Once the mud has dried you will need to scrape off any dried mud knobs sticking out with a knife and recoat. You should repeat this process at least three times to ensure the patch is even.

If you want to match any texture that the wall might have, put some drywall mud in a kitchen bowl and add some water to thin. Then take a sweater and dip it into the mud and use a very light hand to dab it onto the patch, trying to match any texture and blending the patch into the wall as best you can.

After this step is complete, the final steps in the process is to prime and paint the patch. This will help the patch match the existing wall. Primer should be applied prior to painting. Once the primer has dried it should be sanded lightly before applying the paint.

Adding insulation to an old house is a great way to save money in the long run. Using these steps the project can be completed in under an hour and you can begin saving right away on your energy bills and improving your indoor air quality.

How to Set Up an Ubuntu Based HTPC with XBMC
Setting up an Ubuntu based HTPC with XBMC can be a daunting task if unfamiliar with the process, but with a few simple steps the task becomes manageable. In this guide, we will take you through the process of how to set up your HTPC running XBMC on Ubuntu. 

The first step will be downloading the latest stable versions of Ubuntu and XBMC. Ubuntu can be downloaded from its official website, and XBMC can be downloaded from the XBMC download page. After downloading the files, you can either choose to rip the ISO file downloaded to the DVD itself, or you can create a Bootable USB drive. Once you have either of two requirements met, you may begin installing by clicking on "Continue".

The next step will require you to choose the option to "Erase disk and install Ubuntu". This will erase any files or changes that you may have made in the past, so make sure that you have backed up all the important data or documents. After making sure, click "Install Now" to proceed forward.

The third step includes choosing your location/ time zone, and thereafter, your Keyboard Layout. Make sure these two are accurately set up, as it will save a lot of troubles in the future. 

The fourth step requires you to enter in all your details such as your username, computer name, password, and so on. It is important to enter the correct details and to remember what you have chosen so that you are not locked out in the future. It is recommended that you choose "Log in automatically" if this is a Home PC that does not have sensitive files and is primarily meant for Media Consumption purposes. 

Finally, the installation process can begin. After selecting all the mentioned options, Ubuntu will begin installing itself onto your computer. Wait for a few minutes until the process is complete. 

At the completion of the installation, Click on "Restart Now" to restart the computer. Make sure you log into the account that you had just created. From the start menu search "Terminal". Once you are in the Terminal, execute the following lines of code one at a time, by typing them out and hitting the "Enter" key:

•sudo apt-get update
•sudo apt-get install xbmc

This will install XBMC into the Ubuntu operating system. After that, enter:
•sudo apt-get install xbmc-live

This will add additional features to XBMC. Once you have completed these two steps, you may log out from Ubuntu. At the Log in screen, on the right hand side of the user name, click on the icon for XBMC. It will automatically begin running the software as you launch the XBMC HTPC now set up.

XBMC is now installed, and from that you can navigate around all the features and content that it has to offer. XBMC is very flexible and allows you to control plenty of content and features from your HTPC. From movies, to music, to photos and more, XBMC provides the backbone to your own customized Home Theatre PC. Enjoy!

Knowing the right size of bike for your toddler is key to making a safe, enjoyable ride. The wrong size bike can be difficult to control, uncomfortable, and lead to a frustrating ride. The best way to ensure your toddler has the right-sized bike is to measure them. Here’s how you can measure your toddler for a bike.

Gather the materials needed for taking your child’s measurement. You will need to measure their height and the size of the bike’s wheels, so have a measuring tape, a ruler, and string on hand. You will also need a pen or marker for marking their height on the wall.

To measure the height, have your child stand upright against a wall. Mark their height on the wall with the pen or marker. Then use the measuring tape or ruler to measure their height accurately. Alternatively, you can use string if you don’t have access to a ruler.

To measure the size of the bike’s wheels, you will need to measure your child’s body. Have your child stand against the wall with their legs slightly spread and measure from their crotch area to the floor with measuring tape. Once you have done this, you can compare the measurement to the diameter of the bike’s wheels.

If your toddler is between sizes, such as being in between an 18” and 24” bike, consider their age and their inseam measurement. General rule of thumb is that you should go with a bigger size bike for a younger child and a smaller bike for an older child.

When adjusting the bike to their height, make sure to adjust the seat height so your toddler can comfortably reach the floor with both feet. If your toddler cannot reach the pedals, then lower the seat. Similarly, adjust the handlebars so your toddler can reach them without straining forward. Make sure they can easily press the brake levers. Most bikes have adjustable handlebars and support beams making this process simpler.

When purchasing your toddler’s bike, always be cautious when buying a used or secondhand bike. It’s best to purchase the bike from a sporting goods or biking store as the staff are more knowledgeable about bike sizes and styles than big-box stores. It’s also important to let your child test drive the bike before you purchase it, as they will need to be comfortable riding it.

If your toddler is very young, consider getting them a balance bike instead as it helps them learn how to balance and control the bike, which will come in handy when they upgrade to training wheels. If they are too small for a balance bike, then a thicker-wheeled tricycle or big wheel bike is more suitable. Regardless of the bike, always make sure it has coaster brakes and it is safe and sturdy.

Finally, always ensure your toddler wears safety gear while riding. Make sure you purchase a helmet, elbow pads, and kneepads. Following these steps when measuring your toddler for a bike will ensure a safe and comfortable ride.

When it comes to cold sores, it’s important to understand that HSV-1 infections are quite common. This virus is highly contagious, and it’s passed on through direct skin contact. Identifying the symptoms of a cold sore is the best way to prevent the virus from spreading.

First, you should look out for the predictive signs of a cold sore. Commonly, people experience pre-existing tingling, itching, or burning before they develop a cold sore. In addition, keep an eye out for a raised red spot or area of redness that may signal the start of an infection. This could be followed by swelling, which usually precedes the appearance of an open blister filled with virus particles.

Once the blister breaks, a scab will form in its place. It’s important not to pick at the scab or the blister, as this could cause the virus to spread. To prevent the spread of the virus, pay attention to hygiene and wash your hands often. Keep in mind that there is no cure for the herpes simplex virus, so you must take the appropriate precautions when dealing with a cold sore.

It’s important to recognize the difference between a cold sore and similar blemishes or irritations. Cold sores are easily recognizable because of their location, size, and shape. Other blemishes or irritations can often appear similar, but they usually don’t carry the same risk of infection.

If you do have a cold sore, there are several things you can do to make the infection more bearable. To reduce the pain associated with the cold sore you can try over-the-counter medications like ibuprofen or acetaminophen. Some people also use coconut oil to speed up the healing process, while lysine has been known to shorten the cold sore outbreak.

To prevent future outbreaks, you should learn how the virus is spread so you can take the proper precautions. The virus is mostly likely spread through physical contact, including kissing and sexual contact. People should also avoid foods that are high in arginine, such as chocolate, peanuts, and certain grains. Adding more lysine to your diet, meanwhile, may help suppress the virus and reduce your chances of experiencing an outbreak. Finally, you should familiarize yourself with the possible triggers of the virus so you can avoid them. Common triggers include sunlight, stress, and illness.

Lastly, if you think you have a cold sore, you should get plenty of rest and stay as healthy as possible. Keeping your body healthy overall helps to suppress the virus, and that could mean fewer and less severe cold sore outbreaks. If you have recurrent outbreaks, you may want to speak to your doctor about possible prescription medications that can help alleviate the symptoms.

Greeting people in different languages is an essential part of any global citizen’s repertoire. Whether you’re traveling, establishing contacts around the world, or just wanting to know what are the formal and informal ways to say hello, here’s a guide on how to say hello in different languages.

Say hello in A'Leamona: In A'Leamona, the word for “hello” is tel nĩdo, pronounced “tehl-neye-doe”. This informal greeting is a friendly way to start a conversation.

Say hello in American Sign Language (ASL): ASL is the predominant sign language used in the United States. To formally say “hello” in ASL, squeeze the fingers in your right hand together and touch the tips of your fingers to your forehead, your palm facing outward, and move your hand away from your forehead in a sort of saluting motion.

Say hello in Bremnian: Bremnian is a Germanic language found in the western part of Germany, near the city of Bremen. The formal way to say “hello” in Bremnian is iskoali, pronounced “kowalee”. You will usually hear this greeting in more formal settings.

Say hello in British Sign Language (BSL): BSL is the language form used by many in the United Kingdom, and to say “hello” in BSL, you can perform three possible variations of the sign. The first is the dominant hand wave, from core to outside with the palm facing towards the recipient as the hand moves bring it into a thumbs up gesture. The second is a thumbs up gesture with two thumbs showing, which literally means “well?”. Finally, you can perform the ASL “hello” sign.

Say hello in Cape Verdean Creole: Cape Verdean Creole is a Portuguese-based Creole language, and there are multiple ways to say “hello” in this language. The formal greeting is oi, sometimes accompanied with “olá” or “entao”. Informally, you can say bon dia.

Say hello in Chamorro: Chamorro is the official language of the Mariana Islands and Guam, and to say “hello” in this language you can use either håfa adai or its shortened form, håfa?. This informal greeting is similar to “how’s it going?” in English.

Say hello in Cook Islands Maori: Cook Islands Maori is the language used by the indigenous population of the Cook Islands. To greet someone, say “kia orana”.

Say hello in Esperanto: Esperanto is an artificial language created to facilitate communication between people from different countries. The formal way to say “hello” in Esperanto is “saluton”, and the informal way is “sal”.

Say hello in Fijian: Fijian is the language spoken in Fiji, and the way to formally say “hello” is bula Vinaka, pronounced “buh-la vina-kah”.

Say hello in Hawaiian: To greet someone in Hawaiian, say “aloha”, pronounced “ah-low-ha”. This word also means “hello”, “goodbye”, “love”, and “affection”.

Say hello in Jamaican Patois: Jamaican Patois is the form of Creole spoken in Jamaica, and to say “hello” you can use the phrase whaa gwaan, literally meaning “what’s going on?”

Say hello in Maldivian:To greet someone formally in Maldivian, say Assalaamu Alaikum.

Say hello in Māori: Māori is the name for the language of New Zealand, and to formally say “hello” in this language say “kia ora”, pronounced “kia o ra”.

Say hello in Marshallese: The language of the Marshall Islands is Marshallese, and to say “hello” in this language say “Iakwe”, pronounced “YAH kway”.

Say hello in Naokien: Naokien is a dialect of Japanese spoken on the island of Okinawa. To greet someone in Naokien, the formal way is to say atetgrealot, and the informal way is to say atetel.

Say hello in Niuean: Niuean is the language of the people of Niue, and to formally greet someone in this language say “faka lofa lahi atu”.

Say hello in Palauan: The language of Palau is Palauan, and to say “hello” say “alii”, pronounced “ah-lee”.

Say hello in Samoan: The Samoan Islands are made up of two separate nations, Samoa and American Samoa, and the language spoken here is Samoan. To say “hello” formally, say “talofa”, and informally say “malo”.

Say hello in Sulka: Sulka is an indigenous language of the Solomon Islands, and the way to say “hello” depends on the time of day. To say “morning”, say “vai”, to say “good afternoon” say “peginibi”.

Say hello in Tagalog: Tagalog is the language of the Philippines. The closest equivalent to the word “hello” in Tagalog is “Kumustá?”, which is more informal than the English “hello”.

Say hello in Tongan: Tongan is the language of the Polynesian Kingdom of Tonga, and to greet someone in this language say “Mālō e lelei”, pronounced “maa-low-e-the-lay”.

Say hello in Yapese: The language of Yap, in Micronesia, is Yapese, and to say “hello” in this language say “haode”.

Say hello in Yoruba: The language of Yoruba is spoken widely in West Africa, particularly Nigeria. The way to say “hello” in Yoruba is “bawo”, pronounced “bah-woe”. Knowing this simple greeting not only enriches your global awareness, but can also open a door into the local culture, especially when paired with a smile!

How to Be a Productive Intern at a Talent Agency'

If you are considering working as an intern at a talent agency, you need to understand that it takes more than just a love of the profession to be successful. Being a productive intern requires a deep knowledge of the industry itself and a thorough understanding of the different tasks and responsibilities that come with the job. Here are a few tips to help you become a productive intern at a talent agency.

First, it is important to scan headshot photos and resumes and store them in a folder named with the performer's name. You should also fill in the profile from information on the resume including phone numbers and email addresses plus height, weight, hair and eye color and ethnicity. This will allow you to create an organized list of information about each performer, enabling you to quickly refer to their details when needed.

Next, it is important to effectively organize projects. As an intern, you may be entrusted with tasks such as searching for audition calls, networking contacts, and micro blogging. By effectively organizing these projects, you will be better able to prioritize what needs to be done and will have an overall better view of your job responsibilities.

Additionally, you should learn how to crop headshot images and also how to use screen capture programs. These programs can be used to efficiently capture a head shot directly from a webpage and even annotate it if necessary.

Throughout your internship, you should continue to learn the methodical techniques and habits necessary to keep email contact profiles up to date with headshots, contact info, and notes on resumes and background. This will greatly increase your chances of landing a successful audition from a contact.

You should also regularly search for new casting directors and maintain a group of contacts to do periodic mailings to solicit their submission requests. Creating a complete database of local directors, playwrights, and agents is a great way to expand your contacts.

You should also hone your computer and internet skills. Social networking and collaboration with other interns is a good way to get ahead, so make sure you are always up to speed with the latest social media apps. Additionally, make a habit of using calendars and updating spreadsheets so that others can follow your progress in real-time.

Lastly, you should be sure to document your daily activities and progress. This will help to further build your resume and will also be a great reference to look back on as you create a record of networking contacts. Finally, make it a point to find news sources for the entertainment industry and update blogs and microblogs regularly to build an online following. These small tasks will help you become a successful, productive intern at a talent agency.

How to Become Content With What You Have

Finding contentment with what you have can be an incredibly difficult undertaking. You may often find yourself overwhelmed with feelings of dissatisfaction, dissatisfaction about the past, or anxiety about the future. It can be hard to feel content with what you have when you feel like everything around you is quickly changing. In order to become content with what you have in life, it’s important to remember that true contentment comes from within. Here are a few tips to find happiness and contentment with what you have: 

Find joy in simple things. The key to feeling content is appreciating what you have and finding joy in the little things. It can be something as simple as taking a leisurely stroll outdoors, sitting in the sun, or savoring a cup of tea. Taking pleasure in these small moments can help us to stay connected with the present moment and bring us contentment. 

Stay mindful. Mindfulness is the awareness of your internal thoughts and feelings, as well as of your external environment and bodily sensations. When you practice mindfulness, you can identify feelings and sensations that normally go unnoticed. Staying mindful of your thoughts and feelings will enable you to better understand why you are feeling a certain way, and to make better choices for your mental wellbeing. 

Be generous. Generosity can be an instant shortcut to happiness. Being generous with your time, energy and resources can be incredibly fulfilling as it gives you the opportunity to do something kind for other people. Showing generosity to someone can bring joy to both you and the other person. 

Express gratitude. You need not express gratitude to an individual. Being thankful for the experiences and opportunities you have can help you to appreciate what you have. Expressing gratitude can also help you to remember the things that are going well in your life, allowing you to be more content with your current situation. 

Only keep the things you love. It’s important to appreciate the things you have, so try to get rid of anything that no longer serves you. Letting go of things that no longer bring you joy makes it easier for you to feel content and satisfied in your current situation. 

Practice optimism. When confronted with a difficult situation, believe that things will work out in your favor. Having a positive attitude and an optimistic outlook can help you to handle challenging situations with resilience and courage. 

Be humble. Although setting goals can be beneficial for personal growth, having too many expectations can lead to unhappiness and frustration. Having a humble attitude and continuously being open to learning, growing and improving will help you to be more content with yourself and with what you have. 

Do not make happiness contingent on something or someone else. Do not constantly look for the perfect partner or job with which to make you happy. Instead, recognize that happiness comes from within. Being content with your life doesn’t depend on what happens externally, but rather on how you choose to respond to it. 

Don’t be jealous. Jealousy can be detrimental to your relationships and can make it difficult to find contentment with what you have. Redirecting your focus from what you don’t have to what you do have and how you can make the best of it is the key to staying happy and content. 

Devote time to family and friends. Spending time with happy, positive people will tend to make you happy and positive as well. Spending time with those you care about and with whom you can truly connect can be incredibly uplifting and soothing. 

Get to know your partner. Always aim for a deeper, more intimate level of emotional connection with the one you love. Truly getting to know each other is extremely valuable for your relationship as it will help you to better understand each other on a deeper level. 

Recognize your partner’s complexity. Do not overemphasize the negative qualities of your partner. Each person is a unique individual with a diverse range of qualities and characteristics, so try to focus on the positive attributes as much as possible. 

Don’t fall prey to emotional addiction. Living in fear of ‘not having enough’ can keep us from feeling content. Developing an emotional addiction to material items or certain situations can keep us from savoring the present moment. 

Make yourself useful. Doing something you love is important. Putting your skills and talents to use will not only make you feel better about yourself, but it will also bring you contentment by playing an active role in a productive activity. 

Finding contentment with what you have in life is not always easy, but it is possible. Be mindful of your feelings and thoughts, focus on the positive, and appreciate the little things. Learn to live in the moment and recognize just how much you already have.
