Neutral operations with square roots may seem intimidating at first, but they are simple and can be accomplished easily with Excel. With just a few steps and a few formulas, you will be able to do neutral operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Here are the steps for completing neutral operations with square roots in Excel:

1. Open a new workbook in Excel from the desktop, from the dock, or from within your Applications folder inside the Microsoft folder.
2. In Preferences, set R1C1 to unchecked or Off, set Ribbon to checked or On, set Show Formula Bar to checked or On and set Calculation to .000 000 000 000 001 (without interim spaces) and 100 iterations and Calculate Automatically.
3. Click in the far upper left top corner above the 1 of row 1 and to the left of column A.
4. Title the first worksheet, "NeuOps sqrt(n)" and save the workbook as "Do Neu Ops w Sqrts" into an appropriate folder such as 'Microsoft Excel Imagery', 'Neu Ops' or 'wikiHow Articles'.
5. Enter the Row 1 and Row 2 Headings:

Enter to cell A1, a
Enter to cell A2, By changing cell
Enter to cell B1, sqrt(a)
Enter to cell C1, sqrt(b)
Enter to cell C2, " = sqrt(a)/(sqrt(a)-1)" ...(w/o quotes and with a leading space)
Enter to cell D1, b =
Enter to cell D2, (sqrt(b))^2
Enter to cell E1, c =
Enter to cell E2, sqrt(a) + sqrt(b)
Enter to cell F1, c =
Enter to cell F2, sqrt(a) * sqrt(b)
Enter to cell G1, Goal
Enter to cell H1, Goal Seek to 0

6. Enter the algebraic solution to the problem sqrt(a)+sqrt(b)=sqrt(a)*sqrt(b) in column I:

Select column I and Format Cells Font Bold and Format Column Set Column Width 3.82";
Enter to cell I1, sqrt(a) + sqrt(b) = sqrt(a) * sqrt(b) = c
Enter to cell I2, sqrt(a) + sqrt(b) -sqrt(b) = (sqrt(a) * sqrt(b)) - sqrt(b)
Enter to cell I3, sqrt(a) = sqrt(b) * (sqrt(a) - 1) (divide both sides by (sqrt(a) - 1)) to get:
Enter to cell I4, sqrt(a)/(sqrt(a) - 1) = sqrt(b) (notice this is the same result as in C1 and C2.

7. Format the Goal Seeking columns red.
8. Define the variable names for the worksheet:

Select columns A:C
Do Insert Name Create in Top Row, OK. You should end up with 3 variable names: a, sqrt_a and sqrt_b.

9. Enter the Input cells and formulas for rows 3-5:

Enter to cell A3 the formula, =PI()
Enter to cell A4 the formula, =10
Enter to cell A5 the value, 1, as a preliminary guess.
10. Do Goal Seeking

To do Goal Seeking in Excel, start by selecting the Goal area, in this case cell G5. Then, go to Data > Goal Seek, or press Alt+T+G. In the Goal Seek dialog box, specify the values for Set cell, To value, and By changing cell. Enter G5 as the Set cell, 0 as the To value, and H5 as the By changing cell. Click OK and you should be presented with the result: the value of cell H5 is 0.25.

Now that you have the correct value of cell H5, the result of the Goal Seeking calculation, you can use this result to determine the values for cells A3, A4, and A5. Go to cell A3 and enter the formula: =sqrt(H5). Go to cell A4 and enter the formula: =1/sqrt(H5). And go to cell A5 and enter the formula: =1/(sqrt(H5))^2.

And you are done! You can now easily use Excel to solve neutral operations involving square roots: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

How to Dig Post Holes
Digging post holes for any purpose can be a daunting and laborious task if you are not properly prepared. Knowing the right steps to take can reduce the amount of time needed and make it a more efficient experience. Follow the steps below to ensure your post hole digging project is carried out in the most effective manner.

Obtain a pair of post hole diggers. Post hole diggers are the most efficient tools to use when digging post holes, and come in a variety of materials from fiberglass handles to wooden handles, and from steel blades to carbon-steel blades. They range in length from four feet all the way up to twelve feet.

Select the location for the hole you will dig. Carefully select the area you are going to be digging for the post holes and be sure it is in line with the other posts you will be installing. You will need an open area of soil, free of any vegetation or debris making it unsafe to dig safely in the area.

Determine if there is any possibility of underground utilities being in the area you are digging. Before any digging takes place, it is crucial to contact the local utilities office to be sure there are not any cables, lines or pipes situated near or under the ground where you plan on working. If you find there are utilities present, contact an underground locating service to mark the area, and avoid the possibility of damage or disruption to utility services in the area.

Begin digging by holding the post hole diggers by the handles, one in each hand, with the handles close together. Insert the jaw of the digger into the ground and hold it in one spot or rotate it, depending on what type of soil you are working with.

Spread the handles apart to capture the soil in the jaws (between the hole digger's blades), using enough pressure to grasp it securely, then lift the hole diggers out of the hole. Make sure you lift the jaws vertically to ensure the surrounding walls of the hole holds up.

Swing the hole diggers to the side of your hole, then close the handles back together. To keep the entire project clean, avoid leaving loose earth on the ground.

Repeat the steps above, going deeper with each successive thrust. Depending on the size of your post hole and what you are installing, typically the hole will need to be between 1-2 feet deep. If in doubt, check with your local building provisions for depth recommendations for your area.

Wet the soil if you encounter very hard material or very sandy, dry material you cannot otherwise extract with a reasonable effort. Adding a small amount of water and ensuring the soil within the walls of the hole remain damp will help reduce any potential land disturbances or cave-ins further along in the project.

Install your posts. Whether installing posts for fences, signs, arbors, clothing lines or decks, always take caution when you lift them into the hole to avoid damaging the post or the holes themselves. After the post is set in the hole, surround it with the soil you removed during the digging process and tamp down the soil around the outside walls of the hole.

When using concrete to set the fence posts in place be sure to use proper concrete working techniques to avoid weak fence post anchors. Some contractors prefer to dump dry pre-bagged concrete into the hole and sprinkle with water. Use the minimal amount of water to mix concrete for maximum strength. For large projects it is more cost effective to make your own concrete mix as opposed to using bagged concrete. Make sure you allow the concrete to cure before permanently attaching the post to the fence structure.

How deep to dig the hole? Generally for fences it is recommended to dig a hole of between 12-24 inches for 4x4 posts and 18-36 inches for 6x6 posts. For signs or deck posts, the depth of the hole can be a couple of inches or up to two feet depending on the size and type of post being installed.

Why use concrete? Concrete is one of the most reliable and affordable materials to setting posts in place and preventing movement due to environmental elements such as wind and rain. Concrete is also the ideal material to secure posts in the ground if the area is prone to soil erosion or if it is in an area of heavy foot traffic. For extra peace of mind, allow the concrete to cure before applying any stress to the post, such as while attaching fencing material.

How to Know if You Have Gastritis
Gastritis is a condition that affects the lining of the stomach and can cause a variety of unpleasant symptoms. Some symptoms, like flatulence, bloating, and abdominal pain, are often present in other conditions and can be hard to diagnose. It's important to take note of your symptoms and limit any activities that may worsen gastritis. This article will cover how to know if you have gastritis and how to treat it.

If you think you may have gastritis, it's important to take note of any abdominal pain that you're experiencing. Abdominal pain is usually the most consistent and noticeable symptom and can range from mild to severe. It is often accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Many people with gastritis report feeling like they are experiencing "butterflies" in their stomach.

Besides nausea and vomiting, another symptom that can indicate gastritis is black or tarry stool. This is a sign of bleeding ulcers and is known as "melena." If you see small specs of black in your stools, there's a good chance you could have gastritis.

Another common symptom is a sudden appetite change. Many gastritis patients experience a complete loss of appetite or find that they are not able to eat as much as they used to. Similarly, there is usually excessive belching and gas due to the inflammation.

If you think you might have gastritis, it's best to see a doctor for a physical exam. Your doctor may also take a blood sample, which could be useful in diagnosing gastritis. If you have what are known as "alarm symptoms," such as chills or fever, your doctor may consider an endoscopy to diagnose you more accurately.

If your gastritis is caused by the H. pylori bacteria, your doctor will prescribe you medication to kill it. This is known as the "Eradication Protocol" and usually consists of a combination of antibiotics and histamine receptor blockers. In some cases, a longer course of treatment may be necessary for children.

Once the H. Pylori bacteria is addressed, the remaining treatment for gastritis is supportive in nature. Its goal is to reduce symptoms and improve your quality of life. Stress reduction is a key part of this treatment, as higher stress levels can worsen symptoms. If you have heartburn, it should also be treated with medication.

If your gastritis is linked to Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD), you should avoid alcohol, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS), and smoking. Your doctor may also prescribe Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) to treat your PUD. Surgery may be necessary in some cases.

Finally, if your gastritis is causing nausea and vomiting, it's important that you get treatment for this. Some doctors may prescribe medication while others suggest eating smaller meals to limit the gas produced in the stomach.

Gastritis is a painful condition that can greatly reduce your quality of life. While it sometimes takes time to get an accurate diagnosis, it's important to listen to your body and take note of any symptoms that you're experiencing. If you think you have gastritis, it's best to see a doctor and get the proper diagnosis and treatment.

Eating vegetables is an important part of a healthy diet for babies. Unfortunately, many babies and toddlers are extremely picky eaters and will refuse to eat vegetables. The key to encouraging your baby to eat vegetables is introducing them early and making eating them fun. With some creative thinking and a bit of patience, you can encourage your baby to eat vegetables. 

Start feeding vegetables early on. As soon as your doctor recommends feeding solid foods start incorporating vegetables. Don't give up if your baby has a negative reaction because you are still establishing a positive relationship with vegetables. You don't have to stick to only spoon feeding - try sneaking vegetables into the meal for an extra boost of nutrients. 

Establishing a routine mealtime can be beneficial. This will help your baby understand that it's time for eating and they should be ready to taste what you serve them. Limit your baby's snacks throughout the day so that they are actually hungry and willing to try the vegetables. Use your imagination to make vegetables fun. Dress them up as characters or cut them into shapes to spark your baby's curiosity. 

Demonstrate to your baby that vegetables are good and tasty. Eat them yourself and show that you enjoy them. Change up the vegetables you offer every week. Don't try to feed the same thing that your baby has disliked before. Mix it up and offer different flavors and textures. You can also read stories to your baby that encourage them to try a variety of healthy foods. 

If your baby is refusing to eat vegetables, try hiding them in tasty meals or treats. Make sure you cut up the vegetables finely so that your baby doesn't realize what they are eating. This can help your baby associate vegetables with enjoyment, rather than fear. As your baby grows, encourage them to help you in the kitchen and be part of the meal-preparation process. With some creative thinking and creativity, you can encourage your baby to love vegetables.

How to Write an Analysis
An analysis allows readers to delve deeper into a text, whether it be a book, essay, painting, or any other form of media. Before you start analyzing the text, it is important to read the prompt carefully and understand what it is asking of you. This will help you to determine the scope of your analysis and know which contexts you should consider. Once you have a clear understanding of what is required, you can begin annotating the material you are studying.

Annotating while you read is the best way to approach an analysis. By adding marginal notes or highlights as you read, you can embed key facts, opinions, and messages within the text. This will help to identify the themes and arguments that are presented in the text. To make sure that you understand and haven't missed any of the facts or opinions, it is wise to create a page in a notebook or on a word processor with subheadings such as setting, tone, antagonist, protagonist, themes, figurative language, and imagery. This will make it easier to review your annotations and find meaning.

Once you have read and annotated the material, it is important to take a step back and review the prompt again. Take this time to consider whether you are asked to simply analyze the text in a broad sense like a book review, or if the analysis should focus on a single aspect of the text. Creating an outline to determine which topics should be discussed in the analysis, such as themes, characterization, plot points, and symbolism is often a helpful step.

After you have determined which topics to discuss, read your annotations once more, and begin thoroughly writing about each topic included in your outline. Whether it is a character's development, a setting's significance, or an act of symbolism, it is important to provide evidence and facts which support your arguments. Gather quotations from the text to back up each point you make.

Once you have written out your points, you can use your introduction to summarize the material. Here is where you should briefly touch on the themes and ideas that you plan to discuss later on. Next, try to draw conclusions from the points you make and place it into a larger context using outside sources if necessary. When writing the conclusion, make sure to emphasize the significance of the text and how it relates to the reader.

Proofreading and rereading your analysis are essential before making a final draft. It is vital that you double check the prompt one last time before submitting the paper to be sure you have fully answered what was asked. If all these steps have been addressed, the reader will have an accurate understanding of the text and how it is relevant to society.

How to Weave Hair
Weaving hair is a great way to add some style and length to your own hair or to have a totally new look. However, it can be intimidating to do for the first time. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to properly weave your hair at home or in a professional salon.

Wash and condition your hair. Before beginning the weaving process, it is important to make sure your own hair is clean and healthy. This will help the process go smoother and will also ensure that you don’t damage your natural hair when styling or weaving. 

Gather the necessary supplies. You will need a variety of different items for weaving, including a wig cap, thread, needle, scissors, comb, hair extensions, and detangler. It is important to make sure you have all of these items before starting the process, as it will make the whole process much easier.

Select your part. When weaving, you will need to decide on where you would like your part, or the line where the hair is parted. Depending on the style you are going for, you may choose a straight part, a zig-zag part, or even two or three parts. Make sure your part is even and clean before beginning the weaving process.

Begin braiding your part. You may choose to cornrow or box braid your part. This is the process of taking small sections of your own hair and braiding them in a neat pattern from the root to the tip. This will form a solid foundation for your extension hair to be attached.

Finish braiding your part. Once your part has been braided, you can continue with the weaving process.

Braid the perimeter row. This is the row of braids that will go all the way around your head. Begin at the crown and braid the hair all the way down and around the nape of your neck. Make sure the braids are nice and tight so that the extensions will stay put. 

Begin the center braids. These are the braids that will be formed in the middle of your head. Begin at the crown and braid all the way to the nape of your neck. Make sure the braids are neat and tight to maintain a neat appearance.

Finish your braids. Once the braids are finihsed, you can begin the next step in the weaving process.

Get all of your supplies. Make sure you have all the items you need for weaving, including the wig cap, thread, needle, scissors, comb, and extension hair.

Prepare your needle and thread. In order to sew on the wig cap, you will need to thread your needle and tie a knot at the end of your thread.

Put on your wig cap. Place the wig cap over your braided hair, making sure that it is snug and even all the way around.

Begin sewing your wig cap to your braids. This is the process of attaching the wig cap to your braided hair. Begin at the nape of your neck and sew the wig cap to your part. Make sure you sew it tightly and securely so that it will stay in place.

Sew the wig cap to the perimeter braid. Continue sewing the wig cap until it is securely in place, then move onto the perimeter braid. 

Sew the wig cap around your part. Sew the wig cap to the perimeter braid around your part. Make sure it is secure and even all the way around.

Cut off the excess wig cap. Once it is in place, you can trim off any excess wig cap that is sticking out.

Measure your extension-hair for the perimeter braid. The length of the extension hair should be just long enough to wrap around your part in a neat and secure manner.

Measure the extension to go around the outside of your part. Make sure it is even all the way around.

Prepare your thread. Thread your needle and tie a knot at the end of your thread.

Create your base knot through the weft of the extension. This will be your starting point for weaving the extension hair to your head.

Begin sewing the extension to your wig cap. Begin at the perimeter and sew the extension to your wig cap in small, even stitches all the way around your head. 

Continue sewing your perimeter extension. As you sew, make sure that the extensions stay in place and are even along the perimeter.

Sew your extension around the outside of your part. Make sure to keep the extension nice and even around the outside of your part.

Begin filling in the rest of your head with the extensions.  Start in the center and sew the extensions in a neat and orderly fashion, making sure to cover any gaps.

Finish filling in your head. Make sure that all of your extensions are in place and neatly sewn in.

Sew on your closure for your part. Place your closure piece over the braiding near the part and sew it on securely.

Create your closure for the back of your part. This closure piece will make sure that your weave looks neat and secure.

Adjust your closure piece. Make sure your closure piece looks natural and seamless.

Sew your closure to your head. Make sure it is securely in place, then trim any excess thread.

Cut and style your weave. Trim off any excess thread and then style your weave as desired. This may include applying a leave in conditioner, curling, or straightening your weave. You can also use hair products or styling tools to create the desired hairstyle. 

That’s it! You’ve just finished weaving your own hair! Enjoy your new look and be sure to take care of it so it lasts.

Windows Vista is equipped with a built-in feature, called Program Compatibility Wizard (PCW), that helps support legacy software. Legacy software, such as applications and games, designed for use on older versions of Windows may not work on Windows Vista. The PCW helps ensure that these programs can still run on Windows Vista, despite the differences in the operating system. This article will explain how to open and use the PCW, and how to create compatibility settings for legacy software.

Opening the PCW
The first step to using the Program Compatibility Wizard is to open it. To do this, follow these steps:

Click the “Start” button.
Hit “Control Panel”.
Click “Programs”.
Under the “Programs and Features” heading, select “Use an older program with this version of Windows”.

Now, you will be presented with two options:

Click “Next” to begin the wizard.
Search in your CD-ROM drive for any applications it can find.

The PCW will now display a box containing all the programs it has found. From this box, choose the application you wish to create compatibility settings for. The wizard will then provide a list of Windows versions, including Windows 95, and five settings to help ensure compatibility. These settings include:

256 colors
Disable display scaling on high DPI settings
Run this program as an administrator

Once you have selected the settings you want to apply, click “Next” and the PCW will show you a list of changes you have made. The wizard will then ask you if the program has run correctly. Select “Yes” to set this program to always use the compatibility settings you have chosen, or “No” if you don’t want to send the information to Microsoft. Finally, the wizard will prompt you for details and confirmation. After you have clicked “Finish”, the PCW will have successfully created compatibility settings for the legacy software, and you can now use it on Windows Vista. 

In conclusion, the Program Compatibility Wizard is a great tool for supporting legacy software on Windows Vista. It ensures that applications and games designed for older Windows versions are compatible with the current version of Windows Vista. Once the PCW has finished creating the compatibility settings, you can start using the legacy software.

Knowing if you are at high risk for prostate cancer is important in years to come. The better able you are to recognize early symptoms and take preventive measures, the better your chances of avoiding serious health problems. Consider your age, family medical history, race, and any changes in your urinary or sexual habits or health - all of these elements can increase your risk and should always be communicated to your doctor.

Age is a major factor in prostate cancer risk as the chances of developing the disease increase with each passing year. Men over fifty should consult their doctors about possible screening for prostate cancer. Additionally, if you have a family medical history of prostate cancer you should inform your doctor about it. African American men in particular have a higher risk of prostate cancer than either Caucasian or Hispanic men, so this factor should also be taken into consideration.

If you are experiencing health problems related to urination or difficulties with urination, this could be an early indicator of prostate cancer and should be discussed with your doctor. Additionally, blood in your semen may be an indication of possible prostate cancer and can put you at higher risk. Finally, any pain in the pelvic area, hips, or spine should also be discussed with your doctor, as this is a strong indicator of a possible prostate cancer.

When talking to your doctor, it is important to understand the pros and cons of prostate cancer screening. The decision of whether or not to proceed with a screening is personal and should be discussed with your doctor. If suspicious symptoms appear, your doctor will likely suggest additional tests, such as a Digital Rectal Exam (DRE), to check for further indication of cancer. Similarly, he may order a Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA) test to measure the level of PSA in your blood - and an ultrasound could also be done if suspicious results are found. In any case, if the results are suspicious for a possible prostate cancer, further investigation in the form of a prostate biopsy is the recommended course of action.

By understanding the symptoms and risk factors associated with prostate cancer, you can be better informed when talking to your doctor about your health needs. With early detection and appropriate treatment, survival rates for prostate cancer are the highest of all cancers. Therefore, staying in tune with your body and being aware of changes happening is the best way to ensure that any health problems associated with prostate cancer will be caught and addressed as soon as possible.

Keeping a diary is a great way to express yourself and also document your life, but it’s important to make sure that your diary is secure and private. Here are some tips to help you keep your diary hidden and secure: 

Conceal the cover of your diary with a book cover (make it look like a very boring book so that if anyone finds it, they won't want to read it!). This way, even if someone finds your diary, they won’t be able to tell what it is until they open it.

Hide it inside an old video case if it fits, then set it among the rest of your videos. If your diary is small enough, you can hide it in a case of an older or blank video or DVD. No one would think to search for a diary in there. 

Get a diary with a lock, and carry the keys around your neck or hide the keys. If you want to go the traditional route, you can get a diary with a lock and hide the key. You can either always carry it with you around your neck, or create a hiding spot for it at home.

Write your diary as a word document and lock the document with a password. This is a great way to store your diary digitally, as you can keep it on your computer or phone and lock it with a password so that it’s secure. 

Hide your diary in bookshelf among storybooks. This is an old classic, and especially good for covering the open diary pages. It’s a simple disguise and can be quite effective.

Hide your diary in an old shirt/top and put it somewhere in your dresser where nobody claims to look. This can be a great way to hide your diary if you want to keep it in a stationary spot in your house. Nobody would think to search in your dresser so you can be sure your diary will remain secure here.

Overall, the best place to hide a diary on a computer is inside the system folder. This is a secure folder that is rarely access by anybody, so keeping your diary here will guarantee its security. 

Keeping a diary is a great way to document your life, but make sure it’s secure. With the few methods outlined above, your diary will be sure to remain confidential and safe. No matter the method you choose, make sure your diary is completely concealed so that nobody will be able to find it.

How to Make Trousers
Making your own trousers is an incredibly rewarding experience for anyone who loves to sew. Not only does it allow you to get the perfect fit for any body type, but you can also add your own personal touches to the pants. Read on to learn how to make trousers in just nine easy steps.

Step 1: Find a Pattern for the Trousers You'd Like to Make
The best way to make trousers is by using an existing pattern. You can find one online or from a local fabric store. Make sure that the pattern matches your measurements and desired style.

Step 2: Choose Your Trouser Fabric at a Fabric Store
Visit your local fabric store, or shop online, and select the fabric that will become your trousers. Pick a fabric with the right weight for the season and one that will look great with the fabric that was used to make the trousers.

Step 3: Buy 1.5 Feet (1/2 m) of Washable Lining Material
Lining your trousers will make them more comfortable to wear and help the trousers hold their shape better. Purchase 1.5 feet (1/2 m) of washable lining material and a top stitch color that will either camouflage into the trousers or compliment their color.

Step 4: Practice Top Stitching with Extra Material Before You Start
Top stitching is very important when making trousers. It can help to make them look neat and hold their shape much better. Practice your top stitching with extra material before you start your trousers.

Step 5: Take 6 Body Measurements Either for Yourself or the Person Who Will Be Wearing the Trousers
Take 6 body measurements either for yourself or the person who will be wearing the trousers. These measurements are needed to make sure that the trousers will fit correctly. Measure the waist, hips, outside leg length, inside leg length, crotch length and thigh circumference. Take all measurements in inches. 

Step 6: Cut Out the Pattern Along the Dotted Guidelines
Remove the pattern from the fabric and cut it out along the dotted guidelines that come with the pattern. Make sure to cut out all pieces accurately so it will fit well once the trousers are sewn together.

Step 7: Place the Pattern Pieces on Top of the Underside of the Fabric
Lay the pattern pieces with the rough side (or underside) of the fabric facing up. If you are making a pair of trousers with pockets on the back side, make sure that the pocket pieces are under the back pieces. You can use pins or paper clips to hold the pattern pieces in place.

Step 8: Stitch the Trousers Where the Fabric Meets with a Simple Stitch Along the Outer Edge
Use a simple stitch to secure the trouser pieces where the fabric meets. Make sure to use a straight stitch, and try to keep it even and neat. For more durability, use a double stitch.

Step 9: Use an Iron to Press the Seam to 1 Side, Then Do Either a Double or Single Top Stitch on the Outside Seams of the Pants
Once the seams are fused together and pressed, it's time to top stitch. Check with your pattern to see if a double or single stitch is preferred. Use a matching top stitch or a camouflage stitch to keep the trousers looking neat.

Step 10: Align the 2 Pieces of Fabric That Will Be the Front of Your Pants
Align the two pieces of fabric that will constitute the front of your pants with the fabric facing up. Take your time to make sure the edges are even and secure the pieces together with pins.

Step 11: Align Your Pants Where the Zipper Fly Will Be
Position the zipper fly piece between the two front pieces of the trousers with the zipper facing out. Make sure to align the zipper and fabric pieces properly so that it looks neat and professional when the pants are finished.

Step 12: Match Your Back Portion of Your Pants with the Front Portion with the Underside of the Fabric Facing Out
Match the back part of your trousers with the front part of your trousers, making sure to keep the underside of the fabric facing out. Secure the pieces together with pins and make sure the pattern pieces match up perfectly before stitching. 

Step 13: Stitch the Outside Leg Seams with a Single Stitch
Stitch the outside leg seams of the trousers with a single stitch. Be sure to double check that all edges are matched and aligned properly before stitching.

Step 14: Cut Some Waist Band Interfacing to the Length of Your Waist Measurement
Cut waist band interfacing to the length of your waist measurement using scissors. Interfacing is an added fabric that provides extra support, definition and structure to the waist band.

Step 15: Pin the Waist Band to the Trousers
Pin the interfacing to the trousers, making sure to keep the underside of the fabric facing out. Be sure to double check the alignment before you start stitching.

Step 16: Stitch the Waist Band Ends Together and Trim Any Excess Fabric
Stitch the ends of the waist band together and trim any excess fabric. This will give you a nice, reinforced waist band that will help keep the trousers in place.

Step 17: Try the Pants on to See How Far They Need to Be Hemmed
Once the waistband is attached, it's time to try on the trousers and see how far they need to be hemmed. If they need to be hemmed, mark the bottom edge of the trousers and cut the extra fabric off.

Step 18: Attach a Button and Cut a Button Hole at the Waist Band and Above the Zipper
Attach a button at the waist band and create a corresponding buttonhole just above the zipper. This will give you the perfect, professional look.

Making your own trousers is a fun and rewarding task that anyone can do. With just 9 easy steps, you can make a great pair of trousers that you or your loved one will enjoy for years. So, grab that fabric, pattern and some interfacing and get stitching!

How to Prevent Mold in the Kitchen' 
Having a clean kitchen doesn't only result in delicious meals – it can prevent mold from taking over the room. Mold growth can be a serious health hazard, so taking steps to prevent it is key. Here are some easy ways to reduce the risk of mold in the kitchen:

Use a garbage can that holds about one day's worth of garbage and empty it on a regular basis to reduce the moisture that can lead to mold growth. If you can, try to have two trash cans in the kitchen, allowing you to completely empty one at the end of the day and keep the second one for the next day's trash.

Make sure to clear old food out of the refrigerator regularly. In addition, check any potatoes or other fruit you store outside the refrigerator on a daily basis and discard any signs of mold growth.

Keep your compost container covered and empty it daily. When composting, careful attention should be taken to avoid introducing unwanted bacteria or mold into it.

Run your garbage disposal at least once a day and, for extra protection, pour straight vinegar into it once a week. Straight vinegar works as an excellent cleaning agent and natural mold inhibitor.

Clean the drip tray of your refrigerator a couple of times a year and make sure it is free of any debris.

Reduce mold growth by washing your cutting board with straight vinegar weekly.

Turn on exhaust fans and vents when cooking or working in the kitchen to prevent humid air from causing mold growth.

Fix any leaks in kitchen sinks and pipes and any other water pipes, such as the pipe that supplies water to the freezer's ice maker. Make sure to take care of any damaged areas right away to prevent the growth of any mold.

If it is safe to do so, open windows and doors for a few hours a day to reduce the humidity. Use a dehumidifier if you live in a climate with high humidity.

Clean the countertops with an antibacterial cleanser every day to reduce the risk of mold growth.

When running the water, keep the flow as low as possible to reduce the chance of splashing and damping on the area around the sink.

Use tile or other hard surfaces for the floors in the kitchen. Rugs and carpets are magnets for moisture and can be a breeding ground for mold.

Another option is to use mold-resistant paint in your kitchen. There are many paints on the market now that are designed to inhibit the growth of mold.

By following these simple tips you can reduce the possibility of mold growing in your kitchen. Taking action now will ensure your kitchen remains healthy and safe for many years to come.

The ongoing cost of caring for a dog should also be calculated. Supplies such as food, toys and bedding can be found in pet stores or online and their cost should be estimated. Investing in training is a better option than paying for expensive classes, plus you can learn the skills yourself. Annual pet care costs, such as vet visits, vaccines, and grooming, need to be taken into consideration. It’s also important to save money for a possible medical emergency, and look into pet insurance. 

The type of dog you choose is also an important factor. Take into account the pros and cons of purebred dogs versus shelter dogs. If you’re going for the latter, you may want to also get extra medical screening done. Make sure an emergency vet clinic is identified in case of any health complications. Training classes, private sessions, or online tutorials are all options, so check out what is available. 

Once you’ve made the decision, take your time to prepare for the arrival of your new pup. Dog-proof your home by finding and eliminating potential hazards. Invest in modern pet supplies and setup a comfortable area for them. Dogs should spend most of their day indoors, however they need outdoor spaces, too. Weigh the time factor: It’s true that some breeds need more exercise, but there are also low-maintenance breeds which require less time and energy. Some dogs need someone to be home all day while others can adapt to occasions where they are home alone for a while. This decision will determine your lifestyle following the dog arrival. 

Can’t manage the daily time commitment? Hiring a dog walker or taking them to doggy daycare are two great options. Getting an adult dog or a puppy are both viable options, the latter being a great choice if there is someone that can stay home long enough for proper training. Factor in traveling, and evaluate the schedule you have in the coming years. Children can also benefit from a pet, but plan ahead around their activity schedule. 

Last of all, ask yourself if you’re ready to commit to the daily routine of owning a pet. Proper care involves regular meal times, playtime, potty breaks and walks, training, and a thorough clean up. Remember to plan for outdoor adventures, various competitions and, of course, games. One of the most rewarding parts of pet ownership his the bond that you build as you and your dog get to know each other. 

So, depending on whether you’re looking to adopt a pup for the long run or have a suitable lifestyle for raising a pet, evaluate all the factors before making your decision. Owning a dog is an honorable and rewarding experience, but make sure you are well-equipped for the adventure.

Making a stand from clay for your phone is a great way to use your creativity while also displaying your device in a unique way. You don't need a lot of knowledge or tools to successfully make your phone stand – just a few basic items and some time. With a little bit of patience and practice, you can make a homemade phone stand from clay that will be guaranteed to make your phone stand out and look great. 

To make a phone stand from clay, you'll need:

Clay
Measuring tape
Paint
Clay Cutter/Knife
Clay Smoother Tool 

Step 1: Measure your phone's length and height – this will tell you how much clay you need for the base of your phone stand.

Step 2: Purchase suitable clay. Make sure that the type of clay you buy is soft enough for molding and that it is able to be painted once it is dry.

Step 3: Take about a handful of clay and roll it into a sphere before flattening it on a flat surface.

Step 4: Mold the sphere into a neat square shape that can be used as a base for the phone stand.

Step 5: Fold the edges up on three sides. This will help you create a balance for your phone stand.

Step 6: Take another, more generous handful of clay. Roll this into a ball and flatten it out to create the rectangular cradle piece on which your phone will rest.

Step 7: Hold the rectangle against the base, on the side not folded up. This will create an even surface for your phone. 

Step 8: Fold the edges upward, around the remaining sides of the rectangular cradle piece. Again, this will help make a more secure and balanced base.

Step 9: Take your phone and put it on the stand. This will help you make sure that the cradle piece is the correct shape and size to fit the phone.

Step 10: Smooth out the clay using your thumbs or a clay smoother tool. This will help give your phone stand a clean and professional finish.

Step 11: Add decorative effects, if wished. Here you can be as creative as you like. You can cut shapes out of the clay or use clay tools to create patterns on the surface.

Step 12: Stick clay shapes onto the stand. This will help create a more decorated phone stand with more colour and depth. 

Step 13: Let the whole stand dry for about 48 hours or until stand is completely white.

Step 14: Choose the color(s) that you wish to use for the inside of the phone stand. This will be the color that shows through the clay decorations.

Step 15: Paint the inside of the stand. Make sure you cover all the elements of the stand.

Step 16: Take the color(s) you wish to use for the outside of the phone stand and paint the stand on the outside.

Step 17: Paint the decorations any color you want. Here you can really unleash your creativity.

Step 18: Add more decorative effects if wished.

Step 19: Allow the paint to dry completely before use. 

And there you have it – a homemade phone stand from clay that will be sure to make your phone stand out and look great. With a little bit of creativity and practice, you can create a great and unique phone stand that will really show off your device. Enjoy!

Removing a serpentine belt using auto tensioner is a great task to keep your engine running smooth. It is important to know the steps to safely and correctly complete the task. Follow the guidance below to remove your serpentine belt using an auto tensioner successfully. 

Determine Repair Parts Needed: All moving parts are subject to failure and you may need to remove the serpentine belt to replace the belt itself or one of the components it drives. Examine closely the belt and other components that the belt drives in the serpentine configuration. If there are any issues with the belt or any of the components, it is important to replace the necessary parts prior to removing the serpentine belt. 

Park the Vehicle and Set Emergency Brake: Park your vehicle in a level spot and set the emergency brake. This is particularly important if you are on a slope and do not want the vehicle to move while doing the repairs.

Raise Hood and Set Hood Brace: In order to have access to the serpentine belt, it is important to raise the hood of the vehicle’s engine compartment. Once open, set the hood brace to keep it open if your vehicle has one attached. This will keep the hood secure while doing repairs on the serpentine belt.

Disconnect Negative Battery Cable: Disconnect the negative battery cable connector from the battery terminal to be sure that no one will be able to actuate the engine or starter.

Locate Serpentine Belt and Diagram: Look for a diagram decal posted near the front of the engine compartment that lays out the serpentine belt. This will help in locating the serpentine belt auto tensioner pulley. Make sure engine has cooled before attempting to remove serpentine belt.

Remove Tensioner Pulley: Use one of the tools mentioned below to pivot the tensioner pulley to take the tension off the belt. Be careful to not let the tool slip or release the tool handle suddenly as this could sling the tool and cause damage to the auto or possibly result in serious injury. Then hold the tension from the belt, and slip the belt off the pulley. Slowly release the tension to avoid damage or injury, and then remove the tool from the belt auto tensioner. 

Remove Belt from Remaining Pulleys: Finally, you will want to carefully examine the pattern as you remove the belt from the remaining pulleys, to be sure that you understand the routing of the belt for replacing it later in reverse sequence.

Once the serpentine belt has been successfully removed, then you can proceed with the repairs or replacement of the parts necessary. After you complete the repairs or replacement of the components, the serpentine belt will be replaced using the reverse of the above steps. This means the tensioner pulley will be set first, and then the serpentine belt will be put back in place on the other pulleys in the serpentine belt layout. Be sure to reconnect the negative battery cable before starting the vehicle. 

Removing a serpentine belt using an auto tensioner is not a difficult task to complete, as long as you are familiar with the steps and tools necessary. Follow the steps above to correctly and safely remove the serpentine belt from the vehicle and then proceed with necessary repairs or replacement of the parts. This task will help keep your engine running smooth so always be sure to keep up with regular maintenance.
