How to Lead 'That’s My Mom'

That’s My Mom is an interesting game that involves asking a question about what a mom does at work to identify her unseeingly. It offers a unique and fun opportunity that requires a bit of planning and execution on your part. With this guide, you will be able to lead the game without a hitch. Here is how to do it.

 

Explain the Game

Before you start the game, make sure that everybody understands the rules and objectives. Explain to your participants that you are going to try to match them to their moms using the same types of questions that would be asked at a job interview. Ask them to think of a job they might like to do and to come up with some questions that they would ask to find out if their mother does that job. Let them know in advance that if they do pick their mom, they will receive a prize.

Select the Contestants

Gather the moms who are participating in the game and collect their names, job titles, and organizations. Divide the moms into smaller groups and then select the daughters who will participate in the game. Explain that they will be asked questions about their mother's job and that they will receive a prize if they correctly identify their own mom.

Photograph the Teams

Take a group photograph of the moms and daughters together before the game begins. This will be a nice reminder once the game is over.

Blindfold the Daughters

Have the daughters put on blindfolds before starting the game. Make sure they cannot see or hear anything else that is going on.

Form the Daughters Panel

Assign a leader for each of the daughters’ teams. Explain to them that the leader is responsible for selecting which questions the daughters can ask and to whom.

Form the Mom's Panel

Instruct the moms to form a panel of five to seven members and assign a leader for each of the teams. Change one mom's panelist if necessary, in order that the moms cannot easily identify their own daughters.

Photograph the Moms Panel and the Daughters Panel

Take a photograph of the two panels before they start the game. This will be especially helpful in case the winner ends up not being able to identify their real mother.

Provide Yes / No Signs

Give each participant a yes or no sign when handing out the blindfolds. This will help the participants to keep track of whether or not they correctly answered the question.

Assign a Number to Each Mom

Assign a number to each mom and indicate that on the sign they will be given. This will also help the participants to keep track of which mother they have correctly identified.

Instruct the Daughters

Instruct the daughters to ask a question to one of the moms when they are tapped on their shoulder. Explain that they will be given the opportunity to ask a yes or no question to the mom about her job.

Play The Game

Escort each blindfolded daughter to her new mom as she identifies her and hold her hand until she is done with the question. Do not tell her if she is correct or not until after the question has been answered. Repeat the process until all the daughters have selected a new mom.

Photograph the New Families

Take photographs of the new families once each daughter has selected a new mom.

Ask The Daughters

Ask the daughters if they think they correctly identified their real mom. This will give you an idea of how well they played the game.

Direct the Moms

Direct the moms to remove their new daughter's blindfolds. Also, ask the moms to remain quiet so that they do not give away their identity.

Photograph the Moms Panel and the Daughters Panel Again

Take a photograph of the two panels with the blindfolds removed. This will be a nice reminder of the game once it is over.

Issue Prizes

Present prizes to the daughters who correctly identified their mom as well as to the moms who were successfully identified.

Discuss Parent/Daughter Communication

Discuss the importance of parent/daughter communication. Make sure to acknowledge the teams that correctly identified each other and reward them for their effort.

Present Career Descriptions

Present to the participants the different career descriptions of the moms. Have each mom explain their job and the path they took to get there.

Have a Second Round of the Game

If time permits, have a second round of the game with a different set of questions. This can provide a great opportunity to assess their understanding of the types of questions that may be asked about a job.

Provide an Album of the Photos

Provide an album of the photos to the panelists as a souvenir of the program. This will help them to remember their experience and may even inspire their creativity in other games.

How to Have A Successful First Band Practice

Having your first band practice can be a daunting task but it doesn't have to be. By following the five easy steps below, you'll have the confidence and knowledge to create an exciting and successful first practice session. 

Choose what songs you will be playing. 
Before your first practice, sit down with your band members and agree on five songs to learn. These should be songs that everyone enjoys and is comfortable playing with. Make sure to pick a variety of songs that cater to each of the band members' individual strengths and weaknesses, ensuring that everyone is able to play their part and contribute to the practice sessions. 

Agree which song you will learn first, then go home and learn your parts. 
Now that you've chosen what songs to learn it's time to decide which one will be learned first. Once you make that decision, take that one song home and practice. Learn the lyrics and music of your part so you can come to the practice feeling prepared. It's also a good idea to print out copies of the lyrics and chords so you can easily refer to them during your session. 

Make sure the band members are in time with each other. 
When you meet for the first band practice, the first step should be to make sure the band is in tune. Go over the song you're learning together, slowly at first to ensure everyone is playing in time. It's important to be patient and encouraging when playing with a group of people. It may take a few tries and each person may have to adjust to the different individual playing styles, but once you've nailed it, you're ready to go. 

Once you're all certain you're all in time, play the song through a few times. 
Once you have all picked up the song, proceed to play it through a few times. This will allow the band to get familiar with the arrangement and get a good feel of the song. Jamming together also helps build relationships and encourages each member to get more comfortable playing in front of others. 

Repeat process for next week, but with another song you all want to cover. 
After you've completed the first practice session, it's important to repeat the process the following week with another song. This song should be different from the one you practiced the first week. Show everyone the lyrics and music to the song ahead of time, and play it through on the day of practice. Playing different songs each session will help you have a successful first practice session. 

Remember to practice the first song you learned at your next practice session too. 
The songs you decide to practice should be continuously practiced, such as the song you practiced the first session. This will ensure that you have it down and that everyone is comfortable playing it. When you continue to practice the same song every session you get more comfortable and familiar with it and it allows more exploration with improvisation. 

Consider writing your own music. 
Writing your own music is a great challenge for your band, and will also help to form a tighter connection between all of you. Make sure each member brings anything they have already written to the practices and encourage everyone to share and collaborate on new material. 

Before you go, make sure you have a basic knowledge of chords. 
It's essential to have a basic knowledge of the chords associated with the lyrics and music that you are practicing. This way when you go to your practice the band can seamlessly flow through the song and everyone can improvise knowing they are in key. 

So now you have lyrics and musical parts. You have it all, lyrics, vocals, music, what are you still reading this for? 
Now that you have all elements of a song, it’s time to practice and refine it to get it ready for a public performance. Work on finding the style and sound that you want for the song and let it grow organically. As the performance comes together the band will become stronger and more in sync. 

So now your song fits, hopefully! 
By following these five steps, you can ensure that your first band practice runs smoothly. Practice your song until you are confident with it and have explored each musical element involved. Writing your own music is a great challenge too, as it will help strengthen relationships between every band member. With the right planning, preparation and enthusiasm, you can have a successful first band practice!

How to Rig a Fishing Line
Knowing how to correctly rig a fishing line is an important skill for any angler to have. Having the right combination of hooks, sinkers, bobbers, swivels and leaders can help you catch more fish and make your time on the water more enjoyable. But with so many components available, it can also be confusing to know where to start. 

Before you can start using a fishing line, it’s important to understand the parts of a hook. Hooks come in a variety of types and sizes, and typically have four or fewer points. The points are usually labeled by letter; the bending point (where the hook curves) is often labeled “A” and the point farthest from the eye (the small hole in the hammer end) is labeled “D”. Hooks are also sized from smallest to largest using a numbering system. The smaller the number, the smaller the hook size, with the smallest being size 32. Size 8 is the largest commonly available hook. 

Hooks come in a variety of styles, with the single hook being the most common. Single hooks come in several varieties, including treble hooks (which have three points), circle hooks (designed to hook the fish in the corner of the mouth), and jig hooks (which usually feature a wide gap between the points and an eye at the bottom). 

Sinkers are made from a variety of materials, including metal, lead, tungsten, brass and nylon. Metal sinkers are the most popular and widely available. They come in a variety of shapes, including round, flat, barrel and egg sinkers. Sinkers are used to keep the bait or lure at a certain depth and to add enough weight to cast your line further. 

When fishing from a boat or shore, bobbers are often used to help you detect strikes from fish. Bobbers come in a variety of materials, including wood, plastic and foam, and in a variety of shapes, including egg-shape, ball and pencil. To connect your bobber to your line, use a slip bobber stopper or a snap swivel. When using a bobber, it’s important to choose the smallest one that will keep your bait or lure afloat. 

Swivel knots are used to keep the line from twisting. They come in a variety of sizes, from very small to quite large. They are also available in a variety of colors, so you can match the color of your line.

Leaders are an important part of rigging a fishing line. Leaders are typically made of monofilament line and are attached to the hook surrounded by a swivel knot. This allows the leader to move freely when a fish strikes, while keeping the lure or bait near the hook. When tying a leader, two of the most common knots are the improved clinch knot and the Palomar knot. 

The improved clinch knot is one of the most popular knots used when tying a hook to a line. It’s easy to do and is used to fasten a hook or swivel to the line. A variation of it, known as the uni-knot, is also popular and can be used for many other needs in fishing. 

Once you’ve learned the basics of rigging a fishing line, there are a few ways to assemble it for specific tasks. The most common is the basic bobber rig. This is great for still-fishing live bait from shore. It’s also easy to assemble a sliding sinker rig that can be used for drift fishing or slow trolling from a boat. For drift fishing or trolling when you want to suspend your bait off the bottom, use a 3-way rig. And for fishing live bait directly under a boat or ice shanty, use a drop shot rig. 

By understanding the various components of a fishing line, the correct knots for setting up the line, and the different styles of rigging available, you’ll be better equipped to find success and enjoy your next fishing trip.

How to Drive in a Metropolitan Area if You're from the Country'

Driving in metropolitan areas can be intimidating if you're used to the wide open roads of the country. Follow some important rules to ensure your safety and make sure you enjoy the experience.

The first rule is to find someone who is an experienced driver in the metropolitan area to give you a few lessons. If possible, have this person drive with you for awhile so you can become accustomed to the pace and flow of city traffic. This person should also be able to give you helpful tips and tricks to make your driving experience much smoother.

For those who drive a car with a manual transmission, you should be prepared for a leg workout if you get caught in rush hour bumper to bumper traffic, as most drivers would rather not be in this situation. Make sure to relax your muscles and not strain them too much as you try to move forward while the traffic is at a standstill.

Once you are out on the roads there are a few basic rules of thumb to follow. The first one is to signal when you are turning or changing lanes. This allows other drivers to be aware of your intentions and prepare ahead of time. The second rule is to be in the right lane when you make a turn, as turning in the wrong lane is illegal in most metropolitan areas. If you get to the intersection and realize your mistake, don't turn anyway. Make the U-turn at the next left turn lane instead.

Another basic rule is to be courteous to other drivers. If someone is trying to get into your lane, for instance, slow down a bit to give them room and use your turn signal to let them know you are allowing them to get in. Similarly, if someone is signaling to change lanes from your lane to another lane, don't try to crowd them out by passing them on that side before they can switch lanes. It's just not a nice thing to do.

One final issue to think about is when there are multiple lanes in one direction. Most of the time, you should make right turns from the rightmost lane and left turns from the leftmost lane, unless signs or arrows are present telling you otherwise.

Also, don't be too upset if someone waves at you and you don't return the wave or if someone flips you off. Just keep your eyes on the road and move along.

All in all, don't let the "big city" scare you away from driving in a metropolitan area. With a little bit of practice and some basic rules of thumb, you can quickly become adept at driving in the city. So get out there, have a blast, and enjoy your drive!

Now it's time to close your pool for fall/winter. To do this correctly, balance the water chemistry and follow some important steps to ensure a smooth closing.

First, adjust your pool water to the recommended ranges. The pH should be between 7.2 and 7.6, alkalinity should be between 80 and 120 ppm, and calcium hardness should range from 180 to 220 ppm. Add pool shock to sanitize the water and remove any bacteria. A chlorine shock or non-chlorine shock can be used, at least 1 lb. per 10,000 gallons.

Once the water has been prepared, remove any skimmer baskets, wall fittings, pool cleaners, solar blankets and ladders from the pool, and store them in a safe and dry place. Then, lower the water level in the pool using a filter pump or a submersible pump. For mesh covers, the water should be 12-18 inches below the skimmer, and 3-6 inches below the tile for solid, floating covers.

Drain all the pumping, filtering, heating and chlorinating equipment. Make sure to access all the drain plugs so that any remaining water can be properly drained. This is also a great time to lubricate the pump lid o-rings with Magic Lube.

Next, clean the pool thoroughly one last time before covering it. Skim away any debris, vacuum the pool, and brush the entire surface to remove any buildup.

If you have an in-ground pool, blow out the lines using a MightyVac from the skimmer, through the equipment, and back to the pool. Also, add winterizing algaecide and other floaters. Don't add algacide and shock at the same time.

Once all of these steps have been correctly followed, you are now ready to cover the pool. Make sure to select a quality cover and secure it properly so it won't get blown off in a storm. Congratulations, you can now have your pool rest safely over the winter, and look forward to an enjoyable and safe summer pool season.

How to Protect Your Rare Maps and Manuscripts
Taking care of your rare map and manuscript collection is very important, not only for its preservation but also so you can be sure to enjoy it for years to come. If you have a collection of valuable maps, manuscripts, and other artifacts, here are some tips to ensure their longevity: 

Handle them carefully. Always handle your rare maps and manuscripts with two (clean) hands and never handle them by the edges, particularly if tears are already evident. Do not use any abrasive cleaners. The oils and dirt on your hands will take longer to fade away from the paper than just a cloth, so it’s always best to wash your hands prior to handling maps and manuscripts.

Prepare a clean viewing surface on which to enjoy your collection, with no liquids, foods, ink pens or other messy objects nearby. Avoid any use of paper clips, staples post-it notes or other potentially damaging stationery items.

When it comes to storage, don’t store your collection in a space where there are extreme changes in temperature or humidity. Avoid anywhere frequented by insects or rodents--such as attics, basements, and garages. Maps and manuscripts should generally be stored flat, either in a shallow drawer or acid-free box. If the artifact is too large to store flat, then carefully roll it into a large diameter tube. Keep your maps and manuscripts away from strong direct or reflected sunlight, as this will fade the colors and worsen the deterioration of the paper. Don't display your collection in spaces prone to damp, such as a bathroom or basement or outside surface, as the excess humidity will also damage the paper.

When it comes to framing your maps or manuscripts, it is usually best to employ someone who is trained in proper framing techniques. Proper framing should be superficially artistic - after all, your collection is supposed to be enjoyed! Be sure that the frame is sealed, and that materials included in the frame are of the highest quality. The frame of your map or manuscript should also be periodically inspected for any problems which can damage the artifact, as should the dust cover. Test the bumpers and hanging mechanisms of the frame regularly to make sure they are secure. 

By taking these few simple steps, you can guarantee the satisfactory protection and preservation of your rare maps and manuscripts for years to come.

Having trouble downloading apps, games, or content from the Microsoft Store on your computer? No worries; there are a few things you can try to do to fix this problem and get back to downloading quickly.

Next, open your computer's search bar again. This time, type in "Store". The "Store" icon will appear, along with the downward-facing arrow next to the search bar. Click the arrow to review your downloads, and make sure that the Microsoft Store app is open. 

After that, click your account icon to the left of the search bar. Select your account name, and click "Downloads and Updates" in the pop-up window. You should then click the "Check for Updates" button and wait for the updates to apply. Then, simply return to the app download page, and make sure that your Store app is open.

How to Replace a Flat Roof
Replacing a flat roof is a project that can make a huge difference to the look and the safety of your home. A well installed flat roof can last for decades with just routine maintenance, and provide protection from the elements. Replacing your flat roof is not a job that should be taken lightly, and should only be attempted by experienced contractors.

Decide what type of low pitch, flat roof you want to install. There are several types of flat roofs to choose from, and you should research the benefits and drawbacks of each type before you make your decision. The most common kinds of flat roofs are built-up roof (BUR), modified bitumen, and single-ply membrane. Consider the environment you are in, the type of building you have, and necessary maintenance for the material you choose.

Determine what materials you will need to complete the job. Once you know the kind of roof you want to install, research the materials you will need to get the job done. In addition to the different types of roofing materials, you may also need wire mesh, plywood, felt (paper), flashing, and sealants. Make sure you know how much of each material you need and plan ahead for any unforeseen circumstances.

Remove the old roofing. Before you can begin to install the new roof, you must remove any existing roofing material, fasteners, nails, and plywood decking. Wear protective gear and use the appropriate tools when removing the old roofing material.

Replace any sections of the plywood decking that have been damaged by water or "dry-rot" (fungus) before you install a new roof. After you have removed the old roofing, inspect the plywood decking and replace any sections that are damaged. Many roofing materials require stable, supportive substrate to adhere to, so replacing any damaged decking is essential for a safe and durable roof.

Install wooden or synthetic can't strips. These strips can help to provide a continuous seal along the roof edges and where the roof meets the walls or chimney. They also act as an anchor for the new roofing material.

Lay down the felt (paper) base sheet (if required for your process). Depending on the type of roof you are installing, you may need to lay down a layer of felt paper before you begin roofing. This sheet provides an extra layer of protection to ensure your roof lasts for years to come.

Add flashing to the roof. Flashing helps to provide extra protection along the edges of the roof and helps prevent water from getting underneath the roofing material. Install flashings along the edges of the roof and seal any joints between the flashing and the roofing material.

If BUR is legal as some cities do not allow BUR, especially on residences, then "build up roofing" layers held in place by mopping molten, hot tar or asphalt -- coal tar is a known carcinogen. Installing asphalt BUR roofing typically uses LP gas as heat, contributing to air pollution, and toxic, green-house gases are released during installation.

Cut a 12 inch (30.48 cm) starter strip to mop it down as the first row of the starting edge, often the lowest edge and working up to the higher elevated part of the roof. Start at the lower sections of the roof and work your way up the roof. The starter strip provides extra protection along the starting edge.

To apply the first coat of hot asphalt over the nailed felt base, spread the hot asphalt with a large mop -- as the felt is rolled out into the mopped hot "cement", one row at a time. Pour the asphalt onto the roof and spread it evenly with a long handle rubber mop. Check for bumps and make adjustments where necessary.

Continue laying each row with a 24 inch (61 cm) overlap of the one before it, using full width felt, over the entire roof for the first complete layer. Make sure each row has an overlap of 24 inches (61 cm), which provides an extra layer of waterproofing.

Hot mop each felt as the next layer is rolled on. This will ensure a secure and waterproof seal between the layers of felt and the asphalt.

Optional: Finish it by spreading crushed granite aggregate (called ballast/gravel) after you've installed all of the desired layers. This adds an extra layer of protection to the roof and makes it look more attractive. Spread the ballast/gravel evenly and then use a broom or brush to sweep it into the tar.

Finally, seal all of the joints and corners in the roof. This can be done using an elastic sealant or rubberized asphalt.

Replacing a flat roof can be a big job, but the extra layer of protection it provides will keep your home safe from the elements for many years. Follow the steps outlined above and you should have no trouble completing your project. With careful planning and attention to detail, you can make sure the job is done safely and correctly.

How to Read The Mayan Calendar
The Maya civilization occupied much of Central America, stretching from southern Mexico to northern Guatemala. The Maya used three different calendars to measure days, months, and longer cycles of time. To properly read a Mayan calendar date, it is important to understand the structure and symbolism of each calendar. This article will provide a step-by-step guide on how to read the Mayan calendar.

Learn the divisions of the Haab calendar. The Haab calendar is one Mayan method of counting time. This calendar was used in conjunction with a second system known as the Tzolkin calendar, to give more robust measures of time. The Haab was made up of 18 months (‘uinals’) each composed of 20 days (‘kin’). The Maya added an extra five days at the end which were known as "Wayeb".

Count using the months of the Haab calendar. Each 20-day uinal and the 5-day month Wayeb are counted beginning with day 0 and ending with day 19 or 4, respectively. The uinals were given their own names, although they did not always adhere to specific seasons. To understand the dates of the Haab calendar, count each day from zero.

Count using the Tzolkin calendar. The Tzolkin calendar has 20 days. In the Tzolkin, each day was associated with one of the 20 day names and one of the 13 numbers. On any given day, the day name and the number could be said to be in sync. There were four Tzolkin cycles in a Haab year.

Reckon using the days of the Tzolkin calendar. Each day in the Tzolkin cycle has a sacred significance (honoring a particular god, for instance), and a unique name. The day names are each associated with a symbol of a particular bird, animal, or element. In the Mayan older cycles, each day name can repeat up to 20 times consecutively.

Put the Haab and Tzolkin Calendars together to make a whole date or calendar round. Most Mayan dates are expressed as a combination of the Haab and Tzolkin calendars. The two form an interlocking system known as a calendar round, forming long cycles between repetitions of each date. For instance, a calendar round date would look something like 12 Lamat 7 Yax.

Use the Long Calendar for greater spans of time. The Mayan calendar also has larger cycles for reckoning spans of time that are longer than 52 years. This is the Long Calendar, where the cycle of dates is broken into cycles of 260 days, or “Tun”, from 0 to 10, and then repeats itself.

Read the Mayan long count date. The Mayan calendar reckons any date in terms of its distance from a fixed start date. This fixed start date, known as the 0.0.0.0.0. date, can be expressed as 13.0.0.0.0. in the long count notation. This notation counts the number of tuns, katuns, baktuns, piktuns, kalabtuns, and alautuns since that date.

Understand how dates are recorded and read using the Gregorian calendar. The format used by the Maya in the long count notation is the same used by the Gregorian calendar. Dates are read from right to left, with each block counting up in tens or twenties.

Compare this familiar system to the same date written using the Mayan calendar. Each long count date can also be written in Mayan numerals, which are written in the bar-and-dot system. In this system each period is written as a line of dots and bars, with a bar signifying five and a dot signifying one.

Express the Mayan creation cycle date. Long count dates will also contain a creation cycle date, written as 0.0.0.0.0. or 13.0.0.0.0. This is the Mayan equivalent of a Christian era date, and marks the start a creation cycle.

Use a calendar converter. Understanding Mayan calendrical systems can be confusing. Using a calendar calculator on the internet can help to translate each type of Mayan calendar date into a more familiar, Gregorian format. With this information, anyone can now understand the meaning of longer cycle calendrical dates in the Maya civilization - and read the Mayan calendar.

How to Get a Cow With Nerve Damage to Her Hind Legs from a Long Birth or Hard Pull to Stand Up is an important task that must be done to ensure the health and safety of the cow. There are several steps you can take to ensure a successful outcome.

First, contact your local large animal veterinarian to assess whether the reason your cow is down is really from nerve paralysis and not something more serious. Once you have determined the cause that she is down from nerve paralysis, it is time to get her to stand up. There are several procedures that you can do, but, be sure to exercise caution.

Begin by gently lifting her back feet off the ground and raising them up to her chest in a rocking motion. Once she is up on all four legs, grab her tail to keep her from falling. Try to keep her on her feet for a few minutes. If she goes down again, let her rest for a few minutes before trying to get her up again. Repeat the procedure until she can stand and walk on her own.

Once she is up and moving, make sure she can stand and walk on her own before you leave her and her calf alone. If the cow still cannot stand, keep her in an area where there is straw or soft hay for her to lay on. Make sure the area is dry and well ventilated.

Keep an eye on her until you are certain that she's figured out how to manage by herself. If her nerve issue is serious, your vet may prescribe anti-inflammatory medications, Vitamin E, Selenium and steroids for her to assist nerve healing and reduce swelling.

Finally, check on her often and keep trying to get her up. If she goes down again, carefully lift her back legs and try to help her stand again. It is important to turn her over a couple times a day so she's not always laying on one side all the time. This will help ensure that she does not get sores or pressure ulcers.

Most cows will get up after a few hours or a few days, especially if you are persistent in helping them get up. However, if she has been down for a while when you do find her, the outcome may not be as good, and she may need to be humanely euthanized. Keep in mind that no matter what the outcome, it is important to do what is best for the health and safety of your cow.

How to Prepare and Install an Above Ground Swimming Pool Liner

Preparing and installing an above ground swimming pool liner can be a daunting task, but with a little effort and care, you can get a quality installation that will last for years. With a few easy steps, you can get your pool ready to start using it and enjoying it. 

First, you'll need to temporarily unroll your new liner in a sunny, debris-free area. This will help you spot any factory-made defects or issues. After unrolling the liner, seal the through-the-wall skimmer hole area with cardboard. Then, seal the water return and lighting holes with duct tape. To make sure these areas stay secure, it is also recommended to insert two feet of shop vac hose through the card boarded skimmer area.

After doing the needed preparations, it’s now time to inspect all duct taped areas. Make sure everything is secure and in place. Then, re-inspect the pool base to make sure it is still clean, flat and debris free. Once you’re satisfied, attach two wooden clothespins to each upright. Now, fold the new liner in half and place it in the pool area, but make sure to retain both ends. 

Start the installation process by carefully unfolding the liner in the pool area. Then, attach it to the pool wall using the clothes pins while evenly pulling the liner further over the wall. While doing so, also make sure to release and attach pins as needed. Gently brush and tap the liner towards the walls to make sure it is correctly in place.

Then, inspect and adjust the liner as needed. Once you’re happy with the appearance, it’s time to get some help for the next steps, like hooking up the shop vac to the vac hose and turning it on. Be sure to release the liner evenly as it tightens by releasing and attaching the clothespins. Keep brushing and tapping the liner around the entire perimeter. Once the liner is completely seated and even, inspect the liner for wrinkles and alignment.

If all looks good, start filling the pool with water. Keep filling the pool until at least an inch of water covers the entire bottom of the pool. Then, shut off the shop vac and reassemble all the pool equipment, like the seat clamps, pool ledges, and top plates and rail. Continue to fill the pool with water until a foot of water covers the bottom of the pool.

After that, install all the face plates and gaskets. Carefully cut out all the liner material from the gasketed areas and remove all duct tape seals. Lastly, fill the pool to its appropriate operational level. Hook up the filtration system and any other accessories. Then, add your start up chemicals and you’re done!

Taming pigeons to be out of cage permanently is an achievable goal and can be a rewarding process. Adopting or buying young birds is the best way to begin the taming process and can help ensure the health of your new pet birds. It’s important to find a breeder online to buy a specific species, and avoid attempting to tame a wild bird.

For outdoor pigeons, build a large and safe aviary. Ensure that the aviary has enough space for your birds to fly and hop. Put in perches, mirrors, and plenty of bird dishes in the aviary. Making it easy to clean is key. Lay down drain rock in the aviary and locate in a sunny outdoor area.

For indoor birds, you’ll need a spacious and safe cage. Choose a bird cage that’s away from fumes and near a window. Allow your birds to adjust to their cage and new home by remaining patient and not stressing them out. Talk in a calm voice and make slow movements around the birds. Let them become familiar with your presence by spending time near their cage or aviary.

After your birds become more comfortable, offer them treats when they’re in their enclosures. For indoor birds, you can let them explore your home. Make sure to always supervise your birds, however, as they’re still taming. Never let a domesticated pigeon fly freely, as they can become confused and lost in this unfamiliar territory. Also, remember to protect your birds from other animals, such as cats and dogs, as well as any other potential predators.

For both indoor and outdoor pigeons, provide plenty of items inside their enclosures to keep them entertained. Shelves, perches, and mirrors should be added. Also, create an artificial bathtub for your birds to play with. This can be fun for them, as pigeons actually love water. Always keep giving your birds fresh, clean water to drink.

Feeding your pigeons should consist of bird seed and leafy greens daily. If you are unable to give them these treats, get them commercial bird food that is high in nutrition and low in fat.

With enough patience and care, you can successfully tame pigeons to be out of cage permanently. Carefully follow these steps to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. With quality bonding time and access to plenty of food, perches, and water, your birds will be well-adjusted to their new home.

Now that you have all the items start by disconnecting the negative side of the battery. This is an important safety step in case you make any mistakes or short circuit anything. Then, remove the battery terminal top by un-clipping it. 

Afterwards, remove the fuse panel and drivers side piece of dash. Use the steering wheel removal tool to remove the steering wheel in order to gain access to the fuse box. After you have removed the panel, move on to removing the T20 Torx Screws located underneath the drivers lower dash (AKA - Kick Panels). 

After that is done, pull the lower dash piece out but be careful because there is a clip there. You will then need to remove the dead pedal by unscrewing the T20 screws and then simply slide the pedal upward until all the 3 clips are detached. Afterwards, move on to removing the hood pull panel, side panels that run down the side of the vehicle, and the seat belt panel which has 2 Phillips screws at the bottom. The last panel is the easiest to remove. 

Now to run the cables + - push the cables through the firewall in the engine bay into the cockpit of the car. Once the cables are inside the vehicles cockpit ties down the cable as neat as possible with zip ties to ensure tidiness. Then, run cables parallel to the existing power cables going to the trunk. Once the cable is fed into the rear seating area feed the cables underneath the seats to penetrate in to the trunk area. Now do the same exact thing on the other side for the RCA cables and signal switch cable. 

Remove the car stereo using the OEM Removal tools and then it's time to solder. Make sure everything is connected correctly, then connect your power cable to the battery and connect all your cables to the amp. 

Now when your system is functional proceed on re applying the panels in their correct areas. Also to make your trunk look tidy zip tie and tuck away any noticeable cables. It's important to dress appropriately for a job interview, and choosing the right outfit in the summer can be especially tricky. If you’re interviewing at a company, chances are that your interviewer will expect you to look professional and well-groomed. To make sure you make the right impression, follow these tips on how to dress for a job interview in summer. 

First off, make sure you ask the hiring manager what the dress code is. While some companies have more relaxed dress codes in the summer months, others might still expect you to dress formally. Knowing what you should wear for your interview will help you to dress appropriately and give off the sensible and professional impression you want.

No matter the dress code, you should always make sure any clothes you choose to wear are impeccably clean, mended and ironed. No professional ensemble is complete without a freshly-pressed outfit that makes the right impact. How to Make a Camp Tent More Comfortable
Making your camping experience comfortable begins when you select a campsite that is well situated. Choose a quality site for pitching the tent. Give yourself bonus points if the ground has a soft cover of grass or pine needles that may provide an additional layer of insulation under your tent. Plan ahead by thinking how the sunshine will change your site in the morning and afternoon.

Choose the right sized tent for everyone and their gear. A tent too small means that you will be cramped, extra space means you can store all your belongings without fear of them getting wet. Use a tarpaulin sheet underneath the tent. The tarp will ensure that the bottom of the tent is waterproofed, create an extra layer of insulation and that your things stay dry. You should ensure that the tent has a fly and that it's in great condition, to help keep the tent cool in the summer and warm in cooler temperatures.

Steps for setting up a comfortable camp tent include:

1. Lay out the moisture barrier or tarpaulin sheet, making sure it is at least one foot larger than your tent.

2. Lay out the tent over the moisture barrier.

3. Set the stakes and finish raising your tent according to the manufacturer's instructions.

4. Bring self-inflating or inflatable mattresses with you. These mattresses provide extra cushion, insulation, and support, all of which will make you more comfortable when you're camping.

5. Bring your duvet and real pillows. Nothing makes camping more comfortable than a warm duvet and real pillows.

6. Consider using bed sheets. They will provide a smooth, comfortable surface and insulation against the cold ground.

7. Decorate your tent. Bring some posters, fairy lights or bunting  and use them to decorate the inside of your tent.

8. Place a chair, and mini table inside your tent. This will make it easier for you to eat and relax inside the tent.

9. Have books, magazines, and different games to have in your tent. 

10. Hang up lanterns. They will help to create a comfortable atmosphere and will provide a light source should you wake up in the middle of the night.

11. Have sufficient, safe lighting. Torchlight and lanterns provide enough light for walking around the campsite but not so much as to bother other campers. 

12. Pack a set of interlocking play mat foam tiles. These will be great when you have a break from nature and can’t stand the cold ground any more.

13. Set up the tent as per the instructions above.

14. Install the interlocking foam tiles inside your tent in the room that you will use for your sleeping bags.

15. Set up the rest of your equipment and gear inside the tent, as outlined above.

16. Realize that comfort isn't your number one priority, but you still need to consider it.

17. Carry a small self-inflating air mattress. This will provide a doable alternative to sitting or sleeping on the ground.

18. Purchase a small down-filled pillow that squashes right down. This will make a great addition to your camping equipment.

20. Make seating that beats the rocks. You can use foam seat cushions, foam blocks, and pillows to make comfortable seating arrangements outside the tent or in the tent.

21. Obtain and carry a very lightweight door mat. Since the ground gets damp at times, it's nice to have something that will keep the internal area of the camp tent dry.

With a bit of extra care and preparation, you can make the experience of camping more enjoyable. By following the steps listed above, you should be able to create the perfect camp tent for you and your family that will keep everyone relaxed and comfortable.

How to Get to Logan Airport
Logan Airport is located just outside Boston, Massachusetts and is one of the busiest airports in the United States. Ensuring that you get there on time and without any issues requires careful planning. If you’re flying out of Logan Airport, here’s how to get there.

Purchase an airline ticket to Logan Airport. Before you even think about leaving for the airport, you need to reserve and pay for your flight. Make sure to double-check your booking details and the flight's departure and arrival times. This will provide you with a timeframe for when you'll need to leave the house.

Ready yourself for travel. Packing lightly is essential for a smooth trip. Make sure you have your ticket, identification, and boarding passes as well as any medications that you might need along the trip. If you need to bring a laptop or other item, make sure that these are already packed and ready to go. Pack any snacks and drinks needed for the trip as well, so that you aren't tempted to buy junk food while in the airport or on the plane.

Travel to your airport of departure. Whether you are using public transportation, a taxi, a ride-sharing service, or are getting a lift from a family member, arrange your transportation ahead of time. Plan to reach the airport at least two hours before the departure time to ensure enough time for check-in, security lines, and any other procedures needed before boarding.

Learn your route. Getting to Logan Airport may vary depending on where you are located. The Massachusetts Bay Transport Authority (MBTA) offers travel options with service directly in front of the airport. Below are the directions you can take to reach Logan Airport from various parts of the city.

From the north, find the Orange Line and take it to State Station. From the northeast, find the Blue Line to Airport Station. From the northwest, find the Red Line to South Station. From the west, find the Green Line to Haymarket Station. From the south, find the Orange Line to State Station. From the southeast take the Commuter Rail or the Red Line to South Station.

Take the non-stop Logan Express. Logan Express offers direct, nonstop service to Logan Airport from five park-and-ride locations in Braintree, Framingham, Woburn, Peabody, and North Attleborough. Trip duration will vary depending on the traffic conditions on the day you are traveling.

Take a city bus. The Logan Direct Bus offers shuttle trips from several locations in Boston and Cambridge to Logan Airport. Costs and schedules may vary depending on the destination.

Pay your fare. Keep a few coins with you to feed the fare meters if using bus or subway services. Your fare can also be paid with a Charlie Card, which can be purchased on-site from a fare-machine at many of the major stops.

Take the ferry boat to the Logan Fairy Terminal. Ride the Massachusetts Bay Transport Authority (MBTA) ferries to Logan Airport from the commuter boat terminal located at Fore River Shipyard, 703 Washington Street in Quincy, or from Pemberton Point in Hull.

Take a taxi. Licensed taxis are waiting in the designated area in front of the terminals. If you are taking a taxi from your departure point, call the company in advance and book your trip.

Take an Uber or Lyft car. As an affordable and convenient option, ride-sharing services such as Uber and Lyft can be an excellent choice for getting to the airport. Request your ride from the designated area in front of the terminal.

Take a Boston Water Taxi. A unique option, taking the water taxi from one of the four Harbor Islands is a fun way to reach the airport.

Leave early. Give yourself some extra leeway and leave your house a bit earlier. You never want to be left stranded when you are flying and delaying a flight can cost a lot of money.

Get directions. Plan out the route you will be taking and map it out using a smartphone app or a navigation system. Leave yourself enough time to get to the designated pick-up spot and reach the airport on time.

Park in a designated airport parking lot. Logan Airport offers several parking options for short and long-term travelers. Check the parking lot’s hours of operation and fees before you leave home.

Walk to Logan airport. If you live close enough, you might be able to walk to the airport. Remember it will take you at least 15 minutes to get to Terminal A on foot.

Ride your bike. Take advantage of the bicycle lanes and bike racks located throughout the areas around Logan Airport.

Ask a someone to drop you off. Have a friend or family member take you to the airport. If you plan on using this mode of transportation, make sure that you are picked up at the designated area. 

No matter which mode of transport you decide to take to get to Logan Airport, make sure to plan ahead and be aware of any potential delays or road closures. Keep your identification and flight information handy and continue to check the status of your flight in the days leading up to your departure. With the right preparations, you can ensure a smooth and stress-free trip to Logan Airport.

How to Convert a Wasteful Hot Burning Wide Mouth Chillum Into a Screened Long Stemmed One Hitter

If you're an avid smoker of herbs, it can become frustrating to waste an entire cigarette or a large amount of herb material each time you take a puff. Happily, there is a cost-effective and time-saving solution to this problem. With some basic supplies, you can convert your existing wide-mouthed chillum pipe into a screened long-stemmed one-hitter for far more efficient smoking. Here's what you need to do:

1. Gather your materials:  You'll need a socket-wrench piece fat enough to exactly match the inner diameter of the chillum bowl if cylindrical, otherwise a drill to create a cylindrical opening matching the exterior diameter of the fat part of the socket-wrench piece you have selected, a metal-ring screen-support, some tinfoil if you can't find a metal-ring support, and a 3/16" diameter dremel bit.

2. Preshape the screen: With the dremel bit, make a quarter-inch hole (or crater) in the socket-wrench piece. This is where the screen-support will go. Make sure to leave 3/16" (5-mm.) of material around the hole so that the screen will be secure and the herb material won't be able to escape.

3. Insert the screen-support: Place the metal-ring screen-support (or alternatively, the tinfoil ring you made) into the crater of the socket-wrench piece. Make sure the fit is snug and secure.

4. Insert into the chillum: Now you'll need to insert the socket-wrench piece (with the metal-ring screen-support attached) into the wide mouth of the chillum. Tap it gently until the fat part fits securely, flush with the top of the chillum. The narrow end with the screened crater should stick out about a centimeter (7/16 inch). 

5. Long drawtube: Two options are available to add a long drawtube which will allow the user to draw and inhale the hot smoke without getting burned. One is a special semi-vaporizer technique which involves inserting just 25mg (1/40 gram) of pre-sifted herb or shredded tobacco product into the crater of the one-hitter. As few smokers seem to be aware, the ashes of these materials, even tobacco, are non-toxic and contain nourishing minerals that are easily digestible. The other option is to use a small paper cone and fill it with the herb material you would like to smoke. This method is much less efficient, as more of the material will be burned directly than with the semi-vaporizer technique, but can still be used to great effect.

With a little practice and patience, you can quickly transform your wasteful wide-mouthed chillum into an efficient screened long-stemmed one-hitter. This method is far more cost and time effective, as it allows users to enjoy only as much of their desired material as they desire. Not to mention, eliminating the waste associated with smoking cigarettes or large chillum pipes. Try it out and see for yourself today!

How to Make a Schoolgirl Bow Tie'
Creating the perfect schoolgirl bow tie is not as difficult as it may seem. With a few simple steps, you can make a unique, stylish bow tie that is sure to turn heads. Here is what you'll need to do:

1. Begin by laying the fabric on a flat surface and taking the necessary measurements.

2. Using your pencil, draw the outline of the bow.

3. Cut the fabric approximately 1 to 2 centimeter (0.4 to 0.8 in) away from the measured edge or the lines you have drawn.

4. Fold the fabric over and align the edges together so they meet or match up.

5. Sew a rectangle along the drawn line.

6. Turn the fabric inside out and fold both ends of the bow towards the center.

7. Place two opposite pins in the middle of the bow to hold it in place and then thread the center.

8. Lay the bow on the remaining fabric and use your pencil to sketch the bow's tail.

9. Cut out the tail shape, again cutting approximately 1 centimeter (0.4 in) to 2 centimeter (0.8 in) away from the pencil line.

10. Turn the cut out shape over and use it as a guide to trace another tail, but going in the opposite direction. Repeat this process so you end up with two pieces of the tail going in one direction and two pieces of the tail going in the other direction.

11. Match up the fabric pairs with the backsides (the un-decorative and not shiny side) facing outward on each pair.

12. Pin and sew the edges on each tailpiece, taking care to make sure that there is no puckering.

13. Turn the pieces inside out.

14. Pinch and sew the tail fabrics together, sewing each tailpiece separately.

15. Attach the bow to the tails by using thread.

16. For the middle section of the bow, measure the middle and cut a smaller strip of fabric.

Once you've finished, you can proudly show off your schoolgirl bow tie. With a few supplies and a little bit of determination, you can create a unique look that will get you noticed.

How to Make a Professional Music Video
Are you looking to make a professional music video to go along with your track? It can be intimidating and challenging for beginner music producers and video creators, but don’t worry—with a little bit of planning, you can make a video that looks as good as it sounds! Read on for tips on how to create a professional music video.

Before anything else, you’ll need to record a high-quality version of the track you wish to make into a music video. You can’t make a good video without good audio! When you’re finished recording, plan out what you want to convey with the video’s narrative: What’s the story you want to tell? What kind of characters would bring it to life? 

Next, you’ll need to storyboard the video to get your concept down on paper. Create a storyboard by drawing what your video will look like, step-by-step—draw each frame, come up with angles, and figure out the characters that will be involved. You’ll also need to scout a location for the principal backdrop of your video.

Once you have the concept finalized and a feel for the location your video will be filmed in, you’ll need to cast the shoot with performers if needed. This could be just you and your friends, or actual actors. You’ll need to hire a crew to assist you, as well. This could be videographers, sound technicians, editors, and more, depending on the scale of your video. 

Secure the cast and crew and give out dates and times for the shoot. Make sure you have high quality cameras: If you have a DSLR camera, you’re good to go! Record more than you think you need—you probably won’t use it all, but you want to have more than enough footage.

Once you have the footage you need, you can upload it into the editing software of your choice. Import the recorded audio of your track into the software so you can start synchronizing it with the visuals you’ve filmed. Cut shots in accordance with changes in the story line, or the sound of the song. You should also color correct the shots to create a consistent color palette.

Lastly, review and edit your work one final time to make sure it’s up to your standards. 

Making a professional music video may seem intimidating, but with some planning and creativity, you can make something special that captivates your audience. Good luck!

Roping is an important skill to master in the Western world, whether for recreational purposes, rodeos, or conventional ranching operations. Not only does successful roping require knowledge of the target it is thrown against, but also a great deal in terms of the equipment that is used. While the targets will always vary in size and shape, the lariat used should be chosen carefully in order to ensure safety and accuracy in the roping process.

A lariat (also known as a reata, riata, or simply “rope”) is a length of rope designed for throwing, generally made of nylon or hemp. When selecting what type of material to use for a lariat, consider the length, diameter, and the lay of the rope. The length of a lariat will depend on the age and size of the person using it. Generally speaking, a lariat should be about four feet longer than the distance from fingertips to fingertips when arms are outstretched. As for the diameter, a thicker rope is more durable and recommended for experienced and strong ropers. Thinner ropes however, are lighter and easier for inexperienced or younger ropers to use. Lastly, the lay of the rope is referred to as the number of strands it is composed of - usually between three and twelve. A three-stranded rope is the most common for roping because it is more flexible and affordable.

When purchasing a lariat, shop around for the best price. A wide range of ropes and accessories can be found at local hardware stores, western stores, and even online. Make sure to look at the quality of the product, as cheaper lariats may fray or break easier.

In order to begin roping, make sure that you have a clear and safe area to practice and throw the lariat. Create a target for yourself, such as a wall, tree, or post. You will also need to make sure you have enough distance between you and the target - usually 15-20 feet (6.1 meters). This is so that you can properly swing the lariat without it catching the target before it is supposed to.

Once you are in the right spot, follow these steps to rope your target:

1.	Create a loop in the lariat and hold it in your dominant hand, while holding onto the excess coils with your other hand.

2.	Raise your dominant arm overhead and start twirling the loop. Make sure you slide your hand away from the eye by at least 18 inches so that the loop moves freely.

3.	Maintain your grip on the loop and the spoke - they need to be lightly held while twirling. Ensure that you are using enough speed to control the direction of the lariat.

4.	Select the proper moment to throw the lariat and jerk it taut after it lands on the target.

By properly following the steps outlined above, you should be able to successfully and accurately rope your target. Keep practicing and you should quicly become a master of the art of lariat roping.

How to Operate a Mini Excavator
Operating a mini excavator can be intimidating if you are unfamiliar with construction machinery. With some preparation and know-how, you can quickly become familiar with this powerful machine. Here is a step-by-step guide to help you start using a mini excavator. 

Select a machine for your project. Before you invest in a mini excavator, compare the rental cost versus the labor cost of a project. Consider the needs of your project when making a decision. Visit your local rental business and ask if they do demonstrations and allow customers to become familiar with the machines on their premises, so you can get a better idea of what type of mini excavator you need for your project.

Look over the operator's manual. Before you get started with the mini excavator, it's important that you are familiar with the location of the controls as well as the exact description of them. Take some time to read the manual and try to memorize the placement and usage of the controls.

Look out for labels and warnings. Don't forget to look for warning labels and stickers posted around the machine for other specific warnings or instructions on the particular machine you are going to rent or use.

Have the excavator delivered or pick it up. When it's time to use the excavator, you can have it delivered or arrange to pick it up from the rental business if you have access to a truck with a heavy duty trailer.

Find a level and clear area to practice. Once you have your mini excavator in place, find a level and clear ground in a wide space in order to have plenty of room to try out the machine. This will give you a safe environment to try out the controls without having to worry about obstacles.

Take a look around the excavator. Before you start operating the excavator, take a quick look around the machine and make sure there is nothing loose or damaged that will make operating it hazardous.

Mount your machine. When you are ready, you can now climb into the cab of the mini excavator, make sure you can comfortably reach all the controls, and put on the seat belt.

Familiarize yourself with the controls. Take some time to familiarize yourself with the controls, gauges, and operator restraint system. Try gripping the joysticks and move them around to get the feel of the motion. 

Look at the control sticks. You will find two long steel rods with handles attached on top, two more less-used controls on the floorboards, and two more levers or control sticks on the right side of the instrument cluster. Get an understanding of what they are and what they do before you start using them.

Start up the engine. Now with all of your safety equipment on, you are ready to start up the engine. Flip the switch to turn on the engine.

Start operating the excavator. Begin maneuvering the machine around a bit. Turn and back it up to get used to the handling and speed. Then, find a suitable place in your practice area to try out the digging feature of the machine. 

Lower the dozer blade. To lower the dozer blade, push forward the control handle on the front of the console on your right. Keep pushing until it firmly hits the ground. 

Move the secondary boom segment. To move the secondary boom segment, move the left joystick forward. Make sure the bucket is clear of the ground and there are no obstacles on its way up. 

Now, you are ready to start excavating! Make sure you have your safety equipment on and you are familiar with the controls before you start operating the Mini Excavator. With some practice, you will soon become a pro with the machine and you will be able to take on any construction project with ease!

Becoming a sports lawyer is a great career choice for people wanting to combine their love of the game of sports with their legal inclination. To do this, you'll need to take certain steps and meet certain qualifications in order to become a successful sports attorney. This guide will discuss the steps you need to take to become a sports lawyer. 

The first step is to earn an undergraduate degree in a field relevant to law. Many law school-bound students choose to major in fields that relate to the legal field, such as pre-law, criminal justice, or business. However, this is not always necessary. To maximize your chances of admission to a good law school, however, it's best to choose a major that the admissions officers value.

Another important step to becoming a sports lawyer is to gain experience in public speaking and communications. This is important for any law-school-bound student, as these skills are invaluable when it comes to presenting evidence in the courtroom or delivering arguments to a jury. Becoming a teaching assistant is one way to gain much-needed experience in the area of public speaking and communication.

To gain insight into the path of a sports lawyer, it's helpful to intern with a practicing sports attorney. This is a great way to gain an understanding of the profession and make valuable contacts in the sports lawyer community. It's also a great opportunity to gain experience in the legal field without having to invest in a full-time educational program. 

The next step to becoming a sports lawyer is to consider whether this is the path you really want to pursue. Law is a demanding profession, and it requires a lot of dedication and hard work to be successful. Furthermore, the competition in the legal field can be fierce, so you'll have to make sure you are up to the challenge.

Once you have decided that becoming a sports lawyer is what you want to do, the next step is to register for the Law School Admission Test (LSAT). This is a national standardized test that law schools require as part of the admissions process. You will need to study for the LSAT, as the questions on the test can be very tricky and challenging. If you don't score well on the first test, you should consider retaking it until you can get a good score.

After you take the LSAT, the next step is to create an account with the Credential Assembly Service (CAS). Through the CAS, you will be able to submit your credentials and letters of recommendation to law schools all over the country. 

You will also need to write a personal statement and an addendum, if necessary. A personal statement is a chance for you to share why you wish to pursue a career in sports law, while an addendum is a place to explain any additional reasons why you are an ideal candidate for a position. This could include any activity or leadership experience in the sports law field.

When it comes to choosing a law school, there are some important aspects to consider. Most importantly, you should look for schools with high job placement rates. It's also important to consider location, as certain states have more sports law opportunities than others. Additionally, compare the costs of different schools, and look for schools with relevant sports law clinics. 

In addition, you should apply to multiple law schools. That way, you can increase your chances of getting accepted and find the school that is best for you. 

Once you are accepted into a law school, it is crucial to take required courses and strive to get the best grades possible. Aside from this, you can also take relevant electives and courses in sports law-related topics. This will give you a better idea of what the profession entails and help you stand out from the competition. 

In addition, joining the Sports Lawyers Association (SLA) can be very beneficial for aspiring sports lawyers. The SLA is a professional organization for those in the sports law industry and provides networking opportunities and sports law resources. Additionally, look for internships in the sports law field so that you can gain more experience in the industry.

In order to become a sports lawyer, you will also need to pass the Multi-State Professional Responsibility Exam (MPRE) and the bar exam for the state you want to practice law in. To prepare for the bar exam, make sure you are studying materials and topics covered in the exam. Finally, you will need to complete the background survey with the state bar to finish the process.

After you pass the bar exam, you can start applying to jobs with sports organizations. Participate in On Campus Interviews (OCI), search online for job postings, and reach out to former employers for potential job opportunities. You should also set up informational interviews with sports lawyers and organizations in order to gain more insight into the industry. 

Once you get your first job in the sports law field, stay connected to the sports law community by attending conferences and building more networks. This will ensure that you stay up-to-date with the industry and will position you for long-term success. 

In conclusion, becoming a successful sports lawyer requires a lot of effort and dedication, but it can be a rewarding and fulfilling career if you are able to prepare and take the right steps. Good luck on your journey to becoming a sports lawyer!

How to Redefine Yourself

Redefining yourself can be an empowering and liberating experience. You can choose to change what defines you with some thoughtful planning and preparations. It takes time, space, and understanding to successfully accomplish this important project, so be sure you are ready to devote the necessary energy. Whether you need something new or are looking for a complete overhaul, you can learn how to redefine yourself by following these steps. 

Determine what defines the current you.
The first step to redefining yourself is to understand who you are at the moment. Take time for self-reflection and ask yourself questions like, “What am I like now? What have I achieved so far? What do I need to keep in my life? What must I let go of?” Identifying both the positive and negatives helps you to assess what you need to keep in your life and what needs to be removed. 

Explore your relationship with yourself.
Our relationship with ourselves affects how we view ourselves and how others see us. Discerning our connection can help us understand if we love or dislike ourselves, if we accept or reject ourselves, or whether we feel that our opinion is valid or invalid. 

Talk to yourself about yourself.
Creating a dialogue with yourself can give insight into where you are and help you come up with solutions as to who you want to become. Ask yourself if what you’ve been saying or doing is appropriate, or if maybe it’s time for some changes. 

Realize it’s never too late to reinvent yourself.
When we think about changing, it can often feel like it’s too late, but that isn’t true. No matter our age, background, or accomplishments, we all have the power to redefine ourselves. 

Let go of the past.
The more we cling to the past, the harder it will be to move forward. Instead of holding on, forgive yourself or other from any wrongdoings and move on. Learning from the past can be beneficial, but dwelling on it can only keep us stuck. 

Learn from past mistakes.
It’s important to pay attention to the mistakes we’ve made. Examine the missteps you've taken and try to learn from them. Focus on what you have learned and use that wisdom as fuel as you embark on this journey. 

Choose one bad habit to break.
Making the conscious effort to change just one bad habit can open the door for many other new habits. Maybe you start with making your bed, or even meditating for 10 minutes daily. Be sure to choose something that is doable yet challenging. Doing something that is too daunting can leave you feeling unmotivated.

Replace negative thoughts with positive ones.
Negative self-talk can be detrimental to rediscovering ourselves. Instead, focus on replacing your negative thoughts with positive ones. Believe it or not, the words we say to ourselves are powerful, so be sure to speak with kindness to yourself. 

Stop worrying about others' opinions.Your opinion of yourself is formed in part by your idea of how others see you. They can shape our opinion of the world around us, but ultimately it’s us who creates our own lives. Instead of worrying about others opinions, focus on what is important to you. 

Evaluate your priorities.
Ask yourself which aspects of your life should be treated with the most care regardless of whether those aspects actually receive the care they deserve. Think about how you want your life to look, and determine what aspects need your attention. 

Ask yourself which qualities you'd like to develop.
Make a list of the qualities you’d like to develop. This list should include both physical and personality traits. Examples of potential qualities may include confidence, empathy, or even public speaking. 

Make a plan.
Do your best to break down the task of redefining yourself into achievable steps. Develop a plan to move forward and think of all the potential obstacles. Anticipate any challenges and make sure you have contingencies in place.

Spend a little time each day pursuing your goals.
Set aside a little time each day to do something that contributes to redefining yourself. It could be something as mundane as researching a topic or as thrilling as archery! Investing in this activity daily is a surefire way to make progress. 

Step out of your comfort zone.
Seeking out new experiences, people, and places is a great way to change yourself. Don’t be afraid of trying something you’ve never done before. Consider enrolling in classes or joining a club. 

Pursue an old passion.
Have you ever revisited a lost hobby or passion of yours? Doing so can help you to remember who you were and use that same passion to help you become who you are now. A hobby can give life a sense of purpose. 

Meet new people and make new friends.
Meeting new people can open the door for many valuable moments and experiences. Try being intentional and open-minded when engaging with others and seek out relationships that can help you grow. 

Take a moment to reconnect each morning.
Making the effort to take a moment or two for yourself each morning can be a great way to move through the day. Choose something that can help you become present in the present moment. This could be a meditation or a few moments of deep breathing. 

Move along at a steady pace.
Understand that redefining yourself doesn't happen overnight. Change is an incremental process and requires patience. Celebrate and take it all in, but remember to take small steps and then follow through with those steps to make lasting changes. 

Remember, why we do things offers more insight into who we are than how we do them. Redefining yourself can be a long process and it takes time to have sustainable results. Push yourself and stay committed to your goals and enjoy the journey. You can redefine yourself anytime and anywhere with the right understanding and approach. So go ahead, and redefine yourself!

Stretching for Splits, Scorpion and Other Positions: How to Start'
Are you looking to improve your flexibility and expand your range of motion for those impressive splits, scorpion, and other positions? Fear not, for with regular practice you can make these positions look like second nature. Here's what you need to know to get started.

Stretching is an important part of any physical fitness routine, as it helps keep the muscles and joints flexible while allowing for greater range of motion. Therefore, with that in mind, it is essential to take it slowly and breathe correctly as you stretch.

First, start by stretching each leg with a lunge. Stand comfortably on one foot and flex the other one back behind you; hold the position for 30 seconds, taking deep breaths throughout. Then, drop your back leg, while keeping the forward leg extended with the knee locked. You should feel the stretch but not pain. From here, you can slide your front leg further to explore deeper stretches. Continue this on the other side, before attempting any more complex positions.

If you feel ready, then go ahead and push yourself for more difficult stretches. While it is not recommended to push yourself into the splits, it's a must for those hoping to achieve the most impressive positions. To try a scorpion or a needle, begin by leaning back into your splits, then arching your back while pushing your hands on the floor. You can also further stretch your back by doing bridges and practice the positions slowly.

To perform a needle, stand against a doorway and push your back into the frame with your elbows to help you get your body closer to your legs. Start by pushing lightly and increase the pressure gently as you feel ready.

The key to making the most out of these positions is to practice regularly. However, take it slow and don't push yourself too far, as injuries can occur from overexertion. Pay attention to your breathing to stay relaxed, and your body will thank you for it. Good luck!

Traveling often means that mundane tasks such as doing laundry take a back seat. With the wash cycles, temperature changes, and the fact that you may be using a foreign machine, doing the laundry while traveling can be confusing and tedious. But it doesn’t have to be! Follow this simple guide on how to do laundry while traveling.

The first step is to plan ahead. Take an inventory of your loads before you go. If you’re looking to do laundry while traveling, make sure to bring laundry supplies such as a detergent, bleach, fabric softener and a laundry bag. Do some research to find out if the place you are staying at has their own self-service laundry facilities. If you can’t find one, consider alternatives such as a Laundromat or a laundry service.

Watch your timing. You should always plan to do the laundry in the morning or late in the afternoon to ensure that the clothes have plenty of time to dry. If you take a shower before doing the laundry, make sure to place the sink stopper in the sink before you start adding water. This will prevent any water from spilling over during the washing and rinsing process.

Now it’s time to start the washing process! Begin by adding your clothes and an appropriate detergent or soap, shampoo, or detergent to a sink of either cool or warm water. Swirl the clothes around in the soapy water and then let them soak for a few minutes. Gently rub the fabric against itself in the water to help the soap do its job.

Once the clothes are done soaking, drain the soapy water and squeeze the laundry gently to get most of the soap out. Next, fill up the sink with clean water and let the clothes sit for a few minutes to rinse off the soap. Drain the sink again and let the laundry drip out for a few moments. To get rid of excess water, squeeze out the water with your hands.

Lay the damp garments in a single layer on a bath towel. Roll up the towel around them and squeeze to remove most of the excess water. If you don’t have access to a heavy object with which to press the water out of the clothes, you can roll the towel on the floor floor and walk back and forth on it. Once you’ve gotten rid of the excess moisture, hang the clothes to dry. Don’t forget to hang the towel to dry as well! The clothes usually need about two hours to dry, and if the air is humid you may need more time. Once dry, you can put away your clothes. 

Now you can travel stress free knowing that you are prepared for any extra loads of laundry that may come your way. Doing laundry while traveling need not be a daunting task. If you follow this simple guide and plan ahead, you can easily manage all of your laundry needs while away from home.
