Creating a rustic table runner is easier than you might think! Whether you're an experienced sewer or a beginner, the steps outlined below will help you craft a beautiful and eye-catching accessory for your home. 

First, you'll need to gather the material and supplies you need. For this project, you'll need to have at least two pieces of fabric, an optional additional backing fabric, optional wadding, greaseproof paper or thin sew-in interfacing, a sewing machine, and scissors. To make a table runner, you'll also need to cut the following pieces:

• Two 2-1⁄2in squares in dark red, cut in half on the diagonal 
• Ten 2-3⁄8in squares in dark red 
• Ten 2-3⁄8in squares in cream 
• Eight 2- 1⁄2in squares in cream 
• Ten 2-1⁄2in squares in dark red
• Twenty-four 2-3⁄8in triangles in either cream or dark red

Once you've prepared the pieces, trace the foundation template onto greaseproof paper or thin sew-in interfacing. Then, place a piece of red fabric, RS up, on the foundation and put a piece of cream, RS down, onto it. Sew from the back exactly on the line and extend a couple of stitches past the end of the line. Use a smaller stitch than usual. 

Make four foundation blocks for each fight block you are making. Carefully cut five 3-3⁄4in square pieces from the dark red fabric. Lay the squares and foundation units in position following the layout shown in Figure 2. Then piece the squares into rows and join to make one complete block. 

Take the cream 2-1⁄2in squares and draw a line on the diagonal on the WS. Cut apart along the line, press open, reposition, make the centre unit, and join into one block. Add strips. Cut a piece of backing fabric and wadding 1 1⁄2in larger all round than your finished top.  

Now quilt as needed, and cut 24 triangles. Sew pairs of triangles, RS together, leaving about 1 1⁄2in on a straight edge to turn through. Join the triangles together at the corners only using a large bead. Add tassels by threading through the large bead and adding a string of bugle and seed beads. 

To finish, add either a binding strip or binding flap around the edges of the table runner. The binding strip should be cut 2in wide, folded in half lengthwise, and ironed. The binding flap should be cut 3in wide and finished with a bias binding. 

Creating a rustic table runner is a rewarding sewing project and can add great character to your home. Following these instructions will help you make a beautiful runner that will last for many years.

How to Make Fossils
Are you looking to make a unique and stylish memento of a pet, an important item or a special memory? Then making fossils may be just the project for you! It’s an interesting way to preserve your most treasured items, and make them into a timeless piece that you will enjoy forever. In this article, we will discuss how to make fossils.

Choosing a Mixture
While there are many different types of mixtures you can use to create a fossil, the most popular mixture is two parts mixture to one part plaster. This mixture is probably the most recommended because it has been proven to be a sturdy and reliable material to use for making fossils. The plaster component can be bought from your local hardware store, and the mixture component can be any type of sediment such as soil or sand.

Stirring your Mixture
Once you have gathered obtain the necessary materials, pour both the plaster and the mixture into a mixing bowl. Using a spoon or a popsicle stick, stir the mixture until it has become consistent throughout. This may take a few minutes, and you want to make sure that no lumps of plaster remain in the mixture.

Collecting Objects to Fossilize
There are many different objects that you can choose to fossilize, however, you should pick something that is a little bit sturdier than a leaf or flower. For example, consider using a shell, pet toy or a bracelet. Also, consider what size of fossil you want, as you may want more details with a smaller item.

Applying Petroleum Jelly
After you have chosen the item you want to fossilize, apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly (or vaseline) over the entire surface. This is necessary to make sure that once you cast the fossil, you will be able to easily remove the object from the shape of the fossil.

Pouring the Mixture into a Foam Cup
The foam cup is needed to shape the fossil into whatever form you would like. Once you have covered your object with the petroleum jelly, pour in the plaster and mixture mix into the foam cup. Be sure to fill the cup almost completely full, and make sure there are no air bubbles in the mixture.

Casting the Fossil
Now that the mixture has been poured into the foam cup, take the object that you’ve chosen to fossilize and push it part way into the mould. Make sure that it’s further down than half way, otherwise it may float to the top and ruin the shape of your fossil.

Allowing Time for the Mould Fossil to Harden
Once you have cast the fossil and placed it somewhere safe to harden for at least one day, you can now begin the process of making a more realistic fossil.

Tearing Open the Cup
Carefully tear off the foam cup to reveal the fossilized object.

Removing the Mould for an Imprint
With the help of the petroleum jelly, carefully remove the object you’ve fossilized from the mould. This should create a nice imprint of the object that you will now use to make a more authentic looking fossil.

Weather the Mould for Authenticity
To make a more realistic looking fossil, weather the mould by using a small precision hammer, chisel and any rocks you may have in your garden. With careful and precise hammering, you can chip away at the plaster mould in areas that you would like your fossil to be more eroded. This is a great way to make the fossil more weathered and age it for a more realistic effect.

Once you have chiselled away at your mould, your fossil is now complete! You can now display this timeless piece and show off this amazing project! Making fossils is a great way to preserve your beautiful memories and keep them for a lifetime.

Traveling by plane can be a daunting experience, but with the right preparation, it can also be a hassle-free and enjoyable experience. Here are some tips to help you plan ahead and make the most of your flight.

Determine whether you need just a carry-on item or if you also need a checked bag. Most airlines will allow passengers to carry one bag for free if the dimensions and weight of the bag meet the airline’s restrictions. Those with a higher-priced ticket may be allowed to check a bag or even two without needing to pay an additional fee. However, those with a lower-priced ticket will likely need to pay additional fees for checked bags.

Make a list of any items you plan to pack that might be regulated. The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) has a list of items that passengers are not allowed to bring in their carry-on or checked bags. These items include weapons, flammable materials, and sharp objects, so it’s important to make sure you’re not bringing any of these items with you on your plane ride.

Learn whether you can take these items in your carry-on or if you have to check a bag to take them. Some items, such as laptops, may be permitted in the cabin but must be in a clear, plastic bag. Other items will need to be put in a checked bag, such as toiletries and items that are over 100ml in size or in pressurized containers.

Pack as lightly as you can. There’s no need to bring more than you need on a plane ride, as airlines will usually charge additional fees for additional luggage. Try to consolidate your items into one bag to reduce weight and the number of bags.

Understand how liquids must be packed. Liquids and gels that are greater than 100ml are not allowed in your carry-on. Rather, they will need to be placed in your checked bag. Smaller containers of the same liquid or gel items, such as shampoos, hairsprays, and hand sanitizers, can usually be brought on the plane in a clear plastic bag that’s sealed.

Roll your clothing to pack it, instead of folding it. This trick will allow you to fit more items in your bag, and can help to reduce wrinkles in your clothes.

Layer your packed items from heaviest to lightest. This will help to ensure that the weight is evenly distributed throughout your bag.

Consider packing some clothes inside other items, like shoes. Shoes can make a great packing space for clothing that are of a similar size.

Plan to pack a change of clothing in your carry-on. In the event that your checked bag is delayed or lost, having a change of clothes in your carry-on item can come in handy.

Put thin items or nothing at all in the outer zip pockets. These pockets are often easiest to find for baggage handlers, so they can be susceptible to theft.

Avoid locking your luggage. TSA agents can open locked luggage, and can become frustrated if you’ve locked it.

Check in for your flight up to 24 hours before departure. Many airlines will allow you to do this online. This can save you time before your trip, and can allow you to secure a better seat on the plane.

Print or secure your boarding pass ahead of time. Some airlines may allow boarding passes to be stored on your phone, but it’s smart to have a physical copy as well, just in case.

Have the appropriate identification ready in order to get through security. In the United States, you will need a form of government-issued photo identification, such as a driver’s license or passport, as well as a boarding pass.

Arrive at the airport with plenty of time to spare. Most airlines suggest arriving at least two hours prior to departure, just in case there’s a backup at security.

Have all necessary items for the security checkpoint easily accessible. Items such as your identification, boarding pass, and electronic devices should be readily available in order to speed up the security process.

Take off, remove, or avoid wearing metal items from/on your person before going through the screening. Any objects such as belt buckles, jewelry, and other metals will usually set off the metal detector at the security checkpoint.

Know how to declare medications and items for infants and children. Once you’re through the metal detector, there is a separate line for those with special needs, such as those flying with medication or infants.

Find your gate and wait for boarding to start. Once you’re past the security checkpoint, you can find your gate, locate your seat on the plane, and relax until your flight begins.

Move anything you might want during the flight to the carry-on item you will keep with you at your seat. Your carry-on should have items that you might need during the flight, such as a jacket, snacks, and a book or magazine.

Have snacks and drinks. You can usually bring your own snacks and drinks on board, or purchase snacks on board from the airline’s selection.

Use your technology sparingly. Use your devices when necessary, but avoid using them in distracting ways, as they can be annoying for those around you.

Take books or other forms of entertainment. Depending on the duration of the flight, you might need to entertain yourself. Consider bringing a book, magazine, or digital device with you on the plane.

Take a nap. Operating on little or no sleep during a flight can be difficult, and taking a nap can help you to stay alert on the flight. But make sure to stay prone in your seat and avoid reclining, as this may bother those seated behind you.

Watch a movie or TV show. Many airlines will often have a selection of in-flight movies and TV shows you can watch. Don’t be afraid to take advantage of this form of in-flight entertainment.

First, check out shady places in your backyard like under a thick growth of plants. Next, find a corner where two walls meet. Now, look in any place where insects fly, and where there are branches to connect the corners of the web. Here, you’ll be sure to find a caterpillar. 

To look for hornworms, look on tomato plants. They’re mostly green and their stark pattern gives them away. In sandy places, you might find funnels. They’re often found next to a house foundation where grass never grows. Head to the local flower patch and see what else you can find. 

Moths, butterflies, bees, and wasps alike, all congregate around flowers in search of their nectar-y treat. You might even find a foreign visitor like a shield-shaped bug. Plus, many other types of beetles take refuge in flowers.

How to Get Work Done While Sick
It's an all too common situation: You're feeling under the weather, but still need to get your work done. Without a plan or the right resources, these are tasks can be especially daunting. But, with a few tips and strategies, it's possible to tackle your work efficiently and productively even when feeling ill. 

First, decide whether you should call in sick. If your symptoms are mild and you feel you can still accomplish your tasks, then work from home. However, if your symptoms are serious or if you're putting yourself or others at risk of infection, don't feel guilty about taking the day off. 

Once you make a decision, ask if you can telecommute in lieu of a sick day. This often means arranging a conference call with your boss or colleagues. Telecommuting is a great way to make sure you get your work done while still protecting yourself and those around you.

Next, stay calm. Being sick can be stressful; you may worry about not getting your work done or whether you can safely manage both your tasks and your health. But it's important to take a deep breath and think logically. Staying calm and taking the appropriate steps can help you find a way to get your work done.

To stay productive while sick, organize your work if you feel like you're coming down with something. Prioritize the items on your agenda, break up large tasks into smaller chunks, and consult with colleagues and your boss in order to meet important deadlines. Also, work on low-stakes projects if possible; this allows you to get something done and still maintain a sense of accomplishment, despite feeling under the weather.

Additionally, set priorities carefully. It's highly unlikely you'll be able to complete all tasks, so you should consider which items take precedence. Create a loose timeline for yourself, take breaks frequently, and do not feel compelled to complete every task before returning to work or leaving for the day. And don't be afraid to ask for help from co-workers or supervisors - after all, if you're not feeling well, there's no harm in asking for some extra assistance. 

Likewise, consider alternative forms of productivity. If required tasks are impossible to accomplish, boost output in other ways. Have virtual meetings using digital tools for collaboration or, if possible, use the day to brainstorm innovative ideas or to do some planning.

At the same time, make sure you still take care of yourself. Drink three times as much water as coffee; take a nap, if needed; relax and lie down for a short period to recharge; and purchase necessary items such as a vaporizer, over-the-counter medications, or supplies for a hot shower to ease your symptoms. Eating healthy, comforting foods will also help reduce your ills and help to keep you on task.

Finally, make a schedule for your return. It's important to stay up to date on projects, even when you're out sick. However, make sure that when you do come back, your expectations are more realistic. Delay certain meetings or tasks until you’re feeling better to avoid setbacks. And reward yourself with a day or two off when your work is done.

It's difficult to stay productive and get your work done while sick, but it is possible. Follow these steps to keep yourself and those around you safe while getting your tasks done. How to Make Momos
Making momos is a tradition that originated centuries ago in various parts of Asia. The Tibetan version—the most popular one— is a delicious kind of dumpling filled with flavorful ingredients, steamed or pan-fried. If you’ve ever tried to make them on your own, it’s time to reconsider. With this easy step-by-step guide, you'll become a momo master in no time!

Take out the amount of flour you’ll need to make your momos. Mix the flour, salt and oil. Then add the water bit by bit to the flour mixture and form the dough by hand. Let the dough sit for 30 minutes.

Decide on the ingredients for your filling. You can get creative with the ingredients, but some of the most popular include ground beef, pork, chicken, or even vegetables. Assemble these ingredients, season the mixture and cook the vegetable filling. Set the filling aside until you’re ready to use it.

Prep your ingredients to make the momo sauce. Roast tomatoes, bell peppers and chilies and place all the ingredients in the blender until the mixture is smooth. Refrigerate the sauce until your momos are ready to be served.

Now is the time to prepare the dough. Roll pieces of dough into flat circles. Although some Tibetans prefer to mold the dough into flat circles using a particular technique, you can create flattened circles of dough using a simpler and quicker method.

Once the circles are done, place the filling in the center of each one and then fold and shape the dough. For a round momo, simply pinch the edges together at the top. Otherwise, fold it in half for a half-moon momo.

Decide how you’d like to cook your momos. The traditional way is to steam them, but you can also pan fry or deep fry them. Serve hot with a side of the momo sauce. Enjoy!

Visiting the dentist is the best course of action to treat dental cavities, but there are some natural methods for preventing and healing cavities without the need for fillings or other interventions. The key is to boost the strength of the enamel and minimize the impact of bacteria in the mouth. Beyond visiting the dentist regularly, here are some natural strategies for protecting your teeth and helping heal cavities.

Consult Your Dentist

It's important to consult with your dentist to properly diagnose and treat dental health issues. Your dentist will inspect your mouth to identify any cavities. If a cavity is found, your dentist will recommend treatments, which may include fillings, sealants, or crowns. In addition, your dentist will typically recommend daily dental hygiene habits to help prevent the occurrence of cavities.

Get More Vitamin D

Long known to be beneficial for general bone health, vitamin D boosts your calcium metabolism and induces cathelicidin, which is an antimicrobial peptide that attacks the bacteria known to cause dental cavities. Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin that is not easily available through your diet, although fatty fish (like salmon, mackerel and tuna) are an excellent source of the vitamin.

Consume More Foods That Contain Vitamin K2

Vitamin K2 is an important nutrient for healthy teeth and bones. It encourages remineralization of teeth and helps reverse tooth decay. Foods rich in Vitamin K2 include animal organs, grass-fed dairy products, bone broths, aged cheeses, chicken, and a fermented soybean food called natto.

Try Fermented Cod Liver Oil to Get Those Fatty Vitamins

Extracted from cod livers, fermented cod liver oil is a source for vitamin A, vitamin D, and omega-3 fatty acids. Vitamin A and D are critical in preventing cavities as they are involved in the remineralization of teeth. Plus, omega-3s are essential for healthy teeth and gums which helps with the maintenance of a healthy mouth.

Consume Foods High In Calcium

High-calcium foods are essential for fighting cavities. Look for foods like dairy, leafy greens, and nuts to get your daily dose of calcium. If you’re vegan, look for calcium-rich foods like almonds, spinach, and sesame seeds.

Use Mineralizing Toothpaste

Mineralizing toothpaste helps strengthen dental enamel and prevent cavities. Toothpastes that contain key ingredients like calcium and remineralizing agents can help remineralize tooth enamel and protect teeth from decay.

Monitor the Healing Process

After receiving treatment from the dentist and implementing some natural remedies, it’s important to monitor the healing process. Visit the dentist regularly to make sure the cavity is healing as expected and that there are no remaining signs of decay.

In addition to regular dentist appointments, there are other steps you can take to help keep your teeth healthy and free of cavities. Brush your teeth regularly with a fluoride and Fluoridex toothpaste to ensure full coverage. Floss your teeth daily to remove the particles of food and bacteria that accumulate and can cause cavities. Use fluoride on a regular basis to strengthen tooth enamel and reduce the risk of cavities.

To further protect against cavities, reduce your intake of carbohydrates and sugar and cut back on snacking and sipping. Eating certain fresh fruits, like apples, strawberries, and pineapples, can help reduce bacteria growth in the mouth. Also, be sure to chew every bite completely, as this can help mitigate the acidity of sugar and also break down food particles into smaller pieces, making them easier to wash away with saliva.

Finally, don’t worry about phytic acid present in grains, seeds, nuts, and legumes—it doesn’t have any significant effect on your teeth. You can also take a mineral supplement to help remineralize your teeth, as well as drinking plenty of water throughout the day.

By combining regular visits to the dentist with these natural methods, you can help to heal cavities and inhibit decay. Taking care of your teeth with good oral hygiene habits is essential to preventing cavities in the first place, and combining those good habits with natural remedies, vitamins, and minerals can help keep your teeth strong and healthy for life.

For many, tax season is an intimidating time of the year. People often feel confusion and overwhelm as they try to understand the complicated tax forms required by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). Completing IRS Form 1040 is not quite as difficult as it may seem and with the right guidance and breaking it down step by step, the process can be fairly straightforward.

Locate the correct form. During tax season, you can easily find Form 1040 (U.S. Individual Income Tax Return) on the IRS website. This form will guide you through the process of filing your income taxes.

Determine if you are required to file income taxes. Everyone's tax situation is different and filing requirements depend on several factors. It is important to review the IRS website to determine if you are required to submit this form.

Decide whether you want to file income taxes, even if you are not required to. Even if you are not legally required to file Form 1040, you may still want to take the opportunity to check if you qualify for deductions or a tax refund.

Gather all information you will need to complete your taxes. Before you start filling out Form 1040, make sure you have all the relevant information in front of you. This information includes any documents related to your employment, investments, deductions, credits, or other information related to your tax return.

Fill in your personal information. The primary taxpayer’s full name and Social Security Number will go on the top line of Form 1040. You will also need to enter your address, as well as that of your spouse if you are married and filing jointly.

Choose your filing status. Form 1040 allows you to choose from several filing statuses. These include Single, Married Filing Jointly, Head of Household, Qualifying Widow(er) with Dependent Child, Married Filing Separately, and a few other options.

Check exemption boxes for you and your spouse, if applicable, on lines 6 a-d. You may also need to list your dependents' information in Section 6c. Don’t forget to enter all pertinent information in the “Exemptions” section of the form.

Enter income included on your W-2 forms on line 7. You must list all sources of income, such as wages, salaries, alimony, and investment and business income. Make sure to report all income earned in the tax year you are filing.

Fill in the rest of the Income section, lines 8a - 22. This section of the form includes information related to rental income, qualified retirement plans, distributions from a qualified plan, casino and gambling winnings, Social Security benefits, self-employment income, etc.

Enter any adjustments to your taxable income on lines 23 - 35, the Adjusted Gross Income section. In this section you should reference any adjustments related to IRA contributions, educator expenses, student loan interest payments, alimony payments, health savings account deductions, moving expenses, and other qualified deductions.

Calculate your Adjusted Gross Income by adding the appropriate figures in this section. Then, transfer this information to line 37.

Start the Tax and Credits section. Begin by copying your adjusted gross income from line 37 onto line 38. This will help you decide if you should itemize your deductions or use the standard deduction for your filing status.

Calculate the formula on for exemptions, which is listed on line 42. Exemptions are tax deductions that can help reduce the income you are taxed on. This amount varies based on the type of filing status you have and will determine the amount of taxes you must pay.

Determine the amount of your tax. This is the total amount of taxes you owe the IRS. It is the total of all the taxes listed in the Tax and Credits section.

Fill out the Credits section, lines 48 - 54. This section provides information about any credits you may qualify for, including the Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Credit, Child and Dependent Care Credit, and Education Credits.

Finish the Tax and Credits section. Add up all the lines and make sure the total on line 69 equals the one from line 63. If this is the case, ignore lines 70 - 86 on the form.

Complete the Other Taxes section. Here you will need to provide information related to alternative minimum tax and your estimated tax payments.

Complete the Payments section. Most filers will only need to fill in one or two lines in this section. This allows you to list any payments you made through withholding tax, estimated tax payments, and any refundable credits you are claiming.

Calculate your refund, if applicable. If line 63 is larger than line 74, then subtract line 63 from line 74, enter the result on line 75, and move on to the "Refund" section on page 4 of the form.

Calculate the amount you owe. If line 74 is larger than line 63, then subtract line 63 from line 74, enter the result on line 78, and move on to the "Amount You Owe" section on page 4 of the form.

Complete the Third Party Designee. This allows the IRS to discuss your return with another party, a type of "power of attorney," if you will. If you do not want the IRS to discuss your return with someone other than you or your spouse, check the box beside “No” in this section.

Sign your form. By signing the form, you are swearing to the truthfulness of the contents and acknowledging your willingness to abide by IRS policies and regulations. A spouse must also sign the form if filing jointly.

After you complete Form 1040, it's time to submit it. Make sure you include any required documents and submit everything on time to avoid any penalties from the IRS. If you understand what information is needed and follow the steps above, completing the tax form should be a breeze.

How to Put Together a Good Party

Having a good party isn't just about showing up and hoping for the best. It's about being prepared and having fun planning the event. With these tips, you can make your party a memorable event for all your friends and family. 

Before you get started, it's important to plan out all the details. Start by making a planning notebook, and going through the steps below. 

State the event and purpose. Make sure you know what the event is going to be and who it's for. Keep this in mind when making your guest list and deciding what food and activities to include. 

List the people to invite. Think about who should be invited, and then create a guest list. You will need ample time to make sure everyone receives an invitation. 

Consider doing a themed potluck. This is a great way for everyone to get involved. You can also make a list of the dishes expected from each guest. 

List all food into two categories of perishables and non-perishables. This will help you plan out food shopping and storage for party day. Make sure you have enough options to serve everyone, and ensure there's something for everyone to enjoy. 

List all beverages. Keep in mind to provide enough drinks for everyone, and remember to have a variety of non-alcoholic, non-caffeinated, and non-sugar drinks available. 

List all non food items. These can include napkins, plastic glasses, dripless candles, ice, and flowers or centerpieces. 

One week before the party: 
Purchase all non-perishables and make any casseroles. Now is the time to make any dishes that don't need to be served cold. 

Select the serving dishes you'll be using and set them aside. You'll want these ready and on hand when the food is ready. 

Three days before, do the dusting and all the heavy cleaning, such as the floors and bathrooms. This is the time to make sure the house is ready for party day.

Decide where guests' coats, purses, etc., will go. Make sure you have a place ready for everyone to put their things. 

Two days before the party: Buy the perishables. This includes all the food that needs to be served cold and all the ingredients you'll need for the cooked dishes.

One day before: Prepare the dishes that can be reheated or served cold. This is a good time to prepare any dishes that can just be served right away. 

Set the mood with music. You can use low-key classical, folk, or jazz music during the arriving period to get everyone relaxed. 

The day: Give the house a once-over in the morning, and pick up flowers and ice. Do a final check of the house to make sure everything is how you want it. 

Prepare the main cooked meal. Depending on the food you're making, you can prepare this in the oven or on the stove. 

Pay attention to your guests. You don't have to spend the whole night talking to people, but keep an eye out for anyone who looks like they need a hand. 

Plan an ice-breaker. This is a great way to get people talking and let them learn about each other in a fun and casual way. You can hand each person a little note and make them find someone who shares a common interest. 

Remember you are the host and it is your responsibility to make sure people are enjoying themselves and have what they need. Make sure everything is stocked and people are comfortable. 

Set up the buffet line. This is an important step and should be done carefully. Start with plates, then the main dish, vegetables, salads, breads, and drinks. Make sure all the options are visible and properly labeled. 

With these tips, you can now plan to have a great party that all your guests will enjoy! Have fun and don’t forget to take pictures of all the memories.

Creating a square of spherical helixes can be a challenging task and one that requires a lot of mathematical knowledge and skill. The process involves using Microsoft Excel to define variables, formulas and create a chart. To begin, we will need to open a new Microsoft Excel workbook and name two worksheets in it, the first "Data" and the second "Chart".

On the Data sheet, we will need to enter the following Defined Variable Names in Row 1, Columns A thru G (without quotation marks): "AdjRows" (in cell A1), "GMLL" (in cell B1), ""Factor", "N", "Multer1", "Multer2" and finally "p". After the names are entered, we should select the range A1:G2 and align it in the center.

In Row 2, columns A thru G, we should enter the following Defined Variable values: 1439 (in cell A2), =0.618033988749895 (in cell B2), -.25, 1,1,1,1.

The next step is to enter the column headers across Row 4, into columns A:H. These will be (without quotes): "Base t" (in cell A4), "c" (in cell B4), "cos", "sin", "x", "y", "x of p" and "y of p".

After these have been entered, we should enter the column formulas. To begin, we should enter 25680. in cell B5. From here on, the tutorial will follow the little note in cell H1: "0,P to P,P then P,P to P,0, then P,0 to 0,0, then 0,0 to 0,P."

The last step is to create the chart. To do this, we should select the cell range E5:F1445 and either do Chart Wizard Smoothed Line Graph or select the Charts item from the Ribbon (if you can't find Charts on the Ribbon go to Excel Preferences Sharing and Privacy Ribbon and have everything turned on or checked except "Hide group titles"). 

When completing this tutorial, make use of helper articles when proceeding throughout it. These articles will provide a comprehensive list of articles related to Excel, Geometric and/or Trigonometric Art, Charting/Diagramming and Algebraic Formulation. With these in hand, creating a square of spherical helixes should be a much simpler task.

Making a samurai armor is a great way to show your appreciation for Japanese culture and make yourself stand out at the same time. It may seem intimidating at first, but with a bit of patience and effort, it's a project that can be accomplished relatively easily.

First, you'll need to make the chest plate. To do this, take a shirt or other piece of clothing to use as a pattern. Lay it flat on a table and trace it, making sure to draw the sides, top, and bottom of the shirt. Once it's traced, divide the pattern into eight equal segments and number them F1 through F8. Cut the pieces out and save them for later.

Next, trace and cut out slightly larger pieces out of a piece of fake leather. Cover the front of each segment of the chest plate with the fake leather and hot glue the edges down to keep it secure. Then, turn the pieces over and repeat the same steps for the back of the chest plate.

Once that's done, punch two rows of holes on each side of your chest plate segments. Starting with segment F1, thread two long pieces of cording through the holes on the left side of the piece. Cross the cords over each other, then feed them down through the next set of holes. Thread them up through the next set of holes, then place F2 on top of F1 and feed the cords through the next set of holes. Cross the cords and continue lacing the pieces together. Repeat this process on the other side. Once complete, tie the cords off at the bottom, then trim the rest off.

To attach the front and back chest plates together, punch holes through the sides of each piece. Feed two pieces of cording through the holes and crisscross them, then tie off the ends and trim the excess.

To finish the samurai armor piece, you'll need to decorate a hard hat. Paint the hard hat a glossy black, then cut 10 thin strips out of craft foam and paint them gold. Hot glue the foam strips to the helmet to create the "horns" that you see on traditional samurai armor. Add a gold coat button to the top of the helmet, too.

To make the neck protector, trace a circular shape (the size of your neck) on the same fake leather you used for the chest plate and cut it out. Then, fold the edges in and create pleats in the middle of the circle with some needle and thread. Secure the neck protector to the helmet with hot glue.

You'll also need to create a crest for the armor piece. Trace a crest shape onto a piece of craft foam, then cut it out and paint it gold. Hot glue the crest to the helmet. Lastly, paint a costume samurai mask with glossy black paint and add some details to give it more personality.

Congratulations - you've created a gorgeous and authentic-looking samurai armor piece. It may have taken some time to make, but the end result is worth it!

How to Become a Rockstar
Being a rockstar is the dream of many people, and why not? It’s an exciting and glamorous life! But, there is also hard work and dedication that comes with it. To become a Rockstar, here are a few steps you can follow:

Step One: Learn how to play an instrument or take vocal lessons. Learning how to play an instrument or take singing lessons is essential to becoming a great musician. Depending on your taste, you can choose the type of instrument or genre of music to learn. From electric guitar to blues and classical guitar, there is a wide range of instruments to choose from. Many people also take singing lessons to further develop their vocal abilities.

Step Two: Put together a band. When you know how to play an instrument or sing, you will need to find other people who share the same musical tastes as you. Create your own band, and practice hard to make sure the music you create is the best it possibly can be.

Step Three: Practice, practice, practice! After you and your band have figured out the instrumentals, it’s time to start practicing. Dedicate a certain amount of time every day to practice so you can make sure you sound great once you go on stage.

Step Four: Write your music and make it something you like. Writing your own music is a great way to express yourself artistically. Once you have the melody and the lyrics for a song, practice it to make sure it is something you really like.

Step Five: Record some of your music, after you’ve memorized the lyrics/notes by heart. Recording your music is a great way to show off the hard work you have been doing. When you are recording it is important to make sure you know the song by heart, so don’t be afraid to practice the song over and over again.

Step Six: Allow your closest friends to listen and consider your music. Once you have recorded your music, listen to it with your closest friends and consider their opinion. It’s important to get feedback and to know if it is something you like and works for you.

Step Seven: Let a group of people listen to your music after you’ve made changes. Take the advice of the friends who listened to your music and make the necessary changes. Once you have made the changes, let a larger group of people listen and get feedback.

Step Eight: Play at gigs. Playing at gigs is one of the essential things you need to do when trying to build a career as a musician. Don’t forget to bring plenty of copies of your music and hand them out.

Step Nine: Save your money wisely, and don’t quit your full time job or get a part time job. Being a musician is not easy, and it may take some time before you start making money from your music. To make sure you are financially secure, keep a full time job or get a part time job to cover your expenses.

Step Ten: Create a band/artist website featuring pictures, your show calendar, and previous employers for other pubs to see will give you a leg up. Create a website for your band so that people can find you easily. Put up pictures, your show calendar, and let everyone know about the places you have played. This will help you gain a larger fan base.

Step Eleven: Hand out CDs of your music to people you know/meet, or even to strangers, this might help you get more fans and/or get a record deal. Handing out CDs of your music to people you know or strangers can be a great way to build a fan base and get a record deal.

Step Twelve: Record your band’s music on a video and upload it on YouTube. Recording your band’s music on video and then uploading it on YouTube can be a great way to show the world your music. People have been signed after their music videos went viral on YouTube, which is a big plus!

Step Thirteen: Tell your friends to recommend your music to as many people as possible; the effect will snowball, and you may have an even larger fan base. Encourage your friends to recommend your music to as many people as possible. Word of mouth is one of the best ways to get more fans for your music.

Step Fourteen: Never ever give up, even when it seems like you are not getting anywhere; you can’t call it quits. This should go without saying, but never give up when it seems like you are not getting anywhere. If you give up, you will never be able to become a rockstar and your dreams will never come true.

Step Fifteen: Love it: It ultimately is key to love what you do in life, especially if it is your career. If you want to become a rockstar, you must love the music you are playing and the genre you are playing. Without this passion, you will never succeed in becoming a rockstar. 

Step Sixteen: Try to compose your own type of song. Creating your own music is a great way to stand out from the crowd. Music fans love to discover new genres of music and singers, which is why creating your own style of music is important. This way, you will make your mark in the music industry and be remembered for years to come.

How to Do Well in College Algebra

College algebra is a challenging and rewarding class, but it’s important to be prepared in order to do well. Here are some tips for success:

1. Take the math placement test at your school before the semester starts. This will help you find out what level of math you can handle, and which class is right for you.

2. Choose your professor carefully. Ask around and see what other students have to say about the professor's teaching style and material.

3. Sign up for a course that allows you take exams in a testing center. This will give you the option of taking exams on your own time without disturbing your classmates.

4. Schedule the course during your optimal learning time of day. If you're a morning person, try to take it in the morning if possible.

5. Take the class over the summer as your only course. Focusing solely on the class will make it easier to remember the material and give you the time to practice and understand the concepts.

6. Know how homework, quizzes, and exams contribute to your grade. Ask your professor to confirm the breakdown of your grade.

7. Master pre-algebra before the first day of class. Taking the time to do this will make college algebra much easier.

8. Buy the books and supplies a month before class. This will give you enough time to get to know the books and understand the material for the start of the semester.

9. Read the syllabus. This will tell you what you are expected to learn and when the exam dates are planned.

10. Read the textbook before class. This will help you keep up in class and have a general understanding of the material.

11. Go to all of the classes, even the optional ones. You never know when something covered in class will be on an upcoming exam, so it’s important to attend every possible class, even if it is optional.

12. Listen and take notes in class. Note-taking will help you keep track of the material, and will help you remember it for the exams.

13. Do the homework. Doing the homework will help cement the concepts in your mind and make it easier to remember and understand the material for the exams.

14. Invest in and learn how to use a graphing calculator. A graphing calculator will save you time on the exams and make graphing and solving equations easier.

15. Use graph paper for graphs. This will make graphing equations easier and more organized.

16. Attend office hours. Office hours are a great way to get help from your professor, and to get additional practice in the class material.

17. Take advantage of free tutoring. Many universities offer free tutoring for college classes, and college algebra is often one of them.

18. Start a study group. Practice and review of material with classmates can be a great help when exam time comes.

19. Pay for additional tutoring if you need it. More resources can be very helpful when it comes to difficult material.

20. Get sample tests with answers. Taking sample tests will help you understand the structure of the exam, and will give you an idea of what material is covered.

21. Review your quizzes and homework. If you keep track of the right and wrong answers, you can review what areas need improvement and focus on those areas.

22. Complete any and all reviews offered by your professor. These are a great way to prepare for exams and can help identify areas where you are weak.

23. Show all of your work. Partial credit is a great way to gain points on quizzes and tests.

24. Answer the easy questions first. When taking the exam, work on the easiest questions first. This will help boost your confidence and will give you the time to work on the tougher questions.

25. Get enough sleep the night before the exam. Cramming late into the night is not going to help you during the exam as much as a good night’s sleep will. Even if you feel like you haven’t studied enough, getting a good night’s rest is essential.

By following these tips, you’ll be well on your way to a successful semester in college algebra. Good luck!

How to Use a Portable Bandsaw
A portable bandsaw is a great tool to have when you need to make curved cuts or rip long lengths of lumber. If this is something you need to do, you may need to purchase or rent a portable bandsaw. Before you do so, you should familiarize yourself on how to properly use a portable bandsaw. 

Rent or Buy the Portable Bandsaw Best Suited for Your Needs
Depending on the size and type of job you are performing, you may decide to buy or rent a proper portable bandsaw for the job. Measures to consider include if you need to cut curves in or rip long lengths of lumber. The size of the power source should also be taken into account when deciding what type and size of saw to buy or rent. A smaller saw is better for smaller jobs, meaning a smaller engine. For heavier jobs, a larger engine will be required. Make sure that the saw is covered by a warranty in case of malfunction. 

Familiarize Yourself with the Tool
After you have acquired the portable bandsaw you need, read the operator’s manual and become familiar with the saw’s unique characteristics and the safety recommendations from the manufacturer. Read up on the types of blades that are best for your saw. Know what type of adjustment it has and how to use them. Be sure to know how to adjust the height of the blade. 

Use the Two Handles
This tool is meant to be used with two hands, one located on each end of the saw. This is to ensure maximum control of the saw while it is operated. With one hand on each end of the saw, it will be easier to maneuver the saw as you need. As you use the saw, keep it close to your body and avoid putting too much strain on your body. 

Dress Appropriately for Using the Tool
Make sure you are wearing the proper clothing when using the saw. Wear safety glasses, ear protection and a dust mask. Wear comfortable clothes that don’t restrict movement or restrict breathing. Be sure to avoid loose clothing as it can get caught in the saw blade or get caught up in the saw while working.

Support Loose Material when Cutting
Be sure to support the material you are cutting so it is held securely in place. This will help ensure accuracy while making the cut and prevent the material from bowing or flexing as it is cut. If you are making a long rip cut, it is a good idea to use a straight edge as a guide along with a clamped support, which will help keep the material in place and cut true to the line. 

Mark the Stock You Cut at the Correct Angle for Your Needs
When cutting, be sure to mark the stock at the exact angle of the cut you need. A miter box is another helpful tool that can provide a better way to make accurate cuts. By using the miter box, the saw blade will be firmly held and supported at the perfect angle. Be sure to measure the cut down to the fraction if you need a precise cut. 

Place the Sawblade Against the Stock To Be Cut
Make sure the blade is parallel to the cut line you have marked, and perpendicular to the stock. If the cut is to be square, or 90 degrees, make sure the saw blade is lined up exactly right. Turn on the saw and wait for the blade to come to full speed. 

Start the Saw and Make the Cut
When the blade is working at its peak, start the process by squeezing the trigger to start the saw. Allow the saw to cut its way through the stock and continue making the cut. Along the way, watch the blade to make sure it is aligned with the cut mark. As you come close to finishing, slow the cut down so you can anticipate the blade binding if the material flexes or bends suddenly during the cut. When the cut is complete, release the trigger and allow the blade to stop moving before setting the saw down. 

Lastly, familiarize yourself with any material type you may cut and its characteristics, if possible. Adjust the saw so that it will cut the material in a way that eliminates splintering, especially when you are cutting hardwoods. With the proper knowledge and usage, a portable bandsaw is a great tool to have for both home and professional use.

Using an encyclopedia can be a powerful way to learn about a wide range of subjects, from biology to history and beyond. Knowing how to use this powerful tool, however, can be a challenge. This guide will show you step-by-step how to make the most of your encyclopedia research. 

Step One: Ask a reference librarian what encyclopedias are available for your use. Reference librarians have knowledge of the many different encyclopedias in their library and can offer you information about which ones to use for your research. 

Step Two: Choose a person, place or thing that you want to research. This could be something as broad as a general theme or concept, or something as specific as a person or a place. Be as specific as possible; the more information you have at the start, the better results you will get.

Step Three: Use the first letter of the topic to find the encyclopedia volume you need. Generally, encyclopedias are arranged by topics, and they can be found in the indexes. For a particular person or place, you may need to find the volume in which it is listed.

Step Four: Take out the volume. Remove the volume from the shelf, and take it to a comfortable area, such as a table or chair. Be careful not to damage the binding or pages.

Step Five: Make a photocopy of the page or pages that have information on your subject. You can make a photocopy of the page to use as a reference and to take notes on. Highlight important terms and words in the first encyclopedia entry.

Step Six: Find additional subjects to research in your highlighted words. Using the highlighted words and terms, start looking for additional subjects that may be related to your initial topic.

Step Seven: Return to the shelves that house the encyclopedia. Once you have a few more subjects in mind, go back to the encyclopedia shelves and look for the volumes that contain them.

Step Eight: Photocopy the pages that include the subject you are looking for. Make photocopies of the pages that have the second, third, and fourth subjects based on your search for more information. 

Step Nine: Highlight, annotate, and research new subjects to learn more information on a subject. As time goes on, and you become more familiar with the encyclopedia, begin to note important words, phrases, and people as you go. You can use these for further research.

Step Ten: Look for references to other reference books. Your research subject may lead you beyond the encyclopedia itself, and into other reference books. Make a list of the books you need, and use the library's card catalog to find the location of the books.

Step Eleven: Ask your teacher whether you are being asked to cite sources in Modern Language Association (MLA) or Chicago Style. MLA and Chicago Style are two different formats for citing sources, and you should consult your teacher about which one is required for the assignment. 

Step Twelve: Format your MLA encyclopedia citation as Last Name, First Name. The citation should include the article title, author, volume, publisher, year, and page numbers.

Step Thirteen: Cite an online encyclopedia in MLA Style as Last Name, First Name. The citation should include the title of the article, author, the website title, date of publication, URL, and the date you accessed the article.

Step Fourteen: Format your Chicago Style encyclopedia entry as Last Name, First Name. The citation should include the article title, author, volume, publisher, year, page numbers, and the library where the article is located.

Step Fifteen: Cite an online encyclopedia in Chicago Style as Last Name, First Name. The citation should include the title of the article, author, the website title, date of publication, date you accessed the article, and the URL.

Using an encyclopedia as a tool for research is a great way to learn more about a subject. As long as you have a basic understanding of how to use the encyclopedia, you'll be able to make the most of your research. Just remember to cite your sources, and always consult a reference librarian if you have any questions.

Achieving the vintage look in Photoshop is not only easy, but it also yields amazing results. The vintage look adds a sense of nostalgia and authenticity that can take an ordinary image to the next level. Here is an easy guide on how to achieve the vintage look in Photoshop. 

First, open an image in Photoshop. Then, click “Layers” in the menu bar. After that, select “Duplicate Layer…” in the dropdown menu and confirm by clicking “OK.” If you do not provide a new name for the layer, it will appear as “copy” in the layers window. Next, click the “eye” icon next to the Background layer to hide it. 

Now, click “Layer” in the menu bar and select “Smart Objects” from the drop-down menu. Click “Convert to Smart Object.” After that, select “Filter” in the menu bar, then “Filter Gallery…”. Choose the “Texture” folder and then select “Grain.” After that, click “OK.” 

Next, click “Filter” in the menu bar and select “Lens Correction…”. Click on the “Custom” tab and adjust the “Amount” slider to -100 in the “Vignette” section. Then, click “OK.” 

After that, click “Layer” in the menu bar and choose “New Adjustment Layer” from the drop-down menu. Select “Hue/Saturation…” and click “OK”. Adjust the sliders to change the levels, and then click the arrow icon in the upper-right corner of the dialog box. 

Now, click the “Opacity” option in the upper right corner of the Layers window. Set the opacity to 45% and click the duplicate layer in the Layers window. Click “Styles,” then select the drop-down menu in the upper-right corner of the Styles window. After that, select “Image Effects” then click “OK.” Now, you should select a style effect for your image from the options available. To finish, save your image. 

This guide should have given you a good idea of how to achieve the vintage look in Photoshop. With practice and experimentation, you too can achieve amazing vintage-looking images. Have fun!

Drawing a circle in GIMP is easy and simple. With a few steps, you can create perfect circles for your graphic design projects. Here are the steps to draw a circle in GIMP:

1.  Click the Ellipse Select Tool in the Toolbox. This is located in the Toolbox at the left of your window.

2.  Click and drag on your canvas to begin creating an ellipse. Keep dragging until you have the size of ellipse you want.

3.  Press and hold .⇧ Shift while dragging to make a circle. This will ensure that the ellipse you are creating is a perfect circle.

4.  Click the Select menu from the GIMP menu bar and choose "To Path." This will convert the ellipse you have created into a path.

5.  Click the Select menu again and choose "None." This will deselect the path.

6.  Select the color you want to use for the border in the color picker. Make sure you have the color you want to use as the foreground color.

7.  Click the Edit menu and select "Stroke Path." This will create an outline along the path with the color you selected.

8.  Set the width of the circle border in the "Line width" field. You can set the border width to any size you want by entering the number in the "Line width" field.

9.  Click "Stroke" to create the circle. This will create an outlined circle with the line width and color set earlier.

10. Fill the circle with another color if you'd like. Select the color you want to use to fill the circle as your foreground color.

11. Click the Ellipse Select Tool in the Toolbox. Start creating an ellipse by clicking and dragging.

12. Hold .⇧ Shift after you start dragging to create a perfect circle.

13. Choose the color you want to use for the circle border as the foreground color.

14. Click the Edit menu and select "Fill with FG color." This will fill the circle with the color you chose.

15. Fill the center with a different color if you'd like. Select the color you want to use to fill the center of the circle as your foreground color.

16. Click the Edit menu in the GIMP menu bar and select "Fill with FG color." This will fill the center of the circle with the color you chose.

With these steps, you can easily draw perfect circles in GIMP and add them to your graphic design projects. Whether you’re creating logos or images for your website, GIMP can be an easy and powerful tool for creating circles.

Learning how to build a sod house can be an exciting addition to any lifestyle or homesteading project. A sod house is a traditional home, usually found in more rural areas, that is made of grass, and is usually somewhat akin to an earthbag building style. If you plan ahead, it can be a relatively easy and fun process. To get started on building your own sod house, follow these steps.

First, choose a suitable location, preferably one with big open spaces, a lot of grass, and fairly level land. September is the ideal month to start building your sod house; the grass' roots are overly embedded in the ground at this time, making them the strongest and most secure.

Now, mark the perimeter of your house, making sure to include placement for windows and doors. Dig up the turf inside the area you marked, and then prepare the dirt beneath by raking it until it's smooth and level. In order to prevent the turf from rolling away, you can tamp down the dirt as much as possible.

Mow the grass inside the marked area to a height of four inches. Next, slice the sod blocks into two-foot strips and then cut these strips into one-foot intervals. Start laying your first row of sod bricks at the base of the house, grass-side down. Your second layer should overlap the first one. Continue to build your walls out of the sod bricks until you get to the bottom of the windows.

Once you reach the bottom of the windows, start to build the walls around the window and door frames. An easy way to do this is to measure and add framework pieces around the windows and doors before you begin using hand tools like hammers and chisels to sculpt and fit pieces together.

To finish the construction of your sod house, you will need to add a roof. This can be done with wooden planks and rafters or with a straw bale and foam. Once it's built, cover the roof with pieces of sod. Install the doors and windows and fill any remaining spaces in the walls with additional sod or grass. For extra protection and security, suspend a muslin sheet to the roof to form a sort of interior ceiling. This will protect against dirt and water that may fall from the roof.

Once the construction is complete, it's important to remember to give your sod house a finished look. Smooth the inside of the walls and whitewash them. Finally, furnish the interior of your newly built sod house to give it a warm and inviting feel. 

Now that you know how to build a sod house, you have all the tools and knowledge needed to take on this unique project. Get creative and enjoy your new, traditional, earth-friendly home!
