How to Cleanse Yourself of Prejudices and Race Based Behaviors

It is important to recognize that we all have biases and preconceived notions about certain races or cultures, as they are often a product of the information we received throughout our lifetime. The first step towards overcoming these prejudices is to accept that they exist within us and that we are not immune to them. In this article, we will outline practical steps that you can take to cleanse yourself of race-based behaviors and prejudices.

1. Get Ready for a Mental Journey

Recognizing and overcoming prejudices and racial perceptions is not a physical journey, but rather a mental one. It requires introspection, self-doubt, and a willingness to be wrong about some of your beliefs. Therefore, it is essential to prepare yourself for this journey mentally. Accept that it is going to be a challenging and uncomfortable process.

2. Understand that We are a Product of the Information We Receive

We are all a product of the information we receive. It is incredibly difficult to step out of the times we live in, especially when we are continually bombarded with images and bits of information that promote thinking and stereotypes. Realize that you too have been a recipient of a specific type of information that may promote certain beliefs or ideas.

3. Accept That You Must be Filled with Bits of False Information

Understand that it is okay to have false bits of information or beliefs. It is almost impossible to know everything about everything. Accepting that you must be filled with bits of false information created by others allows you to approach new ideas and information with an open mind.

4. Understand That Perceptions Do Not Determine Actions

Having a perception does not mean that you will act on that faulty perception. Knowing that your beliefs or perceptions can be incorrect and that they do not determine how you will behave is a powerful tool. It allows you to separate yourself from negative or harmful actions.

5. Practice the Process of Examining Information

Examine the information you receive and practice critical thinking regularly. This process prepares you for the information that you receive. It allows you to analyze and scrutinize the information you receive, separating facts from beliefs.

6. Attempt to Increase New Types of Information

Expand the information you receive by seeking out new experiences and perspectives. Challenge yourself to explore different cultures, read books about history and diverse cultures, or attend events that promote inclusion and diversity. Increasing the type of information you receive helps you gain a new perspective on people and beliefs.

7. Practice Replacement Experiences

Replace old beliefs and experiences with new, more accurate ones. Practice replacing negative beliefs with positive or inclusive ones. For example, if you hold certain stereotypes about a particular group, expose yourself to individuals from that group or read positive stories or articles that challenge those stereotypes.

In conclusion, cleansing yourself of prejudices and race-based behaviors is a process that requires introspection, self-awareness, and a willingness to change your perspective. With these practical tips, you can work to overcome your biases and create a more inclusive and accepting worldview. Remember, with a willingness to be wrong and a desire to learn and grow, anyone can overcome their prejudices and racial stereotypes.

How to Use Siri on an iPhone

Siri is a personal assistant that is tailored specifically for Apple devices. With Siri, you can easily make calls, send messages, set reminders, check the weather, and perform many other tasks on your iPhone without even touching it. Here’s how to use Siri on your iPhone:

Part 1: Enabling Siri

1. Make sure your iPhone supports Siri. To use Siri, you need an iPhone 4s or later.

2. Open Settings. Tap the Settings app on your iPhone’s home screen.

3. Scroll down and tap Siri. You will find Siri under the General tab.

4. Slide Siri right to the "On" position. This will enable Siri on your iPhone.

5. Tap Enable Siri. Once you have enabled Siri, you can customize its preferences.

6. Customize your Siri preferences. You can customize Siri’s language and accent, and also choose whether or not you want Siri to respond when the iPhone is locked.

Part 2: Using Siri

1. Press and hold your iPhone's Home button. This will activate Siri and the microphone icon will appear on the screen.

2. Wait for a rainbow line to appear at the bottom of the screen. This means that Siri is active and is ready to receive your commands.

3. Ask or tell Siri something. You can ask Siri for almost anything, such as the weather, directions to a specific place, or to call someone.

4. Tap ?. If you're not sure what to ask Siri, tap the question mark icon. Siri will provide you with some suggestions.

5. Press the Home button again. Once you've finished using Siri, press the Home button again to exit the app.

6. Activate Siri. To activate Siri without pressing and holding the Home button, just say "Hey Siri" if you have this function activated.

7. Say "Call " to make a phone call. Siri will automatically dial the number for you.

8. Say "FaceTime " to initiate a FaceTime call. This will video call a person instead of making a regular phone call.

9. Say "Tell " followed by a text message. Siri will automatically compose and send the message for you.

10. Say "Yes" when Siri finishes reading aloud your message. This confirms that you want to send the message.

11. Say "Send an email to ." Siri will help you compose and send an email.

12. Ask Siri to search the Internet. Siri can quickly get relevant search results from the internet on the topic you request.

13. Ask Siri to set up a meeting. Siri can help you manage your schedule by syncing with your calendar app.

14. Ask Siri to give you a reminder. Siri can also remind you of scheduled events or tasks.

15. Ask Siri to check the weather. Siri can inform you about the weather forecast in your area.

16. Ask Siri to set an alarm. Set an alarm using only your voice.

17. Ask Siri to write a note. Siri can create context-sensitive notes.

18. Ask Siri for information. Siri can provide information on different topics.

19. Ask Siri to play a song. Siri can also play or search for your favorite song or track, be it Apple Music or Spotify.

20. Establish personal connections. Ask Siri to call or send a message to a specific person or a contact by name.

21. Correct Siri's mistakes. If Siri interprets your words incorrectly or doesn’t understand what you say, simply correct the mistake.

22. Change Siri's default search engine. If you prefer to use another search engine besides Apple’s default one, you can choose between Google, Bing, or Yahoo!.

23. Ask Siri to tell you a joke. Siri has a sense of humor and can share some funny jokes or anecdotes.

Part 3: Using Dictation

1. Enable Dictation. Tap Settings, select General then Keyboard and turn on Enable Dictation.

2. Open an app that allows you to type. Make sure the app has a keyboard.

3. Tap the Dictation button next to the space bar. The microphone icon on the keyboard pops up and you can start dictating the text.

4. Speak what you want to type in a clear, measured voice. Dictate what you want to say, and Siri will convert it to text.

5. Say punctuation marks. You can dictate punctuation marks such as commas or periods.

6. Start a new line or paragraph. You can dictate new lines or paragraphs using commands like "new line" or "new paragraph."

7. Turn caps lock on and off. You can dictate capital letters by saying “Caps on” or “Capital A”. Saying “Caps off” will enable lower case typing again.

Siri is a powerful tool that can save you a great deal of time and effort. By using Siri, you can interact with your iPhone without having to take your hands off the steering wheel while driving, or even without looking at the screen. With a little practice, Siri can become an indispensable part of your daily routine.

Running a guesthouse in a developing country presents unique challenges for entrepreneurs looking to enter the hospitality industry. Though these challenges can be daunting, with careful planning and a bit of talent, running a successful guesthouse is a very achievable goal. This article will discuss some considerations you should make when operating a guesthouse in a developing country. 

Consider these questions when you choose the location:

The first step in running a guesthouse is finding a suitable location. In a developing country, this can be especially challenging due to a lack of infrastructure and services. When scouting out locations, ask yourself: 

1. How simple or complicated is it to find your place when you give directions to someone who has never been to your city or village? 

2. Will you be able to deal with noise if it is present in the area?

3. Are there any fun and enjoyable areas for guests to explore?

4. Is the environment properly decorated with original paintings and mirrors?

5. Is there an outdoor space for guests to relax?

6. Are there clear directions towards common areas, toilets, and the kitchen?

7. Are you implementing green initiatives? 

Provide the essentials:

After finding a suitable location, the next step is to equip your guesthouse with the essentials that guests require. It is important to provide the following: 

1. A cozy bed 

2. Soft and comfortable bedding 

3. Towels and other personal hygiene items 

4. Side tables with lamps 

5. A small table and chairs 

6. Suitable storage facilities for clothing and shoes 

7. Hooks on the doors and walls 

8. Thick curtains for privacy and noise protection 

Seek to get as many customers as possible:

Once the guesthouse is established and outfitted with the necessary accommodations, it is time to attract customers. Use these tips to get more business: 

1. Create simple, colorful brochures that advertise your guesthouse.

2. Build a website for your guesthouse with high-quality photos.

3. Establish a commission system that incentivizes local travel agents or booking companies to refer guests to your guesthouse.

4. Offer food at the guesthouse, such as breakfast, lunch, and dinner for an additional fee.

5. Sell local handicrafts to your guests to fundraise for the development of the area or to gift the items to the guests. 

6. Be cooperative and collaborative with others in the vicinity of your guesthouse. 

Know how to make a profit:

Running a guesthouse in a developing country presents an opportunity to make a tremendous profit. But, profitability depends on keeping your expenses under control. Make sure you consider these things: 

1. Hire employees with experience who understand the guesthouse business and are willing to work on a part-time or full-time basis. 

2. Keep overhead costs low by finding a reasonable rent and energy usage practices. 

3. Find ways to save money, such as by outsourcing linen cleaning or investing in quality furniture that won't have to be replaced frequently. 

Running a guesthouse in a developing country requires careful planning and a business mindset. Remember to consider the necessities, environment, marketing, and profitability when seeking to provide travelers with a comfortable and affordable lodging experience. Implement these tips, and you are likely to reap the rewards of operating a successful guesthouse.

If you have a loved one with Alzheimer's disease or dementia, finding a nursing home that can meet their unique needs is important. There are several steps you can take to find the best nursing home for your loved one. In this article, we'll explore the different factors to consider when choosing a nursing home.

1. Determine your ability to pay for nursing home care.

Before you start looking for a nursing home, it's important to determine your budget and what you can afford. Nursing home care can be expensive, so you'll want to factor costs into your decision-making process. Consider whether your loved one has long-term care insurance or qualifies for Medicaid.

2. Research available nursing homes online.

The internet is a great resource for finding nursing homes in your area. Many nursing homes have websites that you can visit to learn more about their services and amenities. You can also use review sites like Yelp and Google Reviews to read about the experiences of other families who have used the nursing home's services.

3. Contact individual nursing homes through their websites.

Once you've identified a few nursing homes that seem like a good fit, reach out to them directly. You can typically do this through their websites or by phone. Ask about the availability of beds and whether they have experience working with Alzheimer's and dementia patients.

4. Consult with experts in nursing home care for recommendations.

There are a variety of professionals who can provide recommendations for nursing homes. This includes doctors, nurses, and social workers who work with older adults. You may also want to consult with your state's long-term care ombudsman, who can provide insight into the rankings for a given nursing home as well as a record of complaints filed against that home and their resolution.

5. Balance your loved one's needs with your own.

When choosing a nursing home, you'll need to balance your loved one's needs with your own. This includes considering things like location, visiting hours, and the availability of specialized care. It's important to find a nursing home that meets both your loved one's needs and your own needs as their caregiver.

6. Visit prospective nursing homes.

Once you've narrowed down your list of potential nursing homes, visit each one in person. Take along copies of any nursing home checklists you may have found online. During your visit, pay attention to cleanliness, the friendliness of staff members, and the availability of activities and amenities.

7. Listen as well as look.

During your visit, listen to your gut instincts as well as your observations. Take note of any red flags or warning signs, such as a strong antiseptic smell that may indicate poor handling of incontinent residents.

8. Interview the nursing home's administrator and staff.

Talk to the nursing home's administrator and staff members to get a better sense of their approach to care. Ask about how the home handles Alzheimer's and dementia patients as well as how it handles general issues such as falls and incontinence. Ask the staff about their workload, employee morale, and turnover rates.

9. Ask both the administrators and staff about any upcoming changes in ownership.

Sometimes nursing homes may be in a state of transition and undergoing ownership changes. It's important to know about any upcoming changes that could impact your loved one's care.

10. Ask residents' families about the quality of care the home delivers.

Lastly, ask other families who have loved ones in the nursing home about their experiences. This can provide valuable insights into the quality of care your loved one can expect to receive.

Finding the right nursing home for someone with Alzheimer's disease or dementia can take time and effort. By taking these steps, you can increase your chances of finding a home that meets your loved one's needs and gives you peace of mind.

Maintaining the health and speed of your Windows 8.1 Pro hard drive can be accomplished through performing regular disk defragmentation. This process works by reorganizing fragmented data on the hard drive, making it easier and quicker for your computer to access and process information. In this article, we will guide you through the steps to defrag (disk defragment) a hard drive on Windows 8.1 Pro.

1. Navigate to your Desktop
Begin by navigating to your desktop. Once you have reached your desktop, right-click anywhere (not on an icon) and select "Personalize" from the drop-down menu.

2. Open Personalization Settings
After clicking "Personalize", a window called "Personalization" should appear. From there, click on the "Change desktop icons" option located on the left-hand side of the window.

3. Enable Computer Icon
Next, click on the checkbox next to the "Computer" or "This PC" option and click "Apply" and "OK" to save the changes. You should now see the Computer icon appear on your desktop.

4. Open Disk Properties
Double-click on the "Computer" or "This PC" icon to open the Hard Drive Properties. From there, select the Properties option from the context menu.

5. Run Disk Cleanup
In the Hard Drive Properties window, click on the "Disk Cleanup" button located at the bottom right-hand corner. Wait for the system to calculate the amount of data that can be deleted.

6. Access the "Optimize Drives" Option
After completing the disk cleanup, select the "Tools" tab from the Hard Drive Properties window. You will then see the "Optimize Drives" option. Click on it to open the defragmentation tool.

7. Optimize Hard Drives
Once the "Optimize Drives" window has opened, select the hard drive you want to defragment. If you have multiple drives, select the one you want to optimize by clicking on it such that it highlights in blue. Then click "Optimize" next to the "Analyze" button.

Conclusion
By following these simple steps, you can defragment your hard drive in Windows 8.1 Pro, ensuring optimal performance and speed for your computer.

Calculating the days of the week may seem daunting, but with a simple formula and some basic codes, anyone can do it. In this article, we will show you how to calculate days of the week like Rainman.

Step 1: Assign a Number to Each Day of the Week

To start, assign a number to each day of the week. Monday is 1, Tuesday is 2, Wednesday is 3, Thursday is 4, Friday is 5, Saturday is 6, and Sunday can be represented as 0 or 7.

Step 2: Have a Number for Every Month

Next, assign a number for every month. January is 6 (or 5 in a leap year), February is 2 (or 1 in a leap year), March is 3, April is 5, May is 0, June is 3, July is 5, August is 1, September is 4, October is 6, November is 2, and December is 4.

Step 3: Create a Year Code

Create a code for every year. Starting with the year 2000, assign the code 0 and then add one to each successive year. Use multiples of seven to get as close as possible to the answer. For example, (7 * 10) = 70, so the year 2070 would have a code of 0.

Step 4: Use the Formula

To calculate the day of the week for a specific date, use the formula: Month Code + Day + Year Code. Once you have this number, use multiples of seven to get as close as possible, then subtract the difference and use the remainder as the Day Code.

Step 5: Examples

Let's use Christmas 2009 as an example. December has a month code of 4, and Christmas Day is the 25th. The year code for 2009 is 4. So the formula is 4 + 25 + 4 = 33. The closest multiple of seven is 28, so 33 - 28 = 5, and Friday is the Day Code.

For another example, let's calculate the day of the week for Christmas Day in 2010. The month code for December is 4, the day is 25, and the year code for 2010 is 5. The formula is 4 + 25 + 5 = 34. The closest multiple of seven is 35, so 35 - 34 = 1, and Saturday is the Day Code.

In conclusion, calculating days of the week like Rainman may seem complex at first, but with a little practice and these simple codes and formulas, it can become second nature. Try using this method to impress your friends and family with your Rainman-like abilities.

How to Make Apple Baby Food

Making baby food at home is a great way to give your little one healthy, nutritious meals that are free of harmful additives and preservatives. Apples are a great fruit to use in making baby food, as they are full of vitamins, fiber, and natural sweetness that babies love. Here's how to make apple baby food that your little one will adore!

Part 1: Preparing the Apples

1. Look for organic apples. It's always best to choose organic produce when making baby food, as it will be free of harmful pesticides and chemicals.

2. Choose apples with a mild, sweet flavor, such as Gala, Braeburn, Fuji or Red Delicious. These varieties of apples are less tart and more palatable for babies.

3. Examine the apples to make sure they have a consistent coloring and aren’t bruised or damaged. You want to choose apples that are firm and unblemished.

4. Wash the apples well under clean, running water. This will help remove any dirt or debris that may be present on the apples.

5. Peel the apples with a peeling knife. Removing the skin of the apples will make them easier to digest for your baby.

6. Remove the core of the apples. Cut the apple in half, then use a small pairing knife to remove the core and any seeds.

7. Slice the apple into 1 inch (2.5 cm) pieces. This will make it easier to cook the apples.

8. Place two handfuls of prepared sliced apples in a saucepan on the stove with 1 cup of warm water. You want to use enough water to just cover the apples.

9. Take out a piece of apple and press it with a fork to check if it is cooked. If it is soft and tender, it's ready to be pureed.

10. Remove the saucepan from the heat. Use a slotted spoon to remove the apples from the water.

11. Place the apples in a blender and make a puree. Blend until the apples are completely smooth and there are no lumps.

12. Refrigerate any leftover applesauce. This can be stored for up to 3 days in the fridge.

Part 2: Making Apple Porridge

1. Prepare the ingredients for the porridge. You will need 2 apples, 1/4 cup of rolled oats, and 1 cup of milk.

2. Grate the apples with a grater. This will make them easier to cook and chew for your baby.

3. Add the grated apples to the boiling water. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the apples are tender.

4. Add the milk and the rolled oats to the saucepan with the boiled apples. Stir until everything is well combined.

5. Prepare the ingredients. You will need 2 apples, 1/2 cup of cooked rice, and 1/2 pound of ground beef or chicken.

6. Pour all the ingredients into a saucepan and place it on the stove. Cook on medium heat for 10-15 minutes until everything is cooked.

7. Check to make sure everything is cooked. Use a fork to test the tenderness of the apples and the meat.

8. Remove the pan from the stove. Let it cool for a few minutes before blending.

9. Put apples and meat in a blender to make a smooth puree. Blend until everything is well mixed and there are no lumps.

10. Make sure the food is room temperature before serving it to your baby. This will help prevent burns and discomfort.

Part 3: Baking Apples for Baby

1. Do not peel the apple if you are going to bake it. The skin will help the apple keep its shape and flavor.

2. Cut the apples in half and remove the cores. Use a spoon to scoop out any seeds or tough parts.

3. Pour 1-2 inches of water into a shallow oven proof baking dish. This will help cook the apples evenly.

4. Bake the apples in the oven for 30 minutes at 400 degrees Fahrenheit (200 degrees Celsius). Check on them occasionally to make sure they are not burning.

5. Take the apples out of the oven and leave them to cool for a few minutes. You can sprinkle them with a little cinnamon or nutmeg for added flavor.

6. Finished! You can serve these baked apples whole or cut them into small pieces for your little one. They make a great snack or addition to a meal.

With these simple steps, you can make delicious and nutritious apple baby food that your little one will love. It's a great way to give your baby a healthy start in life!

How to Make a Low Cost Door Knob Extender for People with Hand Pain

If you or someone you know suffer from hand pain, opening and closing doors can be a real challenge. The good news is that you can make a low-cost doorknob extender to make this task easier. With a few simple tools and a length of plastic tubing, you can create your own doorknob extender that is effective and affordable. Follow the steps below to get started.

Materials:

- 3⁄4 inch (1.9 cm) plastic electrical conduit or similar plastic tubing
- 2 inch (5.1 cm) drywall screws
- Drill
- Saw

Instructions:

1. Obtain a length of 3⁄4 inch (1.9 cm) plastic electrical conduit or similar plastic tubing.

2. At the 1.5 and 4.5 inch marks, cut a notch in the tubing.

3. Cut through the tubing at the 3 and 6 inch marks to make two 3 inch (7.6 cm) pieces, each with one notch.

4. In one piece, drill a small hole all the way through the tubing so that when this hole is parallel to a flat surface behind the tubing, with the notch facing up at about a 45-degree angle.

5. Place the two 3 inch (7.6 cm) pieces on opposite sides of the doorknob and run 2 inch (5.1 cm) drywall screws through the pre-drilled holes to connect the tubes together behind the knob.

6. Return to the tube you marked in step one, and cut it off at the 13 inch (33.0 cm) mark, now 7 inches (17.8 cm) from the end after cutting off the two 3 inch (7.6 cm) pieces.

7. Notch the tube to about half the diameter so that the notch will fit over the knob.

8. Drill a small hole all the way through the tube on each side of the notch, so that the line of the holes will be perpendicular to the door when the notch is placed over the knob.

9. Place the 7 inch (17.8 cm) piece you just completed over the knob with the screws run almost as far in as they can go.

10. Screw the 7 inch (17.8 cm) piece to the 3 inch (7.6 cm) pieces.

With your doorknob extender in place, you can enjoy the simple pleasure of opening and closing doors without experiencing pain or discomfort. This low-cost solution is easy to make and can be a lifesaver for anyone who suffers from hand pain. Give it a try and see the difference it can make in your daily life.

Tanning in the sun is a popular leisure activity that many people enjoy during the summer months. However, it is important to tan safely and take precautions to prevent skin damage and skin cancer. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to tan in the sun safely and effectively.

1. Change into clothes that expose your skin to the sun.
Wear comfortable, lightweight clothing that will allow your skin to breathe and soak up the sun's rays.

2. Tan before 10 AM or after 4 PM for the safest results.
During these times, the sun's rays are weaker, and the UV index is less intense, making it less likely that you'll burn.

3. Apply sunscreen with SPF 15-30 at least 20 minutes before heading out.
Choose a broad-spectrum sunscreen that will protect against both UVA and UVB rays. Apply liberally to all exposed skin, paying close attention to areas that are prone to burning, such as your nose, ears, neck, and shoulders.

4. Wear UV-protecting sunglasses.
Protect your eyes from harmful UV rays by wearing sunglasses that block at least 99% of UVA and UVB rays.

5. Do not use "accelerating lotions" or other quick-tan methods.
These products can damage your skin and increase your risk of skin cancer.

6. Understand how tanning works.
Tanning is your skin's way of protecting itself from the sun by producing melanin. The more time you spend in the sun, the more melanin your skin will produce, resulting in a darker tan.

7. Lie in direct sunlight for 20-30 minutes.
Gradually increase the amount of time you spend in the sun, taking breaks every hour to reapply sunscreen and hydrate.

8. Reapply sunscreen and flip over to get an even tan.
Make sure to cover all exposed areas with sunscreen, and reapply every two hours or after getting wet or sweating.

9. Hydrate while you tan.
Drink plenty of water to prevent dehydration and heat exhaustion.

10. Do not tan for more than 1 hour at a time, even with sunscreen.
It's important to take regular breaks and give your skin a chance to rest.

11. Stop tanning if you feel pain or your skin becomes red.
These are signs of sunburn, which can cause permanent damage to your skin and increase your risk of skin cancer.

12. Supplement your tan with bronzing cream.
If you want to enhance your tan, use a bronzing cream or spray instead of spending more time in the sun.

13. Adjust the time in the sun based on skin type.
People with fair skin are more prone to burning and should spend less time in the sun than those with darker skin.

14. Know that you do not need to burn in order to get a deep tan.
Burning your skin will only cause damage and increase your risk of skin cancer.

15. Use gentle moisturizing lotions, like aloe, to treat burns.
If you do get sunburned, use aloe vera or other gentle moisturizers to soothe your skin.

16. Drink a lot of water.
Drinking water can help prevent dehydration and heat stroke.

17. Take some ibuprofen.
If you experience pain or inflammation from a sunburn, ibuprofen can provide relief.

18. Place a cool, damp towel on your skin.
Cooling down your skin with a damp towel can help reduce redness and inflammation.

19. Do not pick off skin or pop blisters.
This can cause further damage to your skin and increase your risk of infection.

20. Check your skin head to toe each month.
Take note of any moles, freckles, or other spots that look unusual or change in size or appearance. See a dermatologist if you notice any changes or have concerns about your skin.

By following these tips, you can safely and effectively achieve a sun-kissed glow without putting your health at risk. Remember, always practice safe sun habits and protect your skin from damage.

Tsoureki, the sweet braided bread traditionally enjoyed in Greece during Easter, is a delicious treat that can also be enjoyed year-round. While the recipe may seem intimidating at first, with a little patience and attention to detail, you can easily bake a beautiful and flavorful loaf of Tsoureki. In this article, we'll walk you through the steps to make your own Tsoureki from scratch, including a unique step involving spice water and even a fun tradition involving a coin!

Ingredients:
- 1 stick of cinnamon
- 5 bay leaves
- 1 cup of water
- 1 package of yeast
- 1 teaspoon of sugar
- 1 can of milk
- 1 can's worth of water
- 1/2 cup of butter
- 7 eggs
- 2 cups of sugar
- 1 teaspoon of masticha
- 1 teaspoon of machlepi
- 8 cups of flour
- 1 coin wrapped in aluminum foil
- 1 tablespoon of sesame seeds

Instructions:

1. Make the spice water by boiling 1 stick of cinnamon and 5 bay leaves into a cup of water for 15 minutes.

2. Let the spice water cool for 10 minutes and add the yeast and 1 teaspoon of sugar to it. Stir gently and let sit for 10 minutes.

3. In a saucepan, heat up the can of milk on low flame. Once the milk is warm, add in one can's worth of water followed soon after by the butter. Stir until the butter melts and turn off the heat.

4. Beat 7 eggs and 2 cups of sugar in a separate, large bowl.

5. Add the milk mixture and the yeast mixture to the egg/sugar bowl. Stir to combine.

6. Grind masticha and machlepi in a mortar and pestle with a teaspoon of sugar until it forms a fine, sticky paste.

7. Mix the ground masticha and machlepi into the growing mixture.

8. Slowly add flour to the mixture, kneading with your hands until the dough is soft and slightly sticky.

9. Wrap the coin in aluminum foil and knead it into the dough.

10. Place the dough into a pie tin or on a baking sheet, cover it with a towel and let it rise until it doubles in size (usually 2 to 3 hours).

11. Preheat your oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.

12. Mix the remaining two eggs with sesame seeds and then lightly brush the mixture onto the top of the dough once it has risen.

13. Bake the Tsoureki at 350 degrees for 5 minutes.

14. Lower the oven temperature to 250 degrees Fahrenheit and let the Tsoureki bake for 45 minutes or until it turns golden brown.

15. Once it's finished baking, place the cooled Tsoureki onto a large plate.

16. Gather everyone around the table and have the primary caregiver in the house place $20-40 dollars onto the center of the table near the Tsoureki.

17. Carve a cross shape into the top of the Tsoureki (the ritual begins with a remembrance of Christ).

18. Spin the Tsoureki three times (also a religious reference, this time to the Trinity).

19. Cut the Tsoureki into equal sections, in this order: Christou (For the Church), Spitiou (For the House), Thoulia (For the Work), Nikoukidi (For the 'Man' of the House), Nikoukida (For the 'Woman' of the House), Bethiou (One slice for each of the children starting with the oldest).

20. Search each slice for the coin.

21. Whoever finds the coin in their piece of Tsoureki gets to keep it and spend the prize money on something frivolous that makes them happy! 

22. The only situation in which the money is used seriously is if the Church wins.

23. Keep the coin in a safe place for the next year and DO NOT SPEND IT!

Enjoy your homemade Tsoureki and the fun traditions that come along with it. You can also share this delicious bread with your family and friends as a special treat during holidays or any time of the year.

How to Promote a Music Festival: A Step-by-Step Guide

Music festivals are a great way to bring people together and celebrate the power of music. Whether you're organizing a small local event or a large-scale festival, proper promotion is essential to attracting attendees and creating buzz. Here's a step-by-step guide on how to promote a music festival that will generate excitement and draw in a crowd.

1. Decide on a Broad Genre of Music That the Festival Will Be Catering to and Choose Artists Within That Genre to Play.

The first step in organizing a music festival is to decide on the genre of music you want to feature. This will help you determine what type of artists to book and what kind of audience to target. Once you have decided on a genre, research and choose artists within that genre to perform at your festival.

2. Choose a Location, Date(s), and Times for Your Music Festival.

The next step is to choose a suitable location, date(s), and times for your music festival. Consider factors such as accessibility, capacity, and available amenities. Make sure your chosen location can accommodate the number of attendees you expect, and that the dates and times don't conflict with other major events in the area.

3. Rent Your Venue for the Decided Upon Dates and Times.

Once you have chosen your location, secure your venue by renting it for the dates and times you have selected. Be sure to read the rental agreement carefully and understand the terms and conditions.

4. Negotiate and Book Artists for Your Music Festival.

With your venue secured, it's time to negotiate and book the artists for your festival. Contact their agents and negotiate contracts that specify performance fees, technical requirements, and other details.

5. Contact Artists' Publicists as Well as Radio Stations, Television News Stations, Newspapers, Online Blogs, Networking Sites, and Music Sites to Spread the Word and Stimulate Word-of-Mouth Promoting for Your Music Festival.

Use a variety of media channels to promote your music festival. Follow up with artists' publicists to ensure proper communication, and promote your festival on social media, local radio stations, newspapers, and other media outlets. Be sure to encourage word-of-mouth promoting to increase attendance.

6. Contact and Meet with Possible Sponsors.

Reach out to potential sponsors and discuss the benefits of sponsoring your music festival. Be creative and offer attractive sponsorship packages that will attract a wide range of sponsors.

7. Make Music Event Promotion Tools, Such as Posters and Flyers, for Your Festival.

Design promotional materials such as posters, flyers, banners, and other marketing tools to promote your music festival. Use eye-catching designs and include important information such as the date, time, and location of the festival.

8. Reserve Your Crew and Technical Equipment for the Date of the Music Festival.

Make sure you have the proper crew and technical equipment for your festival. Reserve all necessary equipment, including sound systems, lighting, and staging, well in advance.

9. Confirm Your Radio and TV Advertising Slots within 5 Weeks of Your Music Event.

Confirm your radio and TV advertising slots at least five weeks before the event to ensure proper promotion. Make sure your ads reach your target audience and communicate all essential information about the festival.

10. Send Press Releases and Announcements to All of Your Confirmed Media and Communication Outlets Within 4 Weeks of the Music Festival.

One month before the festival, send out press releases and announcements to all of your confirmed media and communication outlets. Include detailed information about the festival and highlight any special features or events.

11. Post and Pass Out Your Music Festival Promotion Posters and Flyers Within 4 Weeks of the Event.

Maximize your promotion efforts by posting and handing out your promotional materials four weeks before the event. Advertise the festival in high traffic areas and distribute flyers and posters to local businesses and community centers.

12. Confirm All of Your Crew and Equipment 2 Weeks Prior to the Music Festival.

Two weeks before the festival, confirm all of your crew and equipment to ensure everything is in place. Make any necessary adjustments and address any potential issues before they become major problems.

13. Contact All of the Artists' Publicists to Confirm Contract Details and Communicate Any Event Updates.

How to Manage a Change in Ownership (when Taking over a Business)

Managing a change in ownership can be a daunting task, especially when it comes to taking over someone else's business. However, it can also be an exciting opportunity to create something new and rewarding. As the new owner, it is your responsibility to make sure that you handle the transition smoothly by communicating effectively with employees, ensuring that everyone is on the same page, and keeping the business running smoothly. Here are some tips to help you manage a change in ownership:

1. Communicate with your employees

The first step in managing a change in ownership is to communicate with your employees. Hold individual sessions with each of your employees, explain the reason for the change in ownership, and help them understand how it will affect them. Make sure that you listen to their concerns, answer their questions honestly, and reassure them about their job security.

2. Develop a strategy for each employee

Once you have communicated with your employees, it is time to develop a strategy for each of them. Consider what their strengths and weaknesses are, and how they could fit into the new business. Be transparent about your goals and give your employees a sense of ownership in the transition.

3. Develop personal relationships with your staff

Developing personal relationships with your staff is a crucial step in managing a change in ownership. Take time to get to know your employees individually and find out what motivates them. Create a sense of camaraderie and team spirit to help them feel at home in the workplace.

4. Offer your employees a range of options

It is important for your employees to feel that they have a range of options that they could pursue in the short term or long term. Offer them training opportunities, promotions, and other incentives that will help them feel valued and invested in the future of the business. Be open to new ideas and suggestions from your employees, and encourage them to take ownership of their roles.

5. Keep your employees informed

Communication is key when managing a change in ownership. Keep your employees informed about the progress of the transition, any changes in policies, and any other developments that may affect them. Make sure that they have the information they need to feel confident and secure in their roles.

In conclusion, managing a change in ownership can be a challenging process, but it can also be a rewarding one. By communicating effectively with your employees, developing personal relationships with them, and offering them a range of options, you can help ensure a successful transition and a bright future for your business.

Halloween is a time of spooky decorations, and nothing screams Halloween more than a "Gateway of Gore." Creating a gruesome entrance-way is the perfect way to set the tone for your Halloween party or scare-trick-or-treaters. Follow these steps to create your own "Gateway of Gore."

Step 3: Use your measurements to mark pieces of plywood to the lengths needed to fit around the entrance-way. Make sure to mark where the ends of each piece overlap so that you will know where to attach them together.

Step 4: Use a circular saw to cut the wood to the lengths you need. Be sure to wear protective eyewear and gloves while using power tools.

Step 5: Determine a shape you wish the outer edges of your gateway to be. This could be a series of jagged, uneven cuts or a more graceful, arched design.

Step 7: Utilize a jigsaw to cut the edge design that you have planned. Take your time and make sure that you are cutting along the line as accurately as possible.

Step 8: Layout your cut pieces of wood and make sure that everything is matching up nicely. You may need to sand down any rough edges or add additional pieces of wood to fill in gaps.

Step 9: At this point, you have the option of using masks to decorate your gateway. You can use plastic or latex masks to create a gruesome effect. Simply attach them to the wood with screws or nails.

Progressive aphasia is a neurological condition that affects an individual's ability to communicate effectively. It is a degenerative disease that worsens over time, and there is currently no cure. However, there are treatments available that can help manage the symptoms of progressive aphasia. In this article, we will discuss some steps you can take to treat progressive aphasia.

1. Make an appointment with a speech and language therapist

One of the mainstays of treating progressive aphasia is to work with a speech and language therapist. These professionals can help you address the challenges that you are having with language and communication. They will work with you to find alternate modes of communication, such as using a communication board or a tablet app.

2. Learn alternate modes of communication

Some people struggle more with language comprehension, while others find expressive language to be the primary challenge. Working with a speech and language therapist can help you identify which areas you need to focus on and give you strategies to practice.

3. Know that progressive aphasia can be managed, but not cured

When you go to see a speech and language therapist, there is nothing she can do to reverse or otherwise slow the progression of your condition. However, she can help manage your symptoms and improve your quality of life.

4. Connect with others who also have progressive aphasia

The challenges of those who suffer from progressive aphasia are unique, and to connect with others who are in the same boat can be extremely helpful. Support groups can be found both online and in person.

5. Carry information about your illness with you

Because progressive aphasia affects your communication abilities, it can be difficult to explain your illness to others. Carry information with you that explains your condition, including symptoms, treatments, and emergency contacts.

6. Ask for modified duties at the workplace

If you are still working, talk to your employer about modified duties that may better suit your abilities. This can help you stay employed for longer and maintain your independence.

7. Ask your doctor to perform regular clinical exams

It is important to receive regular clinical exams from your doctor to assess how your disease is progressing and how you are coping. Doctors can also ensure that nothing else is going on and rule out other degenerative brain diseases.

8. Consider asking for a head CT or MRI

In addition to ruling out other degenerative brain diseases, it is also key to differentiate progressive aphasia from other causes of aphasia, such as aphasia resulting from a stroke or a traumatic brain injury. Your doctor can perform a head CT or MRI to help with this diagnosis.

9. Learn the causes of progressive aphasia

There are a variety of causes of progressive aphasia, including Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Understanding the underlying cause of your condition can help guide treatment options.

10. Know the expected course of progressive aphasia

As you seek treatment for your progressive aphasia, it is important to know what to expect. The course of the disease varies from person to person, but in general, it worsens over time. Your healthcare team can help you understand what to expect and provide you with resources to manage your condition.

In conclusion, progressive aphasia is a challenging disease, but there are steps you can take to manage it. Working with a speech and language therapist, connecting with others who have the disease, and staying informed can all help you cope with the challenges of progressive aphasia. Remember to seek support, stay optimistic, and work with your healthcare team to find the best treatment plan for your unique situation.

How to Remove a Rootkit

A rootkit is a type of malware that can be extremely difficult to detect and remove. Rootkits are often used by hackers to gain unauthorized access to a computer system or to maintain control over an already-compromised system. If you suspect that your computer is infected with a rootkit, it's essential to know how to remove it properly. In this article, we'll guide you through the process of removing a rootkit from your PC.

Part 1: Initial Steps
1. Download your tools on another computer. Before you can begin removing the rootkit, you'll need to download the necessary tools to another computer. This is important because it helps to ensure that you're not downloading any more malware onto the infected PC.
2. Reboot the infected computer into Safe Mode. To boot your system into Safe Mode, start your computer, and press the F8 key repeatedly until the Advanced Boot Options menu appears. From there, select Safe Mode and press Enter.
3. Run TDSSKiller once you've booted into Safe Mode. TDSSKiller is a rootkit removal tool developed by Kaspersky. Once you've downloaded it onto a flash drive or CD, insert it into the infected PC and run it.

Part 2: More Advanced Steps
4. Run RKill in Safe Mode. RKill is a small utility designed to terminate processes running on the infected computer that may interfere with the operation of other malware removal tools. Run it in Safe Mode to help eliminate potential interference.
5. Run the Malwarebytes Antimalware installer and scan with it. Malwarebytes is a well-known anti-malware tool that can help identify and remove rootkits. After installing, run a complete scan of your system.
6. Run RogueKiller. RogueKiller is another free software that can assist in removing malicious software. Run it in Safe Mode.
7. Look for a removal tool designed for your specific infection. Depending on the type of rootkit infecting your system, there may be specific tools available to help remove it.
8. Download the free BitDefender RescueDisk ISO file. This tool acts as a bootable CD or flash drive, allowing you to remove malware from your computer even if it won't boot normally.
9. Burn the ISO file to a blank DVD or CD. You'll need a CD or DVD burner and a blank disc to burn the RescueDisk file properly.
10. Reboot your computer with the burned disc inserted. This will launch the BitDefender RescueDisk tool. Use it to scan your system for rootkits.
11. Click "Continue" to download any available updates. This ensures that you're using the most up-to-date version of the BitDefender tool.
12. Wait for the scanning process to complete. This may take some time depending on the size of your hard drive and the number of files to scan.
13. Delete or quarantine any infection that is found. The tool will alert you to any infections detected on your system and offer options for removing them.
14. Exit the BitDefender Rescue CD. Once you've removed the rootkit successfully, you can exit the tool and restart your computer.

Part 3: Final Steps
15. Know when to format and reinstall. If none of the above steps work, it might be necessary to format your hard drive and reinstall your operating system.
16. Backup any important data. Before wiping your hard drive, make sure to backup any important files and documents onto an external hard drive or flash drive.
17. Download DBAN and burn it to a blank disc. DBAN is a powerful data wiping tool that can help ensure that your hard drive is completely erased before reinstalling your OS.
18. Remove any external drives you don't want erased. This includes any USB drives or external hard drives that are connected to your computer.
19. Insert your burned DBAN disc and reboot your computer. This will launch the tool and erase your hard drive.
20. Press the .Enter key to start DBAN. Follow the prompts to ensure that your hard drive is erased completely.
21. Reinstall your operating system. Once your hard drive is erased, you'll need to reinstall your operating system.
22. Ensure your router firewall is enabled. This will help protect your computer from future attacks.
23. Install a trusted antivirus program. Make sure to install a reputable antivirus program to protect your computer from future attacks.
24. Ensure User Access Control (UAC) is enabled. This will help prevent unauthorized changes to your system.
25. Pay close attention to every screen when installing programs. This will help ensure that you don't inadvertently install any malware or unwanted software.
26. Download drivers from trusted locations only. Only download drivers from trusted sources to ensure that you're not inadvertently downloading malware or other malicious software.

How to Reduce Expenses

Reducing expenses is a critical component of responsible financial planning. While it may be challenging to fully control our expenses, taking a few select steps and making smart choices can help reduce them. In this article, we will take a look at ways to trim expenses, without needing to make significant sacrifices.

1. Work out what you're spending money on now: 

The first step to reducing your expenses is to figure out how much you spend. You should identify all your sources of income and track your spending for at least a month. Once you have a clear idea of where your money is going, you can work on ways to reduce your costs.

2. Determine where you spend your money: 

It is essential to determine where your money is being spent. Sorting your expenses into categories like utilities, food, entertainment, and clothing will make it easier to determine where to make cuts.

3. Immediately remove unnecessary routine purchases: 

Eliminating routine purchases that are not required will bring about significant savings quickly. This could include buying coffee, eating out regularly, or purchasing snacks during the day.

4. Address your utilities:

You should assess your utility bills to see if you can save money with more efficient options. Swapping to solar lighting and implementing eco-friendly measures around your household can result in significant savings.

5. Reconsider gasoline and miscellaneous auto costs:

The cost of maintaining an automobile is often a significant expense, so it's crucial to find practical ways to reduce these costs. Checking the tire pressure regularly can increase fuel efficiency and lower your gasoline expenses. Also, swapping to a more economical car could save you money.

6. Cut down on entertainment:

Entertainment expenses can add up quickly, so it's important to cut costs here. You don't have to sacrifice having a good time, but instead of going to the cinema, you could consider a movie night at home or borrow books and DVDs from your local library or a friend.

7. Make the most of your clothes and other fashion accessories rather than buying more unnecessarily:

It's common to buy more clothing than we need. Buying classic, timeless pieces and statement accessories can help save you money in the long run.

8. Consider taking your lunch to work instead of buying lunch each day:

Eating out every day can cost hundreds of dollars each month. Making a packed lunch saves money and provides healthier food options.

9. Use coupons whenever possible:

Coupons can help save a significant amount of money on items you would regularly purchase. Check out local stores or online websites for discounts and deals available.

10. Look into joining a warehouse club:

Purchasing in bulk can be an option for those in larger households or for those who require more products. Warehouse stores often offer discounts, so make sure to conduct research on which club works for you.

11. Actively manage your credit:

Late fees and interest rates on credit cards can add up over time, so it's essential to manage your debts and avoid overdue payments.

12. Avoid the overdraft on debit cards:

Overdraft fees can be expensive, and it's essential to keep track of your funds to avoid them.

13. Avoid excessive housing expenses:

Housing costs can be the most significant expense for many people. Downsizing or moving to a less expensive location may be an option to reduce housing expenditure.

In conclusion, reducing expenses requires a shift in mindset and a willingness to make changes in our habits. The important thing is to identify your expenses, determine where savings can be made, and implement small changes that will lead to significant savings in the long run.

How to Steal the Blinds

If you're a beginner to poker, stealing the blinds may seem like a daunting task. However, it's an important skill to have in your arsenal, as it can help you accumulate chips and win more pots. In this article, we'll discuss some tips and strategies you can use to successfully steal the blinds and increase your winnings.

1. Start at a full table
If you're a beginner, it's best to start at a full table. This is because you'll have more time to make decisions and won't be overrun by more experienced players. As you gain more experience, you can transition to playing at tables with fewer players.

2. Play only your good hands
When you're in the blinds or button and the player before you raises, it's best to play only your good hands. This means hands like Aces, Kings, Queens, and Jacks, as well as suited connectors and high-value suited cards.

3. Practice playing heads-up poker
To improve your ability to steal the blinds, it's helpful to practice playing heads-up poker. You can do this by playing in a play money game or computer game. This will help you develop your skills and strategies without risking any real money.

4. Return to your full ring game after playing heads-up
After playing a few thousand games on the computer and in play money games, return to your full ring game. You'll be better equipped to steal the blinds and win more pots.

5. Notice the playing style of other players
When playing poker, don't just focus on your own cards. Notice the playing style of the other players at the table. This can help you determine when and how to steal the blinds.

6. Raise to steal from the small blind
When you're in the small blind, it's often easier to steal the big blinds' money because you're only playing against one opponent. This makes it easier to get them to fold and take the blinds.

7. Steal with better hands from the button or cutoff
From the button or cutoff, it's best to steal with better hands than from the small blind. This is because you'll be playing against more opponents, making it harder to win the pot.

8. Be aware of the ratio of your stealing raise to the amount in the pot
When making a stealing raise, be aware of the ratio of your raise to the amount already in the pot. You don't want to risk too much of your own chips to try and steal the blinds.

9. Have a plan when the player before you is attempting a steal
If the player before you is attempting a steal, have a plan based on your read on that player's style. You may want to re-raise, call, or fold, depending on your own hand and the other player's style.

10. See the flop at little cost and merely call if your opponents after you are passive
If your opponents after you are passive, it may be worth seeing the flop at little cost. This can help you gain more information about their hand, which can be helpful in making your own decisions.

11. Don't steal if your opponent after you is loose in a ring game
If your opponent after you is loose, it's best not to attempt to steal the blinds. This is because they're more likely to call and win the pot, making it a risky move.

12. In a no-limit tournament, don't steal if the proper strategy is to go all-in
In a no-limit tournament, you may need to go all-in to win the pot. In this case, it's not recommended to attempt to steal the blinds.

13. In no-limit sit n go, don't steal if your opponent has a big stack
In no-limit sit n go, it's generally not recommended to attempt to steal the blinds if your opponent has a big stack. However, if the big stack is complacent, you can steal and keep stealing with small raises.

By following these tips and strategies, you'll be better equipped to steal the blinds and increase your winnings in poker. Happy playing!

When it comes to catching a student cheating on a written test, prevention is always better than cure. Teachers and educators should take proactive measures to prevent cheating, such as reminding students of the rules and penalties for cheating. However, if a teacher suspects that a student has cheated on a test, there are a few steps they can take to confirm their suspicions.

1. Separate the students or seat them in such a way that they cannot easily look onto one another's papers. This will minimize the opportunity for cheating.

2. Watch out for students who are glancing at their lap, their pencil case, or another potential hiding place. This is a common tactic used by students who are trying to cheat.

3. Maintain complete silence in the exam so whispering can be easily detected. This will make it easier to identify any students who are either giving or receiving help.

4. If the student wasn't paying attention during class and you had to call their name, they were probably cheating. Students who cheat often lack confidence in their knowledge and become distracted easily.

5. If the student acts abnormally when you award them a pass, they might have been copying someone else's paper. This could include overreacting or being excessively happy.

6. Always let students practice before a test so they can get the idea of what they are doing. This will help them understand what is expected of them during a test.

7. If you are given a paper or project that seems beyond a student's usual ability, a quick oral test will usually determine if they know the information or if they were cheating.

Concrete is an essential component in many building projects and can provide robust, sturdy foundations, but pouring large spans of concrete can be a challenging and time-consuming task. However, with the right tools, techniques, and preparation, you can finish a large span of concrete to fit with a handsaw. This wikiHow article will guide you through the necessary steps to ensure your finished product is of the highest quality.

1. Determine the width you are able to place and screed off in a single pass.
Before you begin pouring, it is essential to establish the width of the concrete you are comfortable placing and screeding off in a single pass. This will help ensure that the distance covered is consistent and minimize the chances of ending up with uneven concrete. 

2. Set a "floating form" or a "pipe screed" along the length of the pour.
Setting a floating form or a pipe screed along the length of the pour will provide a straight line along which you can screed. This will help you achieve a level and even surface throughout the whole span.

3. Leave a "lane" in your slab area to back the concrete truck so that the discharge chute will be able to swing sufficiently to place the concrete near the screed board as you work down the form.
Creating a lane in your slab area where the concrete truck can back up will help you position the concrete chute correctly. This will make it easier to pour and smooth out the concrete as you work down the form.

4. Place 3⁄4 inch (1.9 cm) plywood or 2x12 lumber along the path spaced for the concrete truck wheels to travel on if the subgrade is not packed sufficiently to support this heavy load without creating ruts, or damaging reinforcing bars or wire.
If your subgrade is not paved securely enough to support the weight of the concrete truck without being damaged or creating ruts, you will need to use 3⁄4 inch (1.9 cm) plywood or 2x12 lumber to create a secure path for the wheels.

5. Lay out any control joints along the outside forms and the intermediate floating forms.
Control joints will allow the concrete to contract and expand as it dries, helping to prevent cracks and other unwanted marks. Be sure to lay them out along the outside forms and the intermediate floating forms.

6. Install any reinforcing and/or moisture barrier.
Reinforcing and/or moisture barriers will provide additional strength and help prevent moisture from seeping through the concrete. Make sure to install them before pouring the concrete.

7. Figure the concrete.
Calculate the amount of concrete you will need for your project to avoid any additional trips to purchase more material.

8. Get your help together.
Enlist the help of skilled individuals, including a reliable concrete driver and other skilled people to assist you during the pouring process.

9. Check the weather forecast for the day you plan your concrete placement.
Make sure the weather is suitable for a concrete pour as high humidity, rain, or excessive sun can alter the drying process.

10. Gather up necessary tools.
Make sure to have all the necessary tools required for pouring and finishing the concrete, such as shovels, rakes, and screeds.

11. Order your concrete.
Call in your order ahead of time to ensure the delivery arrives on schedule.

12. Back your concrete truck down the path you have prepared, or down the outside of the forms if the width allows.
Have the concrete truck come down the prepared lane, so it can be delivered nearest to the screed board to minimize your work.

13. Check the "slump" of your concrete.
The "slump" of the concrete, or how much it settles, may impact the amount required for the pour, how much you will need to pull the screed, and how long it will take to dry.

14. Begin placing your slab at the farthest, or back side.
Start at the farthest side of your project, working backward to ensure the oldest and driest concrete is toward the finish line so that there is no delay with the drying schedule.

15. Pull the screed.
Use the screed to level and smooth out the surface of the concrete. This ensures that the surface is even, and will prevent water accumulation.

16. Rake the "high" concrete down in front of the screed board.
Make sure the screed board remains level as you push any high spots down the board.

17. Cut any joints using the screed board as a straight edge as you work past them.
Cut any expansion or control joints (depending on what is called for) in the concrete, allowing the moisture to work through appropriately.

18. Back the truck back down the slab on the next section of your placement.
After the concrete is poured and screeded, make sure the concrete truck is positioned for the next section requiring concrete.

19. Begin placing concrete again at the "far" end of the pour.
Start pouring the next section of the project at the opposite end from where you started to keep the oldest and driest concrete closer to your planned finish.

20. Bull float the concrete before it begins to set.
After the concrete has been screeded, use the float to smooth over and blend the concrete surface, working quickly before the concrete begins to set.

21. Work the edges of your slab with an edger, and clean up the joints and any "cat faces" (rough spots) with your magnesium float by working off of knee boards when the concrete will support your weight.
Use an edger to give the concrete a professional-looking, curved edge. Then, finish the slab by using a magnesium float to smoothen over any rough spots.

22. Finish the slab by either dragging a wide, soft bristled push broom across it, or trowel with the power trowel.
Either use a push broom to brush a distinctive texture onto the slab or use a power trowel to give it a smooth and polished finish.

23. Cure the concrete with plastic sheeting if the temperature range and humidity require it.
Cover the concrete with plastic sheeting to ensure that it dries well before removing any tape and plastic, which could remove the finish.

24. Clean up your tools, find a recliner, and hope the Tylenol will help you out of bed the next day.
Clean all concrete tools after each use, relax, and take the Tylenol before you head to bed, to ease any aches and pains after a long day of pouring and finishing concrete.

Flying a Remote Control Plane can be a thrilling experience if done correctly. It's a great way to enjoy the outdoors and hone your piloting skills. In this guide, we will go through the steps needed to fly a remote control plane effectively.

Step 1: Decide on ready-built versus build-your-own.
The first step is to decide whether to buy a ready-built remote-control plane or to build your own. Ready-built planes are convenient and easier to get started with, but building your own plane allows you to customize and more thoroughly understand the mechanics of the craft.

Step 2: Buy a remote control plane.
If you decide to buy a ready-built plane, choose one that fits your skill level and interests. Consider the type of flying you want to do, the size of the plane, and the type of power, either gas or electric.

Step 3: Build the plane (if assembly is required).
If you decide to build your remote-control plane, follow the manufacturer's instructions carefully. Make sure to secure and glue all parts correctly.

Step 4: Pre-flight the plane.
Before flying, check for any defects or damage to the plane. Ensure that all of the electronics are functioning correctly.

Step 5: Check which control stick operates which surfaces.
Once you are ready to fly, familiarize yourself with the controller's layout and the function of each control stick. Test each stick to ensure that it is functioning correctly.

Step 6: Do a range check with the antenna on the transmitter collapsed.
To check the range of your remote-control plane, collapse the antenna on the transmitter and walk 50-100 feet away from the plane. Check if your control surfaces still respond without chattering or unwanted movements.

Step 7: Determine approximate wind speed by tying a ribbon to the end of the antenna of the remote and holding the controller parallel to the ground.
You can use a ribbon tied to the antenna of the remote to help determine the wind speed. Hold the controller parallel to the ground and observe how the ribbon moves.

Step 8: Determine wind direction by throwing some grass clippings or other light material into the air.
To determine the wind direction, throw some grass clippings or light material into the air and observe which way the wind is blowing.

Step 9: Slowly advance the power on your aircraft and wait for it to gain sufficient speed on the ground.
When you are ready to take off, slowly push the throttle forward, and wait for the plane to gain sufficient speed on the ground.

Step 10: Keep the throttle at 100% until the plane reaches a sufficient altitude for the size plane you're flying.
Once the plane gains enough speed, increase the throttle to 100% and wait for it to reach the correct altitude.

Step 11: Use a very light touch.
Use a very light touch when changing the direction or altitude of the plane. Overcontrolling the aircraft can lead to unwanted movements or crashes.

Step 12: Turn to the left or right by moving the appropriate control stick left or right.
Turn the plane to the left or right by moving the appropriate control stick in the same direction.

Step 13: Keep the plane as level as possible; if you raise the nose too much, it may cause a stall.
Keep the plane level. Raising the nose too much can cause a stall and potentially crash the plane.

Step 14: Practice an oval shaped flight pattern, keeping all turns in the same direction.
Practice flying in an oval shape, keeping all turns in the same direction. This pattern is easy to learn and can help you build your piloting skills.

Step 15: Land the airplane by first making note of the wind direction to land into the wind.
To land the plane, first note the direction of the wind and plan to land into the wind.

Step 16: Flare just before the plane comes in contact with the ground by raising the nose at the last second so all three wheels touch at the same time.
Flare the plane just before it touches the ground to allow all three wheels to touch down simultaneously.

In conclusion, flying a remote control plane takes practice and patience. By following these steps, you can become an experienced pilot and enjoy hours of flying fun.

How to Cook With Your Kids: Mini-Pizzas

Cooking with your kids can be a fun way to bond and teach them important life skills. One delicious and easy recipe to try with your little ones is mini-pizzas. With just a few ingredients and minimal prep time, you and your kids can create tasty homemade pizzas in no time.

Here's what you'll need:

- A cookie sheet
- 4 English muffins
- 4 teaspoons salad or olive oil
- 8-ounce can tomato sauce or tomatoes, mashed
- 2 teaspoons dried oregano
- 1 teaspoon dried basil
- 8 slices mozzarella cheese
- 8 teaspoons grated Parmesan cheese
- Any toppings (pepperoni, cooked sausage, raw mushrooms, etc.)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
2. Slice the English muffins in half and place them on a cookie sheet.
3. Brush the tops of each muffin half with olive or salad oil.
4. Spoon tomato sauce or mashed tomatoes onto each muffin half.
5. Sprinkle the oregano and basil on top of each muffin half.
6. Add your choice of toppings on top of the sauce.
7. Place a slice of mozzarella cheese on top of each muffin half.
8. Sprinkle some grated Parmesan cheese on top of each muffin half.
9. Bake for 10-12 minutes or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
10. Let cool for a few minutes before serving.

Enjoy your tasty mini-pizzas with your kids! 

Other fun and easy recipes to try with your kids include Bear Paw Cookies, Early-Bird Cereal, Apple Volcanoes, and Nectar Smoothies. With a little time and patience, cooking with your kids can become a fun and rewarding activity for both you and your little ones.

How to Keep Your Office Warm During Winter Cheaply and Easily

Winter can be a challenging time for offices, as it is important to maintain a comfortable temperature for employees while also keeping costs manageable. Here are some tips on how to keep your office warm during winter cheaply and easily:

1. Use a centralized room heater. This type of heater can be a cheap option for heating up the entire office space, and it can be installed with the help of an electrician. However, remember to prioritize safety and quality when choosing a heater.

2. Maintain the room temperature between 18-21 degrees Celsius. This is the ideal temperature range for a comfortable workspace, according to studies. Make sure to adjust the temperature during the day to save energy when the office is not fully occupied.

3. Cram up the area with furniture. The more furniture you have in the room, the less space there is for cold air to circulate, making heating more effective. However, don't overdo it to avoid clutter.

4. Arrange furniture and computers close to each other. This will create a more insulating atmosphere and prevent cold spots. Be conscious of health and safety regulations when rearranging office furniture.

5. Place large woolen rugs on the floor. This can help insulate the room from the cold and dampness from the floor, making it more comfortable for those who are sitting.

6. Encourage employees to wear warm clothing. If your office has a relaxed dress code, advise your employees to wear thick woolen clothes and shoes during the winter season.

7. Use thick, dark-colored curtains. These curtains can prevent cold drafts from seeping through the windows and help to create a warm atmosphere. Be sure to open them during the day to allow sunlight to warm up the room.

8. Offer hot water during meetings. Providing hot drinks like tea and coffee can help employees stay warm and alert during meetings.

9. Use heavy lighting. Bright lighting can help to create a warmer and more inviting atmosphere. Consider investing in LED lights to reduce energy use.

10. Seal gaps around windows and doors. Use wooden planks to fill in any gaps and prevent drafts from entering the room.

11. Build a fireplace. If your office allows it, consider building a fireplace to create a cozy and welcoming atmosphere. Be sure to follow all safety precautions and check with your landlord before installation.

12. Offer hot drinks and snacks regularly. Keep employees warm and motivated by providing hot drinks and snacks during the day. This can be a simple but effective way of maintaining a comfortable working environment.

13. Keep warm throws on hand. Provide soft woolen throws to employees so they can warm up during breaks. This can also add a cozy touch to the office decor.

By following these tips, you can keep your office warm during the winter season without breaking the bank. Remember to prioritize safety and comfort for your employees, and enjoy a cozy and productive work environment!

Changing a headlight bulb on a Honda C90 Cub 12V might seem daunting, but with the right tools and guidance, it can be done easily and without any hassle. Here's a step-by-step guide on how to change a headlight bulb on a Honda C90 Cub 12V:

1. Take off the fitted windshield/windscreen.
To access the headlight assembly, you need to remove the fitted windshield/windscreen from the front of the bike. Hold each screw in place with a wide flat blade screwdriver, while you undo the 10mm nut on the other side of the bracket.

2. Remove the four 10mm nuts and four washers and put them in a safe place.
Once the nuts and washers are removed, bring the windscreen towards you, guiding it past the indicators and headlight. Then, with some gentle waggling, the lower attachments will come away. Put the windshield fairing to one side where it won't get scratched.

3. Remove both medium-sized cross point screws on each side of the plastic headlight housing.
These screws hold the headlight assembly in place. Remove them and put them in a safe place.

4. Hold the chromed part of the headlight assembly and gently pull towards you.
This will release the assembly from the plastic housing. Look at the back of the curved reflector and you'll see the housings for the two bulbs and their wire connectors.

5. Peel-back the edges of the black rubber gaiter surrounding the headlight connection gently.
This will allow you to remove the headlight bulb.

6. Get your replacement bulb.
Ensure that the replacement bulb is the correct one for your Honda C90 Cub 12V.

7. Look at the circular base plate of the bulb and you will see a 'key' which sticks out beyond the circle.
This key ensures that the bulb is inserted in the proper position.

8. Put the new bulb into the recess.
Be careful not to touch the glass part of the bulb as this can cause damage and shorten its lifespan. Get the rear connector and place it over the base of the bulb and carefully push and twist it into the brass bayonet connection and check that it's properly attached. Ease the rubber gaiter back down over the connection so that it sits flush with the back of the reflector.

9. Put the headlamp assembly back in.
Make sure that the headlamp is the right way up. Hold the headlamp assembly by its chrome surround and guide it back into the plastic headlamp housing.

10. Get the two 'funny looking' cross-head screws.
Look into the screw holes on the side of the headlamp housing and adjust the headlamp assembly's position until you can see the threads in the center of the hole. Put each screw in and do-up finger tight at first to ensure that you don't damage the threads.

11. Tighten the screws with your cross-point screwdriver and check that the headlamp is secure.
Start the bike and run it up so that the voltage is steady. Now, switch your headlight on and check both the dipped beam and full beam to make sure that they work properly.

12. Get the windshield fairing, plus the four sets of attachment screws, washers, and nuts.
Lift the fairing onto the front of the bike and carefully guide the cutaways onto the headlight and indicators. Bring the fairing onto the front attachments while looking into the holes to line it up with the bracket. Do up the four fairing attachments properly by holding each screw in place with a flat-blade screwdriver and tightening the nuts with a 10mm spanner.

Changing a headlight bulb on a Honda C90 Cub 12V is a simple task that can be completed by following these steps. With a little care and attention, you'll be able to complete the job easily and effectively, ensuring that your bike is roadworthy and safe to ride.

Do you want to delete protected system fonts in your Windows 7 operating system?
