How to File Bankruptcy in California

Filing for bankruptcy in California can be a daunting process, but it is a legal option that can help alleviate financial hardship. Before initiating the bankruptcy process, there are several steps to take to hopefully avoid bankruptcy. If, however, you determine that filing for bankruptcy is your best option, there are several key steps to take to properly file your case. Here's a step-by-step guide on How to File Bankruptcy in California.

Avoid Bankruptcy on Your Own
1. Contact Creditors: Reach out to your creditors as soon as you suspect you may need to file for bankruptcy. Try to negotiate payment plans or settlements with them, which may help you avoid filing.
2. Obtain a Debt Consolidation Loan: Consider applying for a debt consolidation loan, which allows you to combine multiple debts into a single, more manageable payment.
3. Complete a Credit Counseling Plan: All individuals filing for bankruptcy in California are required to complete a credit counseling plan with an approved agency prior to filing.

Get Professional Help
4. Ask for Referrals: Ask friends or family for referrals to a reputable bankruptcy attorney.
5. Use Your State's Bar Website: Look up the recommended attorneys on the State Bar's website to verify that they are in good standing.
6. Conduct Initial Consultations: Schedule consultations with several attorneys to find one who is experienced and who makes you feel comfortable.
7. Ask About Fees: Inquire about fees and payment options so you understand what you will owe.

Understand Your Options
8. Make a Decision: After weighing all your options, make a decision whether to file for Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy.
9. Understand the Course's Purpose: Attend a debtor education course, which is required by the Bankruptcy Court's administration to educate filers on how to better handle finances in the future.
10. Find an Approved Counseling Agency: Look up and schedule a class with an approved counseling agency in your area.
11. Pay Any Required Fee: Be prepared to pay a fee for the class.
12. Complete the Counseling: Complete the counseling and obtain your certificate.

Qualify for Chapter 7
13. Look at Your Options: Determine whether you are eligible for Chapter 7 bankruptcy based on your income.
14. Determine if You Have to Take the Means Test: Take the Means Test to determine if your income qualifies for Chapter 7.
15. Consider the Debts That Will Be Discharged: Understand which debts Chapter 7 bankruptcy will discharge.

Select Chapter 13
16. Understand That Some Debts Are Excepted from Discharge: Know that some debts that cannot be discharged in Chapter 7 can be reorganized and repaid in Chapter 13 bankruptcy.
17. Protect Certain Assets from Creditors: Use Chapter 13 bankruptcy to protect certain assets such as homes or cars from creditors.
18. Obtain the Required Documents: Collect all the documents required for bankruptcy filing.
19. Gather Paperwork: Gather all the paperwork including income tax returns, bank statements, pay stubs, and bills.
20. Fill Out All Required Chapter 7 Documents: Fill out and file all forms required for Chapter 7 bankruptcy.
21. Fill Out All Required Chapter 13 Documents: Fill out and file all forms required for Chapter 13 bankruptcy.
22. File Your Documents with the Correct Court: File your documents with the correct court and pay the required fees.
23. Wait for the Automatic Stay to Go into Effect: After filing for bankruptcy, the automatic stay will go into effect, halting all collection efforts and lawsuits against you.
24. Have a Trustee Appointed: A trustee will be appointed to handle your case.
25. Meet with Creditors: Attend a meeting of creditors.
26. Respond to Any Challenges: Respond to any challenges and complaints filed in your case.
27. Attend Hearings: Attend all required hearings.
28. Complete a Financial Management Instructional Course: Complete a financial management instructional course before receiving a discharge. 

Filing for bankruptcy can be a difficult process, but with the right help and guidance, it is possible to obtain relief from your financial hardships. Be sure to consult with a qualified attorney who can guide you through the process and ensure that you make the best decisions for your financial future.

How to Make up After an Argument

Arguments are a natural part of any relationship. Regardless of the severity or the frequency, what’s important is how we handle them. By implementing the right strategies, it’s possible to make up after an argument and strengthen your bond with the other person. Here are the steps to make up after an argument:

1. Apologize immediately if possible.

If you realize you’ve made a mistake, it’s best to apologize right away. This shows the other person that you regret your actions and that you value the relationship. Be sure to apologize sincerely and take responsibility for your actions.

2. Wait until you are calm before making up.

If you’re feeling angry or emotional, it might be best to wait until you’ve calmed down before trying to make up. This will help you approach the situation with a clear head and avoid saying things you don’t mean.

3. Manage your impulses.

When emotions run high, it can be difficult to control our impulses. However, it’s important to keep in mind that lashing out or making accusations will only make the situation worse. Instead, take a deep breath and focus on calming down before trying to make amends.

4. Separate your feelings from the issue.

It’s important to distinguish between your feelings and the issue at hand. By separating the two, you can focus on resolving the problem rather than getting caught up in your emotions.

5. Avoid discounting the other person’s feelings.

Just because you don’t agree with someone’s perspective doesn’t mean their feelings aren’t valid. Make an effort to understand where the other person is coming from, even if you don’t necessarily agree with them.

6. Avoid mind-reading.

Assuming you know what someone else is thinking or feeling can lead to misunderstandings. Instead, ask the other person to express their thoughts and feelings in their own words.

7. Write down your feelings.

Putting your thoughts and feelings down on paper can help you get a clearer perspective on the situation. Writing can also help you organize your thoughts and express them more effectively.

8. Choose your moment wisely.

Timing is everything when it comes to making up after an argument. Choose a time when both of you are calm and can focus on the issue at hand.

9. Arrange to meet with them in person, if possible.

While it’s possible to make up over the phone or online, meeting with someone in person can help you communicate more effectively and resolve the issue more quickly.

10. Frame your invitation as an offer, not a demand.

Instead of demanding that the other person meet with you, frame your invitation as an offer. This will make them more likely to accept and help create a positive atmosphere.

11. Give the other person space to talk.

Letting the other person express their thoughts and feelings can help you understand where they’re coming from and find a resolution to the problem.

12. Listen to what the other person has to say.

Active listening is key to any effective communication. Make sure you’re focused on what the other person is saying and avoid interrupting or tuning out.

13. Verbalize your understanding of the other person’s feelings.

Repeating what the other person has said in your own words can help them feel heard and understood.

14. Remember the “Three R’s”.

When making up after an argument, it’s important to remember the “Three R’s”: recognize, regret, and resolve. Recognize and acknowledge the other person’s feelings, express regret for your actions, and work together to resolve the issue.

15. Express empathy for the other person.

Putting yourself in the other person’s shoes can help you understand their perspective and create a more positive atmosphere for making up.

16. Use “I” instead of “You.” Keep the focus on what you did and how you felt, rather than making accusations about the other person.

By using “I” statements, you can take responsibility for your actions and avoid making the other person feel defensive.

17. Don’t just say “I’m sorry”.

While saying “I’m sorry” is a good start, it’s important to follow up with actions that show you’re committed to making amends.

18. Avoid the “but”.

Using the word “but” can feel like an excuse for your actions and negate the apology.

19. Don’t stand your ground.

Standing your ground and refusing to acknowledge the other person’s feelings will only prolong the argument and create more tension.

20. Talk about the future.

After resolving the issue, it’s important to talk about the future and how you can work together to prevent similar conflicts from happening again.

21. Avoid making promises you can’t keep.

If you promise to change something, make sure it’s something you can realistically follow through on.

22. Suggest a pleasant activity to do together.

Doing something enjoyable together can help reinforce the relationship and create positive memories.

23. Talk about what caused the argument.

Understanding what caused the argument can help prevent similar conflicts from happening again in the future.

24. Prioritize communication.

Effective communication is key to any healthy relationship. Make an effort to communicate openly and honestly with the other person.

25. Check in with the other person.

After making up, it’s important to check in with the other person and make sure they’re feeling okay.

26. Understand that a certain degree of conflict is normal.

No relationship is without conflict. Understanding that disagreements are a natural part of any relationship can help you approach them with a more positive attitude.

If you find yourself in the unfortunate circumstance of needing to jump-start a dead car battery, it can be daunting to know where to start. Thankfully, with the right tools and knowledge, it is possible to safely and effectively charge a dead car battery. Follow these steps to learn how to charge a dead car battery.

Part 1: Preparation

1. Open the hood or compartment on each vehicle in which the batteries are located. It's important to ensure that the batteries are in close enough proximity to connect the cables between them. 

2. Take note of the positive and negative terminals on each battery. This is important as you will need to know which cables to connect to each terminal.

3. Locate a set of jumper cables. These cables are typically black and red and can be found at most automotive stores or online.

Part 2: Connecting the Jumper Cables

1. Connect each end of the positive jumper cable to the positive terminals on each car battery. The positive terminal is typically marked with a plus (+) sign.

2. Connect one end of the negative jumper cable to the negative terminal on the functional, charged battery. The negative terminal is typically marked with a minus (-) sign.

3. Attach the other end of the negative jumper cable to a grounded metal component of the car that contains the dead battery. This could be a bolt or screw in the engine compartment.

Part 3: Charging the Dead Battery

1. Start the engine of the car with the charged battery. Allow it to run for at least five minutes before attempting to start the other car. 

2. Try to start the engine of the car that contains the dead battery. If it doesn't start after a few tries, turn off both engines and double check that the cables are connected correctly.

3. Disconnect and remove the jumper cables from each car after the engine has started in the reverse order in which you connected them. This means removing the negative cable from the dead battery first, followed by the negative cable from the charged battery. Then remove the positive cable from the charged battery, followed by the positive cable from the dead battery.

4. Allow the car which had the dead battery to continue running for at least another five minutes. This will help the battery recharge slightly and regain its strength.

5. Drive the jump-started car for at least 20 minutes or allow it to idle for the same amount of time. This will help the battery fully recharge and regain its strength.

In the event that the dead battery cannot be jump started, it may be necessary to replace the battery altogether. Always take the necessary precautions and follow this guide carefully to safely jump start a dead car battery.

Are you in need of a cute and functional drawstring backpack? Look no further! With just a few materials and some basic sewing skills, you can create a personalized drawstring backpack that's perfect for school, work, or any adventure. Follow these easy steps to make your own drawstring backpack:

Part 1: Obtain Needed Materials

Before you can start sewing your backpack, you'll need to gather the necessary materials. Here's what you'll need:

- Two rectangular pieces of fabric (size depends on how large you want your backpack to be)
- Fabric scissors
- A narrow strip of fabric for the attachment loop (around 3 inches wide and 12 inches long)
- Sewing machine or needle and thread
- Rope or cord for the drawstring (around 60 inches long per rope)
- Pins

Part 2: Cut Two Rectangles

Using your fabric scissors, cut two rectangles of your chosen fabric to the desired size for your backpack. Make sure they are the same size and shape.

Part 3: Fold the Cloth Rectangle

On one of the rectangles, fold each of the shorter ends inwards towards the center by about 1/2 an inch (1.3 cm), then iron them down to create creases. This will form the top edge of the backpack opening.

Part 4: Cut a Strip of the Outer Material

Cut a 3 inch (7.6 cm) wide and 12 inch (30.5 cm) long strip of the outer material. This will be used to make the attachment loops for the drawstring.

Part 5: Fold and Iron the Long Edges of the Narrow Strip to the Center

Fold and iron the long edges of the narrow strip to the center.

Part 6: Fold the Strip Again and Top Stitch It

Fold the strip again and top stitch it. This will create the attachment loops for the drawstring.

Part 7: Cut the Folded Top Stitched Strip into Two 6 Inch Long Pieces

Cut the folded top stitched strip into two 6 inch (15.2 cm) long pieces. These will be used for the attachment loops of the drawstring.

Part 8: Pin the Attachment Loop Strips to the Outer Shell

Unfold the main bag pieces and pin the attachment loop strips to the outer shell on each side by the center mark, on the "right" side of the material. Make sure they are evenly spaced and staying flat against the material.

Part 9: Re-Fold the Fabric and Stitch the Side Seams

Re-fold the fabric so that the "right" sides are together, then stitch the side seams. Carefully sew several seams over the "raw" ends of the loops you have formed.

Part 10: Sew the Optional Lining Material Together

If you want a lining for your backpack, sew the (optional) lining material together, "right" sides facing, along the long sides to form a long tube.

Part 11: Place the Lining Tube Inside the Outer Shell

Place the lining tube inside the outer shell with "right" sides of both fabrics facing each other, and sew around the top edge to attach the lining tube to the outer shell.

Part 12: Turn the Outer Shell "Right" Side Out

Turn the outer shell "right" side out. You should now see the lining peeking out from beneath the top edge of the backpack.

Part 13: Turn the Remaining Raw Edge of the Liner Over on Itself

Turn the remaining raw edge of the liner over on itself to hide the raw edges, and stitch it closed. This will prevent any raw edges from being visible on the inside of your backpack.

Part 14: Tuck the Liner Back Down into the Bag

Tuck the liner back down into the bag, so that it is sandwiched between the exterior shell and the drawstring casing.

Part 15: Cut Two Lengths of Rope

Cut two lengths of rope approximately 60 inches (152.4 cm) each (for adults), and fold them so that you can hold two strands of it at the top of the bag.

Part 16: Pin the Top Edge of the Bag Flat

Pin the top edge of the bag flat so that the liner does not show. Then, measure the rope from the top edge of the bag, adding two rope widths and a quarter inch. Mark this measurement on the top edge of the bag to create your drawstring casing.

Part 17: Sew a Seam at the Mark

Sew a seam at the mark, all the way around the top of the bag to form your rope tunnel for closure.

Part 18: Open the Side Seams of the Bag Over the Rope Tunnel

Open the side seams of the bag over the rope tunnel, creating two holes for the drawstring to pass through.

Part 19: Use These Holes to Pass the Rope Through

Use these holes to pass the rope through from each end, so that you end up with two "U" shapes with strings pulling from opposite sides of the bag.

Part 20: Pass One Rope End from Each Side Through the Corresponding Sewn Loop

Pass one rope end from each side through the corresponding sewn loop at the bottom of the bag. Then, tie the rope ends together.

Part 21: Test Fit and Cut off Excess Rope Ends

Test the fit of your new drawstring backpack. If there are any excess rope ends, cut them off and seal them with either glue or heat. And there you have it - your very own personalized drawstring backpack!

Mounting your horse without a saddle or block can be a daunting task, but with practice and patience, it can be done successfully. The first step in this process is to sack out your horse, getting them used to the idea of you jumping on them. Here’s how to do it:

1. Sack out your horse. Approach your horse with a soft, plush object, and allow your horse to smell it. Rub it on your horse’s body, starting with their shoulder and working down their neck and back. This will help your horse get used to the object and any movements you might make.

2. Practice mounting. Have somebody hold your horse while you practice mounting. Remember to start on the left side, with your right foot back and your left foot near your horse’s left front leg by its hoof. Take a liberal amount of mane along with the reins so that you don't lose control if your horse moves while you are mounting. 

3. Use momentum. When you’re ready to mount, place all your weight on your right leg and use your momentum to swing your right leg and arm over your horse’s back. Use the mane and reins to help keep yourself steady.

4. Try again. If you don’t succeed on the first attempt, don’t worry about it. Relax, slide off and pet your horse for standing still and letting you try to mount. Another great option is to practice mounting on a mounting block or with a saddle, then move on to trying without. With practice, and time, you will be able to do it!

Remember to always be patient and take your time while sacking your horse out and practicing mounting without a saddle or block. If you’re uncomfortable or feel unsafe at any point, stop and try again later. With perseverance and practice, you’ll be able to mount your horse confidently without a saddle or block.

If you're feeling under the weather, you may be experiencing a fever. While a fever is a natural response to infection or illness, it can be uncomfortable and cause additional symptoms like chills, body aches, and fatigue. Fortunately, there are several steps you can take to get rid of a fever fast. Here's how:

1. Use over-the-counter medication for fevers caused by colds and flu.
Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help reduce fever and relieve other symptoms like pain and headaches.

2. Try taking a bath in lukewarm water. 
Taking a bath in lukewarm water can help bring down a fever and make you feel more comfortable. Make sure not to use cold water, as this can cause shivering and worsen the fever.

3. Drink water. 
Staying hydrated is essential when you have a fever. Drink plenty of water, and avoid caffeine and alcohol, as these can dehydrate you.

4. Take supplements to boost immune health. 
Supplements like vitamin C, zinc, and echinacea can help boost your immune system's response and help fight off the cause of the fever.

5. Administer "wet socks treatment" at home. 
This treatment involves wearing wet socks to bed, which can help improve circulation and stimulate the immune system.

6. Cool children's bodies if necessary. 
If your child has a fever, you can help bring it down by removing layers of clothing, giving them a lukewarm bath, and offering them plenty of fluids.

7. Stay as comfortable as possible. 
Resting, keeping cool, and wearing loose clothing can all help make you more comfortable while battling a fever.

8. Hydrate and eat mild foods to recover from gastrointestinal (GI) infection. 
If your fever is caused by a GI infection, it's crucial to stay hydrated and eat mild, easy-to-digest foods like plain crackers and toast.

9. Consume herbs known to fight fever. 
Herbs like ginger, garlic, and turmeric are all known for their immune-boosting and fever-fighting properties.

10. Take care not to spread infection. 
If you have a fever, take steps to prevent the spread of infection, like covering your mouth and nose while coughing and sneezing.

11. Keep a temperature log. 
If your fever doesn't resolve on its own, keeping a temperature log can help your doctor better understand your symptoms and determine the best treatment plan.

12. Seek medical advice. 
If your fever is high or accompanied by severe symptoms, it's important to seek medical advice.

13. Follow your doctor's instructions for viral infections. 
If your fever is caused by a viral infection, your doctor may recommend rest, fluids, and pain relievers.

14. Take antibiotics for bacterial infections. 
If your fever is caused by a bacterial infection, your doctor may prescribe antibiotics to help clear the infection.

15. Talk to your doctor about other causes of fever. 
If your fever persists or is accompanied by other symptoms like rash or joint pain, talk to your doctor about other potential causes.

16. Use a digital thermometer to take your temperature orally. 
Taking your temperature orally with a digital thermometer is a quick and easy way to monitor your fever.

17. Take your temperature in the armpit. 
If taking your temperature orally is difficult or uncomfortable, you can also take it in the armpit.

18. Decide which measurement method to use on a child. 
Oral, armpit, or rectal measurements are all options for taking a child's temperature. Talk to your doctor about which method is best for your child's age and symptoms.

19. Take the child’s temperature rectally with a digital thermometer. 
If taking your child's temperature rectally, be sure to sterilize the thermometer tip with rubbing alcohol first.

20. Interpret the results. 
Fever is generally defined as a temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher.

21. Get vaccinated. 
Vaccines can help prevent certain illnesses that can cause fever.

22. Get enough sleep every day. 
Getting enough sleep is essential for a healthy immune system and can help lower your risk of getting sick.

23. Eat a healthy diet. 
Eating a balanced, nutritious diet can help your body fight off infections and illnesses.

24. Avoid contact with germs. 
Taking steps to avoid contact with germs can help reduce your risk of getting sick.

25. Reduce your stress levels. 
Stress can weaken your immune system's response, so finding ways to reduce stress is crucial for overall health and wellness.

By following these tips, you can help get rid of a fever fast and get back to feeling your best.

How to Survive a Severe Weather Outbreak

Severe weather can strike at any time, and it's important to be prepared for whatever Mother Nature throws your way. From tornadoes to heavy rainstorms, severe weather outbreaks can pose a serious threat to your safety. In this wikiHow article, we will walk you through important steps to follow in order to stay safe during a severe weather outbreak.

Stay tuned.

The first step in staying safe during a severe weather outbreak is to stay tuned to your local news and weather reports. Listen to updates about any watch or warning that may be issued in your area. These reports will give you time to prepare for the incoming weather, so you need to pay close attention.

Get prepared.

Besides staying tuned to the weather reports, you need to prepare your home and family for severe weather. Inspect your home for any potential hazards that could be dangerous during a storm. Make sure to have an emergency kit with water, non-perishable food, a first aid kit, and flashlights in case of power outage.

Before we get started in the rest of the planning, it's important to know what a tornado watch, tornado warning, severe thunderstorm watch, and a severe thunderstorm warning means.

It's important to know the difference between these terms. A tornado or severe thunderstorm watch means that weather conditions are favorable for severe weather. A tornado or severe thunderstorm warning means that severe weather is imminent, and you need to take shelter immediately.

Is everyone home?

If possible, make sure that everyone in your family is at home and accounted for before severe weather hits. It's essential to create a plan, so everyone knows what to do in case of severe weather.

Make sure everything is working.

Check your emergency equipment such as generators, weather radios, and flashlights. Make sure that your cell phone is fully charged and have a backup power source. Having multiple sources of communication is vital during severe weather.

Do not go outside.

Never leave your home during a severe weather outbreak unless it's necessary. If you must go outside, take shelter in a sturdy building and stay away from windows.

Stay calm.

Staying calm is key during a severe weather outbreak. Panic can cloud your judgment and make you more vulnerable to danger. Take deep breaths and try to remain calm as you make your decisions.

Make sure the storm in your area is over, But exercise caution.

After the storm has passed, do not be too quick to assume that the danger has completely dissipated. Be cautious and wait for all clear alerts. Organize a clear-up plan to get everything back in order.

Access the local resources for help.

If you need help or assistance during a severe weather outbreak, make sure to contact local emergency services. They are equipped to help you during an emergency.

Rebuild with the future in mind.

If your home or property is damaged during severe weather, rebuild with the future in mind. You can consider adding a shelter or reinforced structural elements to your home to make it sturdier in the future.

Look into counseling if you were traumatized by the storm.

A severe weather outbreak can be traumatizing for many individuals. If you find that you are struggling to feel safe or overcome anxiety after a storm, consider reaching out to a mental health professional for counseling.

If you made that mistake of leaving without checking the forecast and find yourself in the midst of a forming tornado, don't rush to an overpass.

An overpass may seem like a safe spot to wait out a tornado, but it's not. The wind speeds underneath the overpass can actually increase the danger.

If you get caught in a heavy rainstorm, pay undivided attention to the road, and turn on your emergency blinkers.

Heavy rainstorms can be dangerous to drive in, with decreased visibility and slippery roads. Turn on your emergency blinkers to alert other cars on the road of your presence.

Learn the sound of the sirens of the nearby towns you're traveling in/by, it could save your life!

Sirens are a warning sign that severe weather is about to happen. Learn the sound of the sirens in nearby towns so that you can recognize them in case of an emergency.

Depending on the circumstances of your situation, you may want to head back unless the same threat is at your home.

If you are traveling during a severe weather outbreak, it's important to assess your options. Consider heading back home if it's safe to do so.

Keep in mind that not all severe weather counts as tornadoes and hail.

Hailstorms, lightning storms, and other severe weather can be just as dangerous as tornadoes. Make sure you take every severe weather outbreak seriously.

Understand that winter weather outbreaks usually consist of blizzards and avalanches.

Winter weather outbreaks can be just as dangerous as summer weather outbreaks. Learn how to protect yourself during blizzards and avalanches.

Keep in mind that a drought, or a long period of dryness, is still equally dangerous.

A drought can lead to wildfires. Make sure that you are prepared with an evacuation plan if a wildfire strikes your area.

Learn how to escape from a sinking car.

You never know when a severe weather outbreak will leave you stranded in your car. Learn how to escape from a sinking car to protect yourself and your loved ones.

Know how to survive a wildfire.

Wildfires can be unpredictable and fast-moving. Learn how to protect yourself from wildfires, including evacuation procedures.

In Conclusion

A severe weather outbreak can pose a serious threat to your safety. But by staying tuned, getting prepared, and making smart decisions during a storm, you can keep yourself and your loved ones safe. Remember to stay calm, access resources for help, and always be prepared for the unexpected.

How to File a Wrongful Death Claim in California

Losing a loved one is a painful experience. But if your loved one's death was caused by another party's negligence or recklessness, you may have the right to file a wrongful death claim. In California, wrongful death claims can be filed by surviving family members, such as spouses, children, and parents. If you believe that a loved one's death was a result of wrongful conduct, here is how you can file a wrongful death claim in California.

Identify if you can sue.

Not everyone can file a wrongful death lawsuit in California. Only certain family members, such as a spouse, child, or parent, may be eligible to file a wrongful death claim. If you're unsure whether you have the right to file a wrongful death lawsuit, contact an attorney or consult the California Code of Civil Procedure.

Obtain a police report.

If the death was caused by a car accident, a medical error, or another incident that required a police report, obtain a copy of the report. The report may contain vital information about what happened and who was involved.

Collect other information about what happened.

Gather as much information as possible about the circumstances surrounding your loved one's death. This may include medical records, witness statements, and any other evidence that can support your claim.

Gather medical bills.

In California, families may be entitled to recover medical expenses related to their loved one's injury and death. Collect all medical bills related to your loved one's death to include in your claim.

Find financial information about lost wages.

If your loved one was the primary breadwinner, you may be able to recover lost wages. Collect information about his or her income and work history to include in your claim.

Identify other compensation that is available.

Depending on the circumstances of your loved one's death, you may be entitled to additional compensation, such as funeral expenses, loss of companionship, and emotional distress. Identify all sources of compensation to include in your claim.

Avoid delay.

In California, wrongful death claims must be filed within a certain amount of time, known as the statute of limitations. Do not delay in filing your claim, as waiting too long can prevent you from recovering compensation.

Get referrals to personal injury lawyers.

It's important to find a personal injury lawyer with experience handling wrongful death claims in California. Contact your state's bar association or ask friends and family members for recommendations.

Schedule a consultation.

Meet with a personal injury lawyer to discuss the details of your case. During the consultation, be sure to ask about the lawyer's experience with wrongful death claims and what to expect during the legal process.

Ask questions at the consultation.

Be sure to ask any questions you may have about the legal process, fees, and your chances of success.

Talk about a “survival action.”

You may also be able to bring a "survival action" if your loved one survived for even a brief period of time after being injured. A survival action allows you to recover damages that your loved one would have been entitled to if he or she had survived.

Discuss fees.

Personal injury lawyers typically work on a contingency fee basis, which means they only get paid if you win your case. Be sure to discuss the lawyer's fees during your consultation.

Identify who to sue.

Identify the person or company responsible for your loved one's death and include them in your lawsuit.

Provide advance notice if you are suing a healthcare provider.

If you are suing a healthcare provider, you must provide advance notice before filing a lawsuit. Check with a personal injury lawyer to learn more about the notice requirements.

File a complaint.

Your personal injury lawyer will file a complaint with the court outlining the details of your case.

Read the defendant's response.

The defendant will have a certain amount of time to respond to your complaint. Be sure to carefully review the response to understand the defendant's position on the matter.

Engage in fact-finding.

Both sides will engage in fact-finding to discover evidence and build their case.

Assess the need for expert witnesses.

Depending on the facts of your case, you may need to hire expert witnesses to provide testimony.

Oppose any motion for summary judgment.

The defense may attempt to have your case thrown out on summary judgment. If this happens, your personal injury lawyer will oppose the motion and argue that your case should go to trial.

Consider settlement.

Prior to trial, the defendant may offer to settle your case for a certain amount of money. Your personal injury lawyer will help you decide whether to accept the settlement or proceed to trial.

Deal with pretrial motions.

Prior to trial, both sides may file motions to exclude evidence or dismiss certain claims.

Get your evidence in order.

Your personal injury lawyer will help you gather all the evidence you need to present your case at trial.

Pick a jury.

Both sides will select a jury to hear the case.

Deliver opening statements.

Both sides will make opening statements to the jury, outlining their respective positions.

Testify at trial.

You and other witnesses will be called to testify at trial.

Cross-examine the defense witnesses.

Your personal injury lawyer will cross-examine the defense witnesses to challenge their testimony.

Deliver a closing argument.

Both sides will deliver closing arguments to the jury, summarizing their case.

Wait for the verdict.

The jury will deliberate and deliver a verdict.

Think about appealing, if necessary.

If you are not satisfied with the verdict, you may be able to appeal.

Collect on your judgment.

If you win your case, you will be entitled to collect on your judgment. Your personal injury lawyer will help you pursue collection of any awards for damages.

A bilge pump is an essential safety feature for any boat, as it evacuates any excess water from the bilge or casing. In this article, we will outline the steps required to wire a bilge pump correctly. 

Part 1 - Mount the bilge pump securely in the bilge.

1. Choose the location in your boat where you want to install the bilge pump. It should be low enough to collect water but high enough to avoid flooding in heavy seas. 

2. Using brackets or epoxy, attach the bilge pump securely to the bilge floor. This will ensure that it stays in place even in rough water. 

Part 2 - Mount the float switch.

1. Make sure that the float switch is positioned high enough to activate the bilge pump when water levels rise. 

2. Mount the float switch securely, so it does not come loose or float away. 

Part 3 - Connect the pump to the discharge using a hose with a smooth interior.

1. Choose a hose that is the appropriate size and length for your bilge pump. 

2. Place the discharge higher than the waterline to prevent backflow. 

Part 4 - Lead bilge pump wiring up and out of the bilge in a timely manner.

1. Make sure that all wiring is neatly arranged and secured to prevent sagging or contact with bilge water. 

2. Choose adequately sized wiring for the bilge pump and use crimp-on butt connectors between the pump leads and supply wires. 

3. Center the tubing over the butt connectors and apply adequate heat to shrink the tubing. 

Part 5 - Connect the bilge pump directly to the battery.

1. Loop supply wires under the battery's terminal wing nuts, install crimp-on ring terminals followed by a copper washer between the ring terminal and the wing nut. 

2. Install a fuse in the positive wire very close to the battery. If your 3-way switch panel does not come with a fuse, this must be attached using another crimp-on butt connector. 

Part 6 - Wire your float switch to your 3-way switch.

1. Use adequately sized wiring to connect the bilge pump to your 3-way switch. 

2. Follow the instructions on your 3-way switch to wire your float switch correctly. 

By following these steps, you can ensure that your bilge pump is installed correctly and will function correctly, keeping you and your boat safe from excess water.

How to Excel in High School

High school can be a challenging time, but with the right attitude and strategies, you can excel academically and personally. If you're in 7th or 8th grade, it's not too early to start preparing for high school success. Here are some tips to help you make the best grades you possibly can, get involved in extracurriculars, and balance your commitments.

Part 1: Getting Started in 7th and 8th Grade

1. Make the best grades you possibly can in your 7th and 8th grade years. These grades will set the foundation for your academic career and determine which classes you will be eligible to take in high school.

2. Start your extracurriculars now. Join clubs, sports teams, or community groups to start building your interests and skills outside of the classroom.

3. Pick the classes you enroll in carefully. Consider your academic strengths and weaknesses, as well as your future goals, when choosing which classes to take.

4. Obtain the textbooks early, and supplemental ones, too. Being prepared will help you keep up with your coursework.

Part 2: Excelling in High School

1. Always pay attention in class. This will help you absorb the material and ask questions when you need clarification.

2. Do the homework. Completing assignments on time and to the best of your ability is key to academic success.

3. Organize everything. Use a calendar or planner to keep track of deadlines, assignments, and extracurricular activities.

4. Make and maintain a study place. Find a quiet, comfortable place to study and make sure it's stocked with everything you need.

5. Know the syllabus for every class. Understanding the requirements and expectations for each class will help you stay on track.

6. Set high standards for yourself. Strive for excellence and challenge yourself academically.

7. Do a little studying every night. Consistent studying is more effective than cramming before a test.

8. Take good notes. Write down key points, definitions, and important details.

9. Get a tutor. If you're struggling with a subject, a tutor can help you catch up and stay on track.

10. Start studying a few days before a test. Giving yourself enough time to review the material will help you feel more prepared.

11. Avoid pulling an all-nighter to study for a test. Getting enough sleep is essential to academic success.

12. Do some extra credit. Take advantage of opportunities to boost your grades and show your dedication to your studies.

13. Give yourself a study break when you need it. Taking a break can help you recharge and stay focused.

14. Begin working on long-term projects as soon as they are assigned. This will prevent you from feeling overwhelmed and rushed at the last minute.

15. Form a study group with friends. Collaborating with others can help you learn new perspectives and reinforce your knowledge.

16. Study when you have small bits of free time. Use your breaks between classes or on the bus ride home to review your notes.

17. Cram as a last resort. It's better to spread out your studying over time to avoid feeling overwhelmed.

18. Get involved. Find clubs, sports teams, or volunteer opportunities that align with your interests and passions.

19. Get involved in more than one thing. Explore different interests and challenge yourself to try new things.

20. Volunteer. Giving back to your community is not only fulfilling, but it can also show your dedication and leadership skills.

21. If your school doesn't offer an activity, try starting it yourself. Take initiative and create the opportunities you want to see.

22. Prioritize your after-school activities. Balance your academic and extracurricular commitments to avoid feeling overwhelmed.

23. Sleep plenty. Getting enough rest is essential to physical, emotional, and mental health.

24. Eat a good breakfast every day. Fueling your body with healthy food will give you the energy you need to focus and learn.

25. Ask for help when you need it. Whether it's from a teacher, tutor, or friend, don't be afraid to seek assistance.

26. Make time for fun. Balancing your commitments with activities you enjoy will help you stay motivated and happy.

How to Green Your Personal Care

Personal care is something that we all indulge in, on a daily basis. However, the products we use to keep ourselves looking and feeling great, often have adverse effects on our health and the environment. It is essential to understand the problems associated with commercial personal care products and take steps to green your personal care routine. In this article, we will discuss everything you need to know about greening your personal care practices.

1. Take a look at the ingredients of your shampoos, conditioners, moisturizers, hair gels, lipsticks, mascaras, and perfumes.

Many commercial personal care products contain harmful synthetic chemicals that can have adverse effects on our health and the environment. Take a closer look at the ingredients label of the products you use, and try to avoid those that contain harsh chemicals such as parabens, phthalates, and synthetic fragrances.

2. Understand the problems you face when using many everyday commercial personal care products.

Many beauty products are not well regulated, and health and beauty products top advertising breaches (they don’t do what they claim they do). Many use varying mixtures of synthetically produced chemicals, and many of these synthetic chemicals have not been approved by regulation authorities but find their way into products and onto shelves through loopholes in regulations. As much as a third of personal care products contain at least one chemical linked to cancer. Mineral oil and petroleum are the basic ingredients in many cosmetic products – these have their origins in fossil fuels. The meanings of "natural" and "organic" are generally not regulated and can mean whatever the company wants them to mean!

3. Choose organic products.

Organic products are made from natural ingredients and do not contain harmful synthetics. Look for products that are certified organic or natural. These products are generally gentler on the skin and do not contain any harsh chemicals that can harm the environment.

4. Be careful of sunscreen.

Sunscreen is an essential part of personal care, but many commercial varieties contain harmful chemicals that can damage both your skin and the environment. Look for sunscreens that use mineral-based ingredients like zinc oxide or titanium dioxide. These ingredients provide a physical barrier that reflects the sun's harmful rays without harming the environment.

5. Be careful with body lotions, face creams, make-up.

Many commercial face creams, body lotions, and makeup products contain synthetic chemicals that can be absorbed by the skin and harm your health. Look for products made from natural ingredients that do not contain preservatives or synthetic fragrances.

6. Be aware of the ingredients in your deodorants and toothpastes.

Deodorants and toothpaste are products that are applied to your skin and mouth. Look for products that are free from harmful chemicals like SLS (sodium lauryl sulfate), SLES (sodium laureth sulfate), parabens, and synthetic fragrances.

7. Stay aware with hair care.

Hair care products can contain many harmful chemicals that can strip your hair of natural oils and cause damage. Look for shampoos and conditioners that are free from sulfates, parabens, and synthetic fragrances.

8. Keep learning and researching (see links below).

There is always something new to learn about the products we use and their impact on our health and the environment. Keep researching and stay up to date with the latest developments in green personal care.

9. Make your own personal care products.

If you want to ensure that your personal care products are entirely natural, you can try making your own products at home. Many simple recipes are available online that use natural ingredients like coconut oil, shea butter, and essential oils.

In conclusion, greening your personal care routine is essential for both your health and the environment. By making small changes, such as choosing natural and organic products, you can contribute to a greener, healthier world.

A pinhole lens is a simple lens made out of a small hole in a flat surface. Creating a pinhole lens for your SLR camera can be a fun project that enables you to capture unique and creative images. This wikiHow article will guide you through the steps of making a pinhole lens for your SLR camera.

Part 1: Making the Pinhole Lens

1. Find the center of the body cap.

Use a ruler or other measuring tool to measure and mark the center of the body cap with a pencil.

2. Drill a hole measuring approximately 1/4" / 6.35mm.

Use a drill and a drill bit to make a hole in the center of the body cap. The hole should be approximately 1/4" or 6.35mm.

3. Cut a square piece measuring approximately 3/4"x 3/4" / 1.9 centimeter (0.7 in) x 1.9cm (approximately) from the aluminum sheet.

Use a pair of scissors or a craft knife to cut out a square piece of aluminum foil that is approximately 3/4"x 3/4" or 1.9cm x 1.9cm.

4. Make a dimple in the center of the aluminum piece.

Use a toothpick or other pointed object to make a small dimple in the center of the aluminum foil square.

5. Sand the dimple.

Use fine-grit sandpaper to sand down the dimple until a small hole appears in the aluminum.

6. Clean the aluminum piece and the pinhole with rubbing alcohol and blowing through the pinhole.

Use rubbing alcohol and a clean cloth to thoroughly clean the aluminum piece and the pinhole. Then, blow air through the pinhole to remove any debris.

7. Apply adhesive.

Apply a small amount of adhesive to the back of the aluminum piece.

8. Carefully place the aluminum piece into the center backside of the body cap.

Carefully position the aluminum foil with the pinhole over the hole in the body cap. Press down on the aluminum piece to adhere it to the body cap.

9. Tape the aluminum piece in place while the adhesive dries.

Use a small piece of tape to hold the aluminum piece in place while the adhesive dries.

10. After the adhesive dries, carefully remove the tape.

Once the adhesive has dried, remove the tape carefully so you do not disturb the aluminum piece.

11. Cut a very small square piece of tape and cover the pinhole.

Use a small piece of tape to cover the pinhole, ensuring that it is completely sealed.

Part 2: Finishing the Pinhole Lens

1. Mask the body cap.

Use masking tape to cover the sides and the outer front of the body cap.

2. Spray flat black paint over the aluminum piece.

Use flat black spray paint to cover the entire exposed part of the body cap. This will prevent light from entering the camera body through any exposed areas.

3. Remove the small square piece of tape covering the pinhole.

Are you tired of constantly holding your phone while watching a movie or video? Why not make a phone stand out of clay that can hold your phone for you! Follow these simple steps to make your very own clay phone stand.

Part 1: Making the Stand

1. Measure your phone's length and height. This is important as you want to make sure your phone will fit snugly on the stand.

2. Purchase suitable clay. You can use air-dry clay or oven-bake clay, just make sure it is suitable for your intended use.

3. Take about a handful of clay and flatten the sphere. This will form the base of your stand.

4. Mold the sphere into a neat square. Use your fingers to shape the clay until it is a perfect square.

5. Fold the edges up on three sides. This will create a rectangular cradle piece to hold your phone.

6. Take another, more generous handful of clay and flatten the sphere.

7. Hold the rectangle against the base, on the side not folded up. This will allow you to mold the clay around the cradle and provide support.

8. Fold the edges upward around the remaining sides of the rectangular cradle piece. This will create a stable structure to hold your phone.

9. Take your phone and put it on the stand. Make sure it fits comfortably and doesn't wobble.

10. Smooth the clay out using your thumbs or the clay smoother tool. This will give the stand a neat and polished finish.

11. Add decorative effects, if wished. Stick the clay shapes onto the stand to create a unique design.

12. Let the whole stand dry for about 48 hours or until the stand is completely white. This will ensure that the clay is dry and ready to paint.

Part 2: Painting the Stand

1. Choose the color(s) that you wish to use for the inside of the phone stand. Make sure it complements your phone's color.

2. Paint the inside of the stand using a brush. This will add a nice touch to the overall look of your stand.

3. Take the color(s) you wish to use for the outside of the phone stand. You can either use the same color as the inside or mix it up.

4. Paint the stand on the outside. Be careful not to paint over the cradle piece as this will affect the stability of the stand.

5. Paint the decorations any color you want. This is your chance to get creative and personalize the stand to your liking.

6. Add more decorative effects if wished. Use different colored clay to create shapes and stick them onto the stand.

7. Allow the paint to dry completely before use. This will prevent the colors from smudging or rubbing off.

8. You are finished! Enjoy your new phone stand and use it to comfortably watch your favorite shows or videos.

Creating a phone stand from clay is a fun and easy DIY project that anyone can do with a little patience and creativity. So why not give it a try and make your very own stand today!

William "Bull" Halsey, Jr. was a decorated naval officer who played a significant role in naval warfare during World War II. His leadership and strategic decisions were instrumental in securing victory at some of the most pivotal battles in the Pacific theater. If you're interested in learning more about this historical figure, here are some steps you can take:

1. Seek insight into how people thought, felt and acted in the time when he was born in the 1880s.

Understanding the culture and society in which Halsey grew up can give you a better appreciation of the challenges and opportunities that shaped his life.

2. Research the teaching methods of the academy during his time, as well as current teaching modalities for insight into his motivations, decisions and actions.

3. Consider how someone not so academically inclined helped change the course of history.

Halsey was known for his tough, no-nonsense leadership style, which was shaped in part by his lack of success in academics. Examining how this experience influenced his outlook on leadership can provide valuable insights.

4. Study how life was aboard such vessels then, and consider how that might shape a man.

Naval life in the early 1900s was vastly different from what we know today. Exploring the living conditions and challenges faced by sailors can deepen your understanding of the kind of environment in which Halsey was accustomed to operating.

5. Discuss with your friends how dedication means learning all one can about a field of interest.

Halsey's passion for naval warfare and his commitment to excellence can provide inspiration for anyone looking to pursue a career or hobby with dedication and passion.

6. Think about wartime situations and how disparaging the enemy might have been necessary to inspire his sailors.

7. Discuss with your friends, family and classmates what life might be like for everyone if his famous battles had been unsuccessful.

The outcome of battles like those led by Halsey had a profound impact on the course of history. Considering the alternative outcomes can help us appreciate the sacrifices made by the men and women who fought in these conflicts.

8. Consider his most major error, termed "Halsey's Blunder".

Halsey's decision to pursue a Japanese fleet during the Battle of Leyte Gulf, leaving his own carriers exposed, is often cited as one of the most significant military blunders of the war. Understanding the circumstances leading up to this decision can provide valuable lessons on leadership and decision-making.

9. Read up on his blunders, and discuss and think about how bold men/women are apt to make crucial mistakes due to their enormous responsibilities.

10. Discuss this important historical figure in naval warfare and appreciate that it was on the deck of his flagship, the USS Missouri, on Sept 2, 1945, that Japan formally surrendered to end the War in The Pacific (of WWII).

Rough plumbing a basement bathroom can seem like a daunting task, but with the right materials and a step-by-step approach, it can be achievable. Follow these simple steps to successfully rough plumb your basement bathroom.

Gather your materials:
Before starting any plumbing work, it's important to have all necessary materials on hand. Here are some materials you'll need to gather before beginning:

- Metal detector
- Scratch paper
- Tape measure

Identify the main waste stack:
The first step in rough plumbing a basement bathroom is to identify the main waste stack that goes from the upstairs bathroom to the sewer. This will help you determine where to connect the new PVC pipe that will connect the new toilet and sink to the cast iron pipe in the ground.

Detect the cast iron pipe:
Use a metal detector to detect the cast iron pipe leading from the main waste stack to the sewer. This will help you identify where to break the concrete floor to expose the necessary section of the cast iron pipe.

Plan the location of the new pipe:
Identify where you want the sink and the toilet to be placed in the basement. This will help you plan the location of the new PVC pipe that will connect the new toilet and sink to the cast iron pipe in the ground.

Prepare your materials:
Once you've identified the location of the new pipe, it's time to prepare your materials. Here are some materials you'll need to prepare:

- Box cutter knife/chisel
- Safety Glasses
- Chalk/tape
- Jackhammer
- Bucket/spade
- Plastic curtain

Remove the existing flooring:
Remove any tile, carpeting, or other flooring materials to expose the concrete above the spot where you have decided to place the new pipe.

Draw an outline:
Use chalk or tape to draw an outline on the concrete floor where you will need to break it, based on where you decided to place the new toilet and sink.

Break the concrete:
Use a jackhammer to break the concrete floor to expose the necessary section of the cast iron pipe as well as the path that the new pipe will lay for the toilet and sink. Clear out the concrete debris and dig out the sand so the new pipe has a place to lay.

Collect the needed materials:
With the area cleared, it's time to collect the necessary materials to complete the rough plumbing job. Here are some materials you'll need:

- PVC sections as determined in Part 1
- PVC primer and cement
- Saw (hand or electric)
- Angle grinder
- Band-seal couplings and screwdriver

Connect the PVC pipe:
Purchase the necessary length of PVC pipe that the new toilet and sink will flow into. Connect the pipe together in the shape that fits your design. Cut an appropriate section of the cast iron pipe so the new PVC will fit in it and attach the new PVC to the cast iron with band-seal couplings.

Prepare the materials:
Finally, it's time to prepare the materials you need to finish the rough plumbing job.

- Bags of sand
- Bags of Ready Mix concrete
- Mason trowels

Cover the pipe:
Cover over the pipe over with sand and then cover over the sand with an appropriate amount of Ready Mix concrete. Smooth out the concrete with the mason trowel so that new flooring can be added later.

By following these simple steps and with the right materials on hand, you can successfully rough plumb a basement bathroom.

Bread and butter pickles are a delicious way to enjoy the crunch of cucumbers with a tangy, sweet flavor. Making them at home is a fun and rewarding kitchen project that can result in jars of pickles to last your family all winter. Here's how to make bread and butter pickles.

Part 1: Preparing the Pickling Cucumbers

1. Obtain pickling cucumbers. Look for cucumbers labeled as "pickling cucumbers" or "Kirby cucumbers" at your local farmers market or grocery store. These cucumbers are smaller and more flavorful than the common salad cucumbers.

2. Wash the cucumbers thoroughly and slice them thickly. Use a sharp chef's knife to slice the cucumbers about 1⁄4 inch (0.6 cm) thick.

3. Slice the onions. Peel and slice one or two onions into thin rings to add flavor to your pickles.

4. Prepare brine for the first soak. Dissolve 1/2 cup of salt for every 4 quarts of water in a large container. Put the sliced cucumbers and onions in the brine, making sure they are completely submerged. Cover the container and allow the vegetables to soak for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

5. Drain the salt water out of the onion and cucumber mixture and discard it. Rinse the vegetables well with cold water and set them aside.

Part 2: Preparing and Canning the Pickling Liquid

1. Prepare the pickling liquid. In a large saucepan, combine 5 cups of apple cider vinegar, 3 cups of sugar, 1 tablespoon of mustard seeds, 1 tablespoon of celery seeds, and 1 teaspoon of turmeric powder. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 10 minutes.

2. Prepare the seals. While your pickling liquid is simmering, sterilize at least a dozen canning jars by boiling them in water for 10 minutes. When the jars are sterilized, remove them from the boiling water and place them on a clean towel to dry. Boil the lids and rings separately for 10 minutes.

3. Pack the cucumbers and onions into the sterilized jars. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the vegetables from the brine to the jars, packing them in tightly.

4. Remove any air bubbles from within the jar using a knife. Insert a long, slender plastic knife down the sides of the jar to release any air bubbles.

5. Wipe the jar rim with a damp, clean cloth to remove any residue. This will help ensure a good seal.

6. Place the filled jars in a water-bath canner or a large stock pot. Use a rack to prevent the jars from touching the bottom of the pot.

7. Bring the canner full of water and jars to a boil and boil for 15 minutes. Add more time if you are at high altitude.

8. Remove the jars from the boiling water and place them on an old towel in a sheltered area to cool overnight. Notice that if the jars are sticky, wait until they have cooled completely, at least 24 hours.

Congratulations! You've made your own delicious bread and butter pickles. Store the jars in a cool, dark place for up to a year.

How to Do an Eskimo Roll

If you enjoy kayaking, learning how to do an Eskimo roll can help you become a more skilled paddler. An Eskimo roll is a technique that allows you to right your kayak after capsizing without having to exit the boat. While it may take some practice, anyone can learn to do an Eskimo roll with a little patience and determination. Here are the steps you need to follow to learn how to do an Eskimo roll:

1. Position your Paddle Parallel to Your Boat

Before you begin, you need to get into position. Position your paddle parallel to your boat with the paddle on the left side, or port, of your boat. This is the starting position for the Eskimo roll.

2. Twist Your Torso to the Right and Retract Your Right Arm

Next, twist your torso to the right and retract your right arm. You will bring your paddle in an arch across your kayak deck in front of you.

3. Practice Your Technique Above Water

Before you attempt to roll under water, it's important to practice your technique above water. Going through the motions with your paddle will help you to develop your muscle memory before you actually attempt your roll under water.

4. Capsize Your Kayak

As you are practicing your roll, you want to know how to flip yourself over. Capsize your kayak and get ready to perform the Eskimo roll.

5. Exit Your Capsized Kayak

After you flip your kayak over completely, you want to make a controlled exit. Practice your exits so that you get comfortable being upside down in the water.

6. Practice Your Exits

Even though this isn’t your complete roll, practicing wet exits can help you to feel comfortable upside down in the water. Keep a friend by your side for emergency surfacing.

7. Capsize Your Boat and Perform the Motions of Your Roll Under Water

Once you've practiced your exits, it's time to perform the Eskimo roll under water. Capsize your boat and perform the motions of your roll. Don't worry if you don't get it on the first try. Just keep repeating the action until you feel confident.

8. Start in a Controlled, Still-Water Setting

As you learn to roll, you want to begin in a setting that is predictable and safe, like a lake or a large pool.

9. Choose a Spot Familiar to You

Choose a spot that is familiar to you so that you feel comfortable while you learn.

10. Kayak with Another Person

It's always a good idea to kayak with another person, especially when you're learning something new.

11. Dress for the Water Temperature

Because you are planning on capsizing to learn how to roll, you want to make sure you have appropriate gear for the weather. Dress for the water temperature.

12. Condition Your Body and Breath

Your physical fitness and mental calm will likely determine your success in completing your Eskimo roll. Take the time to condition your body and breath before attempting the roll.

By following these 12 steps, you can learn how to do an Eskimo roll and become a more skilled kayaker. Remember, practice makes perfect, and with time and patience, you'll be able to do an Eskimo roll like a pro!

Gluten-free diets are becoming more common as people are becoming more aware of gluten intolerance and celiac disease. However, not having gluten doesn't mean that delicious pies are off the menu. A gluten-free spinach pot pie is the perfect solution for those who love pastry and want to avoid gluten. This article will teach you how to whip up a gluten-free spinach pot pie with ease!

Ingredients:

- 3 and 1/2 cups of all-purpose gluten-free flour
- 2 teaspoons of extra virgin olive oil
- 2 small eggs
- 1 stick of chopped butter
- 1-3 cups of hot water or hot organic milk (regular milk may also be used)
- 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil
- 2-3 chopped carrots
- 1-2 chopped stalks of celery
- 1 chopped onion
- 2 cups of corn
- 2 cups of chopped Portobello mushrooms, or any type of fresh mushroom
- 3-5 cups of finely chopped spinach
- 1 teaspoon of parsley

Instructions:

1. To make the pastry, place 3 and 1/2 cups of all-purpose gluten-free flour into a large mixing bowl.

2. Add 2 teaspoons of extra virgin olive oil as well as 2 small eggs.

3. Add 1 stick of chopped butter.

4. Add 1-3 cups of hot water or hot organic milk, (regular milk may also be used) while mixing the dough by hand.

5. Place the dough on a clean working area.

6. Knead the dough until a firm ball forms.

7. Divide the dough into 3 balls and place in the freezer for 15 minutes.

8. On a large skillet, add 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil.

9. Add 2-3 chopped carrots, 1-2 chopped stalks of celery, 1 chopped onion, and 2 cups of corn.

10. Add 2 cups of chopped Portobello mushrooms (or any type of fresh mushroom) and 3-5 cups of finely chopped spinach.

11. Add 1 teaspoon of parsley.

12. Allow the ingredients to boil on low heat for 15-25 minutes, until the filling has thickened enough to your liking.

13. Remove from heat once finished.

14. Preheat the oven to 375* F.

15. Take out the balls of dough from the freezer.

16. Once thawed, knead out the larger ball of dough.

17. Place the kneaded dough in a 9-inch pie dish.

18. Crimp the edges at the top, in order to avoid any unnecessary drooping of the dough when it's being baked.

19. Place your pie filling into the crust.

20. Knead out the last and smallest ball of dough.

21. Place your rolled out dough on top of your pie.

22. Use a fork to pierce the top of the pastry.

23. Place the pie into the 375* F oven.

24. Bake for 40 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.

25. Take out your pie after it has been baked and let it cool for 10 minutes before cutting into slices.

Conclusion:

That's it! With these simple steps, you can make a delicious gluten-free spinach pot pie that will satisfy your hunger and your taste buds. Make sure to use gluten-free ingredients to avoid any allergic reactions. Bon appetit!

If you want to raise chickens or other poultry, one of the most exciting and rewarding ways to do it is by hatching the eggs yourself. Using an incubator allows you to watch the process of life as the eggs develop into chicks. But, to do this successfully, you need to follow a few steps.

Part 1 of 3: Getting Ready

1. Find or purchase an incubator. There are many types of incubators available, from basic models to high-tech ones with automatic egg turners and digital temperature control. Research and choose one that fits your needs and budget.

2. Clean the incubator. Before you use your incubator, thoroughly clean it with soap and water. Then, disinfect it with a solution of 1 part bleach and 9 parts water. Rinse it well and let it dry.

3. Place the incubator in an area with little to no temperature fluctuation. Choose a spot that is away from drafts, direct sunlight, and windows. Make sure the room temperature stays between 65 and 75 degrees Fahrenheit.

4. Plug the incubator's cord into an electric outlet. Make sure the cord is long enough to reach the outlet comfortably.

5. Add warm water to the incubator's humidity pan. Usually, this is located at the bottom of the incubator. Fill it with warm water, but not so much that it touches the eggs.

6. Calibrate the incubator's temperature. This is important to ensure the incubator is set to the correct temperature. Most incubators come with a thermostat, but there may be small differences between the display and the actual temperature. Use a separate thermometer to check the temperature and adjust if needed.

7. Wait 24 hours to re-check the temperature again. Leave the incubator to stabilize for one day before adding eggs.

Part 2 of 3: Preparing the Eggs

1. Obtain fertile eggs for hatching. You can find these at local farms or hatcheries. Make sure to choose eggs that are healthy and come from good breeding stock.

2. Wash your hands before touching the eggs for placement in the incubator. This is important to avoid transferring bacteria to the eggs.

3. Warm the fertile eggs to room temperature. Leave the eggs out of the refrigerator for at least an hour before putting them in the incubator.

4. Mark each side of the eggs with a pencil. This helps to keep track of which way you've turned the eggs.

5. Place the eggs carefully into the incubator. Make sure to position the eggs with the marked side up. Do not overcrowd the eggs; leave some space around them for air circulation.

6. Allow the incubator's temperature to drop after adding the eggs. This is normal, and the temperature will return to normal within some time.

7. Record the day and how many eggs you've incubated on a calendar. This helps you keep track of the 21-day incubation period.

Part 3 of 3: Managing the Incubation Process

1. Turn the eggs at least three times daily. This ensures that the embryo does not stick to the inside of the eggshell and develop properly.

2. Adjust the humidity levels in the incubator. The ideal humidity level is between 45% to 55% during the first 18 days of incubation. During the final 3 days, increase the humidity level to around 65%.

3. Ensure the incubator has adequate ventilation. This is important to make sure the developing chicks get enough oxygen and remove waste gases.

4. Candle the eggs after 7 to 10 days. This is a process of shining a bright light through the egg to see if the embryo is developing. Remove any eggs that do not show signs of an embryo.

5. Find a tin can or a box that can fit over a light bulb. This DIY incubator can be used to hatch any eggs that may not fit into the purchased incubator.

6. Turn on the light bulb. Set the bulb to 100 watts and put it in the tin can or box. Place the eggs inside this new incubator.

7. Remove any eggs that do not show a developing embryo from the incubator. They will likely never hatch.

8. Prepare for the hatch. The chicks will start hatching around day 21. Make sure you have a prepared area for the chicks to move and grow once they hatch.

9. Place cheesecloth under the egg tray prior to hatching. This helps prevent the chicks from slipping, falling, and injuring themselves.

10. Increase the humidity level in the incubator. This will help the chicks to hatch from the eggshell.

11. Leave the incubator closed until after the chicks hatch. Do not interrupt the hatching process or open the incubator during this time.

12. Remove dry chicks to a prepared area. After the chicks have hatched and dried off, move them to a brooder box with food, water, and bedding.

13. Remove empty shells from the incubator and clean it. This will create space for the chicks to move about in the incubator.

Using an incubator can be a fun and rewarding way to raise chickens or other poultry from their very first moments. Follow these simple steps to help ensure a successful hatch.

Starting a conversation with your crush can be nerve-wracking, especially if you don't want it to be awkward. Here are some tips on how to start a conversation with your crush without it being awkward.

1. Wait for the right time and place to start a conversation.

Timing is crucial when starting a conversation with your crush. You don't want to start a conversation when they're in a bad mood or preoccupied with something else. Wait for a moment when they're relaxed, and there are no distractions around.

2. Talk to your crush like you already know him or her.

Approach your crush with confidence and speak to them like you would speak to an old friend. This approach helps to make the conversation feel less awkward and more natural.

3. Think about what he or she might be interested in talking about.

People usually love talking about themselves, so try to find out what your crush is into. You can then use this information to start a conversation that they will enjoy.

4. Freshen your breath before you talk.

Bad breath can ruin a conversation before it even starts. Make sure to freshen your breath by chewing gum or brushing your teeth before you approach your crush.

5. Make a funny or playful comment about the place you are at or thing you are doing.

A playful comment or a joke can help break the ice and make your crush feel more comfortable around you.

6. Get the update on something he or she has been doing, especially if you share something in common.

Find out what your crush has been up to lately, especially if you share a common interest. This will give you an idea of what topics to bring up during your conversation.

7. Ask for his or her opinion on something easy to talk about.

Asking for someone's opinion is usually a good way to start a conversation. Make sure to ask about something easy to talk about, like a recent movie or TV show you both watched.

8. Ask him or her something unexpected but easy to answer.

Asking an unexpected question can be a great way to make your crush feel more engaged in the conversation. However, make sure to keep the question easy to answer.

9. Go with an opening line that pops in your head.

Sometimes the best conversations start with a simple opening line. Don't overthink it too much and go with the first thing that pops into your head.

10. Ask questions about his or her interests, hobbies, or work.

Asking about someone's interests, hobbies, or work can help you find common ground and create a more meaningful conversation.

11. Be an active listener in your conversation.

Listening is just as important as speaking when it comes to starting a conversation with your crush. Make sure to actively listen to what they're saying and engage with the conversation.

12. Show him or her that you are enjoying yourself in conversation.

Smiling, laughing, and making eye contact are all good ways to show your crush that you're enjoying your conversation with them.

13. Make a plan to hang out again, and/or get his or her number.

If things seem to be going well, ask your crush if he or she wants to hang out again or ask for their number. This will help you continue the conversation beyond your initial interaction.

14. Bring the conversation back to something you already talked about.

If the conversation starts to stall, bring it back to something you already talked about. This will help keep the conversation flowing.

15. End the conversation on a good note.

Make sure to end the conversation on a positive note. Thank your crush for the conversation and let them know that you enjoyed talking to them.

Identify the Varieties of Restraining Orders

1. Domestic Violence Restraining Order - this type of order is used when you have been abused by someone who you have a close relationship with or are related to.

2. Civil Harassment Restraining Order - this type of order is used to protect you from someone who is not related to you, but who is harassing, threatening, stalking, or abusing you.

3. Workplace Violence Restraining Order - this type of order is used to protect you from someone you work with or who has contact with your workplace, and who is threatening or violent.

Understand the Restraints Available

Restraining orders come with different types of restraints. Some restraints may include:

1. No contact order - the restrained party cannot contact you via phone, text, email, or in person.

2. Stay away order - the restrained party must stay a certain distance away from you and places where you frequent.

3. Move out order - the restrained party has to move out of your shared home if you live together.

Understand Temporary Restraining Orders (TRO)

In California, you can request a temporary restraining order (TRO) if you need immediate protection. TROs are issued quickly and are valid for up to 25 days. This gives you time to file for a more permanent restraining order.

Going away for a weekend with kids can be a great bonding experience, but it can also be a bit stressful if you're not prepared. To make the most of your time away, it's important to be organized and plan ahead. Here are a few tips to help you prepare for a fun and stress-free family weekend getaway.

Be Organized

The key to a successful weekend getaway with kids is organization. Start by making a to-do list of everything you need to get done before your trip and put together a packing list. Make sure everyone has everything they need, including toiletries and any necessary medications.

Do Some Packing One or Two Days Before the Trip and the Rest the Morning of the Trip

Some things you'll want to pack ahead, so you're not rushed the morning of your trip. This way, you can make sure nothing important gets left behind. But make sure you have some time the morning of the trip to pack anything you missed the first time or to add any last-minute items.

Have the Kids Pack Their Own Bags

Have the kids empty out their school backpacks and use them as their weekend bags. Have them pack their entertainment items, comfort items, and hygiene things like hairbrushes and toothbrushes. This will help teach them responsibility and ensure they have everything they need.

Consider the Travel Time

Consider how long it will take to get to your destination and plan accordingly. Bring snacks and games to keep the kids entertained during the trip. You may also want to plan breaks along the way to stretch your legs and break up the drive.

Before You Leave the House

Make sure everyone has gotten some energy out before you leave. Encourage the kids to run around outside for a bit so they won't mind sitting for a little while. This can also help them fall asleep in the car if they're tired enough.

For the Car Ride

Have the kids sit with their bags close to them so they won't be climbing around trying to get their things. This will make it easier for you to keep an eye on them.

Have the Kids Dress in the Same Color

Having your kids dress in the same color can really simplify things. This way, you'll be able to pick them out of a crowd easily and keep track of everyone.

If You Are Staying at Someone Else's House With Them

Bring a small gift for your hosts to show appreciation for their hospitality. Explain to your kids what you expect of them while you're at their house. Remind them to be respectful and keep their mess confined to their own bedroom or designated play area.

If You Are Staying at a Hotel

Before you get there, tell the kids what you expect of them while you're there. Remind them that they need to stay quiet in the hallways and in their room, and be respectful to other hotel guests. Make sure they understand that this is not their home and everyone needs to be on their best behavior.

With a little preparation and organization, going away for a weekend with kids can be a fun, enjoyable experience. Remember to plan ahead and have everything you need, and you'll be able to relax and enjoy your time away with your family.

1. Always buy armor and a few grenades.
Before you start any game, make sure you have armor to protect you from enemy fire and at least a few grenades to help you dispose of enemies in tricky situations.

If you're going to ditch your current weapon for something better, make sure to empty all of its ammo first. Otherwise, your enemy may pick it up and use it against you.

1. Don't be too cocky, stay a bit behind your teammates and work with them.

3. Walk if you think an enemy may be near.

4. Crouch jump if needed.
