Check the Engine Number
Make sure your engine is the Type 1, air-cooled engine. The valve adjustment process is different for the Type 2, water-cooled engine.
If you're not sure if your engine is the Type 1 or Type 2, there's an easy way to tell. Look for the engine number on the left side of the engine, just below the coolant reservoir. If it says "Type 1," you have the air-cooled engine. If it says "Type 2," you have the water-cooled engine.

Gather Your Tools
You'll need a few tools to adjust the valves on your VW Beetle. These include a flathead screwdriver, a socket wrench, a spark plug wrench, a timing light, a compression gauge, and a torque wrench.
You'll also need a valve adjustment tool, which you can purchase from a local auto parts store or online.

Remove the Spark Plugs
Use a spark plug wrench to remove all of the spark plugs from the engine. This will allow you to turn the engine over by hand to adjust the valves.
Be sure to label each spark plug with a number so you can reinstall them in the same order they were removed.

Loosen the Compression Screws
Use a socket wrench to loosen the compression screws on the engine. This will allow the valves to move more freely when they're adjusted.

Connect the Valve Adjustment Tool
Connect the valve adjustment tool to the spark plug hole on the engine. This will allow you to turn the engine over by hand to adjust the valves.

Turn the Engine Over
Use the valve adjustment tool to turn the engine over by hand, following the correct procedure for your engine. This will allow you to adjust the valves to the correct clearance.

Tighten the Compression Screws
Use a torque wrench to tighten the compression screws on the engine. This will lock the valves in place once they've been adjusted.

Reinstall the Spark Plugs
Use the spark plug wrench to reinstall the spark plugs in the engine. Be sure to reinstall them in the same order they were removed.

Start the Engine
Use the spark plug wrench to start the engine, following the correct procedure for your engine. Listen for any unusual sounds or smoke from the engine, and check the valve clearance with the timing light if necessary.

Check the Compression
Use the compression gauge to check the compression in each cylinder. This will ensure that the valves are adjusted properly and that the engine is running efficiently.

How to Identify if a Child Has Been Traumatized by an Event

Children are especially susceptible to the lasting emotional effects of trauma. A child's developing sense of self, attachment figures, and the surrounding world can all be affected by a traumatic event. In many cases, the effects of such events can lead to significant emotional distress, including anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

As a parent or caregiver, it's important to be aware of the emotional impact that a traumatic event can have on a child. Knowing what to look for and how to respond can help provide comfort and support to a child who has experienced a traumatic event.

This article focuses on how to identify if a child has been traumatized by an event and how to help them cope with the resulting emotional distress.

Symptoms of Traumatic Stress in Children

While each child may react differently to a traumatic event, there are some common symptoms that may indicate a child has been traumatized. It's essential to keep in mind that not all children who experience a traumatic event will exhibit these symptoms, and some may exhibit a few of these symptoms without having been traumatized.

The most common symptoms of traumatic stress in children include:

- Feeling scared, anxious, or nervous
- Having trouble sleeping or frequent nightmares
- Being more clingy or fearful of separation from caregivers
- Feeling angry or acting out more often than usual
- Having difficulty concentrating or finding it hard to focus

Harvest the roots. When the roots are about the size of a carrot and have three prongs, they are ready to harvest. To harvest, gently dig around the roots and pull them out of the soil. Stoichiometry is a key part of chemistry and is used to determine the relative quantities of elements in chemical compounds and reactions. The word stoichiometry is derived from the Greek words stoikhein and metron, which mean "to measure" and "to put in proportion," respectively. In this article, we will show you how to do stoichiometry.

Step 1: 
Define the reaction
The first step is to identify the chemical reaction that you want to use stoichiometry on. This will involve identifying the reactants and the products, as well as the type of reaction (acid/base, redox, etc.).

Step 2:
Write the reaction as a balanced equation
The next step is to write the reaction as a balanced equation, which means that the number of atoms of each element on the reactant side of the equation is equal to the number of atoms of that element on the product side. This can be done by adding or removing parenthesis, combining like terms, and/or multiplying through by a constant.

Step 3:
Identify the limiting reactant
The limiting reactant is the reactant that is present in the smallest amount, or that will limit the amount of product that can be produced. In other words, if there is a shortage of the limiting reactant, the reaction will stop. The amount of product that can be produced is dependent on the amount of limiting reactant that is present.

To identify the limiting reactant, you will need to look at the coefficients in front of each reactant in the balanced equation. The reactant with the smallest coefficient is the limiting reactant. For example, in the reaction between hydrogen and oxygen to form water, the coefficient in front of hydrogen is always smaller than the coefficient in front of oxygen, so hydrogen is the limiting reactant.

Step 4:
Use the balanced equation to calculate the amount of product
Once you have identified the limiting reactant, you can use the balanced equation to calculate the amount of product that will be produced. This is done by multiplying the molar quantity of the limiting reactant by the coefficient in front of the product.

For example, if we have 2 moles of hydrogen and 3 moles of oxygen, and hydrogen is the limiting reactant, we can calculate the amount of water that will be produced as follows:

2 moles of hydrogen * 3 moles of oxygen / 2 moles of hydrogen = 6 moles of water

Step 5:
 Verify the calculation
It is important to verify that your calculation is correct by checking that the number of moles of reactants is equal to the number of moles of products. If the numbers are not equal, then something is wrong with your calculation and you will need to go back and check your work.

Sewing Bench Cushions
This is a guide for sewing bench cushions. A bench cushion is a great way to add comfort and a touch of color to your favorite bench. They are also fairly simple to make, so you can have a custom-made bench cushion in no time at all.
You will need:
A piece of fabric measuring 36" x 48"
A piece of batting measuring 34" x 44"
A piece of fabric measuring 12" x 16" for the cushion back
A piece of hook and loop fastener measuring 2" x 12"
Pins
Thread
Needle
Thimble (optional)
How to make a bench cushion
Cut the fabric, batting, and cushion back
Lay the fabric out on a flat surface. Cut a piece of fabric measuring 36" x 48".
Cut a piece of batting measuring 34" x 44".
Cut a piece of fabric measuring 12" x 16" for the cushion back.
Sew the cushion back
Place the 12" x 16" cushion back piece of fabric right side down on a flat surface.
Place the 2" x 12" piece of hook and loop fastener on one short end of the cushion back, 1/2" from the edge. Pin it in place.
 Sew along the edge of the hook and loop fastener, through all layers of fabric, using a 1/8" seam allowance.
Sew the long edges of the cushion back together. Use a 1/2" seam allowance and sew with the right sides of the fabric facing each other.
Leave the short end open for turning.
Turn the cushion back right side out and press it flat.
Make the cushion top
Place the 36" x 48" piece of fabric right side down on a flat surface.
Place the 34" x 44" piece of batting on top of the fabric.
Pin the layers together, starting at the center and working your way out to the edges.
 Sew along the edges of the cushion top, using a 1/2" seam allowance.
Trim the excess batting and fabric from the seams.
Turn the cushion top right side out and press it flat.
Attach the cushion back to the cushion top
Lay the cushion back on a flat surface with the hook and loop fastener facing up.
Lay the cushion top on top of the cushion back, with the wrong side facing up.
Match the edges of the cushion top to the edges of the cushion back, and pin them together.
 Sew along the edges of the cushion, using a 1/2" seam allowance.
Make the ties
Cut two pieces of fabric measuring 2" x 27".
Lay the pieces of fabric right side down on a flat surface.
Sew along the long edge of the fabric, using a 1/4" seam allowance.
Turn the ties right side out and press them flat.
Attach the ties to the cushion
Lay the cushion down on a flat surface with the wrong side facing up.
Find the center of one long edge of the cushion. Measure 2" from the center in each direction and mark the spots with pins.
Place one end of a tie at each pin, and pin the ties in place.
Sew the ties in place, using a 1/4" seam allowance.
Turn the cushion right side out and press it flat.

How to Treat and Prevent Nitrate Toxicity in Cattle

Nitrate toxicity can be treated and prevented in cattle.

Symptoms of Nitrate Toxicity in Cattle

Nitrate toxicity in cattle can cause a range of symptoms, including:

- weakness
- confusion
- loss of appetite
- rapid breathing
- unusual sweating
- and even death in severe cases.

The most common sign of nitrate toxicity is a lack of appetite.

If you notice any of these symptoms in your cattle, it's important to act quickly and contact your veterinarian immediately.

Treatment of Nitrate Toxicity in Cattle

The treatment for nitrate toxicity is focused on supportive care, as there is no specific antidote.

This may include the following:

- IV fluids and electrolytes to correct dehydration and electrolyte deficiencies
- Corticosteroids to reduce inflammation
- Anti-nausea and anti-diarrheal medications to control symptoms
- Oxygen therapy, if needed

In severe cases, blood transfusions may be necessary.

It's important to work with your veterinarian to determine the best treatment plan for your cattle.

Prevention of Nitrate Toxicity in Cattle

The best way to prevent nitrate toxicity is to avoid feeding cattle high-nitrate feeds, such as fermented feeds, fish meal, and some vegetables.

If you must feed high-nitrate feeds, it's important to do so cautiously and in limited amounts.

It's also important to ensure that cattle have access to plenty of fresh, clean water at all times.

Nitrate toxicity can be a serious and potentially fatal condition in cattle.

By being aware of the risks and symptoms, and taking quick action when needed, you can help keep your cattle healthy and safe.

Aquaponics integrates aquaculture and hydroponics into one production system. Aquaponics relies on the food introduced for fish, which works as the system's input. As fish eat this food and process it, they transform it into urine and feces, both rich in ammonia, nitrogen, and other minerals. These excretions are filtered out of the water the fish live in and are used to feed the plants in the aquaponics system. As the plants absorb the fish waste, they filter the water, which is then returned to the fish.

Because aquaponics works on the basis of a closed-loop system, it is an extremely sustainable method of food production. Not only does aquaponics not require soil, but it also does not require as much water as both aquaculture and hydroponics do when performed separately. Aquaponics also makes it possible to have a fish harvest and a plant harvest at the same time, which is not possible with either aquaculture or hydroponics on its own.

Buttermilk biscuits are a classic Southern recipe that is surprisingly easy to make. The key to the best buttermilk biscuits is to not overwork the dough, which would cause the biscuits to be tough. Just like with any other biscuit recipe, you'll want to keep your butter and buttermilk very cold. You'll also want to make sure that you have everything ready and in place before you start. This will help ensure that you work quickly and don't allow the ingredients to warm up too much. 

Ingredients:
* 1 cup all-purpose flour
* 1 teaspoon baking powder
* 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
* 1 teaspoon salt
* 1 1/2 cups buttermilk
* 1/2 cup cold butter, cut into small pieces
* 2 cups all-purpose flour, for rolling out

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Cut in butter with a pastry blender or rub in with your fingers. (The largest pieces should be the size of small peas.) With your fingertips, flatten butter pieces into small disks. Cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate until butter is very cold, about 15 minutes.
3. Combine 1 1/2 cups buttermilk and 2 tablespoons ice water. Stir into flour mixture with a fork until combined. (Do not overmix; the dough will be a little shaggy.)
4. Transfer dough to a lightly floured work surface; roll out into a 1-inch-thick (2 1/2 cm) round. Cut out biscuits using a 2 1/2-inch (6 cm) round biscuit cutter. Gather scraps, reroll once, and cut out more biscuits. (You should have a total of 12 biscuits.)
5. Place biscuits on prepared baking sheet. Bake until golden brown, about 15 minutes. Let cool on a wire rack for 2 minutes. Serve warm.

The theory of communism was first developed in the early 19th century by Karl Marx, who believed that the working class should rise up and overthrow the upper class, or bourgeoisie. The workers would then take control of the means of production, and the resulting wealth would be distributed equally among all members of society.

Researchers have developed a way to make 3D-printed metals stronger by melting them with a small laser.

"Most commercial 3D printers use a technology called powder bed fusion, in which a powder is spread in a thin layer and then selectively melted with a large CO2 laser," said Yu Attaway, a researcher at the University of Texas at Austin. "But this new approach uses a small, focused laser beam to scan over the powder bed and selectively melt the powder."

The new approach, called laser engineered net shaping (LENS), has been tested on metals, including stainless steel, bronze and titanium.

"With LENS, we can control the thermal history of the metal, and that allows us to make very complex shapes with very high resolution," said Attaway.

LENS uses a computer-controlled laser to trace out the shape of the object being printed. The laser melts the metal powder together, building the object layer by layer.

"We can control the amount of energy that goes into each spot, and we can control the cooling rate after the laser has heated the metal," said Attaway. "This allows us to make very complex shapes with high resolution, and it also allows us to make very strong parts."

So far, the researchers have printed small objects, such as bearings, with LENS. They are now working on printing larger objects, such as engine parts.

"LENS has the potential to change the way we manufacture metal parts," said Attaway. "It's a new way to make metal parts that are strong and complex."

In this article, we'll show you how to make a pan sauce and share some of our favorite recipes.

What is a pan sauce?
A pan sauce is a sauce that's made in the same pan that you used to cook your meat. This is a great way to save time and cleanup. Pan sauces are typically made with a base of butter, olive oil, or chicken stock, and then flavorings such as shallots, garlic, and fresh herbs are added. The pan is then deglazed with wine or vinegar, and the sauce is finished with a few tablespoons of cream or milk.

How to make a pan sauce
There are a few different ways to make a pan sauce, but here's a basic recipe that you can adapt to your own taste and ingredients:

1. Start with a hot pan. If you're making a pan sauce in the same pan that you cooked your meat in, make sure that the pan is still hot when you add the butter or oil.
2. Add the butter or oil. Once the pan is hot, add a few tablespoons of butter or olive oil. Let the butter melt or the oil heat up, then add your shallot or garlic. Cook for a few minutes, until the shallot is softened or the garlic is fragrant.
3. Deglaze the pan. Add a splash of wine or vinegar to the pan and use a wooden spoon to scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let the wine or vinegar simmer for a few minutes to reduce it.
4. Add the cream or milk. Stir in a few tablespoons of heavy cream or milk. Let the cream or milk simmer in the pan for a few minutes to thicken it.
5. Season and serve. Taste the sauce and season it with salt and pepper. Serve the sauce over your cooked meat.

bread and butter pudding

Bread and butter pudding is a staple of the British Isles, and is most often served as a dessert. This is a simple version, but feel free to customize it to your liking.

Ingredients:
4 to 5 slices white bread, crust removed and cut into small pieces
1/2 cup fresh milk
1/2 cup heavy cream
1/2 cup sugar
2 eggs, beaten
1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
1/8 teaspoon almond extract
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted

Preparation:
1. Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

2. In a small saucepan, heat milk and cream over low heat until just warm. Remove from heat.

3. In a medium bowl, whisk together sugar, eggs, vanilla, almond extract, salt, and nutmeg until well combined.

4. Slowly whisk in warm milk and cream, then pour mixture over bread. Let sit for 10 minutes, then stir gently to ensure all bread is evenly coated.

5. Pour bread mixture into a buttered 8-inch square baking dish. Drizzle with melted butter, then cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight.

6. Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

7. Uncover bread pudding and place baking dish in a larger baking dish or roasting pan. Fill larger dish with enough hot water to come halfway up the sides of the smaller dish.

8. Bake for 45 minutes, or until bread pudding is set and lightly browned.

9. Let cool slightly, then serve warm with ice cream or whipped cream.

 Gestational diabetes occurs during pregnancy and may cause high blood sugar levels in both the mother and baby. It typically goes away after the baby is born.

How to Sue for Infringement of Digital Intellectual Property

Introduction
As the world continues to embrace the digital age, protecting intellectual property (IP) in the digital realm has become increasingly important. If you have created an original work or invention, you likely have IP rights in that work. And if someone else infringes on those rights, you may have a cause of action. This article provides information on how you can protect your digital IP and what to do if someone infringes on your rights.

Understanding Intellectual Property
The term "intellectual property" refers to any original work or invention that has been created by a person or group of people. This can include anything from literary works and artwork to inventions and computer programs. IP rights give the creator of an original work or invention the exclusive rights to use, sell, or reproduce their work. These rights are typically protected by copyright, trademark, or patent law.

Digital intellectual property refers to any original work or invention that has been created and stored in a digital format. This can include anything from digital artwork and music to computer programs and databases. Just like any other IP, digital IP is protected by copyright, trademark, or patent law.

Copyright Law and Digital IP
Copyright law protects original works of authorship, including literary works, artwork, and digital works. In the United States, copyright protection exists from the moment an original work is "fixed" in a tangible medium. This means that as soon as a work is saved to a computer file or other digital storage medium, it is protected by copyright.

To be protected by copyright, a work must be original, meaning it must be independently created and not copied from another work. It must also be "fixed" in a tangible medium, which means that it must be saved to a physical or digital storage medium.

Trademark Law and Digital IP
Trademark law protects words, phrases, or symbols that are used to identify and distinguish the goods or services of one party from those of another. In the digital age, trademarks can be used to protect things like domain names, social media handles, and app icons.

Trademark protection exists from the moment a mark is used in commerce to identify and distinguish the goods or services of one party from those of another. However, trademark rights can be enhanced through registration with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO). Registration provides additional rights, such as the ability to bring an action for trademark infringement in federal court.

Patent Law and Digital IP
Patent law protects inventions, including processes, machines, and articles of manufacture. In the digital age, patents can be used to protect things like software, hardware, and electronic devices.

Patent protection exists from the moment an invention is disclosed in a patent application and is granted by the USPTO. However, patent rights can be enhanced through registration with the USPTO. Registration provides additional rights, such as the ability to bring an action for patent infringement in federal court.

How to Sue for Infringement of Digital Intellectual Property
If someone has infringed on your digital IP rights, you may have a cause of action under copyright, trademark, or patent law. To sue for infringement, you must prove that the defendant has violated one or more of your IP rights. This typically requires showing that the defendant has copied or otherwise used your work without your permission.

To prove infringement, you will need to provide evidence of the defendant's use of your work, as well as evidence that the defendant's use is substantially similar to your work. This evidence can include things like screenshots, digital fingerprints, and expert testimony.

Once you have proven infringement, you may be able to obtain damages or injunctive relief. Damages can include compensation for lost profits, damages to your reputation, or damages for any profits that the defendant has earned through their infringement. Injunctive relief can include orders to stop the defendant from using your work or to destroy any copies of your work that they may have.

Suing for Infringement of Digital Intellectual Property
The process of suing for infringement of digital IP can be complex, and it's important to understand the applicable law and the evidence needed to prove infringement. If you believe that someone has infringed on your digital IP rights, it's important to act quickly and seek legal advice to ensure that your rights are protected.

How to Make Irish Car Bomb Cupcakes

These Irish Car Bomb Cupcakes are a fun and easy St. Patrick's Day dessert! They're also perfect for any other time of the year when you're craving a rich, chocolatey cupcake with a boozy kick.

Ingredients:

-1 cup all-purpose flour
-1 cup sugar
-3/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
-2 teaspoons baking soda
-1 teaspoon baking powder
-1 teaspoon salt
-2 cups milk
-2 eggs
-1/2 cup vegetable oil
-2 teaspoons vanilla extract
-1 cup Guinness
-1/2 cup Baileys
-1/2 cup coffee

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a cupcake pan with paper liners.

2. In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt. In a separate bowl, whisk together milk, eggs, oil, and vanilla extract. Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Pour in Guinness, Baileys, and coffee and mix until well combined.

3. Pour batter into prepared cupcake pan and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a cupcake comes out clean. Let cool in pan for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

4. While cupcakes are cooling, make the frosting. In a large bowl, beat together 1 cup softened butter and 1 cup sugar until light and fluffy. Add 1/2 cup cocoa powder and 1/2 cup Guinness and beat until well combined. Spread or pipe onto cooled cupcakes. Enjoy!

How to Evict a Tenant in New York

If you're a landlord in New York State, you must follow specific steps to evict a tenant. You must also understand your rights and responsibilities, as well as those of your tenant. Understanding the process can help you avoid mistakes and ensure a successful eviction.

Step 1: Serve a Notice to Quit
If your tenant has not violated the terms of their lease, you cannot evict them. You must give them written notice to quit the property. You can serve the notice to quit by:

- Delivering it to the tenant personally.
- Leaving it with a roommate or another person at the property.
- Posting it on the property and mailing a copy to the tenant at the property address.
- Delivering the notice to quit to the tenant's lawyer.

If you serve the notice to quit personally or by leaving it at the property, you must file the Affidavit of Service with the court. This proves to the court that you served the notice to quit.

Step 2: Wait for the Tenant to Vacate
Your tenant has five days to respond to the notice to quit. They can choose to move out of the property, cure the violation, or fight the eviction.

If the tenant vacates the property, you can move forward with filing the eviction. If they cure the violation, you must give them a written warning and allow them to remedy the violation. You can then file the eviction.

If the tenant doesn't vacate the property or cure the violation, you can proceed with the eviction.

Step 3: File the Eviction
You must file the eviction with the court in the county where the property is located. You must include the following information:

- Your name and contact information
- Your tenant's name and contact information
- The property address
- A description of the property
- The reason for the eviction
- The amount of rent due
- The date the rent is due

You must also include an Affidavit of Service, proving that you served the notice to quit on the tenant.

The court will issue a Warrant of Eviction. This gives the tenant 24 hours to move out of the property. If they don't, the sheriff can remove them.

Bluffing is a key part of poker and other competitive gambling games. It's a way to win a hand even if you don't have the best cards. While many people think of bluffing as a manipulation or a cheat, it's a legitimate strategy. However, if you want to master the art of bluffing, there are a few things you need to keep in mind.

First, you need to understand why people bluff. In poker, the goal of the game is to win the pot, which is the sum of all the money bet on the hand. If you have the best hand, you'll win the pot automatically. However, if you don't have the best hand, you can still win the pot by convincing your opponents to fold their hands. This is where bluffing comes in.

When you bluff, you're essentially trying to trick your opponents into thinking you have a better hand than you actually do. To do this, you need to make a bet or a raise that's large enough to convince them to fold. The best way to do this is to make a bet that's slightly larger than the size of the pot.

Finally, it's important to keep in mind that bluffing is not a guaranteed strategy. While it can be effective in the right situation, it's not always going to work. So, it's important to be aware of your surroundings and the people you're playing with. If you're playing with a group of experienced players, they might be more likely to call your bluffs. How to Make a Modular Origami Stellated Icosahedron

Stellated icosahedron

 modular origami

folded from 3 equilateral triangles, 6 equilateral squares, and 5 regular pentagons.

The stellated icosahedron is a complicated-looking paper craft that is actually easy to make. It is a great project for people new to modular origami.

What You Need

origami paper
ruler
pencil
paper clips (optional)

Step 1: Draw a Triangle

Draw a line 2 inches (5 cm) long on the long side of one piece of origami paper. Mark the midpoint of the line. Draw a second line 2 inches (5 cm) long on the short side of the paper. Mark the midpoint of this line. Draw a line connecting the two midpoints. Draw another line connecting the end points of the long line with the end points of the short line. You should now have a triangle with two equal sides and two equal angles.

Step 2: Mark the Squares

Place the triangle on one piece of origami paper so that one corner is even with the top corner of the paper. Measure 1 inch (2.5 cm) from the bottom corner of the triangle and make a mark on the paper. Measure 1 inch (2.5 cm) from the left corner of the triangle and make another mark on the paper. Draw a line connecting the two marks. Repeat this process on the other side of the triangle. You should now have a square with one side even with the triangle.

Step 3: Create the Modules

Fold the square into a triangle using the lines you drew in step 2. Unfold the triangle and then fold it along the line connecting the midpoints of the long sides. You should now have a smaller triangle with one side folded in half.

Fold the triangle in half along the line connecting the midpoints of the short sides. You should now have a smaller triangle with all three sides folded in half.

Press the folds firmly. You should now have three equilateral triangles.

Step 4: Fold the Squares

Fold one square in half along the line connecting the midpoints of the short sides. Unfold the square and then fold it along the line connecting the midpoints of the long sides. You should now have a smaller square with one side folded in half.

Fold the square in half along the line connecting the midpoints of the other two sides. You should now have a smaller square with all four sides folded in half.

Press the folds firmly. You should now have six equilateral squares.

Step 5: Connect the Modules

Take one triangle and insert the point into the pocket of one square.

Take another square and insert the point into the pocket of the first square.

Take the remaining triangle and insert the point into the pocket of the last square.

You should now have a five-pointed star.

Step 6: Finish the Stellated Icosahedron

Place the star on top of the first triangle with the points facing down.

Connect the points of the star to the corners of the triangle using the paper clips or a glue stick.

Place the second triangle on top of the first triangle with the points facing down.

Connect the points of the star to the corners of the triangle using the paper clips or a glue stick.

You should now have a stellated icosahedron.

Get started.

Prepare the soil.
To get the right soil mix, you will need to combine one part sphagnum moss, one part perlite, and one part coconut coir. This will give your vanilla plants the right drainage and nutrients. Make sure the soil is well-drained, as vanilla roots are sensitive to sitting in water.

Add a support.
Since vanilla is a vine, it will need a trellis or other support to grow on. This can be a wooden trellis, a bamboo trellis, or even a wall. Make sure the support is strong enough to hold the weight of the plant.

Plant the seeds.
Vanilla seeds are best planted in early spring, as soon as the soil has warmed up. You will need to soak the seeds in water for 24 hours before planting them. Then, simply place them on top of the soil, and cover them with a thin layer of soil.

Water the plants.
Vanilla plants need regular watering, so make sure to check the soil frequently and give the plants enough water to keep them happy. However, be careful not to overwater them, as this can cause root rot and other problems.

Fertilize the plants.

Pollinate the plants.

 Harvest the beans.
Once the beans have grown to about 6-8 inches (15-20 cm) long, they are ready to be harvested. Use a sharp knife or scissors to cut the beans off the plant. Be sure to leave a small portion of the stem attached to the bean.

Cure the beans.
To cure the beans, you will need to take a sharp knife and carefully cut through the skin of the bean. This will allow the vanilla flavor to be released. Then, place the beans in a cool, dry place for two weeks. During this time, the beans will turn a dark brown color and will be ready to use.

How to Make a Christmas Tree Pop up Card (Robert Sabuda Method)

Robert Sabuda is a master at making pop-up books, and he has a method that's easy to learn and use. You can make a pop-up Christmas tree card in less than an hour, and it will look like a professional made it.

 Materials
 - Card stock (or construction paper)
- ruler
- Scotch Adhesive Putty
- Fine-point pen
- X-acto knife (with adult help, please!)

Step 1: Make a Triangle

Fold a piece of card stock in half to form a rectangle. Use a ruler to measure 3 inches from the bottom left corner and make a mark. Measure 3 inches from the bottom right corner and make another mark. Use a straightedge to draw a line connecting the two marks.
You now have a triangle.

Step 2: Cut Out the Triangle

Cut out the triangle, cutting along the lines you drew in step 1.

Step 3: Fold the Triangle

Fold the triangle in half, bringing the left corner down to the right corner.

Step 4: Fold the Bottom Edge

Fold the bottom edge of the triangle up, creasing well.

Step 5: Make the Base

Fold a second piece of card stock in half to form a rectangle. Draw a line 3 inches from the bottom edge. Cut along the line.

Step 6: Attach the Triangle to the Base

Put a small piece of adhesive putty on the back of the triangle near the bottom left corner. Place the triangle on the left side of the base, making sure the bottom left corner is flush with the left edge of the base.

Step 7: Make the Tree

Fold the triangle up, bringing the top edge of the triangle down to the bottom edge of the base.

Step 8: Add Embellishments

Use a fine-point pen to add ornaments, lights, or other decorations to your tree.

Generator
The brake system in your Toyota Corolla is hydraulic. The master cylinder powers the brake system with hydraulic fluid. The fluid travels through the brake lines to the brake caliper. The caliper houses the brake pads. The brake pads squeeze the brake rotor to slow or stop the car.

Over time, the brake pads wear down. If the pads wear too thin, the caliper can bite into the rotor. This causes scoring on the rotor. When the scoring is deeper than the thickness of a sheet of paper, the rotor needs to be replaced. If the scoring is not as deep, the rotor can be machined to remove the uneven surface.

Removing the brake pads and machining the rotor is a good time to replace the brake hardware. The hardware includes the pins that hold the brake pads in place. Corroded or damaged hardware can lead to more expensive repairs later.

Here's how to change the front disc brakes on a 1998 Toyota Corolla.

Examine the brake system
Find a level surface under the shade to work on your car. Set the parking brake and place a block of wood behind the rear wheels. Loosen the lug nuts on the front wheels with a lug wrench. Do not remove the lug nuts yet.

The Toyota Corolla has disc brakes on all four wheels. The front brakes are the only brakes that can be changed with a few basic tools. The rear brakes are replaced together, so a drum brake tool is needed to change the rear brakes.

Here are some things to look for when examining the front brakes:

- The brake pads should be at least 1/4 inch thick. If the pads are thinner, they need to be replaced. 
- If the brake pads look good, check the brake rotors. The rotors should be smooth. If the rotors are scored, they need to be replaced or machined. 
- Check the brake hardware. The hardware is the pins and springs that hold the brake pads in place. Corroded or damaged hardware needs to be replaced. 

Changing the brake pads
1 Find the 14mm bolt on the caliper. This is the slide pin bolt. 2 Undo the slide pin bolt with a 14mm socket. 3 Slide the caliper towards the center of the car to release the brake pads. 4 Remove the brake pads from the caliper. 5 Find the small coil spring on the back of the caliper. The spring is the brake hardware. 6 Press the spring into the caliper to release it from the brake pad. 7 Remove the hardware from the old brake pad. 8 Press the new brake pad into the caliper. 9 Slide the caliper away from the center of the car to secure the new brake pads. 10 Screw the slide pin bolt back into place with the 14mm socket.

Machining the brake rotors
1 Start the car and engage the parking brake. 2 Slow down the engine speed by pressing the clutch pedal. 3 Engage the hand brake. 4 Place a block of wood between the floor and the right front wheel. 5 Spin the wheel to find the highest spot on the rotor. 6 Mark the spot with a piece of chalk. 7 Measure the distance from the floor to the marked spot on the rotor. 8 Use a dial gauge to measure the thickness of the rotor. 9 If the rotor is less than 1/4 inch thick, it needs to be replaced. 10 If the rotor is thicker, it can be machined.

 Machining the rotors
1 Find a qualified machine shop to turn the rotors. 2 Remove the rotors from the car. 3 Take the rotors to the machine shop. 4 Have the machine shop true the rotors. Truing a rotor involves machining the rotor to a smooth finish.

The Mayan Calendar
The Mayan calendar is the dating system of the ancient Mayan civilization and the basis for all other calendars used by Mesoamerican civilizations. The calendar was based on a ritual cycle of 260 named days and a year of 365 days. Taken together, they form a longer cycle of 18,980 days, or 52 years of 365 days, called a "Calendar Round."

The original name of the 260-day cycle is unknown; it is variously referred to as the Tzolkin ("Count of Days"), divinatory calendar, ritual calendar, or simply the day calendar. Within the Tzolkin are two smaller cycles of days numbered from 1 to 13 and an ordered series of 20 named days. Although the names for the ritual days differed throughout Mesoamerica, scholars believe that the various calendars were synchronized based on their use in divination. In particular, each named day was thought to have certain fateful characteristics, but most of the details have been lost. 

The 365-day year was divided into 18 named months (uinals) of 20 days plus one month of 5 "nameless" days, called Uayeb. The nameless days were considered extremely unlucky, causing the Maya to observe them with fasting and sacrifices to deities. Each ordinary day had a fourfold designation—in order, day number and day name in the 260-day cycle and day number within the month and month name in the 365-day cycle. Thus, each of the 18,980 days in the Calendar Round had a unique designation (e.g., 12 Caban 15 Ceh).

The Mayan calendar was a synchronizing device for the motions of the planets and the stars. To determine the time of day, the Maya divided the sky into 18,980 sections, corresponding to the days in the Calendar Round. Each of these sections was named for a day in the Calendar Round. Stretching across the sky in a row, as if on a large wheel, were the various planets and the stars. By noting where the planets and stars rose and set in the sky, the Maya could determine the current date.

Long Count

The starting point for the Long Count was the day of the creation of the world, equivalent to August 11, 3114 B.C. in the Gregorian calendar. The largest unit of time in the Long Count was the "Great Cycle," which was 5,125.366 days, or approximately 18,574 days in the Gregorian calendar. One of the more popular beer styles to come out of the craft beer movement is the white beer or wheat beer. There are a lot of different ways to make a white beer, and a lot of different takes on the style, but a very common approach is to make a vanilla beer.

A vanilla beer is a great summer beer, it's light and crisp and the vanilla adds a nice subtle hint of flavor that really makes the beer stand out. A vanilla beer is also a great beer to pair with food. The vanilla will enhance the flavor of the beer and make it more pronounced.

This recipe is for a classic vanilla beer, but you can certainly play around with the recipe and make it your own. You can add more or less vanilla, you can use different types of vanilla, you can even add other flavors like orange or lemon peel.

Ingredients:

2 1/2 gallons of room temperature water
1/2 cup of Prague malt
1/2 cup of Carahell malt
1/2 cup of Light Munich malt
1/2 cup of Wheat malt
1/2 cup of flaked oats
1/2 cup of corn sugar
1/2 teaspoon of salt
1/2 teaspoon of calcium chloride
1/2 teaspoon of gypsum
1/2 vanilla bean, split and scraped
1/2 cup of chopped pecans (optional)

Instructions:

In a large pot, bring 2 1/2 gallons of water to a boil.

Add the Prague malt, Carahell malt, Light Munich malt, Wheat malt, and flaked oats to the pot and stir until dissolved.

Turn off the heat and let the mixture cool to room temperature.

Once the mixture is cool, transfer it to a fermenter and add the corn sugar, salt, calcium chloride, and gypsum.

 Stir until dissolved, then add the vanilla bean and chopped pecans (if using).

Let the mixture sit for 24 hours, then pitch the yeast and let it ferment for 7 days.

After 7 days, taste the beer and adjust the flavor as needed.

Let the beer ferment for an additional 7 days, then bottle or keg it.

How to Make a Rustic Bread

Rustic bread is a term used to describe a loaf that is made with only basic ingredients, has a crusty exterior, and a chewy interior. Unlike loaves of bread you buy at the store, rustic loaves are often made by hand, without any preservatives or kneading. Instead, they are typically made with a sourdough starter, which gives them a characteristic flavor.

The following steps will show you how to make a rustic loaf of bread.

Ingredients:
- 3 cups flour
- 1 1/2 cups warm water
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 cup sourdough starter

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, warm water, olive oil, salt, and sourdough starter. Use a wooden spoon or stand mixer to mix until a shaggy dough forms.
2. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and let it rest for 18-24 hours at room temperature.
3. Preheat your oven to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. Place a cast-iron Dutch oven or other heavy pot in the oven.
4. Transfer the dough to a well-floured surface. Use a sharp knife or dough scraper to score the top of the dough with three slashes.
5. Use the scored side of the dough as the top as you gently transfer it to the preheated pot. Cover the pot and bake for 30 minutes.
6. Uncover the pot and continue baking for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the bread sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
7. Let the bread cool in the pot for a few minutes, then transfer it to a cooling rack to finish cooling.

Pacman frogs are a nocturnal species of frog that make great pets due to their friendly nature and small size. Setting up a Pacman frog enclosure is quite simple, but there are a few key things you should know to keep your pet happy and healthy.

Select an appropriate enclosure. Pacman frogs should be kept in a terrarium-style enclosure that's at least 10 gallons in size. Look for an enclosure that's made from a material like glass or plastic, as these materials help retain heat and moisture.

Use a humidity-loving substrate.  Pacman frogs need a substrate that holds moisture well. Therefore, you should avoid using materials like lava rocks, pumice, or coconut husks. Instead, use a substrate like wet sphagnum moss, vermiculite, or perlite. These materials will help keep your frog's enclosure moist and humid.

Don't forget to add hiding spots. Pacman frogs like to hide in small spaces, so be sure to include some hiding spots in your frog's enclosure. You could use small rocks, branches, or wood chunks to create hiding spots.

Provide fresh water. Pacman frogs need access to fresh water at all times. This water should be shallow enough for your frog to easily drink from, but deep enough to soak its body. Water bowls should be cleaned and refilled daily.

Maintain the right temperature. Pacman frogs are cold-blooded, which means that their body temperature changes with the temperature of their surroundings. During the day, keep your frog's enclosure somewhere warm, like a kitchen counter or a warm, shady spot in your home. At night, move the enclosure to a cooler location, like a basement or an area with low foot traffic.

Maintain the right humidity. Pacman frogs need a humid environment to stay healthy. Try to keep the humidity in your frog's enclosure above 70%, as this will help ensure that your frog doesn't get dehydrated.

Don't forget to clean. Pacman frog enclosures should be spot-cleaned daily and completely replaced every week. This will help prevent the buildup of waste and bacteria in your frog's home.

Blue cheese is a type of cheese that has been cured with cultures of the mold Penicillium. The cheese has a crumbly texture and a sharp, pungent flavor. Blue cheese can be eaten crumbed on salads, or melted on steaks. Making blue cheese is a long process, so patience is key.

Purchase pasteurized milk. Blue cheese can be made with raw milk, but pasteurized milk is easier to work with because it doesn't have any bacteria in it to begin with. Look for whole milk that is not ultra-pasteurized.
 
 Ripen the milk. Blue cheese is made by adding Penicillium cultures to milk. These cultures are what give the cheese its distinctive flavor and what helps determine what type of blue cheese it will be. The cultures can be added in several ways:
   
- Penicillium can be added by spraying the milk with a solution that contains the cultures.
   
- Penicillium can be added by mixing the milk with a clot of old cheese that contains the cultures.
   
- Penicillium can be added by mixing the milk with a powder that contains the cultures.
   
Let the milk ripen for 1 day. The milk will thicken as the Penicillium cultures multiply. 

Add the rennet. Rennet is a natural enzyme found in the stomachs of ruminant animals. It is what causes milk to clot into curds. The rennet can be added by mixing a few drops into the milk, or by mixing a crushed tablet of rennet into the milk.
   
Let the milk clot. The milk will go through a process of curdling as the rennet works. The time it takes for the milk to clot is dependent on the amount of rennet added, the amount of milk used, and the temperature of the milk. typical clotting time is 5 to 10 minutes.
   
Cut the curds. Once the milk has clotted, cut it into small pieces. This will allow the whey, or liquid, to come out of the curds. The curds should be cut into 3/8-inch pieces.
   
Mash the curds. To begin mashing the curds, take a large paddle or a wooden or bamboo backscraper, and start from the bottom of the pot. Move the paddle or backscraper in an up-and-down motion, bringing the curds to the top of the pot and then pressing them back down again. This will break up the curds and release more whey.
   
Drain the curds. Once the curds have been mashed, they are ready to be drained. A cheesecloth can be used to line a colander for easy draining. Just pour the curds into the lined colander and let the whey drain out.
   
Mash and stir. At this point, the curds should be transferred to a bowl and mashed with a fork or a potato masher. As the curds are mashed, they will begin to separate into small pieces. Continue mashing and stirring until the curds are broken down into small pieces.
   
Strain the curds. Place a strainer over a large pot and line it with cheesecloth. Strain the curds through the cheesecloth and into the pot. The whey will drain out of the curds, leaving just the curds in the pot.
   
Salting the curds. Once all of the whey has been strained out of the curds, the curds are ready to be salted. Add 3 tablespoons of salt to the pot, and then begin mashing and stirring the curds again. As you salt the curds, the curds will separate even more. Continue mashing and stirring until the curds are broken down into small pieces.
   
 Press the curds. Place a cheesecloth over a sieve and set a mold on top of the cheesecloth. Transfer the curds to the mold, and then fold the cheesecloth over the top. Place a heavy object, such as a brick or a book, on top of the mold to press the curds.
   
Aging the cheese. Once the curds have been pressed, they are ready to be aged. Aging blue cheese involves a process of culturing and aging. The curds are transferred to a cooler environment, such as a refrigerator, and are left to cure for a few days. During this time, the cheese will begin to grow a crust of blue mold. The cheese is then transferred to a warmer environment, such as a room, and is left to cure for a few weeks. During this time, the blue mold will grow throughout the cheese.
   
Storage. Blue cheese can be stored in the refrigerator for up to two months, or in the freezer for up to six months.
